blocks.text: Once you arrive in Guwahati, our team representative will greet you with a warm welcome at the airport/railway station.After that, you'll be driven to Kaziranga National Park, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The park is home to dense forests, tall elephant grass, and numerous water bodies.Once you reach there, check into your hotel and freshen up. Take some time for relaxation.In the evening, we’ll take you to the Orchid & Biodiversity Park. A perfect photo op is when the sun is setting over the Kaziranga’s marshlands!There’s also an opportunity to enjoy the Assamese cultural dance show, which takes place in the evening.Enjoy an overnight stay in the Kaziranga.

Get up early in the morning and go out for an exciting Elephant Safari in the park. You’ll get a chance to spot the rhinos, swamp deer, and elephants. Also, the park is home to over 70% of the world’s one-horned rhino population!After your safari session, return to your hotel for a delicious breakfast.In the afternoon, we again set out for a safari. However, this time we’ll go on a jeep safari, where you can find animals like royal Bengal tigers, hog deer, wild elephants, and more.Have a leisurely evening. You can utilise this time to either rest or explore the park on your own.Take a restful night of sleep at Kaziranga.Important Note:Elephant rides are all regulated and controlled by the Forest Department of the Govt. of Assam and are subject to availability only.Places You’ll See
DAY 3: Transfer to Bomdila (230 km / 7 hrs) – Trip to Gontse Rabgyaling Monastery

Have a hearty breakfast in the morning.Now, we’ll leave the park and move towards Bomdila. This charming town is famous for its hand-woven carpets. The drive is quite long – 7 hours. However, the journey is quite scenic. Capture the lifelong pictures of lush tea gardens and river valleys as you pass them.We’ll also make a stop-off at Tipi Orchidarium along the way. This institute houses over 500 orchid species!Once you reach there, we’ll visit the peaceful Gontse Rabgyaling Monastery.Check into your hotel and enjoy an overnight stay.Places You’ll See
DAY 4: Transfer to Tawang (180 km / 7 hrs)

Have breakfast in the morning.Now you’ll be transferred to Tawang. The 7-hour journey is quite scenic as you pass through snow-capped landscapes and strategic mountain passes.Along the way, we’ll be making a stopover at Sela Pass (13,700 ft), which stays covered in snow for a good part of the year. Capture patriotic moments with your camera as the flag flutters with the wind.We’ll also be making a stop at the Sela Lake and Jaswantgarh War Memorial!If time permits, we’ll also visit the hidden gem of Arunachal Pradesh, the beautiful Nuranang (Jung) Falls.Once you get to Tawang, check into your hotel and get a restful night of sleep.Places You’ll See

Have a delicious breakfast and then get ready for a sightseeing tour of Tawang today!We’ll be visiting the following tourist attractions:Tawang Monastery– This is India’s largest and the world’s second-largest Buddhist monasteryUrgelling Monastery– Welcome to the birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama!Ani Gompa– This serene Buddhist nunnery offers a very peaceful environment for meditationBuddha Park– Capture the photos of the majestic golden statue of Lord Buddha hereTawang Craft Centre– Get acquainted with the traditional Monpa handicrafts, like woollen carpets, wood carvings, masks, etc.War Memorial– Pay tribute to the martyred soldiers of the 1962 Indo-China WarIn the evening, enjoy an exciting Light & Sound Show at Tawang War Memorial. Also, take some time out to stroll in the local markets and shop for souvenirs.Return to your hotel and get a restful night of sleep.Places You’ll See
DAY 6: Bumla Pass (37 km) – Madhuri Lake

Enjoy a hearty breakfast at your hotel.Thereafter, you’ll be taken on a full-day sightseeing tour of Bumla Pass. The drive is just 37 km and can be covered in under an hour. Located at an altitude of 16,000 ft, it is a must-visit spot for adventure lovers!From here, you can watch the Indo-China border being manned by the Indian soldiers. Photo ops galore!On the return journey, we’ll make a stop at the Pankang Teng Tso Lake (PT Tso). Enjoy the beautiful scenery of pine forests and snow! Do engage in a little photography session here, as it’ll be worthwhile.Next, you’ll be taken to the Shonga-tser Lake, which is also known as the Madhuri Lake. And yes, it’s named after the Bollywood actress Madhuri Dixit, after she shot a song for the movie Koyla here. Originally, the lake was formed from an earthquake in 1971. Do take the photo shots of reflection in this beautiful lake.In the evening, we’ll drive you back towards Tawang.Also, you can enjoy the Light & Sound Show at the Tawang War Memorial, the tickets for which you have to arrange on your own. The show beautifully portrays the valour of Indian soldiers during the 1962 war with China.Return to your hotel at Tawang for an overnight stay.Places You’ll See
DAY 7: Tawang to Dirang Transfer (140 km / 4.5 hrs)

Have breakfast and then check out of your hotel.Now, you’ll be driven to Dirang, the journey of which will take less than 5 hours. It’s famous for having miraculous hot water springs, which are believed to cure skin ailments.Enjoy the scenic journey filled with picturesque landscapes, quaint villages, and cultural sites.Along the way, we’ll be making a stop at the TDL Monastery.Once you reach Dirang, check into your hotel and take a restful night of sleep.Places You’ll See
DAY 8: Transfer to Guwahati (300 km / 10 hrs)

Wake up early in the morning, and drive back towards Guwahati via Kalaktang. This 10-hour drive is quite long but also scenic.Capture the beautiful picture of lush valleys and farms as you pass them.Once you reach there, check into your hotel and get a restful night of sleep.
DAY 9: Transfer to Cherrapunji (150 km / 4 hrs) and Sightseeing

Have breakfast in the morning.And now you’ll be taken on a sightseeing trip to Cherrapunji, the wettest place on Earth! It’s a quintessential paradise for nature lovers and explorers.Explore the natural falls, like Elephant Falls, Nohkalikai Falls, and Seven Sisters Falls. Don’t forget to capture their timeless beauty with your camera!You’ll also be taken to the following places:Mawkdok Dympep ValleyMawsmai CavesEco ParkAfter a tiring yet fulfilling sightseeing trip, return to your hotel and get some sleep.Note:Accommodations here are basic three-star hotels. Don’t expect too many modern amenities.Places You’ll See
DAY 10: Transfer to Mawlynnong (81 km / 2.5 hrs) – Dawki (31 km / 1.5 hrs)

Take a nourishing meal in the morning. Afterwards, you’ll be taken on a tour of Meghalaya. In particular, you’ll be visiting:Mawlynnong Village– This is Asia’s cleanest village!Living Root Bridge– Get inspired by the locals’ ingenious craftsmanshipLater, we’ll be visiting Dawki, where you can enjoy a thrilling boat ride on the crystal-clear waters of the Umngot River. The river is so clear and transparent that the tourists say that they feel like flying in the air.Come back to your hotel in Shillong and enjoy an overnight stay.Places You’ll See
DAY 11: Shillong to Guwahati Transfer (100 km / 2.5 hrs) and Departure

Enjoy a hearty breakfast at the hotel in the morning.On this last day of your tour, the first half will be spent sightseeing. You’ll be taken to the following places:Ward's LakeShillong CathedralUmiam LakeLady Hydari ParkAfter that, you’ll be dropped off at the Guwahati airport or railway station, as per your choice. Hope you have a great trip!Note:Lady Hydari Park is closed on Mondays.Places You’ll See

blocks.text: There are countless temples in India. However, Jyotirlingas hold a place of their own! Deemed as the ultimate pilgrimage,

the trip to these holy temples is considered highly sacred for it promises Moksha – liberation from the cycle of birth and death! The Jyotirlingas are distributed across the country – from Somnath in Gujarat to Rameshwaram in Tamil Nadu! Although this is a challenging journey, our 12 Jyotirlinga Tour Package takes you to all these special shrines of Lord Shiva across the entire nation.

So think no more! Book this package now, and be the recipient of the abundant blessings that will fall your way once you complete this trip. To get a quote and know more, simply give us a call and we’ll get back to you shortly!

The 12 Jyotirlingas are considered highly sacred, and visiting them is a must for every Lord Shiva devotee. It’s believed that these temples manifest from the very energy of him when he was in the form of an infinite cosmic light pillar.

As per the Shiva Purana, once Lord Shiva appeared in the form of this bright light in order to exert his supremacy over Lord Vishnu and Lord Brahma. And now, each Jyotirlinga is a representation of his divine energy, and is considered to be a self-manifested lingam! Also, it’s believed that taking this sacred spiritual tour of Lord Shiva temples cleanses one’s sins and grants them Moksha, in turn.

Moreover, if you go to these holy temples, you can enjoy the culture and traditions of different places that you get to visit while being on this holy journey. Also, many devotees combine this trip with other tours such as Char Dham Yatra or Shaktipeeth visits, to make this a truly mega pilgrimage!
Book My Quick Trippers’s Jyotirlinga Darshan package and take an easy-peasy comfortable trip to India's most sacred shrines!
Here’s a quick guide to all twelve shrines covered in the 12 Jyotirlinga Tour Package:

items: Somnath: This was one of the very first Jyotirlingas! This sea-facing temple symbolizes eternal faith. Devotes simply love the evening light and sound show here.
Mallikarjuna: Also known as the “Kailash of the South”, this temple is associated with Parvati as Mallika and Shiva as Arjuna.
Mahakaleshwar: This is the only south-facing Jyotirlinga you’ll find. It’s famous for its holy Bhasma Aarti, where Lord Shiva is offered the sacred ash.
Omkareshwar: The specialty of this Jyotirlinga is that it is located on an island that is shaped like the OM symbol. It’s believed that coming here fulfills your wishes.
Kedarnath: This temple has a huge significance associated with it. Not only is it a Jyotirlinga, it’s also a part of the Chhota Dham circuit. It’s also the highest Jyotirlinga in altitude.
Bhimashankar: Surrounded by dense forests, this temple is linked to the mythology about the demon Tripurasura being defeated by Lord Shiva.
Kashi Vishwanath: Located in the ‘spiritual capital of India’, Varanasi, this temple promises Moksha if someone dies here of natural causes.
Trimbakeshwar: This is a unique Jyotirlinga that has 3 lingams, representing Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. This temple is popular for its Narayan Nagbali Puja rituals.
Vaidyanath: This temple sees a load of pilgrim traffic in the Shravan month, that is, when Kanwariyas visit this temple. Lord Shiva is worshipped here as the supreme healer, a Vaidya that is.
Nageshwar: This Jyotirlinga houses a tall Shiva statue, and it’s associated with the demon Daruka.

Ramanathaswamy: This temple has a very old Ramayana link. It’s believed that Lord Rama worshipped Lord Shiva here before he went to the Lanka war. There are also 22 sacred wells inside the temple where one can take a ritual bath.
Grishneshwar: This is the smallest Jyotirlinga, located very close to the Ajanta-Ellora caves. You can enjoy the rich carvings on temple walls here and the ever-present peaceful atmosphere.

blocks.text: To enjoy a smooth trip, simply opt for our Jyotirlinga Yatra booking and travel in comfort!
12 Jyotirlinga Tour Package by Train and Flight

My Quick Trippers also offers you combo 12 Jyotirlinga Tour Packages by Train and Flight , where you get to travel by both railways and plane. This combined trip makes the journey easier and far smoother. With the comfort & high speed of air travel, along with the traditional experience of the train journey, you get to enjoy the best of both worlds.

On this hybrid route, we would cover segments like Mumbai to Madurai and Hyderabad to Deoghar by flight. This is the most suitable way, as these are located far from each other and flying there considerably reduces the travel time. And for the shorter segments like Omkareshwar to Ujjain or Nashik to Bhimashankar, we can go for the scenic train journey.

With this train and flight Jyotirlinga Yatra package , devotees reach the Jyotirlingas in the most optimal time and also reduce fatigue. In general, this fight and train to Jyotirlingas tour is the best way to complete Darshan of all 12 Jyotirlingas (takes about 12-18 days). Book now or call us to know more about this combo package!
Best Time for the 12 Jyotirlinga Tour

The best time to go on this sacred Jyotirlinga tour differs from region to region, as the sacred shrines are distributed all across India. However, for most shrines, you can consider the season of autumn (September – November) for taking this sacred tour. The weather in this window is pleasant for the most part, and therefore can be considered for the holy trip.

Moreover, this is also ideal for the tour to Kedarnath , which gets closed in November, and stays so until April. Also, this window is great for visiting the temple in the south ( Rameswaram and Srisailam ) as well.
Here is some travel advice that you might find useful on this Jyotirlinga Yatra Package:

items: Even before you step out for this sacred tour, make a Sankalp in front of Lord Shiva’s idol in your home or a nearby temple, asking for the success of this tour.

Book your 12 Jyotirlinga Travel Package in advance – at least 3-6 months. The slots get quickly filled up, especially if you’re planning to travel during special occasions, such as Shravan, Navratri, and Maha Shivaratri.
If you’re a senior citizen, then consider going by train or plane, as this will help you reduce the physical strain and exhaustion caused by road travel.
If you plan to take the helicopter services, then make sure you have your ID proof and medical certificate ready.

Try to make your trip even more fulfilling by combining your Jyotirlinga tour with nearby major sightseeing attractions, like Dwarkadhish Temple (in Dwarka), Ellora Caves (in Aurangabad), and Rameswaram beaches (in Rameswaram).

Try to group your Jyotirlinga tour in a region-wise cluster. For example, combine your temple trips in West India, South India, Central India, and North India. This organised tour will help you save time and reduce your fatigue significantly.
There’s always a chance of delays. This could be due to weather and other unforeseeable factors. Therefore, always keep 1-2 days spare in your Jyotirlinga Yatra itinerary.
Throughout your trip, stay hydrated. Always carry a water bottle with you. Also, eat easily digestible, light food to aid digestion.
Always follow the temple etiquette. Some common practices include removing your shoes before entering the temple, wearing modest clothes, and not carrying leather items inside the shrine.

blocks.text: Day 1: : Arrival in Mumbai and Journey to Rajkot

items: Once you reach Mumbai, our travel representatives will greet you with a warm welcome.
Now, it’s time to catch the overnight train to Rajkot, Gujarat. You’ll get full assistance in boarding from our side.
Enjoy an overnight stay on the train. We recommend packing some light snacks and water for this train journey.

blocks.text: Day 2: Trip to Dwarkadhish and Nageshwar Jyotirlinga

items: By early morning, you’ll arrive in Rajkot.
Deboard the train, and now you’ll be driven to Dwarka. This holy city is one of the Char Dhams and also a Sapta Puri.
Now, check into your pre-booked hotel and freshen up!
Later, you’ll be taken to the Dwarkadhish Temple first. It is dedicated to Lord Krishna, where he’s worshipped in his royal form as the King of Dwarka!
Next, you’ll be driven to the very first Jyotirlinga of this tour, that is, Nageshwar Jyotirlinga. Lord Shiva is worshipped here as the protector against poison.
After your Darshan and Poojan, return to your hotel for dinner in the evening.
Get a restful night of sleep at your hotel.
Have breakfast and then check out of your hotel.
Now, you’ll be transferred to Somnath near Veraval. Once you arrive in this city, check into your hotel and take rest for a while.

Afterwards, you'll be taken to Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple, a shrine that enjoys a glorious history. According to the Hindu mythology, it’s believed that the temple was originally built by Chandra Dev in order to please Lord Shiva. Over centuries, this temple has been destroyed and rebuilt 17 times, and now stands as a metaphorical symbol of faith and resilience!
Also, attend the evening Aarti at the temple.
Then, come back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 4 – Somnath to Ujjain transfer (Overnight Train Journey)

items: Wake up early and attend the morning Aarti at Somnath temple.
Now, check out of your hotel and head to the railway station and catch a train to Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh.
This will be an overnight journey by train. We recommend carrying a light shawl or blanket with you as the nights can get a little chilly.

blocks.text: Day 5 – Arrival in Ujjain and Visit to Omkareshwar Temple

items: You’ll arrive in Ujjain early in the morning. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and take a little rest for a while.

Now, you’ll be taken to the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga, which is situated on an island surrounded by the Narmada River. There’s another specialty of this island, which is that it is shaped like an ‘OM’ symbol. You can also choose to circumambulate the island, as many devotees do.
Afterwards, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 6 – Ujjain (Mahakaleshwar Darshan) and Train to Haridwar

items: Get up early in the morning and proceed for the Darshan and Poojan at the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga. This is one of the most revered shrines of Lord Shiv, where he’s worshiped as the destroyer of time itself.
If you reach there early, you can also witness the Bhasma Aarti, which takes place from 4 AM to 6 AM. In this sacred ritual, Lord Shiva is offered the sacred ash.
Later, enjoy a trip to the popular temples like Harsiddhi Mata Temple and Kal Bhairav Temple. Both of these temples have a strong background in the rich Tantric traditions of India.
In the evening, you’ll be driven to the railway station, where you’ll board the train to Haridwar.
Enjoy an overnight stay on the train.

blocks.text: Day 7 – Arrival in Haridwar (Ganga Aarti Experience)

items: You’ll reach Haridwar in the morning. From the railway station, you'll be transferred to your hotel, where you can check in. Take some time to relax and freshen up. The rest of the day is free!
In the evening, drop by the Har ki Pauri and witness the mesmerizing Ganga Aarti. Watch as the thousands of Diyas float by on the Ganga River.
Return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 8 – Transfer to Guptkashi and Visit to Ardhanarishvara Temple

items: Now, begin a scenic drive towards Guptkashi. Once you get there, check into your pre-booked hotel.
Now, you’ll be taken to the Ardhanarishvara Temple. This temple holds a great deal of significance as it symbolizes Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati’s unity.
Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.
In the morning, we’ll depart from Sonprayag to start the trek to the Kedarnath temple.
Begin your 16 km trek via Gaurikund. You can also hire a pony/Palki service to reach the Kedarnath Dham.
Once you reach the temple, engage in the Darshan and Poojan ritual. The views all around are gorgeous, providing you with a backdrop of snow-capped peaks.
Wait till the sun goes down, when you can attend the evening Aarti, which is a soul-stirring experience, to say the least.
Your dinner and overnight stay will be arranged in Kedarnath only.

blocks.text: Day 10 – Morning Aarti at Kedarnath and Transfer to Rudraprayag

items: Wake up early before sunrise and attend the morning Aarti at Kedarnath temple.
Now trek back to Sonprayag. From there, you’ll be taken to Rudraprayag.
Check into your hotel there and enjoy an overnight stay.
Now, you’ll be driven back to Haridwar.
Once you reach there, board the overnight train for Varanasi. Your lunch and dinner will be served on the train itself.

blocks.text: Day 12 – Evening Ganga Aarti at Varanasi

items: Welcome to Varanasi! This is one of the world’s oldest cities, and is quite dear to Lord Shiva.
Now check into your hotel and rest for a while.
Visit the Dasaswamedh Ghat in the evening, where you can witness the grand Ganga Aarti live. Take in the whole experience of chants, bells, and floating lamps!
Come back to your hotel in the evening for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 13 – Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga and Transfer to Deoghar

items: Wake up early to go for a morning Darshan at the Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga. Perform Poojan to your heart’s content.
Next, we’ll take you to the Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple.
After that, board a train to Jasidih. Once you get there, you’ll take a short drive towards Deoghar, Jharkhand.
Enjoy an overnight stay in your hotel at Deoghar.

blocks.text: Day 14 – Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga and Train to Chennai

items: Wake up early in the morning and get ready for Darshan at the Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga. This temple is special since here Lord Shiva is worshipped as a healer (Vaidya).
Perform your Abhishek Puja & Darshan and soak in the calming atmosphere of the shrine. It is believed that Ravana himself worshipped Lord Shiva here by offering his heads as a sacrifice.
Next, board a train to Kolkata from here. Once you reach Howrah station, take a connecting train to Chennai.
Enjoy an overnight stay on the train.

blocks.text: Day 15 – Arrival in Chennai and Train to Rameswaram

items: You’ll arrive in Chennai in the morning.
Take some time to freshen up and relax in the station waiting room.
Later, board the train to Rameswaram, one of the most holy pilgrimage towns in India!
Enjoy an overnight stay on the train.
Once you reach Rameswaram, get to your hotel and check in.

The rest of the day is purposefully made free of any sightseeing. You can take this leisure time to rest or travel on your own around the area. If you go out, do indulge in the local Tamil vegetarian cuisine, which is simply delicious.
At night, enjoy dinner and get a restful night of sleep.

blocks.text: Day 17 – Rameswaram Darshan and Drive to Madurai

items: We’ll visit the Ramanathaswamy Temple early in the morning. This temple houses the very Rameshwaram Jyotirlinga that Lord Rama worshipped after he went to war with Ravana.
Afterwards, you’ll be taken for a drive to Madurai.
In the evening, visit the majestic Meenakshi Amman Temple, which is dedicated to Goddess Parvati. Enjoy the masterpiece of Dravidian architecture that this temple is!
Spend the night in your Madurai hotel.
Treat yourself to a delicious breakfast.
Now, you’ll be transferred to Madurai railway station, where you can board the train to Pune.
Enjoy an overnight journey on the train.
Once you arrive in Pune, check into your hotel.
The rest of the day is free. You can utilize it by either resting or going sightseeing/shopping on your own.
Enjoy the overnight stay at your hotel in Pune.

blocks.text: Day 20 – Visit to Bhimashankar and Trimbakeshwar

items: Have breakfast and then get ready for the Jyotirlinga tour.
Today, you’ll be taken to the Bhimashankar Temple, which is located in the lush Sahyadri Hills. It's also considered to be the source of the river Bhima.
In the latter part of the day, we’ll visit yet another Jyotirlinga, that is Trimbakeshwar Temple, which is located in Nashik.
At night, return to the hotel and get a restful night of sleep.

blocks.text: Day 21 – Trimbakeshwar Darshan, Nashik Sightseeing, and Trip to Shirdi

items: In the morning, set out again for the Darshan at the Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga.

Afterwards, you’ll indulge in a sightseeing tour of Nashik, where you’ll be visiting: Sita Gufa (This is where Sita stayed during exile) Kapileshwar Temple Kala Ram Temple Panchavati and Godavari River
Later in the day, drive towards Shirdi and check into your hotel for an overnight stay.
After breakfast, get ready for Darshan of Shri Sai Baba at the famous Shirdi temple.
Spend ample time here to perform Pooja, Aarti, and pay homage to Baba.
Enjoy lunch and some free time for shopping at the local market for Sai Baba souvenirs.
Return to your hotel for overnight stay.
After breakfast, check out of the hotel and proceed towards Aurangabad.
Check into your Aurangabad hotel and enjoy a relaxed evening. Overnight stay at Aurangabad.
After breakfast, proceed for sightseeing of Ajanta and Ellora Caves. Ajanta caves are famous for their ancient Buddhist rock-cut architecture and murals.
Ellora caves are known for their Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain rock-cut temples, representing India’s religious harmony.
Return to Aurangabad hotel in the evening and enjoy dinner and overnight stay.

blocks.text: Ans. The 12 Jyotirlingas are special shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva. These are spread all across India, and it’s said that whoever completes a visit to all the temples gets his special blessings. The 12 Jyotirlingas are Somnath, Mallikarjuna, Mahakaleshwar, Omkareshwar, Kedarnath, Bhimashankar, Kashi Vishwanath, Trimbakeshwar, Baidyanath, Nageshwar, Ramanathaswamy, and Grishneshwar.
Q2. Why are the Jyotirlingas considered special?

Ans. According to the Hindu mythology, it’s believed that each Jyotirlinga is a manifestation of Lord Shiva. In the beginning of the universe, he took the form of a light pillar, symbolizing his infinite form, which is now manifested as the Jyotirlinga temples.
Q3. How many days are needed to cover all 12 Jyotirlingas?

Ans. For a comfortable trip to all the Jyotirlingas, it’s suggested that you take 25-30 days for this sacred tour. In this plan, you can comfortably cover the tour by giving sufficient time to each of the temples in this trip.
Q4. What is the cost of a 12 Jyotirlinga tour package?

Ans. We offer our 12 Jyotirlinga tour package at INR 95,000 per person. In this plan, all your meals, accommodation, and transfers will be covered completely by us. All you have to do is book our package and relax as we take you to the twelve most sacred shrines in the country.
Q5. Which Jyotirlinga is the hardest to visit?

Ans. The hardest Jyotirlinga to visit is the Kedarnath, which is located in the Himalayan region. The toughest thing about this shrine is that devotees have to undertake a full 16 km trek to reach the temple. Although you can book a helicopter or pony/Palki service, there’s still harsh weather and high altitude conditions that pilgrims have to brave.
Q6. Can senior citizens do the 12 Jyotirlinga Yatra?

Ans. Yes, senior citizens can also undertake this holy tour. My Quick Trippers offers special care towards senior citizens with Darshan assistance, flight arrangements, medical supplies, and 24x7 call support.
Q7. Is there a government package for the 12 Jyotirlinga Yatra?

Ans. Yes, you can also avail of government Jyotirlinga circuit tours (via IRCTC), which offer you a train and bus journey to cover this trip. The best thing about these packages is that they are very affordable and usually well-organised.
Q8. What is the best time to do the Jyotirlinga Yatra?
Ans. The best time to visit the Jyotirlinga is in the autumn season – September – November. During the window, the weather remains quite pleasant to cover them in your trip.
Q9. What is the spiritual benefit of visiting all 12 Jyotirlingas?

Ans. There are lots of spiritual benefits to covering the 12 Jyotirlingas. It’s believed that whoever visits all of them is granted moksha and has their sins cleansed. In addition, it’s said that the devotee is blessed with peace, prosperity, and spiritual fulfilment.
Q10. Which Jyotirlinga is closest to Varanasi?
Ans. The Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga is closest to Varanasi. In fact, it is itself located in Varanasi.
Q11. Which Jyotirlinga is near Dwarka?
Ans. The Nageshwar Jyotirlinga is closest to Dwarka. It is located just 16 km from there. Also, it’s also situated very near the famous Dwarkadhish Temple.
Q12. What is special about Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga?

Ans. This Jyotirlinga is quite special as only here Lord Shiva is worshipped with sacred ash. You won’t find this ritual of Bhasma Aarti anywhere else in India. Also, this is the only Jyotirlinga that faces south.
Q13. Which Jyotirlinga is located in the Himalayas?
Ans. The Kedarnath Jyotirlinga is situated in the Himalayas. In fact, it’s the Jyotirlinga with the highest elevation – 11,755 feet above the sea level.
Q14. What should I pack for the Jyotirlinga Yatra?

Ans. For most of the Jyotirlingas shrines, you can be safe with packing comfortable cotton clothes. However, for the Kedarnath shrine, which is located in the Himalayas, pack warm woollen clothes. In addition, we advise packing comfortable walking shoes, in addition to medicines, a water bottle, and an ID proof.
Q15. Which Jyotirlinga is also one of the Char Dhams?
Ans. Kedarnath Jyotirlinga is also one of the Char Dhams, in addition to Badrinath, Gangotri, and Yamunotri. Being part of the Chhota Dham circuit increases its spiritual significance even more.

Visit Ram Janmabhoomi Temple. It is the original birthplace of Lord Rama. After a long held wait of many years, the temple was consecrated on Jan 22nd, 2024.
Enjoy numerous festivals related to Lord Rama like Ram Navami, Dussehra and experience the city’s sacred charm.
There are many places in Ayodhya like Kanak Bhawan, Dashrath Mahal which will take you back in the time of Treta Yuga.
You will get hassle free pick up and drop service within Ayodhya. Our driver will take care of all the routes while you enjoy your trip with the loved ones.
According to the chosen Tour package, you will get comfortable and centrally located hotels & guesthouses to relax after spiritual tours
VIP and Guided Darshan of Ram Janmabhoomi, Hanuman Garhi, Kanak Bhawan, and Treta Ke Thakur

blocks.text: How to Spend 2 Days in Ayodhya- Perfect Itinerary
Day 1: Arriving in Ayodhya - Feel the divine presence of Lord Rama

On the first day, our tour representative will pick you up from your designated location (station/airport) and transfer you to your pre-booked hotel. After some relaxation, you will enjoy a guided Ayodhya Tour. We will explore the following places-

items: Ram Janmabhoomi- Ram Janmabhoomi is a landmark temple as it is the birthplace of Lord Rama. devotees from all across the world visit here to get the divine blessings of Lord Rama. After a long held wait of many years, the sacred consecration of the temple took place on Jan22nd 2024.

Kanak Bhawan Temple- Kanak Bhavan has kept the stories of Treta Yuga. This sacred temple was a gift to Lord Rama and Goddess Sita just after their wedding by Kaikeyi. It used to be their personal residence.

Dashrath Mahal - It is a popular Siddha Peetha, and divine abode of King Dasharatha, (father of Lord Rama). You will see the beautiful idols of Lord Rama, Devi Sita, Lakshman, Shatrughan and Bharat here.

Hanuman Garhi- Hanuman Garhi is dedicated to Lord Hanuman who is considered as a protector of Ayodhya. It is said that Lord Hanuman resides in a cave and watches over the entire city of Ayodhya to protect them from all the evils.

blocks.text: Evening Tour- Embracing Bhakti, culture and peace wholeheartedly

items: The divine Aarti at Saryu River in Naya Ghat is something which will take your breath away.
Witness the living spiritual heritage of Ayodhya as you stroll along the serene Saryu River Ghats.

blocks.text: Overnight stay- After the sightseeing Ayodhya Tour with your loved ones, the day ends on a happy note. We will return to our hotel room for an overnight stay.
Day 2: Cultural and spiritual escape in the city of Legends
After breakfast in the morning, we will explore the Saryu River to take a holy dip for spiritual purification and enjoy a scenic boat ride.
We will also witness the sacred

items: Ram ki Paidi- It's a beautiful series of Ghats built on the banks of the Saryu River. It’s a place where devotees take holy dip to dissolve their sins.
Nageshwarnath Temple- It is a must not miss place when you are on Ayodhya Tour. We will visit here for sure. It’s a temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, built by Kush ( son of Lord Rama).

blocks.text: If time allows, we will explore,

items: Valmiki Ramayana Bhawan– The sacred Bhawan is dedicated to Sage Valmiki (Creator of Ramayana). Its lush greenery and peaceful vibe are a perfect spot for meditation and relaxation.

Treta Ke Thakur- Treta Ke Thakur is a very popular sacred spot in Ayodhya. It’s the same place where Lord Rama performed Ashwamedha Yagya. There are many statues in this temple made of Blackstone and belonging to the era of Vikramaditya.

Evening- Ayodhya is a place where you will discover your soul and be nourished by the eternal heritage of faith. After sightseeing, we will depart from Ayodhya with the divine blessings of Lord Rama, Mata Sita and Lord Hanuman. We will drop you at your selected location and the trip to Ayodhya will end on a happy note.

blocks.text: Q1. What is the best time to visit Ayodhya with family and friends?

Ans: October to March is the best time to plan your trip to Ayodhya Tour with family and friends. The weather will be favorable to explore all the temples and enjoy boat rides and strolling in the Ghats.
Q2. Is VIP Darshan included in Ayodhya Tour package?

Ans: Yes, you can customize your Ayodhya itinerary to get VIP Darshan facility. Usually, it is available in our luxury tour packages but you can customize any of our packages according to your needs. You will have to pay extra charges.
Q3. What type of accommodation is available for 1 Night 2 Days Ayodhya Tour?

Ans: We offer the best accommodation facilities to our travellers. We have partnered with hotels that offer the best hospitality to the pilgrims. You will get best 3 starts to 5 start hotels, guesthouses or Dharamshalas. Book your tour in advance with us if you are travelling in peak season as the hotels of your choice might get already booked.
Q4. Is 2 Days enough for the Ayodhya Tour?

Ans: Yes, if you are only exploring Ayodhya, 2 days are enough to see all the famous attractions, strolling on the sacred Ghats, trying the best street food and embracing the spiritual vibes of Saryu River Aarti.
Q5. What are the coldest months in Ayodhya?

Ans: December and January are the coldest months in Ayodhya. Day time is still bearable to explore temples and Ghats at night the temperature will drop down to 3 or 4 degrees Celsius. Pack heavy woolens and jackets to travel comfortably in winter.

items: Route: Sightseeing at Western Group of Temples → Visit to Eastern Group of Temples and Departure

blocks.text: Day 1: Sightseeing at Western Group of Temples

After your arrival at Khajuraho, you’ll be transferred to your hotel by our team representative. Drop your bags and freshen up! Now, get ready for sightseeing at the Western Group of Temples! Explore Kandariya Mahadev Temple, Lakshman Temple, Chausath Yogini Temple, and more. In the evening, you can enjoy the cultural Light & Sound Show as well as a local dance performance that is held there regularly. Come back to the hotel and have a restful night of sleep. Places You’ll See
Day 2: Visit to Eastern Group of Temples and Departure

Relish a hearty breakfast in the morning. Today, you’ll explore the Eastern and Southern Group of Temples. See sculptures and statues at Parshvanatha Temple, Adinath Temple, Ghantai Temple, etc.! Enjoy artistic depictions of Apsaras, human emotions, stages of life, and much more! If time permits, you’ll be taken to watch the majestic Raneh Falls, where you can enjoy photography, too. blocks.text: Odisha is a beautiful state, known as the soul of India, located near the Bay of Bengal on the eastern coast.

It has a wide range of tourist attractions because this place is blessed with a vibrant culture, natural beauty, and impressive monuments. Nature lovers can also enjoy its scenic beaches and green forests
Visitors should explore Odisha’s famous Jagannath Temple, especially during the popular Rath Yatra festival. Apart from this, Sun temple is also a perfect place to see its beautiful architecture.

This trip covers four places in Odisha, such as Bhubaneswar, Konark, Puri, and Pipli. It is a 3-day Odisha trip, where you can choose between an affordable holiday tour or a luxury vacation. This tour package is also customizable and includes meals, hotels, and transportation. Book now for this unforgettable trip to see the beauty of Odisha.

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrival at Bhubaneswar (the capital of Odisha)

When you reach Bhubaneswar Airport or Railway Station, our representative will welcome you and take you to the hotel. Next you will visit the twin hills of Khandagiri and Udayagiri, where you can explore Jain Temple and Elephanta Caves, including the Lion Cave and Queen Cave from the first century BC. Bhubaneswar is famous for its temples built from the 7th to the 13th centuries. In this temple city, you can see the temples like Lingaraj, Mukteshwar, Kedargouri, Parashurameshvara Mandir, and Bindusagar.
Note: Nandankanan, the State Museum, and the Tribal Museum are closed on Mondays and state holidays.
Day 2: Bhubaneswar - Dhauli - Pipli - Konark - Puri

After breakfast, drive to Konark and stop to explore Dhauli (a Buddhist Stupa and peace pagoda) and Pipli (a popular village for its decorative work). When you reach Konark, visit the famous Konark Sun Temple. It was constructed in the 13th century by King Narasimha. Now, proceed to Puri, and on the way, visit Chandrabhaga Beach, which has amazing clean sands, and ramachandi Temple. Then, go to Puri and check into the hotel. In the evening, explore Puri and visit Shri Jagannath Temple, this temple is important in Odisha’s culture and religion. Over the years, many kings, religious leaders, worshippers, and devotees come to visit. It is famous around the world. Next, stay overnight at a hotel.
Note: Travelers cannot visit the Jagannath Temple during the “Anavasara’’ period, from the Krishna Paksha of Ashada month until the Jagannath Rath Yatra begins.
Day 3: Depart from Puri to Bhubaneshwar (60 kms /2 hours)

After breakfast, end your ‘Puri Konark Tour’. Return to Bhubaneswar, on the way stop at Raghurajpur, a village popular for its Pattachitra paintings, palm leaf art, wooden toys and more. You will also pass through Pipli and Dhauli. The trip ends at Bhubaneswar railway station.

blocks.text: With our 3 Days Madurai Rameshwaram Tour Package you can explore the real charm of South India in just 3 days. It is a perfect choice for those who have limited time but still want to see everything - famous temples, local culture and calm beaches in a short trip.

items: Route: Madurai - Rameshwaram → In Rameswaram → Rameswaram - Madurai *Departure*

blocks.text: The Madurai tour begins as you are picked up from your selected point - Airport, Railway Station, or your chosen location in Madurai. Our My Quick Trippers team will welcome you and take you to Rameshwaram. If you choose a guide, he will join the driver and help you whole day. On arrival, check into the hotel and later visit- Ramanathaswamy Temple- It is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas , located near the ocean, where the sea waves and scenic views make the place even more beautiful. Agnitheertham Ramjharoka Temple- The temple is famous for Lord Rama's footprints, and many tourists often share that they feel very relaxed here due to the cool wind and peaceful surroundings. After exploring the main attractions in Rameshwaram, return to the hotel for an overnight stay. Note- Ramanathaswamy Temple timings are from 5:00 AM to 1:00 PM and 3:00 PM to 9:00 PM. Places You’ll See

Early in the morning, around 5:00 AM , proceed for a holy bath at Agni Theertham (Sea Bath). Now visit the Sphatik Lingam (Mani Darshan). It is believed that praying here with a pure heart brings good fortune and happiness. After this, bathe in the 22 sacred wells inside the Ramanathaswamy Temple, known as Theerth Snanam. After the holy bath and Darshan, return to the hotel for breakfast. After breakfast, start your Rameshwaram sightseeing tour. Visit the Five-faced Hanuman Temple, Ramar Patham, Kothandaramaswamy Temple, Gandamadana Parvatham, Rama Setu or Adam's Bridge, Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam's House and Dhanushkodi (a beautiful spot to enjoy sunset). After sightseeing, return to the hotel. Overnight stay at Rameshwaram . Places You’ll See

Early in the morning, visit the Ramanathaswamy temple again or take a holy dip in the sea, known as Samudra Snanam . After that, drive back to Madurai. On the way, stop at the Pamban Bridge and Pamban Rail Scissors Bridge , famous for their beautiful views (Don't forget to click pictures here). When you reach Madurai, visit the famous Meenakshi Amman Temple . Spread over 14 acres , this temple will impress you with its size and beauty and there are more than 33,000 stone statues. The Rameshwaram Tour from Madurai ends with wonderful memories as you will be dropped at Madurai Airport or Railway Station for your next journey. Places You’ll See

items: Route: Srisailam - Hyderabad ( → Hyderabad Sightseeing Departure

blocks.text: DAY 01- Hyderabad - Srisailam (213 Kms / 4-5 Hours Drive)

Start your Srisailam Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga Tour with a pick-up from your chosen location in Hyderabad, either from the airport or railway station. Our team from the My Quick Trippers will come to receive you, and then you will proceed to Srisailam. During the journey, visit- Srisailam Dam Bhramaramba Devi Temple- Bhramaramba is the goddess of black bees; many devotees believe that if you listen carefully inside the temple, you can hear a buzzing sound of bees; it is a divine power of Bhramaramba Devi. Sakshi Ganapati Temple Hatkeshwar Temple Octopus View Point- A beautiful viewpoint where the Krishna River flows between the hills, and the shape looks like an octopus (A great spot for photography). Chenchu Lakshmi Tribal Museum Pathala Ganga Ropeway, Srisailam- Enjoy a cable car ride above the hills and forests, with a beautiful view of the valley. After reaching Srisailam, check in at the hotel. In the evening, visit the Mallikarjuna Temple for Darshan. Stay overnight in Srisailam. Note- Mallikarjuna Temple timings are 4:30 AM to 3:00 PM and 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM. Places You’ll See
Day 02- Srisailam - Hyderabad (214 Kms / 4-5 Hours Drive

Begin the morning with Pooja and Darshan at Lord Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple . Afterward, visit Sri Bhramaramba Ammavari Shakti Peeth Temple , then explore Paladara and Panchdara (Beautiful spots for hiking and nature adventure). Climb Sikharam hill to see Shikaresvara Temple , and continue to Sakshi Ganapathi Temple and Pathala Ganga . Don’t miss boating on Krishna River . Later, drive to Hyderabad . If time permits, visit the Statue of Equality near Hyderabad Airport. Enjoy your overnight stay in Hyderabad . Places You’ll See

Early in the morning, have breakfast, check out from the hotel, and proceed for sightseeing. Sightseeing for this day will depend on your departure time (optional). You may visit Birla Mandir , built on a hill. The view from the top is really amazing and worth capturing! After that, continue your journey to Golconda Fort . Later, visit the Salar Jung Museum . Now, go to the famous Charminar . Around it is Laad Bazaar, known for bangles, pearls and traditional Hyderabad items. Continue your trip to Hussain Sagar Lake , tourists enjoy spending time here. The lake view is truly beautiful, and the big Buddha statue in the center makes it even more special. Next, you’ll go to Lumbini Park . If you have some extra time, visit NTR Gardens for a relaxing walk with beautiful fountains, and stop near the Sudha Cars Museum to see some unique car designs. Later, you’ll be dropped at Hyderabad Airport or Railway Station for your next journey. Note- On Fridays, you can’t do city sightseeing in Hyderabad because many places are closed. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Feel spiritually nurtured by undertaking a spiritual pilgrimage with our Indore- Ujjain - Omkareshwar Tour Package that will help you visit the holiest sites of Lord Shiva,

items: Route: Arrival in Indore to Ujjain → Ujjain to Omkareshwar Day → Omkareshwar temple - Indore

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrival in Indore to Ujjain (60 kms / 2-2.5 hrs)

When you get down at the railway station or at the airport in Indore, you shall have to travel to Ujjain. As soon as you reach the city, you need to first check in and then rest. After lunch in the afternoon, you must commence with your sightseeing activities in Ujjain. Some of the places that you will visit today are, the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, ISKCON temple, Shakti Peeth,Gadkalika Temple, and the Harsiddhi Temple, Sandipani Ashram, Bade Ganesh Ka Mandir, Mahakal Lok and Ram Ghat . Later take an evening aarti at Mahakaleshwar Temple and back to the hotel. Have a sound sleep followed by a healthy and sumptuous dinner. Places You’ll See
Day 2: Ujjain to Omkareshwar Day (139 km / 3-4 hrs)

Once you have your light breakfast at the hotel, start your day by getting the darshan of Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga . Have a sacred bath in the River Narmada and pray to her to get a good life. Moreover, the city is also named after Lord Shiva, and its shape is rather close to Om (ॐ). Apart from this, with our Indore Ujjain Omkareshwar tour packages, you get to explore the hanging bridge over the River Narmada. This is one of the best selfie spots where you can make some amazing reels and expand your social media follower list. Moreover, this city is home to 68 Teerths (holding high religious significance) and has a cluster of 108 Shivlingas, making it a must-visit Shiva site. You should also visit the ancient Mamleshwar temple, established beautifully on the left bank of the Narmada. Furthermore, don’t forget to make a visit to the Statue of Oneness (dedicated to Adi Shankaracharya). It is believed that the sacred inscriptions on the temple walls are dated to 1063 AD. Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar was known to be devoted and a patron of architecture, and gave her patronage to this temple, now a protected monument by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). Pay a visit to the temple, then take on the Narmada Parikrama, a sacred circular route around Omkar Hill, which is around 7 km. Apart from this, the path that runs along the parikrama route is filled with many ancient temples, peaceful ashrams, and the meeting of two rivers, hence making the route quite beautiful and spiritual. One can also take a boat ride along the Narmada River (on a direct payment basis) to find the natural beauty and tranquility of the place. Places You’ll See
Day 3: Omkareshwar temple - Indore (78-80 kms 2- 3 hrs)

Get up early in the morning and drive towards the sacred Omkareshwar Temple and witness the religious aura of the place. This is the time to say goodbye to the city and return to Indore. If time allows you then you can visit some of the prominent landmarks of the city, including the historic Rajwada Palace and the elegant Lal Bagh Palace. Your Indore Ujjain Omkareshwar tour ends here. Leave Indore and head toward home. We would like to thank you for spending your time with us. Places You’ll See

items: 4 Days Mahavatar Baba Ji Cave Tour

blocks.text: Have you ever wanted to visit a secret cave filled with peaceful surroundings, natural beauty and amazing stories?

items: Route: Pantnagar - Kainchi Dham → Kainchi Dham - Nainital - Dwarahat → Dwarahat to Mahavatar Babaji Cave → Dwarahat - Pantnagar

blocks.text: Day 1: Pantnagar - Kainchi Dham (70-85 km / 3-4 hours)

Start your journey with a warm welcome at Pantnagar Airport or Kathgodam Railway Station by our My Quick Trippers representative. If you include a guide, they will come along with the driver to make sure you have support all day. From here, enjoy a scenic drive to Kainchi Dham. After reaching, check into your hotel and take some time to relax. After that, explore the following place- Kainchi Dham - Visit Kainchi Dham Temple, enjoy its spiritual atmosphere, and take photos of the beautiful surroundings as the ashram glows with lights. After exploring stay overnight at a hotel in Kainchi Dham. Note - Kainchi Dham Temple timings are 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM. Places You’ll See
Day 2: Kainchi Dham - Nainital - Dwarahat (Total Approx. 110 km / 4-5 Hours Drive)

Wake up early and spend a calm morning at Kainchi Dham Ashram . Pray, meditate, light a Diya, offer flowers, or join the Aarti. After the Darshan, return to the hotel for breakfast. After checking out from the hotel, proceed to Dwarahat . On the way, stop at Naini Lake in Nainital. You can enjoy boating, walk around the lake, and click beautiful photos. Also, visit Naina Devi Temple to pray and enjoy the view of the hills. (Goddess Sati’s eye is believed to have fallen here). After sightseeing, the journey continues towards Dwarahat. Once you arrive, stay overnight at the hotel. Note- Photography is not allowed inside Kainchi Dham. Places You’ll See
Day 3: Dwarahat to Mahavatar Babaji Cave (25 km Drive / 50 minutes + 3 km Trek / 1-1.5 hours)

Start your morning with a healthy breakfast. Then, prepare for a trek to Mahavatar Babaji’s Cave. (This trekking spot is great for bird watching). Visit the holy cave of Mahavatar Babaji where you can meditate and experience the spiritual atmosphere. This place is best for inner peace and positivity. Spend time at the Meditation Hut of YSS , surrounded by nature where you can observe and learn about the different kinds of plants and rare flowers in the area. Next visit Dunagiri Mata Mandir , an ancient temple over 1,000 years old, dedicated to Goddess Durga. It is believed that while Hanuman was carrying Sanjivani Booti some herbs fell here, which makes the temple special. Visit other nearby temples such as a local Vishnu temple and Gujjar Dev Temple , you can take photos of their beautiful architecture. blocks.text: Odisha is a beautiful state, often called the ‘land of temples’.

This place is admirable due to its rich culture, ancient historical sites, unique tribal cultures, and natural beauty. There are many famous temples in Odisha, such as the Jagannath Temple, which is known for its yearly festival called Rath Yatra. The Sun temple is also popular for its special architecture and it is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site in India.

Odisha also has amazing landscapes and wildlife, especially its Chilika Lake, a large lagoon in India, is filled with birds and sea creatures, which makes it a perfect place for nature lovers. If you are looking for a memorable experience, then it is the right place to visit. This trip offers 4-day Odisha tour packages that includes comfortable hotels, delicious meals, and guided tours to learn more about Odisha’s culture and history. Come and explore its charm.

blocks.text: You will be welcomed by our representative when you reach Bhubaneswar Airport or railway station, they will take you to the hotel. Next, you will see the twin hills of Khandagiri and Udayagiri, where you can find the Jain Temple, Elephanta Caves, Lion Cave, and the Queen Cave. Bhubaneswar is known for its beautiful temples constructed from 7th to 13th centuries. You can also visit many temples like Lingaraj, Mukteshwar, Parshuram mandir, Kedargouri, and Bindusagar. Then, stay overnight in a hotel.
Note: Nandankanan, the State Museum, and the Tribal Museum are closed on Mondays and on state holidays.
Day 2: Bhubaneswar - Dhauli - Pipli - Konark - Puri

After breakfast, you will proceed to Konark by vehicle. On the way, visit Dhauli to see the Buddhist Stupa and peace pagoda, and stop to explore Pipli (famous for its decorative work). Once you reach Konark, you will visit the popular Sun Temple that was constructed by King Narasimha in the 13th century. Now, you will travel to Puri. On the way, visit Chandrabhaga Beach, known for its clean sand and peaceful surroundings. You will also visit Ramchandi Temple. Now, go to Puri and check into the hotel. In the evening, Visit its famous Jagannath Temple (oldest Hindu temple). Over the years, it has attracted many kings, devotees, pilgrims, and people from around the world. Now, rest in a hotel for an overnight stay.
Note: Tourists cannot go to the Jagannath Temple during the “Anavasara’’ period, from the Krishna Paksha of Ashada month until the Jagannath Rath Yatra begins.

Next day, (after breakfast) visit Chilika Lake, the largest brackish water body in Asia, where you can see many birds and sea creatures. Take a boat to the island to enjoy nature and visit Kalijai Temple on Kalijai Island (this is an extra cost).
Now, return to the hotel and relax on Puri’s golden beach in the evening. Then, stay overnight.
This concludes the tour with happy memories, now we will drop you to Bhubaneswar airport or railway station for your onward journey.

blocks.text: The Adi Kailash Yatra is a sacred pilgrimage to the revered “Chhota Kailash,” located in the remote Himalayan region of Uttarakhand near the Indo–China border. Adi Kailash is considered one of the most holy abodes of Lord Shiva and holds deep spiritual significance for devotees. The journey offers a unique blend of devotion and natural beauty, surrounded by untouched mountains, rivers, and peaceful valleys. A key highlight of this Yatra is Om Parvat, where the naturally formed “ॐ” symbol on the mountain attracts pilgrims from all over the country.

Our Adi Kailash tour packages are planned to make the journey smooth and accessible, while still keeping the spiritual essence intact. The route passes through scenic Himalayan locations such as Pithoragarh, Dharchula, Gunji, and nearby remote villages, giving travelers a close look at mountain life and raw natural landscapes. The journey includes travel assistance, stays, and guided support throughout the route.

If you are looking for the best Adi Kailash Yatra package in 2026, My Quick Trippers — a Ministry of Tourism approved operator — offers road and helicopter options starting from ₹48,500 per person, with complete ILP registration support. Book now to secure your preferred departure date for the 2026 Yatra season.

items: Ministry of Tourism Approved Since 2009 My Quick Trippers Pvt Ltd is recognised by the Government of India's Ministry of Tourism, ISO certified, and listed on the NIDHI (National Integrated Database of Hospitality Industry) portal. Our credentials are verifiable — not just a badge.

ILP Permit — 100% Handled by Our Team The Inner Line Permit (ILP) at SDM Dharchula is mandatory for every pilgrim and the single biggest logistical concern on this yatra. Our ground team manages your entire application — Aadhaar copies, medical certificate coordination, police verification, and submission. You do not spend a day at a government office.

Private Vehicle Throughout — Not Shared Transport Innova Crysta for groups up to 4, Tempo Traveller for larger groups. Your vehicle does not get shared mid-route. Beyond Dharchula, only private SUVs are permitted on BRO roads — we ensure this is pre-arranged, not sorted on arrival.

Acclimatisation Built Into Every Itinerary A planned overnight at Gunji (approx. 3,300m) before proceeding to Jyolingkong (4,572m) is not filler time — it is medically essential. We carry a basic oxygen cylinder and high-altitude first aid kit on all road-based departures.
KMVN-Coordinated Stays Accommodation is at KMVN rest houses and pre-verified private guesthouses in Dharchula, Gunji, and Kalapani — booked in advance, not arranged upon arrival.

624/7 Trip Coordinator Support A dedicated coordinator is reachable by phone throughout the yatra. Emergency rescheduling, weather-related plan changes, and any mid-trip assistance are managed from our Dehradun operations base.

blocks.text: Places You Will Visit on the Adi Kailash Yatra

items: Adi Kailash (Chhota Kailash) — 5,945m The crown of this yatra. Lord Shiva's earthly abode in the Kumaon Himalayas, considered a sacred mirror of Mount Kailash in Tibet. Pilgrims who behold this peak are said to attain spiritual liberation.

Parvati Sarovar (Gauri Kund) — Jyolingkong A sacred glacial lake at the base of Adi Kailash. According to Shiva Purana, this is where Goddess Parvati bathed before her union with Lord Shiva. A holy dip here is one of the key rituals of the yatra.

Om Parvat — Nabhidhang, approx. 3,600m A peak whose snow naturally forms the "ॐ" symbol, visible on clear mornings between 7–9:30 AM. Best viewed from the Nabhidhang viewpoint. Considered among the most spiritually charged sights in the Himalayas.

Kalapani — Source of Kali River, approx. 3,600m A restricted-zone site near the India–Nepal–Tibet trijunction. The Kali Mata temple here sits at the precise origin of the Kali (Sharda) river. Access is possible only with a valid ILP.

Vyas Cave & Pandav Fort — near Jyolingkong Located 1–2 km from the Adi Kailash base, these mythological sites are believed to be where Maharishi Vyas composed the Mahabharata and where the Pandavas rested during their final journey.

Gunji Village — approx. 3,300m A high-altitude border village and mandatory overnight stop. Acclimatisation here before proceeding to Jyolingkong (4,572m) is critical. The village offers a rare glimpse of Kumaoni border culture.

Dharchula — Gateway to the Yatra The last town before the restricted zone. ILP registration happens here. Last ATM, last mobile network, last pharmacy — everything beyond Dharchula must be planned from here.

Who Issues It: Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Office, Dharchula — or through KMVN (Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam). Official portal: kmvn.in

By Air: The nearest airport is Naini Saini Airport, Pithoragarh — connected to Delhi by scheduled and charter services (approx. 1 hour). Pantnagar Airport (Udham Singh Nagar) has better connectivity from Delhi, Mumbai, and Lucknow; it is 210 km from Pithoragarh (5–6 hours by road). Our team arranges pickup from both airports.

By Train: Kathgodam Railway Station (Haldwani) is the nearest railhead — 175 km from Pithoragarh (5–6 hours by road). Well-connected to Delhi, Lucknow, and Agra. Key trains: Ranikhet Express (12039) and Uttarakhand Sampark Kranti from Delhi. Our road package includes Kathgodam pickup.

By Road: Delhi to Pithoragarh: approx. 490 km via Moradabad–Rampur–Tanakpur (12–14 hours). Lucknow to Kathgodam: approx. 430 km (9–10 hours). Beyond Dharchula, only private SUVs are permitted on the BRO single-lane road — commercial vehicles are not allowed.

Weather / Force Majeure: If the route closes due to landslide, BRO restriction, or natural calamity, we reschedule your trip to the next available departure at no extra cost, or issue a 12-month credit note. Cash refunds are subject to recovery of non-refundable third-party costs.
Q1. What is the cost of the Adi Kailash Yatra package in 2026?

Ans. The road package starts at ₹48,500 per person on twin sharing (8 nights/9 days from Kathgodam). The helicopter package starts at ₹58,500 (4 nights/5 days from Pithoragarh). The extended helicopter package including Mt. Kailash views and Old Lipulekh Pass is ₹65,500. Prices include accommodation, meals, transport, and ILP assistance.
Q2. Is registration mandatory for Adi Kailash Yatra 2026?

Ans. Yes. An Inner Line Permit (ILP) is legally mandatory for all Indian citizens to travel beyond Dharchula. It is issued by the SDM Office, Dharchula. When you book with us, our ground team handles the complete registration — you only need to provide documents.
Q3. When does the 2026 Adi Kailash Yatra season open and close?

Ans. Phase 1 (main summer) opened on May 8, 2026 and runs till mid-June. Phase 2 (post-monsoon) runs mid-September to mid-October. The route is closed November to April due to snowfall, and July–August travel is not recommended due to active landslides.
Q4. Is the Yatra suitable for senior citizens?

Ans. Yes. The BRO road now reaches Jyolingkong (Adi Kailash base) — no mandatory trekking is required. Senior citizens in reasonable health can complete this yatra comfortably. KMVN's practical upper age limit is 70 years. A medical fitness certificate is required for the ILP.
Q5. What documents are needed for the Adi Kailash permit?

Ans. You need: Aadhaar Card (original + 4 photocopies), 4 passport-size photos, a medical fitness certificate (from any registered doctor), a police verification form or passport photocopy, and a notarised indemnity affidavit on ₹30 stamp paper. Our team provides the exact formats.
Q6. Can I see both Adi Kailash and Om Parvat in one trip?

Ans. Yes. All our packages include both. Adi Kailash Darshan is from Jyolingkong, and Om Parvat is viewed from the Nabhidhang viewpoint. The two sites are covered on separate days, each with an early morning start for optimal visibility.
Q7. What is the best time for Om Parvat Darshan?

Ans. The "ॐ" snow symbol on Om Parvat is clearest between 7:00 AM and 9:30 AM. Cloud cover builds from the valley by 10–10:30 AM and can completely block the view. All our itineraries schedule departure from Gunji by 5:45–6:00 AM on Om Parvat day.
Q8. Are there any hidden charges?

Ans. No. Lunches, personal expenses, travel insurance, medical certificate fee, and any costs due to weather disruption are listed explicitly in our exclusions. There are no charges added after booking confirmation.
Q9. Can foreigners or NRIs do the Adi Kailash Yatra?

Ans. The standard ILP is available to Indian citizens only. Foreign nationals and NRI cardholders (OCI/PIO) require a Protected Area Permit (PAP) from the Ministry of Home Affairs — this must be applied for at least 2–3 months in advance and is a separate, more complex process.
Q10. How far in advance should I book the 2026 package?

Ans. For Phase 1 (May–June): 8–10 weeks in advance. For Phase 2 (September–October): 6–8 weeks. Helicopter slots fill faster — book as early as possible for the helicopter package. Our team responds within 2 hours on business days.

blocks.text: Himachal is the land of Gods and a beautiful paradise for touring and for adventure activities in India. It is not that India lacks in attractions. From the sandy stretches of Rajasthan to lush green rainforests of the Northeast and the cold Himalayan ranges to the warm backwaters of Kerala, there is everything one could wish for. Passionate adventure seekers have plenty to explore in India. Adventure tour packages India are specially designed to give one the much sought-after thrill.

Manali is a perfect resort for relaxing and for spending a weekend. It is also perfect for adventure sports such as white water rafting, paragliding, skiing, trekking along mountain trails and fishing. The entire valley is scenic and Kullu is especially beautiful. If trekking is what you like then the Malana village trek is one you should undertake. Just 21 km from Manali, this is a picture postcard destination with mountains, trees, and clouds to make your day. You can just as well go on the Bara Banghal and Bir Trek, the Hampta Herbal Trek or the Hampta pass trek. However, the Jogini waterfall trek is one you should not miss.

Leh and Spiti are altogether different. These destinations are for the hardy who can withstand rigors and challenges of this inhospitable region of wild beauty. Located in the north-east of Himachal, Spiti is slightly easier than Leh, a place where you can go mountain biking or hike leisurely without worrying about crowds.

However, if mountains and steep trails are not your things and you love warm and breezy coastal areas then Goa in the West, Kovalam in Kerala, Diu on the West Coast in Kutch and Orissa have lovely beaches where you can relax, go snorkeling or riding on a boat and enjoy yourself. You could take it a step higher by going on to Andaman and Nicobar Island where adventure sports like snorkeling and scuba diving will thrill you. Of course, these activities are also available on the lovely beaches of Goa. You can easily find adventure tour packages India based taking you to these places.

Trekking in nature parks is enjoyable. There are well-beaten trails one can follow and luxuriate in the diversity of nature. Jim Corbett National park in the North and the Periyar sanctuary in Kerala offer a relaxed experience. The North-east abounds in National Parks where you can trek amid lush greenery. The Kaziranga National Park in Assam, Manas National Park in Assam, Balpakram National Park in Meghalaya and Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh offer an entirely different trekking experience.
You could go to the heart of India, central India, for trekking and to know more about the land and the people. Join the Bandhavgarh-Kanha experience in Madhya Pradesh or head to Mandu.

If you love water sports and have a penchant for white water rafting then head for the North. The petulant and turbulent rivers in Uttarakhand and Himachal are perfect to enjoy a thrilling experience. Head to Rishikesh and upwards and you have great opportunities for white water rafting. Go farther up to Sikkim and the Teesta River challenges you to take on its might. Zanskar is another place where you can experience the thrill of bobbing along on turbulent waters of the Indus while the Brahmaputra rafting is more sedate experience in the North East of India. It is not that the south lacks in rafting opportunities. Head to Coorg and navigate the Barapole River. Just pick the right adventure tour organizer in India for a customized experience.

If golfing is what you like India has quite a few golf courses to help you indulge your passion. Arrive in Delhi and head to the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurgaon or the Qutab Golf Course in South Delhi. You could join a golfing holiday package tour and sample golf courses from Kolkata to Kerala.

If you love desert sands and vast open skies then you have two choices. One is Rajasthan, a colorful land where you can have your fill of trekking outside places like Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, and Bikaner while getting to know about its royal past by visiting the innumerable palaces and forts. For an out and our experience in the desert head to Kutch and walk along the coast or trek farther inland in the Marine National Park, an all-encompassing experience where you get to see aquatic marine life and birds as well as animals.

Adventure tour packages India is available to suit your taste, be it trekking mountain biking, rafting, paragliding or sailing. India is a spicy mix that changes flavor as you travel from one region to another.

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrival in Agartala - Ujjayanta Palace - Heritage Park - Indo-Bangla Border

Welcome to Agartala! Our representative will greet you at the airport or railway station. From there, you’ll be taken to your pre-booked hotel. Check in and relax for a while. Now, you’ll be taken to the following places: Ujjayanta Palace : It’s a state museum that showcases Tripura’s history and culture. Jagannath Temple : Seek blessings of the lord and also marvel at the beautiful architecture of the shrine. Laxminarayan Temple : Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, this temple has a very serene and peaceful environment. Heritage Park : Sit in this park and enjoy the lush greenery that is all around you. Indo-Bangla Border : You’ll be taken here in the evening, so that you can watch the flag-lowering ceremony. Return to the hotel for an overnight stay. Places You’ll See

Treat yourself to a yummy breakfast. Now, you’ll be transferred to Udaipur, where you’ll seek Darshan in the famous Tripura Sundari Temple (Matabari). You also get to feed the fish in the pond here. Now, you’ll be taken to the Chabimura Exploration. You can take a boat ride here on the Gomati River to view the exquisite rock-cut sculptures from the 15th century, such as: Devi Chakrakma (Mahishasura Mardini Durga) Chabimura Cave Neermahal Water Palace Sepahijala Wildlife Sanctuary Other Carvings, like Panels of Shiva, Vishnu, Kartikeya, and Ganesha In the evening, you’ll be transferred to Agartala. Now, visit Purbasha Handicrafts Emporium , where you can shop for souvenirs like bamboo, cane, handwoven items, etc. Return to the hotel for the night stay. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Best Places on Your Trip to Visit in Agra
Agra is one of the most visited tourist destinations in India and the world. In 2024 there Agra’s Taj Mahal welcomed around 6.9 million tourists (Source- ceicdata.com). (nofollow)

Agra is all about timelessness, UNESCO world heritage sites, and represents the Mughal Empire in a very well-preserved manner. Apart from Taj Mahal, there are other places to explore. Here is a list of best places to visit in Agra covered in our Agra travel itineraries-

items: Taj Mahal needs no introduction, it is the most visited tourist destination in India. It is also one of the new Seven Wonders of the World.

Taj Mahal was constructed primarily with white Makrana marble sourced from Rajasthan. It was built by Shah Jahan, the fifth Mughal emperor between 1632 and 1648 in the memory of his beloved by Mumtaz Mahal.
Located in the city of Agra, Agra Fort stand still in pride keeping alive the history and legacy of Mughal empire. It was built by Mughal emperor Akbar in 1565 but completed in 1573.
The fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its beautiful red marble walls stretch 2.5 km in a crescent shape. Inside the fort there are many palaces, gardens, halls and mosques.
Its architecture is a beautiful fusion of Persian and Indian architecture styles.
Itimad-ud-Daulah’s Tomb is one of the top tourist attractions to visit in Agra. It is an inspiration behind the architecture of the Taj Mahal.
It was built between 1622 and 1628 by Empress Nur Jahan in the memory of her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg.
The tomb displays beautiful inlay work known as Pietra Dura with semi-precious stones which forms exquisite floral and geometric patterns.
Mehtab Bagh or Moonlight Garden is a popular point of tourist interest in Agra. It is located on the northern banks of Yamuna River, facing the Taj Mahal.
It is said that Shah Jahan planned to built one more replica of Taj Mahal in black color (Black Taj Mahal) at Mehtab Bagh.

The garden is designed in a classic Persian style Charbagh. It is very famous for its beautiful sunset views. It’s also a photographer’s delight due to the scenic garden views along with the Taj Mahal in its backdrop.
Jama Masjid in Agra was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in 1637 under the patronage of his daughter Jahanara Begum.

it is one of the largest mosques in India. The mosque displays the beauty of Mughal style architecture. It is a blend of red sandstone and white marble with beautiful inlay work, calligraphy, beautiful arches and domes.
Sikandra is a tomb of Mughal emperor Akbar which was supervised during his lifetime according to Turkic tradition. After the death of Akbar Jahangir, his son finalized the construction of Sikandra.
The tomb has a five storeyed pyramidal structure built in a red sandstone and with the top part in white marble.
The arcaded verandas with beautiful floral and geometric patterns will take your breath away.
The UNESCO World heritage site- Fatehpur Sikri is also a prominent tourist attraction to visit in Agra. It was founded by Akbar in 1571. The place served as Mughal empire’s capital until 1585.
The city’s grandeur lasted only for 14-15 years as it was later abandoned due to water shortages and Akbar’s military focus in the areas of Punjab.
There are many monuments to see in Fatehpur Sikri like Tomb of Salim Chishti, Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, Jodha Bai Palace, Birbal’s house and Anup Talao etc.

blocks.text: Top Things to Do in Agra on Your Trip
Agra Tourism offers blend of the sightseeing of historical monuments and cultural experiences . Here are some of the best things to do in Agra recommended by My Quick Trippers-

items: Agra is one of the best destinations for Heritage Tours. See all the historical monuments in Agra to know about the life and times of Mughal Empire and its rulers.
Capture cool pictures to boast on social media platforms. Agra does have monuments which are worth capturing.
Some of the most popular historical monuments to see in Agra are Taj Mahal , Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Mehtab Bagh, Ram Bagh , Jama Masjid, Itmad-ud-Daula’s Tomb etc.
One must not miss this wonderful opportunity of a scenic boat ride on Yamuna River. You will get specular views of Taj Mahal.
You can access the boats from the east gate of The Taj Mahal located close to the hotel Amarvilas.
If you want to see the iconic monuments without crowds, this is a great chance. It offers rare vantage point for photography.

Never miss a chance to shop for souvenirs in Agra . Agra has some of the best markets where you will get silk Sarees, handicrafts, inlay products, leather goods, jewelry, traditional embroidery and textiles.
Some of the most popular markets to visit in Agra are Kinari Bazar, Subhash Emporium, Raja Ki Mandi etc.
Mohabbat The Taj – Kalakriti Dance Drama Show at Kalakriti Cultural and Convention Center near Taj Mahal is a must not miss performances when you are in Agra.
The show runs for 80 to 90 minutes at around 6:15 pm or 6:30pm. The show is a narration of the epic love story of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan and Mumtaz.

The show will overwhelm your senses. You will witness the artists in Mughal Era costumes and the stage will be set according to the Mughal times. You will also see the replica of the Taj Mahal made with Makrana marble weighting 8500kg.
When you are in Agra, you must look for workshops in Taj Ganj, Nai Ki Mandi and Gokulpura etc. for learning Marble inlay craft known as Parchin Kari.
You will learn the craft passed down through generation from skilled artists and it is one of the best things to do and learn in Agra.

It is also part of the Braj region. With a population of roughly 1.6 million, Agra is the fourth-most populous city in Uttar Pradesh and twenty-third most populous city in India.

blocks.text: Upon your arrival in Aurangabad, you’ll be greeted by our team representative at Airport/Railway station. You’ll be taken to your pre-booked hotel. Relax for a while, then enjoy a sightseeing tour in Aurangabad, consisting of Bibi Ka Maqbara, Daulatabad Fort, and Aurangabad Caves. Enjoy the overnight stay at the hotel. Aurangabad: The city of Aurangabad was founded in 1610, on the site of a village, Khirki by Malik Ambar - the Prime Minister of Murtaza Nizam Shah II. When Fateh Khan, Malik Ambar's son turned successor in 1626, he gave the city the name 'Fatehpur'. Aurangabad today is a bustling city of Maharashtra with diverse big and small industries, fine silken textiles, and exquisite hand woven brocades of silver and gold fabrics, Himroo of the world fame. To scholars and lovers of art and culture the city is more familiar as the gateway to the ancient caves of Ajanta and Ellora, both famous as treasure houses of Indian Art and Sculpture. Aurangabad Caves: The almost forgotten caves of Aurangabad lie just outside the city. Excavated between the 2nd and 6th century AD, they reflect TANTRIC influences in their iconography and architectural designs. In all there are nine caves which are mainly Viharas (monasteries). Overnight stay at the hotel. Places You’ll See

Have a hearty breakfast and then get ready for a sightseeing tour! Visit Ajanta Caves & Ellora Caves. Return to the hotel for an overnight stay. Ajanta caves: Nestling in an inner fold of the Sahyadri hills, 100 km from Aurangabad in the shape of a mammoth horse- shoe, are the 30 rock-hewn caves of Ajanta. The Caves date from the 2nd century BC. Discovered in 1819 by a group of British army officers, these startling achievements took around 600 years to create. Carved with little more than a hammer and chisel, Ajanta, once the retreat of Buddhist monastic orders features several 'Chaityas' (chapels) and 'Viharas' (monasteries). Return to Aurangabad and overnight will be at Aurangabad. Ellora Caves: Impressive in their own right are the rock-hewn temples and monasteries of Ellora that lie just 30 km away from Aurangabad city. In all, there are 34 cave temples, 12 Mahayana Buddhist caves (550-750 AD), 17 Hindu caves (600-875 AD), and 5 caves of the Jain faith (800-1000 AD). Kailas Temple (cave16), the central attraction at Ellora, is the most remarkable. If time permits - then visit the Bhadra Maruti Temple (only temple where Lord Hanuman is seen in a sleeping posture). The city also boasts architectural marvels like the majestic Taragarh Fort, offering panoramic views of Ajmer, and the tranquil Ana Sagar Lake, a picturesque spot ideal for leisurely strolls or serene boat rides.

Shopping enthusiasts can explore the vibrant local markets, such as Naya Bazar and Dargah Bazar, known for their traditional Rajasthani handicrafts, textiles, and vibrant souvenirs.

blocks.text: Why should you come to Prayagraj?

You must visit Prayagraj to enjoy a unique blend of history, culture, adventure and spiritual bliss all at one place. Its places, experiences are deeply rooted in Indian heritage and spiritual traditions.
In 2025, this year due to Maha Kumbh Mela , over 60 crore (600 million) pilgrims visited Prayagraj at the holy Triveni Sangam to offer their prayers and get Nirvana.
Here are some other reasons to get attracted to Prayagraj

items: It’s one of few places to feel the mysterious presence of Saraswati River.

The well-connected Highways and availability of cars and buses from North Indian cities makes travel hassle free.
Don’t miss the Tamatar Chaat, Prayagraj's best street snack.
