blocks.text: Immersed in the history of ancient times, in possession of a kind of architecture that you don’t see anywhere else, and proud of having the land where Gods themselves walked, Dwarka is where you find cultural gems at every other corner. The sacred city is where Lord Krishna himself established his home - spirituality is just in the air here! Besides, there are so many things to do here. Many Dwarka tour packages include things like going on a temple spree, enjoying the coastal charm, sauntering around beaches, and much more! Come to Dwarka and get enchanted by its ancient allure.

items: Best Places to See on the Dwarka Tour
Top Things to Do on the Dwarka Tour

blocks.text: Why Choose My Quick Trippers for Dwarka Tour Packages?

The city of Dwarka is every pilgrimage’s dream. From temples with beautiful architecture to coastal landscapes to places with profound history, there are just too many sites to visit to experience Dwarka in its full glory. To make this exact task easy for you, we bring you our custom-curated Dwarka travel packages, so you can enjoy travelling while leaving the hectic overheads to us! In our trip packages, we include sightseeing, accommodation, meals, local transport, and more. Enjoy the holy city carefree and leave the work to us! Book your Dwarka trip today!

The best time to visit Dwarka is during the winter months - October to March . The weather is very pleasant and cool (with temperatures ranging between 12°C and 28°C) during this time and is therefore ideal for pilgrimage, temple tours, and sightseeing.
Moreover, if you travel during this period, you get to take part in the celebration of festivals like Makar Sankranti (January), Diwali (October/November), and Shivratri (February/March).
A tip : Many people book their Dwarka holiday package during Janmashtami (August/September) as well, to witness the larger-than-life celebrations celebrations at Dwarkadhish Temple!
Best Places to See on the Dwarka Tour

The holy city of Dwarka is steeped in spirituality, mythology, and history. Not only do the Krishna Bhakts love to flock to this ancient city, it’s also a travel favourite for many history buffs as well. To enjoy every aspect of this ancient city, make sure to include the following places in your Dwarka travel packages:

As the name suggests, this temple is dedicated to Dwarkadhish, the king of Dwarka, and that is none other than Lord Krishna! Needless to say, it’s a must-addition to your Drwarka tour packages. As per the legend, he created the city of Dwarka by asking the sea god to provide some land. And so the sea god did, and the rest is history!
Once you reach the temple, do not miss the Mangala and Sandhya Aarti , as the temple atmosphere gets another-worldly spiritual then.

Temple Specialities: Devotees just love the ‘ Shringar Darshan’ , where the temple’s main idols are dressed in traditional attires made of silk/brocade in vivid colours like yellow, green, pink, red, etc. In addition, he is also adorned with beautiful jewellery like stone-studded gold crowns, necklaces, bracelets, and anklets. It’s really a sight to behold!

Architecture: Another thing tourists love here is the stunning architecture of the temple. The 2000 year old structure enchants visitors with its whopping 72 intricately carved pillars and a whole five-storeyed building. Devotees also excitedly wait for the flag ceremony where the flag is changed a full five times!

While you’re out for your trip to Dwarkadhish Temple, give Gomti Ghat a visit as it’s right adjacent to the sacred temple. Many pilgrims take a holy dip at the Ghats and watch the majestic confluence of the Gomti River and the Arabian Sea. And sunrise here are simply picture-perfect and incredibly serene! Come in the early morning and enjoy calm surroundings with little to no crowd.

Just a 20-minute boat ride from Okha, this picturesque island sits pretty amid azure waters and pristine surroundings! This place is quite popularised through its various mentions in Mahabharata and various other scriptures. In addition, it holds high spiritually significance as this is believed to be the original residential place of Lord Krishna. Mnay tourists include this on their Dwarka weekend package .

Another fascinating thing about this place is that it has the only temple ( Hanuman Dandi Temple ) in India where Lord Hanuman is shown with his son Makardhwaja. The other specialty of this island is conch shells, which tourists often collect as souvenirs. Besides these, you can soak in the calm surroundings and stroll around the beaches.

This is an essential addition to your Dwarka trip package as this is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. As strong the architecture is, equally strong is the presence of the divine in here. Enter the shrine and you’ll see a 25-meter-tall magnificent statue of Lord Shiva. It is said that the shrine protects the devotees from all the evil forces. In addition, people enjoy the serene atmosphere in the temple, highly conducive for meditation.

Want to saunter along the sandy shores, say hi to dolphins, and get immersed in the vast Arabian Sea views? If yes, then head straight to Dwarka Beach. Either find seashells along the shore or simply sit and watch the sun go down, you’re in for a treat through and through. You’ll also see people taking photographs and enjoying a relaxed stroll amid the backdrop of scenic views! In addition, there are several stalls where you can find quirky seashell jewellery and unique souvenirs.
Top Things to Do on the Dwarka Tour
Dwarka is a unique blend of natural beauty, mythology, and deep spirituality. To get a wholesome experience of all its facets, include the following things on your Dwarka tour packages:

This is an essential visit on your Dwarka trip as this is the prime temple of the entire state, and also one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites. Also, most travellers who visit Dwarka, come to visit this temple, so don’t miss out on this tourist hotspot.

items: Visit the temple at both morning and evening for Mangala Aarti (early morning) and Sandhya Aarti (evening) as the vibe is completely different (yet beautiful) at both the times.
Seek the blessing of the Lord and eat Prasad.

blocks.text: Go for a Camel Ride on the Gomti River Banks

Gomti has two banks and you can go for a camel ride on either one. One thrilling aspect of the ride is that the camel walks right next to the river, making it a bit of an adventurous ride on an otherwise a rather slow walking camel.

Do not forget to add this place to your Dwarka trip packages as there is no better place than Sudama Setu to watch sunrise. Here, the cable bridge connects the two edges of the Gomti River. The whole view – the sunrise, the bridge, and the Gomti meeting with the sea as the fresh sunshine falls on it, is just a pure whimsical experience. Moreover, the sunset views from the bridge are amazing too! However, the Sudama Setu is ticketed, so you have to wait until the ticket counter opens.
Witness the Change of Flag of Dwarkadhish Temple

There is a 52-yard flag at Dwarkadhish temple and it is changed 5 times a day - three times in the morning and two times in the evening. There’s a family that sponsors the flag and they bring it in a huge festive vibe with dancing and singing. Then the Guggali Brahmin climbs the topmost point of the temple (also known as Shikhara) and proceeds to change the temple. The crowd witnessing the flag change burst out in cheer and celebration, every time the new flag comes out.
Watch the Sunset at the Beach

The best place handsdown to watch the sun go down on your Dwarka trip is at the Bhadkeshwar Mahadev Temple. This is a small but ancient temple with high spiritual significance. You can seek Darshan at the temple and then later on enjoy the unobstructed, clear views of the sunset.

If the Lord Krishna is the Dwarkadheesh (king of Dwarka), then Rukmini is the queen of Dwarka. Your visit to the city is incomplete without her temple visit! Moreover, tourists just love the intricate carvings on the temple, especially the gajatharas (elephants) and the beautiful sculptures of Gods and Goddesses.

When in Dwarka, why not visit the place where Lord Krishna was his mischievous best? Yes, we are talking about the place where he frolicked with Gopis! This sacred pond witnessed countless playful meetings between God and many, many Gopis. The yellow sand around the pond is considered super sacred and is popular as Gopi Chandan . Devotees often add this lovely location to their Dwarka tour packages!
Buy the famous delicious Gujarati snacks and sweets at local markets near Dwarkadhish Temple. For souvenirs, people are seen buying small idols of Lord Krishna, conch shells, handicrafts, and beads.
Take a Holy Dip at Gomti Ghat

This sacred Ghat marks the meeting point of Gomti River and Arabian Sea. People plunge into the river, offering their prayers ad whispering sacred mantras. Come in the early morning to take in the serene and peaceful atmospheres.

items: Gujarati cuisine has a lot of lip-smacking vegetarian dishes that you must try on your Dwarka trip, such as:
Traditional Gujarati Thali : It usually consists of Roti/Puri, dal, Kadhi, seasonal vegetable curries, rice/Khichdi, Papad/pickles/chutneys, and sweet dishes.
Gujarati Snacks : Dhokla, Khandvi, Thepla, Khakhra, and more
Sweets and Desserts : Shrikhand, Basundi, Gulab Jamun, Ghooghra etc.
Dry Snacks : Gathiya, Sev, and Thepla
Local Street Food : Pani Puri, Chaat, Dabeli, Bhajiya, etc.

blocks.text: Frequently Answered Questions about Dwarka Tour Packages
Q1. How to plan Dwarka trip?
Ans. Planning for a Dwarka trip is easy, just keep in mind the following things:

items: 1. Decide travel duration: Choose whether you want to see the basics of Dwarka (requires 2-3 days) or want an extended trip (requires 4-5 days) to include nearby locations as well, like Porbandar, Somnath, etc.
2. Plan itinerary: Decide on what places to visit and on which day.
3. Set budget: Decide on your expenses, picking from budgeted travel to luxury tours.
4. Book transport: Check the suitable options to travel (by air, rail, or road) Dwarka from your location.
5. Select accommodation: Book a hotel in advance to avoid accommodation problems.
6. Start packing: Carry modest, lightweight clothes for temple visits. Also, pack hat, sunscreen, and comfortable shoes.

blocks.text: Q2. What is the ideal duration for my Dwarka trip?

Ans. Generally, a 2-3 day visit is perfect for exploring all the key tourist attractions, like Dwarkadhish temple, Dwarka Bet, etc. However, if you plan to extend your trip to include nearby locations, such as Somnath and Porbandar, then 4-5 days are required for your trip.
Q3. Is photography allowed at temples?
Ans. Photography is not allowed inside the temple premises. However, you can click pictures on the outer premises. When in doubt, ask the temple staff or check for signage.
Q4. What are some festivals that are celebrated with great zeal in Dwarka?

blocks.text: Egypt Tour Packages – Book Egypt Packages

Egypt is a place with varied geography located in North-Eastern part of Africa with Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea on its coasts and its vast history and eventful past, to make it an absorbing place to be on Tour Package. Egypt was the place to give birth to one of the oldest civilizations and memorials, ruins and relics of ancient and medieval times make it a paradise for those who are interested in history. Surrounded by desert on East and West and numerous temples, hieroglyphs, mummies and above all pyramids make Egypt a captivating place for travelers on Tour Package.

The Pyramids of Giza and Sphinx have attracted millions of people from around the globe since ages and even today are most sought after destination on Egypt Tour Package. In Giza one can see three pyramids each one of different King of Egypt and facing these pyramids is a massive architecture with cat like face known as Abu Al-Hol or Sphinx, carved out of single block of stone exemplifying the technique and skills of sculptors of that time. Pyramids of Giza and Sphinx is must visit places on Egypt Tour Package.

Close to Giza lies another huge attraction of Egypt, the Abu Simbel, one of the most recognized monuments in the country. These twin temples were originally built by Pharaoh Ramesses II and in 1960 were shifted 60 meters away on to a cliff to protect them, each block was reassembled exactly in the same way and with exact relation with the sun to maintain its charm and charisma. Sound and light shows organized every evening are not to miss attraction of this place on Egypt Travel Package.

Cairo is one of the oldest cities of the world and is full of interesting buildings, churches, mosques and markets built in ancient times. Some of the major historical attractions of this city are the Citadel, Khan Khalili Bazaar, Ibn Tulun Mosque is one of the largest mosques in the world and Al Azhar Mosque which houses world’s oldest university started in 970 AD. Strolling past the market places one can see many handmade items and things to purchase and can also see many interesting things like beautifully carved ancient gates and walls, this city is full of surprises for tourists and one shall devote ample time to explore this city on Egypt Holiday Package.

If one thinks that Egypt Tour Packages are all about history and ancient monuments than it is in correct as this country has natural splendors which are enchanting and enthralling for visitors. The Oasis of Siwa is one such place which is soothing and exciting in the lap of desert. One can swim, relax and enjoy fresh olives at this place, close to Libyan border this place is also famous due to the fact that Alexander the Great stayed here on his way to Oracle of Amun. A truly mesmerizing place and certainly deserves a visit on Egypt Holiday Packages.

There are many other must visit places and plethora of activities to do on Egypt Travel Packages as this country offers much more than one can expect and cover in one trip. Sailing in the river Nile, Temples of Karnak, visiting Valley of the Kings, Hurghada and many more, there is no dearth of tourist attractions in this country.

blocks.text: Kerala is an enchanting destination dotted with breathtaking landscapes, backwaters, historical locations, religious sites, and waterfalls that invite tourists for amazing trips and experiences.

As you arrive at the Kochi Airport or railway station, you’ll be greeted by one of our representatives who will transfer you to your pre-booked hotel. Relax for some time and then prepare yourself to visit the famous attractions of Cochin, including: Jewish Synagogue: The Jewish Synagogue is one of the most religious sites in South India. In the Commonwealth of Nations, it is the oldest synagogue. Dutch Palace (Mattancherry Palace): The Dutch Palace is the finest example of the Kerala architectural style. It is known for its spacious and long halls with its central courtyard. St. Francis Church: St. Francis Church is considered to be the first European Church in India that reflects the colonial past of the city. Chinese Fishing Nets: These are a type of fishing net that you will find along the harbor's mouth at Fort Kochi. Have an overnight stay at your hotel in Kochi. Places You’ll See

Post breakfast, you will be driven to Munnar, one of the most beautiful hill stations in India. On the way, you will witness the breathtaking landscapes and lush green spice plantations. Once in Munnar, you can experience the natural beauty of the hill station, adorned with spice plantations, beautiful rivers, cascading waterfalls, and dense forests. You will check in at your hotel and have an overnight stay.

After breakfast, you will proceed on a sightseeing tour of Munnar and visit the famous attractions. Mattupetty Lake & Dam: Get a chance to experience the best that nature has to offer at this destination. Echo Point: At Echo Point, your voice echoes back to you because three mountain ranges are present in this area –Mudrapuzha, Kundala, and Nallathanni. Rajamalai (Eravikulam National Park): Rajamalai National Park houses Anamudi Peak, the highest peak in the Western Ghats. It spans 97 square kilometres and has a wide variety of flora and fauna. Tea Gardens: Relish the aroma and taste of freshly brewed tea as you explore the tea gardens of Munnar. Have an overnight stay at your hotel. Places You’ll See

In the morning, drive from Munnar to Alleppey. Alleppey is a coastal city interconnected with canals and lakes. The paddy field of Kuttanad, also known as ‘ Kerala’s rice bowl,’ is found in the city. After arriving at Alleppey, you’ll check in to your hotel and indulge in the following activities. Stroll by Alleppey Beach: Alleppey Beach is known for its splendid beauty and long coastline. You can enjoy a sunset by the beach and chill under the palm trees. Sunset Cruise on Vembanad Lake (Optional): One of the best ways to enjoy the sunset is by undertaking a cruise on Vembanad Lake. Shopping: Indulge in shopping at the local markets in Alleppey that offer amazing quality products. Overnight stay at your hotel in Alleppey. Places You’ll See
DAY 5: Alleppey – Kovalam – Trivandrum (4 Hrs/164 Kms)

Savour a tasty breakfast in the morning as your houseboat sails through the backwater and allows you to relish splendid views. As your houseboat arrives at Alleppey fishing point jetty, you will check out and head to Kovalam. You will also visit the famous attractions of Trivandrum. Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple This temple is a sacred Hindu shrine built in honour of Lord Vishnu. It is considered to be one of the 108 sacred places of Vishnu. You will continue your journey to Kovalam and stroll on the Kovalam beach. Have an overnight stay at your Kovalam hotel. Places You’ll See
DAY 6: Kovalam – Trivandrum / Cochin Departure (6 Hrs/220 Kms)
Post breakfast, check out from your hotel and meet our driver outside your hotel. Our driver will transfer you to Trivandrum or Cochin.

blocks.text: Family tour packages in India offer a wonderful opportunity for families to explore the diverse and culturally rich country together. These packages are specifically designed to cater to the needs and preferences of families, providing a hassle-free and enjoyable vacation experience. With a wide range of destinations and activities to choose from, India offers something for every member of the family.

Family holiday packages typically include accommodation, transportation, meals, and guided tours to popular attractions. They are designed to ensure a comfortable and convenient travel experience, taking into consideration the requirements of families with children and elderly members. These packages often include family-friendly accommodations with spacious rooms or interconnected rooms, ensuring that everyone has a comfortable stay.

India boasts a plethora of family-friendly destinations. The iconic Golden Triangle circuit, consisting of Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur, is a popular choice for families. It offers a blend of history, culture, and architectural marvels such as the Taj Mahal, Amber Fort, and Qutub Minar. For nature-loving families, the hill stations of Shimla, Manali, and Ooty provide a refreshing retreat amidst picturesque landscapes. Wildlife enthusiasts can opt for a safari in national parks like Jim Corbett or Ranthambore, where they can spot tigers, elephants, and other exotic wildlife.

Beach destinations like Goa, Kerala, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands offer sun, sand, and water activities that are perfect for a fun-filled family vacation. These places provide opportunities for boating, snorkeling, and beachside relaxation. Cultural hubs like Varanasi, Udaipur, and Kolkata offer insights into India’s rich heritage and traditions. Families can witness captivating rituals, visit ancient temples, and explore vibrant markets.

Family tour packages in India provide a well-rounded travel experience for families, ensuring that every member has a memorable and enjoyable vacation. With a blend of historical, cultural, natural, and adventurous attractions, India offers a diverse range of options to cater to the interests and preferences of families. Whether seeking relaxation, adventure, or cultural immersion, families can find the perfect package that suits their needs and creates lasting memories.

blocks.text: Kerala is an amalgam of the very best of nature. The coconut palm trees, the houses made of red tiles, and the beautiful lakes and beaches will remain forever in every visitor’s heart.
Day 1: Arrival at Cochin and Sightseeing

You’ll arrive in Cochin, where a team member will greet you - either at the airport or the railway station. After arrival, we’ll take you straight to the hotel. Settle in, freshen up - then it’s time to explore Cochin! Explore well-known spots - the Jewish Synagogue, Dutch Palace, and the St. Francis Church - during your trip. Once you're done with sightseeing, head back to the hotel for an overnight stay. Places You’ll See
DAY 2: Cochin - Munnar (4 Hrs/140 Kms) Sightseeing

Savour a tasty breakfast in the morning, and then you will embark on a drive to Munnar, admiring the breathtaking scenery. Witness the sprawling tea plantations, exotic species of flora and fauna, and aromatic spices that make this destination breathtakingly beautiful. After that, you'll head back to your hotel and have a soothing sleep in your room

Relish a tasty breakfast in the morning and then get ready to visit the famous attractions of this region, including: Tea Gardens: Take a stroll through the tea gardens and sample different varieties of tea. Mattupetty Lake and Dam: Mattupetty Dam and Lake are situated at a distance of around 11 kilometres outside Munnar. They offer the perfect setting for exploring breathtaking surroundings, leisurely strolls, and embarking on scenic boat trips. Echo Point: Situated at a distance of 15 kilometres from Munnar and at an altitude of 600 ft., Echo Point is located in the lap of misty hills and a quaint lake. This spot is known for its illustration of the echoing phenomenon. Kundala Lake: This lake is renowned for its pedal boat rides and Kashmiri-Shikara boat rides. You can also see here cherry blossom trees. Rajamalai (Eravikulam National Park): Rajamalai Wildlife Sanctuary is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and it is home to a diverse variety of flora and fauna. Have an overnight stay at your hotel in Munnar after the sightseeing tour. Places You’ll See

Today you will travel to Alleppey from Munnar. Alleppey is famous for its picturesque backwater cruise, lush greenery, and serene atmosphere. It also boasts floating markets and old-style bazaars where you can purchase everything at the lowest possible prices. Alleppey is also referred to as the "Venice of the East." Option 1: Stay at the Hotel Once you reach Alleppey, we’ll get you settled into your hotel. Later, feel free to try these activities. Take an optional sunset boat trip on Vembanad Lake, known for its stunning views Alleppey Beach: It is a lovely spot to unwind, share a meal, and spend time with your loved ones. Shopping: Alleppey boasts several markets where you can get what you want without overspending. Return to your hotel after the exploration and have a relaxing sleep in your room. Option 2: Houseboat Stay Spend your night in a gorgeous houseboat in Alleppey to experience the local life. You can also admire the natural surroundings from the balcony of your houseboat. You can also relish traditional South Indian cuisines during your stay at the houseboat. Places You’ll See
DAY 5: Alleppey - Cochin Airport Departure (90 Kms/2 hrs)

Post a lip-smacking breakfast, check out of your hotel, and then you will head to Cochin. Once you have arrived at Cochin, you’ll be transferred to the railway station or airport from where you’ll continue your forward journey. This also marks the end of the tour, giving you tons of memories.

blocks.text: The glistening white temple dedicated to goddess Ganga graces the bank of the gushing Bhagirathi River in Devbhoomi Uttarakhand. Being a crucial part of the holy Char Dham Yatra annual pilgrimage of India it is located in one of the most scenic and beautifully soothing regions of India. Gangotri tour packages play a vital role in witnessing the incredible spiritual aura of the pilgrimage to the utmost level. Reaching this humble temple when it opens for Darshan after remaining buried under snow for half a year, is a relatively an easy job. The temple is one of the rarest places of worship for Ganga Mata exclusively in country. The temple was built by the brave heart Amar Singh Thapa who realized the true value of this place and took the responsibility of preserving this place in his hand.

However, the current standing temple was remade and renovated by the Maharani of Jaipur. The place holds immense relevance in the life of every Hindu devotee with its history dating to as far back as the birth of Ganga. Ever since the temple was built and revived by the great saint and philosopher Adi Shankaracharya the temple witnesses a massive turnout of domestic as well as international devotees. It is believed that king Bhagirathi is responsible for bringing the heavenly river of Ganga to earth with an aim of providing moksha to he departed souls of his ancestors by immersing their ashes into this pious river. This tradition is now followed by Hindus and believers from all over the world.

According to the Hindu holy texts, it was near Gangotri Temple that the holy river had made her way into the earthly realm from the heavenly realm which is believed to be the matted hair of Lord Shiva. The Gangotri Tour Packages offered by us ensures that you experience the spirituality and divine power of this place just the way it was intended to be. From offering smooth pick-up and drop-off service, sightseeing options, comfortable stay, and delicious meal options this tour package is something you, your family and loved ones. Available exclusively at the best rates and enabling you to have a lifetime worth of spiritual and religiously evoking journey on the hills, this will be something you will remember forever.

The packages are designed in custom and a flexible manner to meet the entire travel requirement you may be expecting. Offering exclusive rates on all of Gangotri Travel Packages you must book one now. Apart from the Temple Darshan and being a part of the divine experience you will be taken for some of the most awe-inspiring sightseeing at the jaw-dropping locations that dot this region like Vasudhara Waterfall and more. Through our packages, you can make the best of this pious and sacred land with the help of our expert advisors and an incredible team of professionals. Exploring this part of India will be an experience to remember and you may even keep coming back for more of the spiritual and adventure experience this place has to offer.

Q2: How can we visit Gangotri Yamunotri?

Ans. The devotees who are planning to seek the blessings of Goddess Ganga at Gangotri Dham and Yamunotri Dham shall read out the beautifully narrated travel guides to these temples and then plan accordingly.
Q3: Can we go to Gangotri in December?

Ans. The gorgeous Gangotri Temple receives huge snowfall in the winter months especially from December to February thus, we don’t recommend you for visiting Gangotri in December. Also, the shrine is closed at this time hence, it is not a great idea to witness the glory of Gangotri Tourism.
Q4: How do I get from Rishikesh to Gangotri?
Ans. One needs to cover a total distance of 257 km to reach Gangotri from Rishikesh and this distance can only be covered by roadways and this journey takes almost 12 hours.
Q5: How can I reach Gangotri from Uttarkashi?

Ans. Both the above mentioned destinations are situated at a distance of 100 km and to cover this distance the traveler has to opt for either roadways that will take 3 hrs or can plan for a helicopter ride which is however a bit economical.
Q6: How can I reach Gangotri?

blocks.text: The best time to visit Gaya is September to March as it aligns with the major festivals and pilgrimage events and rituals. Let's know about the best time to visit Gaya in detail-

items: These months are the peak tourism season in Gaya. During these months' festivals like Pitru Paksha Mela, Buddha Purnima, Navratras take place.
The large crowd of pilgrims and tourists gather here during these months. The price of hotels is also high due to the peak season.
The weather during these months is also best for sightseeing and participating in spiritual rituals.
During these months in Gaya, Shravani Mela and Pitrapaksha Mela are celebrated. Another notable event in the Buddhist circuit is Chokhor Duchen, also called the Dharma Wheel Festival.
So, you can consider Monsoon if you want to witness these festivals. The weather during this time will be humid due to heavy rains.
Terrains may also interrupt your temple visits.
Summer is not the most preferred time to visit Gaya as the heat and high temperature might get unbearable for sightseeing.

During these months Buddha Purnima is celebrated with great pomp and show. So, you can still consider these months to visit if you want to experience the culture and take part in celebrations which include day-long prayers, meditation, and rituals.

blocks.text: Best Places to Explore in Gaya on Your Trip

In 2024 Gaya witnessed a significant rise in tourist footfall. It welcomed around 22 lakh pilgrims. This shows the rising interest in spirituality and involvement in spiritual events. Source: ( Times of India ). Here are some of the best places to see in Gaya covered in our Gaya itineraries-
Vishnupad Temple- Realm of Lord Vishnu

items: Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, Vishnupad Temple is one of the most famous spiritual places to explore in Gaya. It is situated on the banks of the sacred Falgu River.
Here you will witness the actual footprints of lord Vishnu which is impressed in a stone when he killed demon Gayasura.
The temple houses a sacred Akshayvat Tree which is believed to grant Moksha to the ancestors.

Mangala Gauri Temple in Gaya is a famous temple of Goddess Sati in Gaya. It dates back to the 15th century. It is one of the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas where Goddess Sati's breasts are believed to have fallen which is a symbol of nourishment.
The temple also offers scenic views of Mangala Gauri hill as the temple itself is perched on this hill.
Also witness the sacred Akhand Deep (eternal flame) burning continuously within the temple premises.

blocks.text: Pind Daan Ghats- Honor the Ancestors

items: If you are visiting Gaya, Pind Daan might be one of the specific reasons as this is a famous destination to offer Pind for ancestors.
Visit three sacred spots in Gaya for Pind Daan ceremony such as Phalgu river banks which serve as the main place for pilgrims to perform Pind Daan rituals.

Vishnupad Temple which is also the most auspicious place for offering Pind Daan and Akshayavat Tree located within the Vishnupad Temple. This ancient banyan tree is believed to grant eternal blessings to ancestors.

blocks.text: Gayatri Shakti Peeth Gaya- Abode of Goddess Gayatri

items: Dedicated to goddess Gayatri, divine mother of the Vedas and the personification of Gayatri Mantra, Gayatri Shakti Peetha is a prominent Hindu temple to visit in Gaya.
The temple is famous for its beautiful idols of Gayatri Mata along with depictions of Kundalini and Savitri.
You can take part in the divine rituals, daily prayers and chant the auspicious Gayatri Mantra.
Also known as Brahmayoni Hill, Brahmajuni hill is the highest hill in Gaya. It represents the female Yoni of Lord Brahma.
Atop the hill is a temple of five-headed female deity worshiping the representation of Brahma's energy.
It is one of the best places to offer Pind Daan during Pitrapaksha Mela.

blocks.text: Best Things to do in Gaya on your Trip
Gaya is a spiritual place and the best activities in Gaya will revolve around spiritual activities. Here is a list of some of the best things to do in Gaya -

items: Phalgu is one of the most sacred rivers to explore in Gaya. It holds immense spiritual significance for Hindus, and Buddhists.
Visit here during Pitrapaksha Mela to offer Pind Daan for your ancestors.
It is also a significant place for Buddhists as it is believed that Gautam Buddha practiced asceticism and achieved enlightenment near its banks.
Located in Gaya, Dungeshwari caves is an important spiritual site. It is also known as Mahakala caves.
These are the rock cut caves which date back to the 3rd century BCE.
It is believed that Gautama Buddha mediated here for six months before attaining enlightenment in Bodhgaya.
Just 24 km from Gaya, Barabar Caves is a must visit spot. It is one of the oldest surviving rocks which dates back to the 3rd century BCE.
These caves were primarily used by ascetics of the Ajivika sect, a spiritual group in Buddhism and Jainism founded by Makkhali Gosala.
There are some inscriptions in the caves which bear the name of Emperor Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha Maurya which proves that they patronized the caves.

Gaya is a wonderful place to indulge in shopping for art and handicrafts. Gaya is famous for its wood craft art which you will witness idols of Buddha and other religious artefacts made of Gamhar wood.

Some of the other notable things to buy here are artistic textiles, pottery works, Tikuli paintings, Fresco rock paintings, Khatwa works, brass works, and block printing on cloths, bamboo products, Jewellery products, and Zari Works in various markets of Gaya.
Try authentic food in Gaya to tickle your tastebuds with the rich flavors of the region. The food of Gaya is connected with the spiritual heritage. You will get vegetarian meals.
Some of the best foods to try in Gaya are Litti Chokha, Sattu Paratha, Kadhi Bari, Thekua, Maitha, Peda, Tilkut, Balushahi, Khaja and Dal Puri.

blocks.text: How to Reach Gaya by Air, Rail and Road

For most tourists, the fastest way to travel to Gaya is by a flight from Delhi or Kolkata to Gaya International Airport, followed by local cab to reach Gaya or Bodhgaya. By Train, Mahabodhi Express is the best option to reach Gaya . It is also a budget friendly option for many travellers. By Road you can take NH 83 which offers scenic views of rural Bihar. Let's know in detail how to reach Gaya by Air, Rail and Road-

rows: Gaya International Airport, the only international airport in Bihar, is the best way to reach Gaya. It is located 12-15 km from Gaya which receives both domestic and international flights.

Gaya is connected with major cities like Delhi, Kolkata and Varanasi domestically. International routes include Bangkok, Yangon (Myanmar), Paro (Bhutan), Colombo, Singapore, and Tokyo (seasonal charters).
1.5 to 2 hr. flight from Delhi. From Patna - 40 min flight or 3-4 hr. drive
Operated under East Central Railway, Gaya Junction is the major railway station on Delhi- Kolkata Grand Chord Line. It is the busiest railway junction in Bihar.

By Rail, Gaya is connected with Patna, Varanasi, Mumbai, Chennai, Nagpur, Indore, and Lucknow. You will get Major trains: Mahabodhi Express (Delhi-Gaya, 16 hr.), Rajdhani Express (Delhi-Gaya, 12-13 hr.), Howrah Rajdhani (Kolkata-Gaya, 6 hr.).
Delhi-Gaya: 12-16 hr.; Kolkata-Gaya: 6 hr.; Patna-Gaya: 3-4 hr.
You can reach Gaya via NH-83 and NH-2 (Grand Trunk Road). The GT Road connects Delhi-Kanpur-Allahabad-Varanasi-Gaya-Kolkata. You can also opt for regular state and private buses to reach Gaya.
By Road Gaya is around (120 km from Patna via NH-83), Ranchi (230 km), Jamshedpur (370 km), Raurkela (390 km), Hazaribagh (130 km), Kolkata (480 km), and Delhi (990 km).
From Patna - 3-4 hr. drive; Ranchi - 5 hr.; Delhi - 14-16 hr.

blocks.text: Q1. Is the spring season recommended to visit Goa?
Ans. Yes, if you prefer a less crowded holiday. However, it is generally recommended to plan your holiday in Goa during the winter season as the weather is more pleasant.
Q2. Does this package include airport/railway station transfers?
Ans. Yes, it includes pick-up and drop-off services at the Goa airport or railway station.
Q3. Are the Mandovi River Cruise tickets included in the package?
Ans. Yes, the itinerary of Day 3 includes the river cruise, with all arrangements managed by our representative.
Q4. Is it possible to rent a bike or a scooter at reasonable rates?
Ans. Absolutely! Biking is a popular activity in Goa. Our agent can assist you in locating reliable rental services.
Q5. Do the Goan churches open up daily?
Ans. Yes, most churches, including the Basilica of Bom Jesus, open daily. However, hours may differ, and temples are more crowded on Sundays and festivals.
Q6. What are some must-try street food items?
Ans. You should try Goan snacks like Ros Omelette, Cutlet Pav, and Choris Pao to enjoy the local flavor.
Q7. Does the package include Ayurvedic therapy?
Ans. No, Ayurvedic therapy is not included in the package and requires additional payment. Our travel representative can help you select the best and legitimate centers in the area.

blocks.text: Half of Goa is Covered in Forest

items: You will be amazed to know that over a third of Goa is covered in forest. Goa is a very popular beach destination, but one-third of it is nestled in the beautiful Western Ghats of India.
It is also the best place to visit for nature lovers and honeymoon couples. The forest of Goa is teeming with amazing wildlife.
Goa is India's smallest state, but don't let the size fool you. Goa is a compact treasure chest of adventures, beaches, bars, markets, and luxury resorts.
It might be the tiniest state in India, but its spirit is abundant, as you will get tons of activities to do here and create wonderful memories with your loved ones.

blocks.text: Goa, Once Ruled by the Portuguese

items: For over 450 years, Goa was under the rule of the Portuguese. So, the Portuguese have a great influence on the fabric of daily life of the Goans.

You will feel the Portuguese influence in architecture, food, way of life, cafes, language, surnames, culture, and festivals because when the Portuguese arrived in Goa in 1510, they made it their capital.
Goa Carnival is India's only traditional Latin carnival, which is celebrated with great pomp and show for four days in February or March.

It is celebrated with delightful music programs, dance, and costume parades. The roots of this festival are Christian, but its spirit is Indian. People from all backgrounds are allowed to witness this festival.
We all know that India got independence on 15th August 1947, but Goans did not get independence from the Portuguese on this date. They had to wait a little longer.

Goa got independence on December 19th, 1961, and joined the Indian union. This is the reason why Goa has the privilege to celebrate two independence days. One with the entire nation and another on December 19th by honoring the heroes who fought for their freedom.

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Goa for Holidays

November to February is the best time to visit Goa for enjoying holidays with your family and friends. The weather will be pleasant to enjoy scenic views, relaxation at beaches and outdoor adventure activities. Let's know in details about the best time to visit Goa-

Winter is the best time to plan your Goa trip whether you are family with kids, couples or solo travellers. The weather will be pleasant for outdoor adventures, sightseeing, beach parties and enjoying nightlife .

In summers Goa is less crowded. Only tourists who love the vibe of Goa, reach here to enjoy sightseeing despite the hot weather. It is a great time to explore Goa for budget travellers. You can enjoy sightseeing and outdoor activity swimming, rafting, boat rides, Scuba diving etc.

If you are tolerant of heavy rains then visit Goa during this time. You will see lush landscapes and the cool breeze will soothe your soul. Heavy rains might disrupt your sightseeing plans. But you will witness Calm, quiet beaches, and green countryside; lower prices for stays.

It's the best time to plan your vacation in Goa and book amazing Goa Tour Packages before the crowd returns in peak season. It's a good month for sightseeing and enjoying outdoor activities for budget travellers, couples and solo travellers.
Best Places to Explore in Goa on Your Trip

In 2025, in the first six months, Goa welcomed around 5.45 million tourists. Of these tourists, about 5.18 million were domestic tourists and approximately 271,000 were international tourists. Source: The Print . Here is a list of the best places to visit in Goa-

items: A UNESCO World Heritage Site in Goa. It is one of the most popular places to visit in Goa. Built in the 16th century, this church houses the mortal remains of St. Francis Xavier.
The Baroque architecture of the church will take your breath away.
It's a majestic four-tiered waterfall on the Goa-Karnataka border. You will be mesmerized to see its beauty.
This place attracts many honeymoon couples. The milky white water flowing through lush greenery is a sight worth capturing.
Don't miss the most famous and lively beaches of Goa. Not a single moment is dull here.

You will enjoy the vibrant atmosphere with golden sands, numerous water sports like jet skiing, parasailing, banana boat rides, and dolphin cruises, and the exciting nightlife hotspots like Tito's and Mambo's.
Situated at the confluence of the Mandovi River and Arabian Sea, Fort Aguada is one of the most popular heritage attractions to explore in Goa.

The main highlight of this fort is its sturdy laterite stone walls, which are 5 meters high and 1.3 meters thick, a 4-storey lighthouse and an enormous water cistern. Enjoy the most scenic sunset views here.

blocks.text: A beach and warm weather are all I really need." - Rob Gronkowski

When we think about Goa, the first thing that pops into our minds is the fantastic sights of beaches because life feels less boring around beaches. In the words of Sandy Gingras, "Time on beaches doesn't move hour to hour but mood to moment." Beaches of Goa restore the liveliness of the soul. You must visit some of these beaches once in a lifetime in Goa.

items: Vagator Beach- It has a beautiful crescent-shaped bay, which is the most beautiful sight to capture. It is very famous for its small coves.

Candolim Beach- Before exploring other beaches of Goa, people always prefer Candolim Beach as their first choice. Here you can unwind under parasols with your loved ones and enjoy a fun-filled picnic. Also, savor delicious seafood in beach shacks.

Calangute Beach- It is Goa's most famous beach to visit for a relaxing vacation with your family. It is packed with amazing restaurant shacks, shopping points, nightclubs, and scenic and comfortable accommodation options. You can also enjoy a variety of water adventure activities here.

Baga Beach- It is one of the busiest beaches of North Goa. You can enjoy exciting water adventure activities in Baga Beach, like jet-skiing, banana boat rides, swimming, water skiing, etc. Its delightful shores are filled with popular eating joints and bars.

Agonda Beach -Enjoy swimming and engage in exciting water sports, especially canoeing, as it is one of the best activities to do here. You can also visit the turtle center to watch Olive Ridley Turtle eggs.
Majorda Beach- Peaceful and scenic, Majorda is one of the less crowded beaches of South Goa. You can enjoy a soothing horse ride on this beach.

Palolem Beach- It is one of the loveliest beaches of South Goa. Enjoy a lovely stay at scenic tree houses and campsites. Enjoy the soothing boat rides offered by fishermen for dolphin-watching and sunset views.
Varca Beach -It's a perfect beach spot to laze under the sun. Enjoy local boat rides offered by fishermen, or go for a cruise over the Sal River to spot dolphins.

Cola Beach- Cola Beach is one of the most beautiful beaches of South Goa. It has beautiful coconut groves and Rajasthani-style tents. There is a freshwater lagoon to try swimming and other water adventures.

blocks.text: Goa's fun-filled vibe attracts tourists from all over the world. Here are some of the most famous nightclubs to experience the best of Goa's night tourism.

items: Club Cabana -Don't miss this multi-level open-air nightclub, Club Cabana, which is also known as 'Nightclub in the Sky.' Several bar areas and a beautiful waterfall cascading into an open-air pool make this club the best to enjoy nightlife. Only couples are allowed in this club. So, if you are on honeymoon in Goa, then you can visit this club.

Club Tito's-Club Tito's is a lifeline of Baga Beach. Every Saturday, the dance floor comes alive on retro and Bollywood hits. When the clock strikes 11pm, the soundscape changes to hip-hop and techno music.

Sinq Night Club -It is one of the best places to enjoy for party lovers. There are four entertainment zones in this club-a chic nightclub, a bistro, a poolside deck, and private cabanas-making it an ultimate paradise for party lovers.
Leopard Valley-Don't miss this awe-inspiring open-air venue, Leopard Valley. It has a 22 ft high DJ stage where you can enjoy the best of EDM. Enjoy 3D laser night shows and parties on Friday nights.

blocks.text: Goa tourism is beyond beaches, sunsets, and adventures, as the calendar is also painted with exciting events to celebrate and introduce to the world the music, food, culture, and heritage of Goa. Every month, there is something to enjoy in Goa. Here is a list of some popular events to visit in Goa:

items: Heritage Festival of Goa (January)- It's a three-day Heritage Festival held in January by Goa Tourism. The festival showcases the culture, folklore, music, lifestyle, and traditions of Goa, which have been passed on from one generation to another.
Sensorium (Jan to March)- It is a must-visit place for every art and heritage lover. You will absolutely love the exhibition of arts, cinema, and music at Sunaparanta.
Grape Escapade (April)- This festival is celebrated in the month of April for four days in Panaji with many amazing culinary delights, wine tasting sessions, and grape stomping.

International Film Festival (November)- It is one of the grand international film festivals of India, celebrated in Goa in November. This festival celebrates and honors cinema by screenings of Indian and international films.

Zagor Festival (Dec)- Zagor Fest is a traditional folk-dance drama in Goa, celebrated to protect the harvest from destruction. You will see midnight processions of the village deity Zagoryo. Enjoy folk performances, village feats, and prayers.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Goa on Your Trip

Goa is a versatile destination and has many things to do. Not a single moment in Goa will be boring as it has something for every type of traveller. Mentioned here are some of the best activities to do in Goa to enjoy Goa Tourism-
Enjoy Water adventure activities at Various Beaches

items: Goa is a very famous beach destination so, one of the best activities to do here is enjoying water adventure activities. Try activities like jet skiing, parasailing, banana boat rides, scuba diving, and kayaking at famous beaches of Goa such as Baga, Calangute, Anjuna, and Candolim.
The activities in beaches are family friendly. If you are a beginner, you can hire experienced instructors to enjoy activities.

blocks.text: Enjoy Shopping in Flea markets and Bazaars

items: Goa is a very lively destination to enjoy with family. It is also one of the most loved spots for shoppers.

You can enjoy shopping at some of the most famous flea markets like Anjuna, Arpora Saturday Night Market, Mapusa Market and Bazaars like Calangute Market, Panjim and 18th June road for souvenirs, clothes, jewelry, decor, and artisan products.

blocks.text: Witness the Rich Heritage of Goa

items: Goa has many amazing heritage destinations perfect for cultural enthusiasts, families and history buffs. Most of the heritage monuments here represent centuries of Indo-Portuguese culture and artistic achievement.
Explore Palácio do Deão, Fort Aguada, Basilica of Bom Jesus, Our Lady of The Immaculate Conception Church and Fernandes Heritage House.
Goan Bakeries reflects the rich Portuguese culinary heritage which you must know if you are in Goa.
Explore some of the top bakeries in Goa like Myles High Bakehouse, Simona's Bakery, German Bakery, Padaria Prazeres etc.

Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary is one of the must visit places if you are in Goa for enjoying thrilling wildlife and capturing scenic nature views. Its rich tropical forests are teeming with wildlife. You will spot leopards, elephants, Indian bison (gaur), deer, Malayan giant squirrels, and over 120 species of birds.
There are also many beautiful places to explore like Dudhsagar Waterfalls, Devil's Canyon viewpoint, Tambdi Falls, and the ancient Tambdi Surla Mahadev Temple.
In Goa, you will experience both Indian and Portuguese culinary heritage. You will enjoy Goa's seafood tossed with distinctive spices, and the sweet-and-savory flavors.
You must note these famous foods in Goa such as Goan Fish curry, Pork Vindaloo, Prawn Balchao, Bebinca, Chicken Shagoti, Patoleo, Crab Xacuti and Sorpotel.

blocks.text: How to Reach Goa by Air, Rail and Road

If you opt for flight, it will be the fastest travel mode to reach Goa. Trains along the scenic Konkan coast will be preferred by budget conscious travellers most of the time. Tourists also opt for road trips to Goa from Mumbai and Pune which allows for flexible scenic sightseeing stops along the route. Here is a detailed outline of How to reach Goa by Air, Train and Road-

rows: Goa International Airport (Dabolim, GOI) and Mopa Airport (North Goa). These airports are the nearest airports to reach Goa. Dabolim is 29–32 km from Panaji, allowing both domestic and international flights.

Goa has good flight accessibility. You will get direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Ahmadabad, Pune. International flights from Abu Dhabi, Muscat, Sharjah, Doha, Dubai, Kuwait, Singapore
Delhi-Goa: 2.5 hr.; Mumbai-Goa: 1 hr.; Bengaluru-Goa: 1 hr.
There are two main railway stations: Madgaon (Margao, MAO) and Vasco-da-Gama (VSG) to reach Goa.
Major trains to reach Goa are- Konkan Kanya Express, Mandovi Express, Goa Sampark Kranti Express (Delhi-Goa), Amaravathi Express (Kolkata), Nizamuddin Goa Express (Delhi via Pune).
Mumbai-Goa: 8–12 hr.; Delhi-Goa: 25 hr.; Bengaluru-Goa: 15 hr.

You can reach Goa via NH-66 (Mumbai-Goa), NH-48 & NH-4A (Bangalore), NH-366, NH-566. You can also opt for Multiple deluxe AC and regular bus services from Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru, Belgaum, Kolhapur, Mangalore. Also enjoy self-drive with friends and witness scenic spots along the way to reach Goa.
You will get direct buses from Mumbai, Pune and Bangalore. From Mumbai, Goa is (600 km), Pune (450 km), Bengaluru (560 km), Mangalore (370 km), Belgaum (150 km), Hyderabad (660 km).
Mumbai-Goa: 12–14 hr.; Bengaluru-Goa: 9–11 hr.; Pune-Goa: 9 hr.

blocks.text: Useful Travel Tips to Enjoy Goa Holidays with Family and Friends
Here are some of the best and useful tips from My Quick Trippers for memorable Goa Holidays-

items: Gearless motorbikes are the best way to travel in Goa. You can easily rent it at the best rates. For cheaper options, motorcycle rickshaws are the best way to travel within Goa.
You can visit beachfront restaurants to try delicious Goan, seafood, and Indian cuisines. These offer more affordable food options than conventional restaurants.
You can also download the Dineout app. It's a popular app for table reservations, available on iOS and Android. You will get cashbacks and discounts on restaurant bills.
Check if there is a Ladies Night in any bars and pubs in Goa on weekdays, as you will get free entry and drinks.

You can also check for happy hours in the bars. The timings are 5 to 8 pm. You will get one plus one on drinks and spirits. Alcohol is also cheaper in wine shops compared to restaurants, beach shacks, and bars.
If you want to try your hand at gambling for fun, then you can visit on weekdays. On weekends, the games are very costly.
Include adventure activities, play games, build sandcastles at Calangute, Baga, Candolim, and Palolem beaches. Don't forget to try dolphin spotting cruises at Sinquerim or Morjim.
If you have kids then include places like Goa Science Centre & Planetarium in Panaji. It has interactive exhibits for kids.
For Food and Shopping , Don't miss Goan cuisines and also visit flea markets at Anjuna or Mapusa.
If you want better deals and comfort, book hotels and resorts in Goa in advance. Goa is a popular destination, so it is crowded throughout the year.
Always respect the local customs and traditions. Dress modestly in churches and temples, and follow local etiquette.

blocks.text: The Golden Triangle Trip is a unique journey that takes you to the culturally rich cities of Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur. This triangle-shaped trip is perfect for you if you want to see the country in its old glory. We are talking about its rich architecture, the majestic forts, and vibrant markets! This tour will have you stroll through the narrow lanes and iconic landmarks equally! Book My Quick Trippers's Golden Triangle Tour Packages now and experience the real India.

You'll begin this special tour in the bustling city of Delhi . Admire the iconic landmarks like the Red Fort and India Gate. Now, move to the old city of Agra , where you will witness the timeless beauty of the Taj Mahal pretty closely. Get impressed with the grandeur of the Mughal-era monuments! Conclude the tour in the Pink City, Jaipur. Be in awe of the City Palace and the intricate Hawa Mahal . Our Golden Triangle Group Tour Package will also take you to the bustling bazaars and spice-filled markets. Call us now to know more about this tour plan!
Why Go on a Golden Triangle Tour?
Golden Triangle trip is one of the most iconic journeys in the entirety of the nation. There are several reasons why you should choose this special trip, such as:

items: This trip captures the soul of North India in one trip. Therefore, if you wish to taste the flavour of North India in a span of just 5 to 6 days, this tour is a must!
There is no trip like this that combines the heritage of the British, Mughal and the Rajput so perfectly in one circuit.
The destinations that you're going to visit are remarkably beautiful, and serve as the epitome of the beauty of yesteryear's architecture . Think of the Taj Mahal and Jaipur's royal forts!
If you're visiting North India for the first time , then also this special journey will do justice to your tour like no other.
The circuit covers 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites - Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb (Delhi), Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri (Agra), Jantar Mantar, and Walled City of Jaipur.
All budgets are covered - from ₹12,500 per person group packages to luxury ₹1,50,000 heritage hotel experiences.

blocks.text: And if you wish to go on a comfortable, luxe trip with all your travel logistics being handled, then book our packages. From a 5 Days Golden Triangle Tour to the full-fledged Golden Triangle Honeymoon Package , we offer it all!
Best Time to Visit the Golden Triangle

The best time to go on the Golden Triangle Tour is, hands down, in the months of October to March . The weather in this window is quite pleasant and therefore makes for a perfect time to come here and enjoy sightseeing. The low temperature and the clear skies are a great plus of this season.

rows: Peak tourist season — book early; fog risk in Jan
Extreme heat — Agra and Jaipur especially harsh

blocks.text: Another great time to go on this tour is in the monsoon season, from July–September. You can experience cool weather and the crowds are less compared to the peak season. This would allow you to complete the trip at your own pace.
We recommend that you avoid booking your Delhi Agra Jaipur travel package in the summers (April–June). The temperature can rise beyond scorching 40°C, especially in Rajasthan.

Important January note: Dense fog frequently affects morning flights and road visibility in Delhi and Agra in December–January. Early morning Taj Mahal visits can be obscured. Our itineraries build in flexibility for this.
How to Reach the Golden Triangle?
You can reach the tour destinations via the following transport modes:

By Air: The Golden Triangle Tour starts from Delhi, and the national capital has a very well-maintained Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGI — code DEL). It's connected to major cities all around the world. Jaipur and Agra, too, have airports with good domestic connections. Approximate flight times to Delhi: Mumbai ~2 hrs, Bangalore ~2.5 hrs, Chennai ~2.5 hrs, Hyderabad ~2 hrs.

By Train: All three cities of the trip have railway stations. With frequent trains like the Shatabdi Express and Rajdhani Express, you can easily access these cities. Book train tickets online at the official IRCTC website. Book 45–60 days in advance during October–March peak season.

By Road: If you wish to go on the tour by road, use the national highways — NH-44 (Delhi to Agra via Yamuna Expressway, ~230 km, 3–3.5 hrs) and NH-48 (Jaipur to Delhi, ~280 km, 4–5 hrs). These are in good condition and make a smooth link between Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur.
You can also book My Quick Trippers's Golden Triangle Family Tour Packages , where all your transport logistics will be handled entirely by us.

blocks.text: Q1. What is the price of Golden Triangle tour packages in 2026?

Ans: Budget 3N/4D packages start from ₹12,500 per person. Standard 5N/6D: ₹22,000–₹32,000. Luxury: ₹85,000–₹1,50,000. Extensions with Ranthambore or Varanasi add ₹8,000–₹20,000. Contact us for an exact quote.
Q2. How many days is the Golden Triangle tour?
Ans: Minimum 3 nights / 4 days for core highlights. Recommended: 5 nights / 6 days. Extended versions with Ranthambore, Varanasi, or Udaipur run 8–12 days.
Q3. What is the best time for Golden Triangle tour?
Ans: October to March — ideal temperature range (8°C–30°C). November and February are peak months. Avoid April–June (extreme heat, up to 45°C).
Q4. Is Taj Mahal closed on any day?
Ans: Yes — Taj Mahal is closed every Friday for Muslim prayers. This is critical planning information. All My Quick Trippers itineraries are built around this.
Q5. How many UNESCO sites are on the Golden Triangle?
Ans: Eight UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb (Delhi), Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri (Agra), Jantar Mantar, and Walled City of Jaipur.
Q6. Is the Golden Triangle suitable for senior citizens?
Ans: Fully suitable — no trekking, no altitude. All travel by private AC vehicle. Wheelchair assistance at monuments on request. We pre-book ground-floor rooms.
Q7. What is the Taj Mahal entry fee in 2026?
Ans: Indian citizens: ₹50. Foreign nationals: ₹1,300. Paid directly at monument — carry cash.
Q8. Can I add Ranthambore tiger safari?
Ans: Yes — add 2 nights between Agra and Jaipur for two jeep safaris. Ranthambore has 70+ tigers. Adds approximately ₹8,000–₹15,000 per person.
Q9. What is Fatehpur Sikri and should I visit?
Ans: Emperor Akbar's 16th-century ghost capital — UNESCO-listed. Sits on Agra–Jaipur highway. Add 90 minutes. All Standard+ packages include it. Do not skip.
Q10. Is the Golden Triangle tour private or group?
Ans: My Quick Trippers tours are 100% private — your vehicle, your guide, your schedule. No shared coaches or group schedules.
Q11. Can I customise the itinerary?
Ans: Yes — duration, hotel tier, guide language, dietary requirements, extension destinations — all customisable.
Q12. Is the Golden Triangle good for international tourists?
Ans: India's most popular international circuit — English-speaking specialist guides, international-standard hotels, direct Delhi flight connectivity from all major hubs.
Q13. What is the Sheesh Mahal at Amber Fort?
Ans: Hall of Mirrors — ceiling and walls entirely covered in intricate mirror mosaic. A single candle reportedly illuminates the entire room. Go at 8 AM sharp before crowds arrive.
Q14. Are tripods and drones allowed at Taj Mahal?
Ans: No — tripods and drones are strictly banned inside the Taj Mahal complex. Mobile phones and personal cameras are permitted.
Q15. What is the best hotel in Agra for Taj Mahal view?

Ans: Oberoi Amarvilas offers a direct Taj Mahal view from every room — considered the most spectacular hotel position in India. ITC Mughal and Trident Agra are excellent alternatives at lower price points.

blocks.text: The Golden Triangle trip takes you on an exciting journey to the three famous cities in India such as Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur.

items: Route: Delhi → Sightseeing in Delhi → Delhi to Agra → Jaipur to Agra → Jaipur sightseeing → Jaipur - Delhi

blocks.text: When you land at New Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport, a representative will greet you and assist you in making your way to the designated hotel. You’ll spend the night at the hotel.

After breakfast, begin your full-day sightseeing tours of New Delhi and Old Delhi. On a tour of Old Delhi, there will be stops at Raj Ghat, Jama Masjid, and Red Fort are all included. From Jama Masjid to Chandni Chowk, take a cycle rickshaw and take in the scenery. A New Delhi sightseeing tour includes stops at the spectacular India Gate, Parliament House, President House, Humayun’s Tomb, Qutab Minar, and a drive down Rajpath. You’ll eat and spend the night at the hotel. (The monuments in Delhi are closed on Monday) Places You’ll See
Day 3: Delhi to Agra (221 kms, Approx. 5 hrs drive)

After breakfast, travel to Agra, stopping en route to view Sikandra, the tomb of renowned Mughal emperor Akbar. Upon your arrival in Agra, the city home to the Taj Mahal, a representative from our business will assist you in travelling to the desired hotel. Visit the Taj Mahal and the majestic Agra Fort, two well-known love monuments. The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan as a memorial to his devoted wife Mumtaz Mahal. The breathtaking memorial to love is crafted from white marble and has inlay work. In 1565, Mughal emperor Akbar built Agra Fort. Visit Itmad-ud-Daula Tomb, also known as the Baby Taj Mahal by Daulah. Stay the night and eat breakfast in your hotel.
Day 4: Jaipur to Agra (238 kms, Approx. 5-6 hrs drive)

After breakfast, take a drive to Jaipur, also referred to as the Pink City and the capital of Rajasthan. The Mughal emperor Akbar erected Fatehpur Sikri in the late 16th century but abandoned it because of a lack of water. You will stop at this location along the way. You will also see Buland Darwaza, the largest entryway in the world. Continue your journey to Jaipur, the “Pink City,” our representative will assist you in getting to the hotel once you arrive in Jaipur. You’ll eat and spend the night at the hotel. Places You’ll See

After breakfast at the hotel, go out for the hilltop Amber Fort. travel to the fort on an elephant. Later, take in the city of Jaipur’s sights include City Palace, Hawa Mahal, and Jantar Mantar. Enjoy shopping at the thriving neighborhood bazaars throughout the city as well. You’ll eat and spend the night at the hotel. Places You’ll See
Day 6: Jaipur - Delhi (Departure) (261 Kms, 5-6 Hours Drive)
Drive back to Delhi after having breakfast. We will drop you off at the airport or station with happy memories.

When it comes to eco-tourism, Gujarat is the best place to visit. Do you know that Gandhinagar is the greenest capital city of Asia?

blocks.text: Best Time to Go for the Gujarat Trip

The best time to visit Gujarat depends really on the activities you want to do. However, most tourists prefer to come here in winter, from October to March. These winter months not only have nice, pleasant weather for sightseeing but also host a lot of cultural events during this period. So, it’s a good choice to choose Gujarat holiday packages during this time.
However, besides the peak season, there are other times too when you can visit the land of lions. Here’s the complete overview:
Winter (October to March) - Best Time to Visit
The weather is mostly pleasant with temperatures being anywhere from 12°C and 29°C.
Top Things to Do in Gujarat in Winter

items: Enjoy cultural sites like Dwarka, Somnath Temple, and Champaner-Pavagadh.

Take part in the celebrations of the Rann of Kutch festival (happening between November and February) and relish the mind-blowing cultural performances, moonlit desert views, exquisite crafts, and much more.
Go for wildlife safaris at Gir National Park (open only from October to mid-June)
Partake in the Garba nights and Dandiya Raas during Navratri (October).
Experience the colorfully dotted sky with kites during the International Kite Festival (January).

blocks.text: Festivals and Events in Gujarat in Winter

The weather is cool due to the rainfall around this time. One of the good things about visiting during this period is that the areas are less crowded, and therefore you can enjoy your Gujarat sightseeing in a much calmer and relaxed environment. However, you must avoid coastal areas during this time as they get flooded.
Top Things to Do in Gujarat during Monsoon:

items: Enjoy Gujarat's hill station, like Saputara, it is one of the best hill stations in Gujarat . During monsoon, it gets adorned with lush greenery during this period.
Enjoy the Saputara Monsoon Festival during this time.
Capture the scenic waterfall- Gira Waterfalls. It is also one of the best spots for a picnic in Gujarat with your family.
Visit Polo forest in the Sabarkantha district to enjoy camping, trekking, cycling, and capturing the beautiful temple ruins.
Enjoy bird watching and the scenic beauty of wetlands at Thol Lake Bird Sanctuary in Thol Village.

blocks.text: The weather can get extremely hot during this time, reaching well over 40°C. It’s perfect for tourists who are on a budget, as you can find very cheap accommodations in Gujarat.
Top Things to Do in Gujarat in Summer

items: Visit Mandvi Beach in the early mornings or evenings as temperatures are mild then.
Attend the Mango Festival, which is held in May-June. Here, the season’s fresh mangoes, especially the Kesar mangoes, are showcased.
Visit traditional fairs like the Bhavnath Fair (Junagadh) for cultural displays, performances, and purchasing local crafts.

blocks.text: Places to Visit on Gujarat Trip

Gujarat offers you everything from rich culture, fascinating history, amazing wildlife to calming spirituality. There are several interesting places here that are covered in your Gujarat travel itinerary. Here’s the list:
The capital has a lot of gems to offer to tourists, such as:

items: Sabarmati Ashram: This is a must to include on your Gujarat holiday package as this was the ashram where Mahatma Gandhi resided and also led the freedom struggle of India from here.
Calico Museum of Textiles: Do visit the textile heritage of India and experience the treasure trove with your own eyes.
Adalaj Stepwell: This stunning Stepwell architecture will blow your mind.
Kankaria Lake: This scenic lake is perfect for a family outing. You can also enjoy boating and the zoo here.

blocks.text: This white salty desert is famous for being one of the largest salt deserts in the world. The place has a lot to offer in terms of sightseeing, such as:

items: Great Rann of Kutch: This place needs to be included in your Gujarat travel package, especially during the Rann Utsav which is held from November to February. Also, you get to enjoy the unique landscape of this natural beauty.
Mandvi Beach: This beach is a great option to chill and relax. In addition, you can take a short trip to the famous Vijay Vilas Palace which is nearby.
Kalo Dungar: This is the highest point in Kutch. People love to climb this hill to catch the stunning panoramic views of the white desert around.

blocks.text: Watch the roaring Asiatic lion in its full glory at the Gir National Park. You also meet beautiful leopards, cute deer, fascinating bird species, and many more majestic animals. Don’t miss out on including this treasure on your Gujarat holiday package as the wildlife safari experience here is another level.
This ancient city is a big-time Hindu pilgrimage site and has several must-see places.

items: Dwarkadhish Temple: Dedicated to Lord Krishna, this temple is also considered to be a Char Dham pilgrimage site.
Gopi Talav: This holy pond has so many stories associated with Lord Krishna and is therefore a must-visit place for Krishna devotees.
Bet Dwarka: This serene island is stunning to the core and can be reached by a joyous ferry ride. It also has a lot of religious significance.

blocks.text: This is a highly revered temple of Lord Shiva as it’s one of the twelve Jyotirlingas in India. Devotees make sure to pay a visit to this temple when they are in the state.

Vadodara is a major city in Gujarat, known for its financial abundance, classic music, and beautiful architecture. You should include the following places in your Gujarat holiday package to make the most out of your trip:

items: Laxmi Vilas Palace: Get introduced to the Indo-Saracenic architecture and get bowled by the sheer opulence of this palace.
Sayaji Gardens: This gorgeous park has a museum and a zoo – a perfect day out with family.
Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park: This is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with beautiful temples, mosques, and forts.

blocks.text: Bhuj is one of the key tourist destinations of the state. It never fails to impress its travellers with its intricate architecture, astonishing palaces, meandering streets, and authentic handicrafts. Make sure to add the following places to your Gujarat travel package.

items: Aina Mahal: This is a famous place where you see the hall of mirrors with ceilings and walls adorned with Venetian glass. The mirrors are gilded framed. On top of that, the whole aura is made even grander by the handcrafted chandeliers.
Kutch Museum: This is the oldest museum of Gujarat showcasing the state’s rich history and culture. A must-visit for all the history enthusiasts!

Prag Mahal: Located just next to Aina Mahal, this place showcases Gothic arches and Corinthian pillars. The walls are decorated with animal trophies and antique artwork, reflecting the grandeur of the time.

blocks.text: What to Eat on Gujarat Trip?

Besides being a tourist haven, Gujarat is also a foodie’s paradise. The flavorful and diverse cuisine is a hit with both locals and tourists. And you’re spoilt for choice – for you have a lot on your plate – from delicious street food to wholesome meals. Here’s what to try and relish on your Gujarat trip:
Gujarati Snacks: Enjoy the tangy, spicy, and sweet pleasure of Gujarat’s authentic finger-licking good snacks.
Bread Varieties: These flatbreads are every food lover’s delight.
Sweets and Desserts: Gujarat’s sweets are to die for!
Regional Specialties: From Kutch essentials to Vadodara specialties, these dishes must be tried at least once!
What to Buy on Gujarat Trip?

items: Dhalgarwad: You must visit Dhalgarwad in Gujarat; It’s a popular hub for Gujarati traditional dresses and Lehengas, Bandhani Sarees, Zari work, Patola dress materials, Chaniya Choli, woodcraft items of Surat and Kutch.
Manek Chowk: Famous bullion market packed with an amazing variety of chunky, silver and gold jewellery stores, combined with famous street food stalls.
Sindhi Market: Renowned for Gujarati Textile products, it’s a must-visit market. Look for a variety of Sarees, dress materials, bed sheets, etc.

Raipur Gate: Brighten your space with beautiful home decor items. It also houses many shopping malls and traditional Gujarati food stalls where you will get authentic Gujarati snacks like Dhokla, Farsans, Khandvi and vegetable kebabs, etc.
Lal Darwaza Market: If you wish to buy electric gadgets, Lal Darwaza is a perfect place in Law Garden. You will also witness a variety of children’s garments, toys, books and wallets.

Ramakda Market: It’s one of the most popular markets to go with family, especially those who have kids, as there is a variety of toys available at the best rates. You will also find many beautiful accessories for women.

Gujarat Travel Tips for a Memorable Trip
Follow these tips to maximize your spending power and get the best travel experience in Gujarat with family and friends-

items: Enjoy the Festivals: Plan your Gujarat trip in late September and early October as the month's festivities will make your day unforgettable. During Thai time, people celebrate Navratri with Garba and Dandiya Raas, community gathering, folk music and traditional costumes. It is one of the major festivals in Gujarat .

Plan in Advance: Planning must be perfect to explore- Gujarat is an amazing place, but it is also very vast in terms of tourist places. You need to plan your itinerary to avoid last-minute hassle. You can book your Gujarat trip with us, and we will take care of your complete travel arrangements.

Art and Crafts: Do not forget to explore the art heritage and textile craft of Gujarat . Gujarat is very famous for its art and textile industry. There is a variety of textiles like Patola, Bandhani, Lehariya, Dhamadka, Ajrakh, Mushroo, etc. Also explore Sadeli Art, which is a technique used by craftsmen to carve floral and geometrical patterns on teak or other wood available locally.

Book Hotels in Advance: Hotels and Resorts in Gujarat range from Budget, mid-range, to luxury. You will also get budget guesthouses and Dharamshalas, and tents if you are planning to enjoy Rann Utsav. The quality of hotels will depend on your budget. So, choose wisely and book your hotels in advance. Sometimes, your selected hotels may not be available due to the peak tourism season.
Free to Nominal Entry Spots: You should also explore the best free/nominal entry spots like Sabarmati Ashram, Kankaria Lake, Sun Temple Modhera, Rani Ki Vav Patan, and local markets.
Check for discounts: Sometimes, travel agents run festivals or off-season discounts; always check them.

blocks.text: Q1: What Is the Best Time to Visit Gujarat?

Ans: Gujarat is a dry state and hence winter months are considered best for your Gujarat trip as in this season you find pleasing and favourable weather to complete all the outdoor activities. Participating in outdoor activities in summer and monsoon months is very hectic and troublesome.
Q2: What Is Famous Food in Gujarat?
Ans: Dhokla, Khandvi, Methi Ka Thepla, Khakhra, Jalebi, Gujarati Samosa, Bardoli Ki Khichdi, etc. are some of the most famous foods in Gujarat.
Q3: What Is the Capital of Gujarat?
Ans: Gandhinagar is the capital city of Gujarat that attracts a huge number of tourists with its beauty.
Q4: What Is Gujarat Famous For?
Ans: Gujarat is famous for several things like Dwarkadhish Temple, Somnath Temple, Beyt Dwarka Beach, shopping in Ahmedabad, Rann of Kutch, and many more things.
Q5: What Is Famous in Gujarat For Shopping?
Ans: Khadi, Patola Silk Sarees, dress materials, bangles, handlooms and handicrafts, jewelry, traditional Ghaghra Choli, embroidered and appliquéd quilts are few of the must buy stuffs in Gujarat.
Q6: Which Is the Biggest Mall in Gujarat?
Ans: Ahmedabad One mall happens to be the biggest mall in Gujarat where shopaholics love visiting.
Q7: How Can I Go to Gujarat By Flight?
Ans: There are three major airports in Gujarat- Vadodara Airport, Surat Airport, and Ahmedabad Airport where flights from different cities land.
Q8: How many days are sufficient for my Gujarat trip?

Ans: For a short trip, 4-5 days are sufficient to cover important destinations like Ahmedabad, Somnath, Gir National Park, and Dwarka. However, if your Gujarat tour package has more days to spare, you can extend it to 7-10 days, covering spots like Vadodara, Bhuj, and Rann of Kutch as well.
Q9: Is Gujarat safe for solo travellers?
Ans: Gujarat is generally considered safe, even for women. However, all tourists must exercise caution. Keep your luggage and wallets secure at all times and avoid secluded places at night.
Q10: What are some wildlife experiences that I can enjoy on my Gujarat holiday package?
Ans: Gujarat offers some of the most thrilling wildlife experiences. You can visit places like:

items: Gir National Park: Meet the majestic lions and watch them being their regal self.
Blackbuck National Park: This is an excellent place to spot the blackbucks soaking in the sun or sauntering around in the grass.
Nalsarovar Bird Sanctuary: Thinking of watching those rare colorful birds? Come here and watch their sky show for yourself.
Marine National Park: When you’re done with land animals, head here and enjoy the coral reefs and vast marine biodiversity.

blocks.text: Q11: Do people speak Hindi in Gujarat?

Ans: Gujarati is the main language that is spoken all over Gujarat. However, both Hindi and English are widely understood, especially if you’re in tourist hot spots like Ahmedabad, Vadodara, and Bhuj.
Q12: What should I wear on the Gujarat trip?
Ans: Different seasons call for different attires. For example:

items: In winter (October to March), light woolens are recommended.

blocks.text: Day 1: : Arrival and Welcome in Thrissur

You will be warmly welcomed by our representative at Cochin Airport/ Thrissur Railway Station, and then you will be taken to Kalady, which is the birthplace of Sri Adi Shankaracharya. It is in the place of Kalady that Adi Shankaracharya practiced miracles through his presence. He got the Vedas perfect and devoted his life to the preaching of the Vedic Dharma by founding four mutts at Puri, Sringeri, Dwaraka, and Joshimath. It was rediscovered in the late 19th century by the then Shankaracharya of Sringeri, and the following consecration of a temple to Sri Adi Shankara in 1910. Visit Sringeri Mutt:- Sringeri Mutt was constructed at the same location where the house of Adi Sankara was located. After check-in, later drive to Guruvayur. Take a spiritual tour to Thrissur and Guruvayur temples. Experience the Divine atmosphere of these ancient shrines, covered with complicated carvings and colorful murals. Experience the magical rites and sacrifices, with worshipers coming together to receive blessings of the gods. The calm and the inner spiritual volatility of these temples is indeed a very rewarding experience. Places You’ll See

The green fields and foggy mist cover it, forming a magical sight that is enjoyed by a large number of people.
