blocks.text: Q1. Which month is Kaziranga closed?

Ans. Kaziranga National Park is closed during the monsoon season, which is from May to October. This is primarily due to the heavy rainfall (and consequently floods) that the region receives in this time frame. The park resumes operation in November.
Q2. Which month is better to visit Assam?

Ans. The best time to visit the state of Assam is in winter. The months of November to February mark the best time to come here, as they offer the most pleasant atmosphere with clear skies. The wintery charm is just a cherry on top! You can comfortably go on safaris and other sightseeing at this time.
Q3. What is Majuli famous for?

Ans. Majuli is famous for preserving Assamese art & culture in its monasteries, Vaishnavite Satras, and tribal culture. Moreover, its serene environment is another popular thing about the island that draws tourists in.
Q4. What is the time of the Ferry from Majuli to Jorhat?
Ans. Ferries between Majuli and Jorhat start running in the morning at 7:00 AM and continue until 4 in the evening.
Q5. How long is the Majuli ferry ride?
Ans. The ferry ride from Jorhat to Majuli takes about 1 to 1.5 hours. The duration can change depending on the season and the water levels.
Q6. Is This a Private Tour?
Ans. Yes, this tour is private. No other travelers will join your group, ensuring a personalized experience just for you group.
Q7. Can the Driver speak Hindi or English?

Ans. The Drivers can speak in Hindi and Regional Language. Our drivers understand basic English phrases, which should be sufficient for regular communication during the tour. We also provide complimentary city guides in major cities. However, if you prefer a fluent English-speaking driver, we recommend booking a professional guide to ensure smooth communication. Additionally, we offer guides fluent in languages such as French, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Italian, Russian, and German, available at an extra cost. Please inform us in advance or mention it in the special remarks section while booking the tour online
Q8. How can I get help with my booking?
Ans. You can message one of our live chat teams using the chat with us’ button on the right of the screen, when available.
Q9. Does the Driver Know All the Attractions and Places for Sightseeing?
Ans. Yes, all our drivers are well-versed in the entire region and are knowledgeable about all the attractions and places of interest.
Q10. Will the Taxi and Driver be with us always?
Ans. Yes, the Taxi and Driver will be at your Service from the Start till the End of the Tour.
Q11. Can I Use the Car After 8 PM?

Ans. It depends on the specific tour, but generally, we do not allow the taxi and driver to be on duty after 8 PM. This is to ensure that the driver gets adequate rest and is ready for the next day's activities.
Q12. Does the Taxi Have Roof Carriers for Luggage?

Ans. Only the Ertiga and Innova Crysta vehicles are equipped with roof carriers for luggage. Sedans and Tempo Travelers do not have roof carriers. If you require a vehicle with a roof carrier, please make a special remark during your booking.
Q13. How Can I Rely on Your Company?

Ans. Our company, has been in operation for 15 years and is recognized by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, as well as other state tourism departments. We are an approved travel company with accreditations from IATA, IATO, ABTO, and more. We have built a strong reputation and have successfully served over 100,000 tourists, ensuring reliability and quality service.
Q14. Will Someone Be Available for Assistance While I Am on Tour with You?

Ans. Yes, we will be available to answer any questions or address any concerns you may have during your tour. You can reach out to us at any time. We are committed to providing the best possible service and ensuring our guests have memorable vacations they will cherish forever.
Q15. Why Should I Book with You Instead of Other Travel Companies in the Market?

Ans. We differentiate ourselves from other travel companies through our commitment to personalized service, local expertise, and customer satisfaction. Our team goes above and beyond to understand your travel preferences and provide tailored recommendations. With years of experience and numerous industry accreditations, we ensure that you receive the best possible experience at competitive rates. We are dedicated to making your journey memorable and stress-free.
Q16. Can I Modify or Cancel My Booking?

Ans. Yes, you can modify or cancel your booking. However, it depends on how many days in advance you notify us. Cancellation charges may apply, so please contact us as soon as possible to discuss your options.

Ans. Yes, since this is a private tour, customizations are possible based on your arrival/departure times, duration of stay, and personal interests. Feel free to reach out to your travel expert to discuss your specific needs.

items: Route: Lucknow to Nepalgunj → Mansarovar Darshan - Return to Lucknow

blocks.text: The journey starts from Lucknow at 09:00 in the morning. You will be picked up by one of our representatives and begin the drive to Nepalgunj. Along the way, you will stop for a delicious lunch at a nearby restaurant. After you get there, check into the hotel and unwind for a bit. After that, you'll go to one of Nepalgunj's oldest temples, Bageshwori Temple and be a part of group Havan performed by the Pandit Ji. Later, you will receive a briefing at your hotel on the rest of the Yatra. After savoring the delicious dinner, spend the night at the hotel.Meals:Lunch & Dinner |Hotel:Soaltee Westend Premier or SimilarPlaces You’ll See
Day 2: Mansarovar Darshan - Return to Lucknow

After breakfast, you'll be driven to the Nepalgunj airport or helipad to start your flight to Mansarovar. Pandit Ji will lead you in chanting Shiv Chalisa and Bhajans during the hour-long flight.. You will be able to see peaks like API, Saipal, and Nampha, as well as the eastern and southern faces of Kailash. Enjoy the majestic and awe-inspiring view of Lord Shiva's residence from the comfort of your seat. You'll head back to your hotel for lunch after Aerial Darshan. Afterward, you will begin your return journey to Lucknow, where the trip will conclude.Meals:Breakfast, LunchPlaces You’ll See

items: Kainchi Dham Tour Package from Delhi

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrive Delhi – Drive to Kainchi Dham (330 km / 7 hours)

Welcome to Delhi! Once you arrive at Delhi airport or railway station, you will receive a warm welcome from our tour representative.Now, begin a scenic drive among the Himalayan foothills toKainchi Dham. This spiritual Ashram is located amidst lush green valleys near Bhowali. Also, this ashram is world famous, and celebrities like Apple founder Steve Jobs and Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg have visited this place!Once you get there, check into your pre-booked hotel. Have some rest if you feel like!In the evening, get ready to visit theKainchi Dham Temple. Soak in the utterly calm vibe of this ashram. Take some time out to meditate in its serene surroundings. You can also attend the evening prayers here!Your night stay will be in the Kainchi Dham.Places You’ll See
Day 2: Morning at Kainchi Dham – Sightseeing in Nainital (20-25 km / 1.5 hours)

Have the perfect start to your day with meditation in the peaceful atmosphere of the Ashram. Take this time to ponder over the humanitarian teachings of the Neem Karoli Baba.After that, have breakfast. Now, you can explore the ashram complex and learn more about Baba’s teachings of love, service, and devotion. Also, visit the sacred banyan tree!After your Kainchi Dham visit, you can go on exploring the nearby sightseeing places, such asBhumiadhar Temple. Dedicated to Goddess Shakti, it’s famous for its calm energy and less crowded atmosphere.Later, you’ll be taken on a sightseeing tour of the ever-so-beautifulNainital. ExploreNaini Lakeand theNaina Devi Templehere, which is also one of the 51 Shakti Peethas.Now, go on a trip to a trio of scenic lakes –Bhimtal, Sattal, and Naukuchiatal. You can spot migratory birds here. You can also just sit here in its pure serene vibes!The last trip of the day will be made to the most famous market of Nainital, that isMall Road. Explore the myriad of shops here, selling everything from handicrafts to delicious food. We recommend trying the local Kumaoni dishes such as Bhatt ki Churkani and the spicy Aloo ke Gutke!End the day by going to your hotel in Nainital and getting a restful night of sleep.Places You’ll See

Have a delicious breakfast in the morning.Afterwards, depart from Nainital towards Delhi, as your tour concludes today. Don't forget to capture the beautiful sunrise views over the hills as you leave Nainital!Our driver will drop you off at the Delhi airport or railway station, as per your preference. Hope you have a fantastic trip!

Our Kainchi Dham Packages offer a comprehensive Darshan experience of the Ashram. You can offer your prayers, do Seva and savor the Prasad. blocks.text: Why Should You Visit Kainchi Dham Ashram?

If you are someone who is seeking inner peace, tranquility and a deep spiritual connection, you should visit Kainchi Dham Ashram. Kainchi Dham Ashram experiences very high tourist footfall throughout the year. In 2024, the number of visitors reached 24 lakhs. In the off season also, it receives around 5000 visitors daily. (source- Times of India ).
Other Reasons To Visit Kainchi Dham

items: Kainchi Dham is associated with Neem Karoli Baba, a mystic saint who was an ardent devotee of Lord Hanuman. In this ashram you will learn about his teachings on love, kindness, unconditional service and his guidance for the devotees.
Kainchi Dham Ashram surroundings will take your breath away the serene Himalayan landscapes and the welcoming atmosphere draws travellers from all around the world.
The ashram has also welcomed global icons like Steve Jobs and Mark Zuckerberg and celebrities like Virat Kohli who have credited their visits as spiritually uplifting and life-changing.
On June 15th the Ashram holds a community feast (Bhandara) where thousands of devotees offer Seva, share food and devotion. It is a fest which celebrates inclusivity and kindness.

Dress Code: Cover head, shoulders, and knees before entering the main temple hall. The ashram does not provide scarves — carry your own. Footwear must be removed at the entrance gate.

Cash Withdrawal: Withdraw adequate cash at Kathgodam or Haldwani before heading towards Bhowali. The nearest ATMs to Kainchi Dham are in Bhowali town (6 km) and may run out of cash on high-footfall days like Tuesdays and June 15.

Photography Rules: Photography is allowed in the ashram garden and outer areas. Strictly not permitted inside the main sanctum and Samadhi hall. Volunteers will remind you — keep your phone away before entering the inner temple.

Packing for Weather: Kainchi Dham sits at approximately 1,400m. Even in May–June, evenings are cool — carry a light jacket. October–November nights drop to 8–12°C, so pack thermals for autumn visits.

Senior Citizens: No trekking is required — the ashram entrance and main darshan area are on flat ground. The pathway has ramps and is wheelchair accessible. Ground-floor hotel rooms can be arranged on request.

Ans: The Kainchi Dham Ashram offers Sattvic meals as Prasad (sacred food). The food is prepared with great devotion. During any festival, the devotees get special Prasad items like Jalebis and Kheer.
Q4: Can foreigners visit Kainchi Dham?
Ans: Yes, Kainchi Dham Ashram welcomes foreigners. Anyone with great devotion can visit the Ashram. It is open to all.

Q7: Can families visit Kainchi Dham Ashram?
Ans: Yes, it is the best place for profound spiritual experience with your family. It is best if your kid is a bit older. For toddlers, the place can be difficult to stay engaged for a long time.

Q9: Is photography allowed in Kainchi Dham?

Ans: Yes, photography is allowed in outer zones like ashram premises, gardens and natural surroundings but it is not allowed in sacred and inner temple zones. Don't take photos of sacred sensitive areas without permission.
Q10: What should devotees wear in Kainchi Dham?
Ans: Devotees should wear modest clothes. It is a sacred place, so you need to cover your head, shoulders and knees. Don't wear clothes which are too revealing.
Q11: What are the popular festivals celebrated in Kainchi Dham?
Ans: Some of the most popular festivals celebrated in Kainchi Dham are Pratishtha Diwas, Hanuman Jayanti, Guru Purnima, Maha Samadhi Bhandara, Ram Navami, Navratri and Shivratri.
Q12: What type of Sewa is offered in Kainchi Dham by the devotees?

Ans: Sewa is an integral part to enhance your divine connection with Neem Karoli Baba. Ans: March to June, September to November is the best time to visit Kainchi Dham. The weather will be pleasant for nature walks, meditation sessions, spiritual activities and sightseeing.
Q14: What are the visiting hours of Kainchi Dham?

Ans: Kainchi Dham timings are 6:00am to 7:00pm from April to October and 7:00am to 6:00pm from November to March. Timings may change during peak festivals. Confirm current timings directly with the ashram before your visit. On Tuesdays, darshan continues till 9:00 PM.

Ans: Tuesday visits in Kainchi Dham are considered sacred so it has different timing. On Tuesday the ashram remains open till 9:00pm with Kirtans following the evening Aarti.

Ans: No, the entry to Kainchi Dham is free for Devotees. Entry fees are not required.

The package includes comfortable hotel stays, daily breakfast, guided sightseeing, and safe AC transfers - ensuring a completely hassle-free pilgrimage journey.

Kamakhya Temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas in India and the only Yoni Peetha among them - the spot where the womb of Goddess Sati is believed to have fallen. The temple sits atop Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam , and is dedicated to Goddess Kamakhya, the goddess of desire and feminine power.
Book this short trip to Maa Kamakhya with us and experience the divine presence of Maa Shakti in and around the temple. Ministry of Tourism, Government of India approved.
About Kamakhya Temple - The Supreme Shakti Peeth of India

Kamakhya Temple stands apart from every other temple in India. Perched atop Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam, it is the most powerful of the 51 Shakti Peethas - and the only Yoni Peetha, where the creative energy of Goddess Sati is believed to reside.

According to the Kalika Purana, when Goddess Sati self-immolated at Daksha's Yagna after her father insulted Lord Shiva, a grief-stricken Shiva carried her body through the universe. Lord Vishnu used his Sudarshana Chakra to divide Sati's remains into 51 parts. The Yoni fell here, on these very hills.

What strikes every first-time visitor: there is no idol inside the main sanctum. Devotees descend into a small, dark cave and offer prayers at a natural fissure in the rock - always moist from an underground spring. No statue, no image. Just the raw, living energy of the Goddess.

The temple's architecture follows the Nilachala style - a beehive-shaped dome surrounded by smaller shrines, different from anything in North or South India. The complex houses the full Dasa Mahavidya - ten great forms of the Divine Mother - each with its own temple on the hill.
Ambubachi Mela - Kamakhya's Most Sacred Annual Event

Every June (22nd-25th), Kamakhya Temple closes its doors for three days. This is Ambubachi - the annual period when Goddess Kamakhya is believed to undergo her menstrual cycle. The natural spring inside the temple is said to run red during these days.

When the temple reopens (from 26 June), the Ambubachi Mela begins and runs till 3 July. Lakhs of devotees, sadhus, and Tantric practitioners gather from across India. It is one of the largest spiritual congregations in Northeast India. If you plan to attend, book your Kamakhya tour package at least 3-4 months in advance - hotels fill fast.

Practical tip: Arrive before 8:00 AM on weekdays for shorter queues. Weekends and Hindu festival days are significantly busier. Purchase the VIP Darshan Pass (₹501/-) at the temple counter to avoid the general queue.
Best Time to Visit Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati

From practical experience: October to February is the sweet spot. The weather is pleasant, Darshan queues are manageable, and the Brahmaputra looks its most picturesque. Most families, senior pilgrims, and solo travelers prefer this window.
How to Reach Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati

The nearest airport is Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport (LGBI), Guwahati - approximately 14 km from Kamakhya Temple. Direct flights connect Guwahati to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Pune. Our package includes airport pickup.

Two railway stations serve the temple: Guwahati Railway Station (main, ~10 km from temple) and Kamakhya Railway Station (~2 km from temple, closer option). Major trains include Rajdhani Express, Brahmaputra Mail, and Saraighat Express from Delhi and Kolkata. Our package includes station pickup.

Guwahati is connected via National Highway 27. State buses, private taxis, and app-based cabs are easily available from the city. The temple hill is about 8 km from Guwahati city centre - roughly 25 minutes by road. Note: the final stretch up Nilachal Hill is by road or on foot (~200 steps).

blocks.text: Practical Tips for Visiting Kamakhya Temple

items: Reach early - Arrive before 8:00 AM on weekdays. The morning Darshan is calmer, the air is cooler, and the experience is far more personal.

Carry cash - ATMs are at the temple base but can be crowded. Keep ₹500–700 in cash for the pass, Prasad, flowers, and small donations.

Photography rule - Photography inside the main sanctum (the cave chamber) is strictly prohibited. Outer courtyard is fine.
Combine with Navagraha - Navagraha Temple is a 15-minute drive from Kamakhya. Very few tour operators include it — we do, on Day 2.
Ambubachi planning - Book 3–4 months in advance if visiting during Ambubachi Mela (late June). Hotels at Guwahati book up quickly.

blocks.text: Q1. What is included in the Kamakhya Temple tour package?

Ans. The package includes 1-night hotel accommodation (double sharing), daily breakfast, a private AC vehicle for all transfers and sightseeing, pickup and drop from Guwahati Airport/Railway Station, and all applicable taxes. Excludes VIP darshan pass, ferry/ropeway charges, personal expenses, and airfare/train tickets.
Q2. How many days are needed for the Kamakhya Temple tour?

Ans. Our standard package is 2 days / 1 night, which is sufficient to cover Kamakhya Darshan and all major Guwahati spiritual sites. If you plan to add Kaziranga National Park or Shillong, extend to 4–6 days.
Q3. What is the Kamakhya Temple tour package cost per person?
Ans. Standard package starts at ₹5,650 per person (double sharing, currently at 15% discount from ₹6,500). Deluxe and Luxury options are available on request. Use coupon WELCOME500 for extra savings.
Q4. When is the best time to visit Kamakhya Temple?

Ans. October to February is ideal — weather is pleasant (12°C–24°C), queues are manageable, and the Brahmaputra looks its most scenic. The Ambubachi Mela in late June is the most spiritually powerful time but requires advance booking due to massive crowds.
Q5. What is Ambubachi Mela and when does it happen?

Ans. Ambubachi Mela celebrates the annual menstrual cycle of Goddess Kamakhya. The temple closes from 22–25 June every year, then reopens with a grand Mela running from 26 June to 3 July. Lakhs of devotees attend. Book your Kamakhya Yatra package at least 3–4 months early if you plan to attend.
Q6. Is a VIP Darshan pass available at Kamakhya Temple?

Ans. Yes. The VIP Darshan Pass costs ₹501/- per person and is purchased directly at the temple counter. It allows faster entry and is strongly recommended on weekends, festivals, and peak season (October–February). This charge is NOT included in the tour package price.
Q7. What temples are covered besides Kamakhya in the 2-day package?

Ans. The itinerary covers all major Dasa Mahavidya temples on Nilachal Hill (Dhumavati, Tripureswari, Maa Tara, Maa Kali, Chhinnamasta, Bagalamukhi, Bhuvaneshwari, Banadurga), Umananda Temple on Peacock Island, Navagraha Temple, and a Brahmaputra sunset cruise (optional, direct payment).
Q8. Is Kamakhya Temple accessible for elderly or differently-abled visitors?

Ans. There are approximately 200 steps to the temple, but a road also goes up to Nilachal Hill by car. Elderly pilgrims can be driven to the temple entrance and walk only a short final stretch. Our driver and guide assist accordingly.
Q9. Can I arrange a special puja at Kamakhya Temple through this package?

Ans. Yes. Inform us at least 1 day before your tour date and we will coordinate with the temple priests to arrange special puja or ritual as per your requirements. Additional costs for puja materials and priest fees apply and are paid directly.
Q10. What is the pickup and meet-up process?

Ans. Our representative will be waiting outside the exit gate of Guwahati Airport or Railway Station, holding a placard with your name. Driver and cab details are shared 1 day prior to tour start. Pickups can also be arranged from your hotel or residence in Guwahati.
Q11. Is this tour available for solo travelers?
Ans. Absolutely. Solo traveler packages are available. Pricing differs from twin-share rates — contact us directly for a solo quote. We also run group departure tours that solo travelers can join.
Q12. Can I customize the tour or add more destinations?

Ans. Yes. We offer extended Northeast India packages combining Kamakhya with Kaziranga National Park (one-horned rhinoceros, UNESCO World Heritage Site), Shillong, Cherrapunji, Majuli Island, and Manas National Park. Contact our team for a customized itinerary and pricing.

Kanyakumari, the southernmost tip of India , attracts travelers from all over the world. Why not? It's a place where the world begins to end. Here you see the magical views of the most unique geographical phenomena-the meeting of three water bodies: the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean.

The place gets its name from the virgin goddess Kanyakumari, who is an incarnation of Goddess Parvati and sister of Lord Krishna. Britishers during their rule changed the name Kanyakumari to Cape Comorin, but later it was again renamed by the Indian government to Kanniyakumari.
Why Choose My Quick Trippers for Kanyakumari Sightseeing Tour?

My Quick Trippers offers Kanyakumari travel packages for all budget styles whether you see budget tours, mid-range options or luxury Kanyakumari travel packages. We guarantee you the best deal ever to make awesome memories with your family and friends. blocks.text: Every corner of Kanyakumari is a thing of beauty and joy forever. Its beauty will be etched onto your soul and mind even after you leave its delightful shores. Here are some special highlights of Kanyakumari from our Kanyakumari holiday packages, which are a must-not-miss.

items: The Statue of Saint Thiruvalluvar is a must visit. The grace of sage Thiruvalluvar glows when the first rays of the sun touch the statue. Visiting here in the early morning will give you the chance to capture the best views.

Visit Thanumalayan Temple, as it holds a very significant place for Hindu devotees. You will be amazed to know that it's the only place where the holy trinity-Lord Brahma, Lord Vishnu, and Lord Shiva-are worshipped in a single idol.

Visiting the Triveni Sangam will nourish your mind, body, and soul with positive vibes. It's the only place in India to witness the unique phenomenon of the meeting of three water bodies-the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean.

Get the divine blessings of Goddess Kanyakumari at Kumari Amman Temple. Kanyakumari was named after the virgin goddess Kanyakumari, who is an incarnation of Goddess Parvati. It is also one of the 52 Shakti Peeths of Devi Sati in India.

blocks.text: Once upon a time, there lived a demon called Banasura who got a boon from Lord Brahma that he cannot be killed by any god or demon but only a woman. When he got the boon Lord Shukra intervened and advised him to modify the boon to be more specific. So, Banasura modified the boon- only a virgin girl could kill him.

Taking the advantage of this boon, Banasura felt invincible so he started to destroy the peace of devas and the earth. Devi Kanyakumari was incarnated to kill demon Banasura. She meditated at this southernmost tip which later came to be known as Kanyakumari. Lord Shiva, when he saw Kanyakumari, intended to marry her.

On the day of the wedding Sage Narada intervened by making a rooster crow on the auspicious timing of the wedding to make the wedding auspicious. It was done for a bigger purpose- to make Kanyakumari realize that she has to kill Banasura. She is fulfilling the condition of the boon that only a virgin girl could kill him.

After the disrupted wedding, Kanyakumari felt sad. So, she started destroying everything around and scattered colorful sands which are believed to be the origin of Kanyakumari unique and colorful beach sands. She killed demon Banasura and restored the balance of the universe. Later she revealed herself as Parvati, the divine consort of Lord Shiva.

Kanyakumari is a land of festivals and unique rituals. If you are planning to book Kanyakumari holiday packages, ensure that you are visiting here at peak festive season to get a chance to witness some of the most unique festivals of Kanyakumari.

This festival is celebrated in Kollemcode Temple in Kanyakumari. It is one of the most popular festivals of Kanyakumari. The festival is dedicated to goddess Bhadrakali. In this festival, devotees are suspended in the air by hooks pierced through the skin on their back. They are suspended as an offering to goddess Bhadrakali. This act is significant as it bestows blessings for good health, prosperity and protection from the goddess.

This festival is celebrated in Bhagavathy Temple. The festival starts with a flag hosting ceremony which is witnessed by devotees from all over the region. The main Prasad of the temple is Appam which is made up of rice, Payar and Jaggery.

This festival is celebrated in Suchindram Temple in Kanyakumari. It's a 10-day festival. The festival is dedicated to Lord Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. During this festival the idol is taken in procession on the street. Devotees from all over India witness the cultural expressions (music and religious dance), processions and rituals.

Chaitra Poornima Festival, Cape Festival is a very popular festival celebrated in Kanyakumari. It celebrates the culture and heritage of Kanyakumari by displaying traditional dance, music and folk performances in the backdrop of Kanyakumari sunset.

Kanyakumari, as an integral part of Tamil Nadu Tourism, has seen significant tourist footfall in 2024. Tamil Nadu has welcomed around 286 million tourists in the year 2024, with Kanyakumari being one of the most visited tourist destinations for relaxing holidays. Source: Trade Brains. items: Kumari Amman Temple in Kanyakumari is one of the oldest shrines (approx. 3000 years old) dedicated to the goddess Kanyakumari. Goddess Kanyakumari is an incarnation of Goddess Parvati, or Devi Kumari, who is a symbol of purity and penance.

The temple's Dravidian-style architecture is a sight to behold. The idol of the goddess faces east of the ocean, but the eastern door of the temple is kept closed and opened only for special events. It's a landmark destination in Kanyakumari you must not miss.

It is the only place where you can view both sunrise and sunset over the ocean, which is a great sight to capture for photographers and travelers. In fact, if you are on a honeymoon trip to Kanyakumari, then the views of Kanyakumari Beach would be a perfect backdrop for romantic poses.
You will also witness Sangam on the Beach, as the beach is the official meeting point of three oceans-the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean.

Don't miss Kanyakumari's most popular landmark-the Thiruvalluvar Statue. It stands on a rocky islet next to Vivekananda Rock Memorial. This 133 ft statue is of a legendary Tamil poet and philosopher-Thiruvalluvar.

He is famous for composing Tirukkuṟaḷ, which is considered holy scripture and a guide for many Tamilians. The statue symbolizes 133 chapters of Tirukkural. The 38-foot pedestal represents the chapters on virtue, and a 95-foot figure symbolizes the wealth and love chapters.

Vivekananda Rock Memorial is one of the most famous attractions to explore in Kanyakumari. It was constructed in 1970 in honor of Swami Vivekananda. It is said that he meditated at this spot in 1892 and got some inspiration, which shaped his work in India and the West.
Also behold the sacred Shripada Mandapam as it holds footprints of the goddess Kanyakumari, making it a place of worship for devotees.

blocks.text: FAQs for Best of Karnataka Tour
Q1. What Distinguishes Karnataka From Other States?

Ans. The state is well known for its ancient culture, traditions, and heritage and is one of the oldest places in all of India. Some of the most powerful nations, philosophers, saints, ancient monuments, renowned pilgrimage sites, and innumerable natural wonders have all called it home. It has been a popular destination for travellers of all stripes.
Q2. Which Deity Is Well-Known In Karnataka?

Ans. The majority of the populace of Karnataka worships Shiva (Linga). Along with other well-known temples in Karnataka, the Dharmasthala Manjunatha temple contains an idol of Shiva on its property. It is the main draw of each temple.
Q3. Which Temple In Karnataka Is The Biggest?

Ans. Near Nanjundeshwara Temple lies the Parasurama Temple. Devarajammanni, the queen of the Mysore monarch Krishnaraja Wadiyar III, constructed the nine-story, 120-foot-tall temple Gopuram and its expansive façade.
Q4. Which River In Karnataka Is The Largest?
Ans. The largest river in Karnataka, the Kaveri (or Cauvery), rises in the Coorg district.
Q5. Which Temple In Karnataka Is The Oldest?

Ans. One of the earliest Hindu temples, the Chalukya Shiva Temple (formerly known as Lad Khan Temple), honours Shiva. It is one of a series of monuments at Aihole in the Indian state of Karnataka. It is currently estimated to be from the fifth or sixth century, as opposed to the seventh or eighth.

blocks.text: Himachal Pradesh or the crowning gem of India is filled with explored and unexplored hamlets. From the dry treeless jagged landscape to the thriving rich green-covered rolling hills there is no dearth of places for one to indulge in. Kasauli is one such gorgeous cantonment town on the scenic hills of Solan district. Although established by the British Raj in 1842 it has become a hub of tourism in India. Being well connected and home to several ideal sightseeing options a fun-filled memorable time with your family is guaranteed.

What makes Kasauli a must-visit is the complete absence of loud noises, concrete jungle, and polluted air. It is a much-loved destination among people living in nearby towns looking for an extended weekend getaway or an exciting road trip. Although it graces the lower regions of the Himalayas there is no dearth of scenic beauty and vast open green spaces for you to enjoy or indulge in various fun activities. Kasauli tour packages will prove to be a blessing in disguise and a complete boon for people who feel closely intertwined with nature. items: Kashi Gaya Prayagraj Ayodhya Naimisharanya Trip

blocks.text: Kashi Gaya Prayagraj Ayodhya Naimisharanya tour takes you to places where India’s spiritual heritage and traditions are still alive.

Welcome to Kashi! On arrival at Kashi Airport/ Railway Station, our My Quick Trippers representative will meet you and transfer you to your hotel for check-in and some rest. If you hire a guide, they will travel with the driver and help you during the journey. After checking in, you’ll start exploring the sights of Kashi- Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple - A famous place where devotees come for salvation (moksha) and peace of mind. Darshan at Annapurna Temple - People pray here to the food Goddess for wealth and a life without hunger. Visit to Vishalakshi Temple - A peaceful Shakti Peeth temple, where the eyes of Goddess Sati fell. Baba Kal Bhairav Temple - Popular temple where devotees offer alcohol as Prasad to Kal Bhairav. Evening: Take a boat ride on the Ganges and explore Kashi’s old Ghats, and enjoy the city’s spiritual vibe (optional, extra cost). Later, attend the beautiful Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat , either from the Ghat or on a private boat. Spend a comfortable night at your hotel in Kashi. Note- The Kashi Vishwanath Temple is open from 3 AM to 11 PM Places You’ll See

After breakfast, travel to Bodh Gaya and visit the Mahabodhi Temple , a very peaceful spot and holy site for Buddhists. Later, go to the Mahabodhi Tree , where Lord Buddha meditated. Next, visit Muchalinda Lake , a beautiful spot to take photos, then you will also see the 80-foot Buddha Statue. Next, visit Wat Thai Temple, Japanese Temple, Bhutanese Temple, Metta Buddharam (White Buddha Statue), and Karma Temple, each place with unique architecture. After sightseeing, check into your hotel. Overnight stay at Bodh Gaya. Note- The Mahabodhi Temple is open from 5 AM to 9 PM. Places You’ll See
DAY 3: Bodhgaya - Gaya - Kashi (255-260 km/ 5-5.5 hours)

Early in the morning, after breakfast go to Gaya. On arrival, explore Vishnu Pad Mandir where you can perform Pind Daan, a holy ritual to respect your ancestors (family members who have passed away). Next, visit Phalgu Nadi , a holy river where pilgrims pray and perform rituals. After that, visit Brahmani Ghat and Gayatri Ghat. Then travel to the sacred Sita Kund, and finally see Maa Sarva Mangla Gauri. People believe that visiting this temple brings the blessings of Goddess Gauri, who can remove difficulties and bring luck. Return to Kashi in the evening and enjoy a relaxing overnight stay at your hotel. Places You’ll See

Start your day with a boat ride on the Ganges and see the Ghats like Assi, Manikarnika, and Harishchandra. You can also take a holy dip and optionally visit Kashi Vishwanath Temple. Later, return to the hotel for breakfast. Start your day after breakfast by visiting Kashi’s well-known temples- Sankat Mochan Hanuman (located near Assi River, a great spot for sunset photos), Durga Mandir, Tulsi Manas (where Ramcharitmanas was written), and New Vishwanath Temple. Don’t miss a walk around the BHU campus nearby. In the afternoon, drive to Sarnath, the sacred site where Lord Buddha shared his first teachings. Explore Dhamek Stupa (best photo spot), Chaukhandi Stupa, various Buddhist Temples and the Sarnath Archeological Museum. Return to Kashi and check into your hotel for an overnight stay. Note- Sarnath Archaeological Museum is closed on Fridays. Places You’ll See
DAY 5: Kashi - Vindhyachal - Prayagraj (150 km approx. / 4.5-5 hours)

After breakfast drive to Prayagraj. Enroute visit Vindhyachal Devi for a Darshan at Shaktipeeth. Later visit Sitamarhi , the temple where Mother Sita went into the earth. When you reach Prayagraj, travel to Triveni Sangam, where the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati meet, and take a sacred dip there. Enjoy a peaceful boat ride and experience a holy bath at the Sangam. Next, visit Bade Hanuman Mandir, then go to Akshayavat Temple inside Patalpuri Temple at Prayagraj Fort. It is believed that Lord Ram, Lakshman, and Sita once rested under this holy tree. Visit Prayagraj Fort, also called Allahabad Fort, built by Emperor Akbar in 1583 near the Sangam, and then see the holy Alopi Devi Temple. If time permits, visit Lalita Devi Temple and Shri Nagvasuki Temple. You can also explore Anand Bhavan, home of the Nehru family. On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay at Prayagraj. Places You’ll See

Enjoy breakfast then continue your journey to Ayodhya. Visit Ram Janmabhoomi Temple a sacred place believed to be the birthplace of Lord Ram. Go to Hanuman Garhi Temple located on a beautiful hill, which is perfect for photography. Explore Kanak Bhavan Temple, a beautiful temple with gold plated domes dedicated to Lord Ram and Sita. In evening watch the Saryu River Aarti at Naya Ghat, a truly divine experience. Note - Ram Janmabhoomi Temple is open from 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM. Places You’ll See
DAY 7: Explore Ayodhya’s Culture and Spirituality

Early in the morning you can visit the Saryu River. Take a holy dip in the river or enjoy a peaceful boat ride if you wish (optional). After that, visit Nageshwarnath Temple, which is one of the oldest temple in Ayodhya, dedicated to Lord Shiva. Then see Ram ki Paidi, and later return to Ram Janmabhoomi Temple. Next, visit Dashrath Mahal the palace of Lord Ram’s father, King Dashrath. If time permits, you may explore Valmiki Ramayana Bhawan (famous for Ramayana paintings), Treta Ke Thakur Temple (where King Vikramaditya placed idols of Lord Ram, Goddess Sita, and Lakshman), and also go to Tulsi Udyan. Later, drive to Lucknow. If time allows, enjoy an optional tour of Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza, Residency Complex, Gomati Riverfront, Janeshwar Mishra Park, and Ambedkar Park. On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay in Lucknow. Places You’ll See
DAY 8: Lucknow – Naimisharanya Sightseeing – Lucknow (180-190 km/ 6-7 hours)

After breakfast in the morning, drive to Naimisharanya. Once you reach, visit Chakrateertha first, (the spot where the Lord Brahma's chakra fell) then explore Suth Gaddi, Vyas Gaddi (best photo spot specially in sunrise), and Manu Satrupa Tapsthali. Later, explore other important sites such as Hanuman Garhi, Panch Pandav Kila, Gomati River (a beautiful riverside spot, perfect for evening walk), Vishnu Temple, Dadhichi Kund, and the Lalita Devi Temple (Shaktipeeth temple where Sati’s heart fell). In the evening, drive back to Lucknow. On arrival you will be dropped at the airport/railway station to take your flight/train for your home. This Kashi Gaya Prayagraj Ayodhya Naimisharanya trip plan ends with unforgettable memories. Places You’ll See

These months are the best to enjoy the beautiful landscapes of Kashmir. The weather is extremely pleasant to enjoy Kashmir sightseeing along with different adventure activities. You can enjoy shikara boat rides on Dal Lake, trekking, visiting gardens and lakes, and capture the scenic beauty of the lush green valleys of Kashmir. You can also enjoy the Tulip Festival.

The mornings and evenings will be cooler but the days will be warmer for enjoying sightseeing and adventure activities. If you love to see snowfall and enjoy snow adventure activities then these are the best months to plan Kashmir holidays. During these months, you can enjoy Winter sports such as skiing and snowboarding (Gulmarg and Pahalgam), cozy houseboat stays in Srinagar, and snow sightseeing.

These months are perfect for budget travelers seeking discounts.
Best Places to Explore in Kashmir on Your Trip

Nestled in between the Pir Panjal Mountain range and the Greater Himalayas, Kashmir Valley offers a peaceful respite. In the first half of 2025, Jammu and Kashmir received over 95 lakh domestic tourists which shows Kashmir is one of the top choices for holiday destinations for tourists in India. Source ( Kashmirilife ). Here is a list of some of the best places to visit in Kashmir , covered in our itineraries.

items: Located in Pir Panjal range of Kashmir, Gulmarg is one of the most beautiful places to visit in Kashmir.
It has one of the world's highest cable cars- The Gulmarg Gondola which ascends to around 3,980 meters, offering stunning views of snow-capped Himalayan Mountains.
It is also the best winter destination to visit in India. You can try Skiing, snowboarding, Gondola Ride, Heli Skiing, Snow Trekking, Sledging and Tobogganing, ice skating and snowman building.
Also known as Meadow of Gold, Sonmarg's beauty will melt your heart. It is surrounded by beautiful Himalayan Peaks, turquoise lakes, and lush alpine meadows.
Don't forget to visit the scenic Baltal Valley, it is also the base camp for Amarnath Yatra. Enjoy Camping and the beauty of green meadows.
There are many other places like Nilagrad River, which offers a soothing natural setting perfect for picnics and relaxation. Zoji La Pass, Krishansar and Vishansar Lakes to explore here.
Pahalgam, the valley of Shephards is one of the most beautiful places in the Anantnag district of Kashmir.
Stunning alpine forests, snow-capped mountains, crystal streams and lush green meadows, makes this place worth visiting for a relaxing vacation with family.
There are many breathtaking places to explore in Pahalgam like Betaab Valley, Aru valley, Chandanwari, Baisaran Valley and Sheshnag Lake Etc.

Known for its natural beauty and rich cultural heritage, Srinagar is a must visit place in Kashmir. Here you will enjoy a serene boating experience in traditional Shikaras and visit floating markets which reflects the local way of life.
There are also many heritage places to explore in Srinagar like The Mughal Gardens - Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh, and Chashme Shahi.
You will be mesmerized by the beauty of Dal Lake and Indira Gandhi Tulip Garden which is one of the largest gardens in Asia.
Kargil is one of the best places to visit in Kashmir for its historical significance and stunning natural beauty.
It is located in Dras. Kargil got prominence due to the 1999 Kargil war between Indian and Pakistan. Apart from the military importance, Kargil is culturally very diverse.
You will see a unique blend of Balti Muslim and Buddhist communities. There are also many places to visit here like Wakha village, Suru valley, Kargil war memorial, Phokar hill etc.

It is a quintessential Kashmir experience which is a must not miss.
It is one of the most popular activities to do in Kashmir. The scenic trekking trails in Sonmarg offer the most breathtaking landscapes in Kashmir.
One of the best trekking trails in Sonmarg is Thajiwas Glacier, it's a short trek to view the frozen ice formations and glacial streams.
If you are more adventurous then you can also visit the Kashmir Great Lakes Trek which starts from Sonmarg and passes through alpine lakes like Krishansar and Vishansar.

Don't miss the best snow adventure in Gulmarg. Try snowboarding, Skiing, Gondola Ride, Heli Skiing, Snow Trekking, Sledging and Tobogganing, ice skating and snowman building. The Ski season starts from December and lasts till March.

Gulmarg also hosts winter festivals around December or February where you will get a chance to enjoy Traditional Kashmiri music, folk dances, and witness craft stalls and food stalls which offer authentic Kashmiri dishes like Rogan Josh and Gushtaba.

Devotees from all over India visit Amarnath Cave Temple, Vaishno Devi temple, Kheer Bhawani Temple, Charar-e-Sharief and many more sacred sites.

Nepal tourism is generally growing day by day due to improved infrastructure and rich hospitality. In 2025, there has been a significant rise in the number of tourists in Nepal. Over 577,000 tourists visited Nepal in the first half of 2025, among which most tourists visited Kathmandu ( Rising Nepal Daily ). Here is some essential information about Kathmandu tourism that will help you to plan your trip with family and customize your Kathmandu itinerary.

items: Kathmandu Durbar Square - Also known as Basantapur Durbar Square or Hanuman Dhoka Durbar Square, it is one of the most popular tourist attractions of Kathmandu. Revel in the charm of Newar architecture. It used to be the kingdom of Malla kings and the Shah dynasty.

Swayambhunath - Swayambhunath is Kathmandu's most iconic religious attraction. This beautiful stupa has both Buddhist and Hindu influences. It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Kathmandu. It is also known as the Monkey Temple.

Pashupatinath Temple - Pashupatinath Temple is a sacred site to visit in Kathmandu. It's built in traditional Nepalese pagoda architecture. It is one of the oldest Hindu temples in Nepal dedicated to Lord Shiva. Before becoming a very grand temple in the Licchavi period, it was a basic shrine (Linga). It's also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Boudhanath Stupa - A UNESCO World Heritage site, the Boudhanath Stupa is one of the most beautiful and largest spherical Stupas in the world. Witness its golden spire, which is painted with Buddha's eyes. It is a major pilgrimage center for Tibetan and Nepali Buddhists.

Garden of Dreams - Garden of Dreams is a beautiful neoclassical-style garden located in Kathmandu. It was built in 1920. It used to have six beautiful pavilions in the garden, which represent six seasons of Nepal, though only three pavilions remain today. It has scenic fountains, ponds, and landscaped lawns perfect for leisure walks.

Kopan Monastery - Lama Thubten Yeshe and Lama Zopa Rinpoche established Kopan Monastery in 1969 at the outskirts of Kathmandu on Kopan Hill. If you are interested in doing some courses related to spirituality or capturing the scenic views of the entire Kathmandu Valley, then you must visit this place.

Chandragiri Cable Car - Enjoy the best views of the Himalayan mountain ranges and Kathmandu Valley through the Chandragiri Cable Car ride. It runs from Thankot to the top of Chandragiri hills. At the top of the hill, pay your respects at Bhaleshwor Mahadev Temple, which is dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Ans. The cost of hiring one jeep is INR 3,500 - INR 4,500. The jeep carries 5 to 6 people in one go and the expense is shared by the people. Also, the prices vary slightly from zone to zone.
Q5. Are there tigers in Kaziranga?
Ans. Yes, the Kaziranga Park has tiger. Actually, it has the largest density of tigers in India. However, you might find difficulty in spotting one as the park has dense grasslands.

Group Tour vs Private Tour - Which Kedarnath Package Is Right for You?

From practical experience: solo pilgrims under 45 with flexible schedules do great on group packages. Families with anyone above 60 — always go private. The extra cost is minor. The difference in comfort and pace is significant.
Kedarnath Helicopter Package - Prices and How It Works
Helicopter Yatra is not a luxury — for senior citizens, it is often the safest option. The 16 km trek from Gaurikund is completely bypassed. You land 500 metres from the temple.

IRCTC is the only authorised platform for shuttle tickets. No agent or portal can sell IRCTC shuttle tickets. Booking opens mid-April 2026 for pre-monsoon; mid-June for September–October dates. Slots for Phata and Guptkashi sell out within hours on opening day — have your URN ready before 6 PM.
Fraud warning: Agents on WhatsApp, Instagram, and travel apps 'sell' Kedarnath helicopter tickets every season. Many are fake. Report to cybercrime.gov.in. Only use heliyatra.irctc.co.in.
Kedarnath Yatra Registration - Mandatory QR Pass
Every single pilgrim must register before visiting Kedarnath. No registration = no entry at Sonprayag. Registration is free.

items: Go to registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in — or WhatsApp 'Yatra' to 8394833833
Enter pilgrim details + Aadhaar / Passport number

blocks.text: If you are planning this seriously: book at least 60 days in advance for May–June dates. September–October packages can be booked 30 days out. What happens if you delay? In peak 2025 season, Phata and Guptkashi IRCTC slots sold in 90 minutes. Hotels near the base helipads were fully booked by March. Starting late means paying more and getting less.

Perfect weather for trekking. Snow still visible on peaks. But Sonprayag sees 8,000–10,000 pilgrims daily in this window. Book 60–90 days ahead. Budget at least 90 minutes for Sonprayag queue. Arrive early.

This is where experienced Kedarnath yatris go. Post-monsoon skies are clear, queues are short, Darshan is peaceful. Nights drop to -5°C — carry serious woollens. Helicopter slots are easier to get. First-time visitors: choose this window.
Helicopter suspended. NH-58 landslides close the route regularly. The trek becomes dangerously slippery. No responsible operator recommends this window. Skip it.
Sonprayag is where every pilgrim's real journey begins — and where most itineraries fall apart if not planned correctly.

items: Sonprayag is the last point for private vehicles. From here, a government-authorised shuttle (Mahindra Bolero, ₹50 fixed) covers 5 km to Gaurikund.
In peak May–June, Sonprayag parking fills by 6:30–7 AM. My Quick Trippers drivers know this — our standard departure from base hotels is 3:30–4 AM.
At Gaurikund (1,981 m), take a dip in Gauri Kund hot spring before the trek. Customary, sacred, and practically useful — warm water eases the muscles before the 16 km climb.
Trek milestones: Gaurikund → Jungle Chatti (4 km, toughest) → Bheembali (6 km, rest point) → Rambara (9 km) → Lincholi (13 km, altitude felt here) → Kedarnath (16 km).
Average trek time: 6–8 hours upward. Return: 4–5 hours. Plan minimum 2 days — one to ascend, one for darshan and descent.
Pony: ₹3,000–₹5,000 round trip. Palki: ₹8,000–₹12,000. Helicopter shuttle: IRCTC booking.

blocks.text: What a Real Kedarnath Package Day Looks Like

4:00 AM. Your My Quick Trippers driver is outside the hotel, engine running. You leave Guptkashi while the rest of the town sleeps. The road to Sonprayag is clear at this hour — 35 minutes, no traffic.

5:15 AM. You are at Sonprayag. The parking lot has maybe 20 vehicles. You board the government shuttle to Gaurikund in 8 minutes. Others who arrive at 8 AM will wait 90 minutes for this same shuttle. That is the only difference — departure time.

6:00 AM. Trek begins at Gaurikund. The first 4 km to Jungle Chatti is steep. Your My Quick Trippers guide sets a slow, deliberate pace. No rushing. At Bheembali (6 km), a tea stall. Sit for 10 minutes. Eat something.

By 11:30 AM, you reach Kedarnath. Your VIP Darshan coupon — arranged in advance — takes you to the priority entry. General queue at this time is 3 hours long. You complete Darshan in 40 minutes. The Jyotirlinga up close, the chanting, the high-altitude stillness. That moment is why this Yatra exists.

From practical experience, the single factor that separates a smooth Kedarnath Yatra from a chaotic one is not money — it is departure time from the base hotel. Leave by 4 AM. Everything else follows.

Common Mistakes Pilgrims Make on Kedarnath Tour

items: Skipping Char Dham registration until arrival. Entry denied at Sonprayag without QR e-pass. Takes 5 minutes online — do it 2–3 days before departure, not on the road.
Leaving the base hotel after 7 AM. Sonprayag parking fills by 6:30–7 AM in May–June. Late arrival means 2+ hours wasted before the trek even begins.
Booking helicopter tickets through WhatsApp agents. Every season, pilgrims pay ₹5,000–₹15,000 to agents for IRCTC tickets that either don't exist or are revoked. Use heliyatra.irctc.co.in only.
Not carrying printed documents. Mobile network fails between Sonprayag and Kedarnath. If your phone dies at the checkpoint, a printed Char Dham e-pass and ID copy saves you.
Wearing wrong footwear. Sandals and sneakers on the Kedarnath trek cause ankle injuries on the rocky path, especially on the descent. Trekking shoes or grip-soled boots only.

Rushing at altitude. Pilgrims who push pace above Lincholi (13 km mark) are the ones who end up with AMS symptoms — headache, nausea — and can't complete darshan. Walk slower than you think you need to.

Booking only for themselves, not accounting for delays. If your return train from Haridwar is on Day 4 and your trek Day is Day 3, a single weather delay or landslide destroys the plan. Always keep a buffer day.

blocks.text: Pro Tips for Kedarnath Tour Package

items: Choose Guptkashi as your base for helicopter Yatra — lowest altitude (1,319 m) among all helipads, best hotels, medical facilities, and weather reliability. Worth the ₹6,000 fare difference over Sirsi.
For road Yatra: reach Gaurikund by 6–6:30 AM. This gives you 5–6 hours of trek time before the afternoon cloud buildup and crowd peak at the temple.
September 15 – October 10 is the sweet spot — post-monsoon clarity, 60–70% fewer pilgrims than May, and IRCTC helicopter slots that are actually bookable without a 6 PM alarm.
Carry ₹3,000–₹5,000 in cash. UPI fails above Sonprayag. ATMs at Gaurikund run dry in peak season. Your entire on-ground spending — shuttle, tea stalls, emergency — depends on physical cash.
Book the opening week package (22–30 April) for the Utsav Doli procession. Lord Shiva's palanquin arrives from Ukhimath — a once-a-year spiritual experience most pilgrims don't know about.

Add Tungnath–Chopta to your Kedarnath package. Tungnath (3,680 m) is the world's highest Shiva temple, just 70 km from Kedarnath. The combined 5N/6D package at ₹16,500 gives you two extraordinary shrines in one trip.
Senior citizens: get the medical fitness certificate before departure. Without it, Char Dham registration cannot be completed for 60+ pilgrims. Your doctor signs it — takes 10 minutes.

blocks.text: Kedarnath is the highest Jyotirlinga in India. At 11,755 ft, the air is significantly thinner. Helicopter pilgrims ascend from 1,319 m to 3,583 m in under 15 minutes — zero acclimatisation time.

items: AMS (Acute Mountain Sickness): Headache, nausea, dizziness within 2–4 hours of arrival. Rest and hydrate. Descend if it worsens.
HAPE (High Altitude Pulmonary Edema): Fluid in lungs. Persistent cough, chest tightness, breathlessness at rest. Medical emergency — immediate descent needed.
HACE (High Altitude Cerebral Edema): Brain swelling. Severe headache, disorientation, loss of balance. Requires immediate evacuation.
Walk slowly. Take breaks every 30 minutes above 2,500 m. Never rush.
Heart / BP / COPD conditions: medical fitness certificate mandatory. Declare at registration.
Pregnant women (6+ weeks): not permitted on the high-altitude route.
My Quick Trippers vehicles carry portable oxygen and first aid on all mountain routes.

blocks.text: Key Places to Visit on Your Kedarnath Tour

The holy abode of Lord Kedar (Shiva) is one of the most prominent pilgrimage places for Hindu devotees. In 2026, after the portals of Kedarnath Dham opened on 22 April 2026, it recorded it's highest-ever footfall, of around 1.7 million (17 lakh) pilgrims. Source: ( Headlines India ) Kedarnath not only houses the spiritual abode of Lord Shiva, but it also has a variety of other places, perfect to add to your Kedarnath Tour Packages. Here's the list of best places to visit in and around Kedarnath Temple -

items: Kedarnath Temple (3,583 m): The Jyotirlinga. The entire purpose of the Yatra. The naturally formed pyramidal lingam, the mountain views, the early morning aarti — nothing compares.
Shankaracharya Samadhi : Behind the main temple. Adi Shankaracharya's memorial. 5 minutes of quiet reverence.
Bhairavnath Temple : 100 m from the main shrine. Guardian of Kedarnath. 360-degree peak views.
Gaurikund : Where the trek begins. Hot spring (Gauri Kund), sacred to Goddess Parvati. Dip before the trek.
Triyuginarayan Temple (~25 km from Sirsi): Site of Shiva-Parvati's celestial wedding. Eternal flame burning since that day. Add this if you have time.
Tungnath + Chopta : World's highest Shiva temple at 3,680 m. Ask My Quick Trippers about the combined Kedarnath + Tungnath package.

Reaching Kedarnath Dham by helicopter is the best travel option for those who have limited time but want to get Lord Kedarnath's Darshan fast. There is no direct route to reach Kedarnath. The journey to Kedarnath Temple is challenging. One has to undertake challenging terrains, rugged landscapes to get the divine Darshan of Lord Shiva. Here is a detailed overview on how to reach Kedarnath Temple by Air, Rail and Road.

blocks.text: Kedarnath and the Panch Kedar — The Complete Circuit
Kedarnath is the first of the five Panch Kedar shrines. Each represents a part of Lord Shiva's divine bull form that appeared across the Garhwal Himalayas.

items: 1. Kedarnath (3,583 m) — Hump | 2. Tungnath (3,680 m) — Arms | 3. Rudranath (2,286 m) — Face
4. Madhyamaheshwar (3,497 m) — Stomach | 5. Kalpeshwar (2,134 m) — Hair / Jata

blocks.text: My Quick Trippers offers dedicated Panch Kedar Yatra packages and also the popular Kedarnath + Tungnath + Chopta combination (5N/6D from ₹16,500). Tungnath at 3,680 m is the world's highest Shiva temple — just 70 km from Kedarnath.

After the Kurukshetra war, the Pandavas sought Lord Shiva's forgiveness for the bloodshed. Shiva, unwilling to grant them absolution easily, took the form of a bull and fled to the Himalayas. At Kedarnath, Bhima recognized the bull and grabbed it — but the bull disappeared into the ground, leaving only his hump above the surface.

The hump became the Kedarnath Jyotirlinga. Other parts of the bull are said to have emerged at four other locations — together forming the Panch Kedar . The temple, originally built by the Pandavas and restored by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century, has stood at 3,583 m for over 1,200 years.

blocks.text: Kerala is Nature at its best, a land blessed with ample amount of lush tropical vegetation, mountains, rivers, lakes, waterfalls and golden beaches. This is the perfect mix for the romantically inclined to discover love and let it bloom like the orchids for which the State is so well known. Whether you are going off as a couple on a honeymoon or on your anniversary, My Quick Trippers romantic Kerala tour gives you a lovely experience of being together in the lap of nature. A typical 5 nights 6 days romantic Kerala tour itinerary would go like this:

Welcome to Kochi by our My Quick Trippers tour guide who escorts you to your hotel room where you freshen up. Then, you set out to explore Kochi starting with the Fort followed by the Bolgatty Palace, a trip to the seashore to see how fishermen still use the Chinese style fishing nets, to Mattancherry Palace and the Jewish Synagogue. You will also visit Marine Drive and the Pareekshith Thampuran Museum during the day.

Have a cosy Kerala breakfast together and get ready for the 150 km drive to Munnar, the loveliest hill resort of Kerala. The drive takes you across splendidly breathtaking scenery made up of water bodies, waterfalls, lush green rice fields and a rolling countryside that exudes the warmth of nature and its people. Arrive at Munnar, the queen of Kerala hill resorts, and check into your hotel. From your room, you can see miles of undulating slopes covered by tea plantations. Freshen up and set out to explore the winding lanes of Munnar in the evening. Munnar is at the confluence of three rivers and has colonial overtones as you will find.

Enjoy local steaming hot breakfast and thus fortified set out to explore the beauties of Munnar. During the course of the day, you will visit the Eravikulam National Park, Rajamalai National Park, Kundala Lake, Echo Point and Mattupetty Dam. Starting at Mattupetty you enjoy a morning boat ride that puts you in a nice, romantic mood for the rest of the day. A walk through Eravikulam gives you glimpses of the Nilgiri Thar, an endangered species of goat along with a view of orchids, birds and other fauna. In the afternoon we stop at a tea plantation, watch workers picking leaves that are then processed. Sample tea and buy a pack to remember Munnar. Return to your room and if you are in the mood, visit Chinnakanal waterfalls, a lovely spot or go to Top Station.

Rise early, breakfast on hot Kerala delicacies and board the coach for the 120 km drive to Thekkady and the Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary. Here you check into your hotel, freshen up and set off for Periyar where you go boating on the Lake, one of the best ways to view the innumerable birds, elephants, tigers, leopards and amphibian life. The view is wonderful and acts as a catalyst for romance. This boat trip done we take you to neighboring spice plantations where you can buy choicest spices to take back home.

Bite into delicious steaming hot Kerala style breakfast and get ready to travel to Athirapally, one of the most charming waterfalls in Kerala and a popular picnic spot. The falls are about 80 feet high, surrounded by lush tropical vegetation. Just sit, watch the water cascade and let love bloom inside you. You might want to splash about in the gurgling waters and walk the trails. Later, you return to Athirapally where you enjoy a lovely night in a picturesque resort.

You are treated to a sumptuous breakfast and then check out to go on to Kochi, at a distance of 80 km. This is where the romantic tour of Kerala ends but your journey of love does not. You promise to return to Kerala on a My Quick Trippers Kerala tour very soon. Try it in the monsoon!

blocks.text: Q. Why Is Kerala Ideal For A Honeymoon?
Ans. If you leave the hills to the north, "God's Own Country" Kerala, with its beaches, backwaters, Ayurveda, hills, and natural splendor, is one of the best places to visit in India for a honeymoon.
Q. When Is The Best Time To Visit Kerala For A Honeymoon?

Ans. The months of October to March are considered tourist season, and the months of December 20 to January 15 are considered peak tourist season. As the rains have subsided and the summer heat has passed, October to March is the best time to visit Kerala for a honeymoon.
Q. What Should I Wear On A Kerala Trip?

Ans. Carry dark coloured clothes because you don't want your white or light coloured clothes to get dirty from the rain and slush, especially when visiting tourist attractions in Alleppey. When visiting Kerala during the summer, light cotton or linen clothing is recommended.
Q. What Distinguishes Kerala From Other States?

Ans. Because of its unique geography, Kerala benefits greatly from the south-west monsoon. It has a pleasant climate throughout the year. We might as well leave the extreme weather to other states. It should have been a "must see" destination for ages, with 44 rivers and the mighty Western Ghats.
Q. Which City Is Known As Kerala's Heart?
Ans. Thrissur, Kerala's "cultural capital," is located in the heart of the state and is a hub of festivals and traditions.

You'll love how people take part in these festivals and these happy moments will make you want to visit Kerala again. Don't miss Alleppey's backwaters, Kochi's photo spots, Thrissur's elephant rides, and Thekkady's wildlife.

Best Time to Visit Kerala from Chennai
The best time to visit Kerala is from September to February. The weather is pleasant with less humidity. It's a great time to enjoy the backwaters, beaches, hills, and other beautiful places.
During this time, Kerala celebrates many festivals, and visitors enjoy lots of fun and happiness.

Summer (March to May) - Summer in Kerala is from March to May. It gets quite hot and humid, with temperatures between 32 to 38°C. It's not the best time for outdoor fun, but if you enjoy warm weather you might like it.

Monsoon (June to September) - During this time, Kerala experiences heavy rainfall and temperatures go between 24°C and 30°C. The rain makes the place green but it may cause travel delays. Still, many travelers enjoy the monsoon weather.
Winter (October to February) - From October to February, the weather in Kerala is cool and pleasant, with temperatures from 20 to 24 degrees Celsius and low humidity.
Most Famous Tourist Places in Kerala
There are lots of amazing places to visit in Kerala that every traveler should experience once in their life-

Kumarakom is a peaceful village near the big Vembanad Lake. It is famous for its beautiful backwaters and green surroundings. You can enjoy relaxing boat rides here and see many kinds of birds if you love nature. The calm water and fresh air make it a perfect place to take a break from busy city life.
Time Required to Explore- 2 to 3 days

Munnar is a beautiful hill station in Kerala. It is famous for its tea gardens, lovely valleys, waterfalls and many kinds of animals. Munnar has a rare flower called Neelakurinji that blooms only once every 12 years. During the bloom season, the hills are covered in blue flowers that makes the place truly magical to visitors.
Time Required to Explore- 3 to 4 days

Alleppey is well known for its peaceful canals surrounded by palm trees. These canals are called backwaters. There are many Ayurvedic centers here where visitors can relax and refresh themselves while enjoying the calm surroundings. The Alleppey beach is very popular for its unique beauty and should not be missed.
Time Required to Explore- 3 to 4 days
How Many Kilometers from Chennai- 734 km

Wayanad is a green hill area known for its beautiful forests and cool weather. It is also famous for old caves and waterfalls that are perfect for adventure lovers. Many rare animals, like the shy Malabar civet and Lion-tailed macaque, live here. That's why Wayanad is great for people who love wildlife and photography.
Time Required to Explore- 2 to 3 days
How Many Kilometers from Chennai- 609 km
How to Reach Kerala from Chennai
From Chennai to Kerala travelers have many options like trains, buses and cars. You can choose one that fits your schedule and budget-

By Flight - Many travelers prefer flights to save time. Kerala has four airports and almost all domestic airlines operate daily nonstop flights between Chennai and Kerala. You can fly to Cochin (Kochi), Trivandrum (Thiruvananthapuram), Calicut (Kozhikode) or Kannur airports in Kerala.

By Train - Trains from Chennai to Kerala are comfortable and budget-friendly. Many trains run every day from Chennai to cities in Kerala like Ernakulam and Trivandrum. Journey usually takes around 12 hours.
By Road - There are several options like buses, cabs, or driving your own car. These travel options go directly from Chennai to various cities in Kerala.

Best Places to Visit in Kerala
There are several places to explore on a Kerala trip that make it special:

Cochin, also called Kochi, is a beautiful port city in Kerala. This spot is famous for its blend of cultures — Portuguese, Dutch, British, and Chinese influences are visible in its architecture and food. Tourists can explore Fort Kochi, Mattancherry Palace, the Jewish Synagogue, Chinese fishing nets, Cherai Beach, and more. The peaceful backwaters are ideal for boat rides. Cochin is often called the 'Queen of the Arabian Sea' and is the most common starting point for Kerala tours.

The Valara Waterfalls is located between Neriamangalam and Adimali, on the Munnar–Kochi highway (NH 85). The waterfall cascades from a height of about 1,000 feet and is visible from the highway. While visitors cannot get too close to the falls, the view from the road is impressive — particularly during and after the monsoon when the water flow is strongest. The nearby Cheeyappara Waterfalls (a seven-tiered fall) is also visible from the same stretch of road and worth a stop.

Munnar is situated at around 1,600 metres above sea level in the Western Ghats and is one of Kerala's most visited hill stations . It is famous for its rolling tea plantations, cool weather throughout the year, and fog-covered hills. The Tea Museum explains how tea is processed; Eravikulam National Park (home to the endangered Nilgiri Tahr and the Neelakurinji flower that blooms once every 12 years) is a short drive away. Anamudi Peak — the highest mountain in South India at 2,695 metres — is visible from within the park. Note: trekking to the Anamudi summit is restricted; visitors can explore viewpoints and the 2 km Rajamalai trail within the park's tourism zone.

The Edakkal Caves are among the oldest historically significant sites in Kerala, located in Wayanad district. Inside the caves, there are ancient petroglyphs — carvings and symbols believed to be around 6,000 years old — indicating early human settlements. The caves require a moderate uphill walk of about 1 km from the entrance. The carvings provide a fascinating glimpse into prehistoric life in South India.

Alleppey is Kerala's backwater capital and the most popular destination for houseboat stays . The Alleppey Lighthouse, constructed in 1862, stands 30 metres tall and offers views of the Arabian Sea and surrounding landscape. The broader Alleppey backwater network connects to Kumarakom, Kuttanad, and Vembanad Lake. A night on a houseboat drifting through the backwaters — with rice fields, coconut groves, and village life on either side — is the most iconic Kerala experience for most travellers.

In South Kerala, Varkala is a beach town set against dramatic red laterite cliffs. The Papanasam Beach at Varkala is considered sacred by many Hindu pilgrims, who believe bathing here helps cleanse sins — it draws regular pilgrims to this day. The Janardhana Swami Temple (believed to be around 2,000 years old) sits on the clifftop above. Water sports including surfing are available; the beach is also popular for yoga retreats and Ayurveda centres. Best visited between November and March.

Thekkady is home to Periyar National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary — one of the finest wildlife reserves in South India. Boat rides on the Periyar Lake offer chances to spot elephants, wild boar, Sambar deer, and otters along the lakeshore. The surrounding Spice Hills area grows cardamom, pepper, cinnamon, and cloves — spice plantation tours are a popular add-on. The Kadathanadan Kalari Centre in Thekkady hosts live Kalaripayattu (Kerala's ancient martial art) performances every evening.

Wayanad, in the northeastern corner of Kerala, is a district of forests, tribal communities, and misty plateaus. Key spots include Chembra Peak (the highest peak in Wayanad at 2,100 m, with a heart-shaped lake near the summit), Soochipara Falls , Banasura Sagar Dam (the largest earth dam in India and second largest in Asia), Pookode Lake , and the tribal settlements at Edakkal Caves. Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary shares its border with Nagarhole Tiger Reserve in Karnataka and is part of the broader Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve corridor.

Kovalam, about 16 km from Thiruvananthapuram, is Kerala's best-known beach resort town. It has three beaches — the main Lighthouse Beach (most popular), Hawa Beach, and Samudra Beach. The beach is calm and safe for swimming. Kovalam is also one of Kerala's main centres for Ayurveda treatments — traditional massage, detox, and panchakarma therapies are available at dozens of resorts and clinics. The season runs October to March.

Kumarakom, on the eastern shores of Vembanad Lake, is a bird sanctuary and backwater destination known for its luxury resorts and quieter alternatives to Alleppey. The Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary is a winter destination for migratory birds — Siberian ducks, herons, egrets, and other species arrive November to February (not monsoon season). Houseboat cruises and canoe rides through narrow channels are popular year-round.

items: Kerala has four main airports: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport, Cochin International Airport (largest in Kerala), Calicut (Kozhikode) International Airport, and Kannur International Airport — all connecting to major Indian cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Bengaluru, and Mumbai.

Airlines like IndiGo, Air India, and SpiceJet provide direct flights to Kerala from major cities. (Note: Vistara merged into Air India in November 2024.) Average flying time: 2–4 hours from North India; 1–2 hours from South Indian cities.
Cochin International Airport is the world's first fully solar-powered airport (since 2015) — a useful fact if you are looking for eco-conscious travel touchpoints.
Cochin International Airport is the most convenient arrival point for Munnar, Thekkady, Alleppey, and Kumarakom. Thiruvananthapuram Airport is better for Kovalam and Varkala.

Kerala's main railway junctions are Thiruvananthapuram Central, Ernakulam Junction (Kochi), Thrissur, Kozhikode, and Alappuzha — connected to cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Chennai, and Mumbai.
Key trains: Kerala Express, Netravati Express, and Rajdhani Express connect Kerala to Delhi (~38–42 hours). From Mumbai: approximately 27–36 hours. From Chennai or Bengaluru: 12–15 hours.
Train travel through Kerala's coast and backwaters is scenic — the Konkan Railway route (Mumbai to Kerala) and the coastal route from Chennai are both known for their views.
Book tickets at least 3–4 months in advance for peak season travel (November–February).

You can reach Kerala by private vehicle or public transport from nearby states — Bengaluru (~9 hours to Kochi via NH 544), Coimbatore (~4 hours to Palakkad), Mangaluru (~4 hours to Kozhikode), and Chennai (~12 hours to Kochi).
Travelling through national highways like NH 544 and NH 66 can be scenic, especially as you cross the Western Ghats and descend into Kerala's green landscape.
Long-distance AC sleeper buses from Bengaluru, Chennai, and Coimbatore to Kerala are a cost-effective option.
Kerala is a coastal state with sea access. The Cochin Port (Kochi) handles cruise ship arrivals — several international cruise lines include Kochi on their itineraries.

The Kerala backwaters are connected internally — you can travel between Kollam and Alleppey by the Government Boat (KSRTC water transport) which runs daily, taking about 8 hours through the backwaters.
Visitors can reach Kerala's Lakshadweep islands by ship from Kochi — sailings operate seasonally and require prior booking through Lakshadweep Administration.
Private AC vehicle: Most comfortable for sightseeing — all our Kerala packages include a private car with driver.
Auto-rickshaws: Widely available in cities and towns. Use metered autos in Thiruvananthapuram; negotiate fare elsewhere.
Ferries and boats: Government ferries connect Alleppey, Kumarakom, and Kottayam through backwater routes. Houseboat charters are arranged through operators.
Kerala KSRTC buses: Economical option for longer distances between cities. AC buses run between Thiruvananthapuram, Kochi, Kozhikode, and Thrissur.
Auto apps (Rapido, Ola): Available in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, and Kozhikode.

blocks.text: Tourists can enjoy paragliding in the hills near Varkala, with views of the sea and beaches below. This is a popular adventure activity for those who want to fly over Kerala's coastal landscape. Best experienced during the October–March season when weather conditions are stable.

A houseboat cruise in Alleppey (Alappuzha) is the most iconic Kerala experience. Traditional kettuvallam (riceboat houseboats) have been converted into well-appointed floating hotels — most have 1–3 bedrooms, a kitchen, and a sit-out deck. You drift through the narrow backwater channels, past rice paddies, coconut groves, and small villages, with meals cooked fresh on board. Overnight houseboat stays are the most popular option — book 2–3 months ahead for peak season (November–February).

Wildlife experiences in Kerala are varied. Periyar National Park (Thekkady) is best for boat safaris on the lake — elephants, gaur, and deer come to the lakeshore. Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary borders the Nagarhole Tiger Reserve and is good for jeep safaris. Parambikulam Tiger Reserve (Palakkad district) is one of India's most biodiverse reserves and has guided treks. Kerala is also a good birdwatching destination — Thattekad Bird Sanctuary and Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary draw serious birders.

The Pettimudi area in Rajamala, near Munnar, offers views of tea gardens and the surrounding Rajamala hills. Note: Visitors should check current access status before planning a visit — the Rajamala/Pettimudi area has had restricted access due to safety reasons in recent years. For hilltop views near Munnar, Kolukkumalai (world's highest tea estate) and Meesapulimala ridge are excellent alternatives with clear Himalayan-range-comparable views.

Water sports in Kerala are available at several beach destinations. Kovalam and Varkala are the most popular — offering jet skiing, kayaking, parasailing, and surfing. Alleppey beach has water sports facilities as well. For those who want calmer activities, canoe rides through the backwater channels in Alleppey and Kumarakom are excellent. The Periyar Lake in Thekkady has bamboo rafting.

Kathakali is Kerala's most famous classical art form — an elaborate dance-drama with colourful costumes and face paint depicting stories from the Mahabharata and Ramayana. Kalaripayattu, Kerala's ancient martial art, is another major performance art. Both can be watched at cultural centres in Kochi (Kerala Kathakali Centre near Fort Kochi, Dr. B. Ipe's Kathakali Centre), Thekkady (Kadathanadan Kalari Centre), and Trivandrum. Shows are usually held in the evening — check timings and book ahead.

Kerala is India's primary destination for authentic Ayurveda treatment . Treatments range from a simple 60-minute Abhyanga massage to a full 14–21 day Panchakarma detox program. Kovalam, Varkala, Thiruvananthapuram, and Thrissur have the most established Ayurveda centres. For authentic treatment (not spa-style), look for NABH-certified Ayurveda centres with qualified Ayurvedic doctors. June–August (monsoon) is considered the best time for intensive Ayurveda treatment — the body is believed to be most receptive to therapies during this season.

blocks.text: Kerala cuisine is distinct from the rest of South India — coconut, fish, and rice are the backbone of almost every meal. Here's what visitors should not miss on a Kerala tour :

items: Sadya — the traditional feast served on a banana leaf, with rice, 20+ side dishes including avial, thoran, sambar, and payasam. Essential during Onam and at most traditional restaurants.
Appam with Stew — lacy rice flour crepes served with a mild coconut milk-based vegetable or chicken stew. One of Kerala's most popular breakfast dishes.
Puttu and Kadala Curry — steamed rice cake layered with coconut, served with spiced black chickpea curry. A hearty breakfast found everywhere in Kerala.
Kerala Fish Curry — fish cooked in a clay pot with raw mango, coconut milk, and Malabar spices. Every region of Kerala has its own version.
Karimeen Pollichathu — pearl spot fish wrapped in banana leaf and grilled or shallow-fried. A speciality of the Alleppey backwater region.
Kerala Prawn Curry — prawns in a rich coconut milk and tamarind gravy. Available at coastal towns from Kochi to Trivandrum.
Avial — a mixed vegetable dish cooked in coconut oil and yogurt. A staple of the Kerala Sadya.
Unniyappam — small round rice cakes with jaggery, bananas, and coconut — a popular temple prasad and street snack.

blocks.text: Shopping in Kerala - What to Buy

items: Spices: Cardamom, pepper, cloves, cinnamon, and nutmeg — best bought from Thekkady spice markets or Kumily (better prices than airport shops).
Kasavu Sarees: Kerala's traditional sarees with gold borders — available in Thrissur and Kochi. Good quality from Bhraman Textiles and Co-optex.
Coir Products: Mats, baskets, wall hangings made from coconut fibre — widely available in Alleppey and Trivandrum.
Wooden Handicrafts: Rosewood and teakwood sculptures, carved elephants — best from Kochi's Jew Town antique shops and Trivandrum's SMSM Institute.
Kerala Murals (reproductions): Traditional temple mural art on canvas — available in Thrissur and Guruvayur.
Coconut Shell Products: Bowls, spoons, lamps made from coconut shells — widely available in tourist markets.
Tea: Munnar tea direct from estate shops (cheaper than urban stores). Best bought from the Tea Museum outlet in Munnar.

Honeymoon packages typically include houseboat stays in Alleppey, hill station accommodation in Munnar, beach resorts in Kovalam or Varkala, and candlelight dinners. Typical duration: 5–8 days.
