Ayurveda packages in Kerala range from short 3-day rejuvenation programs to full 21-day Panchakarma detox courses. Kovalam, Varkala, and Thiruvananthapuram are the most established centres. The monsoon season (June–August) is considered ideal for intensive treatment. Prices vary widely — from ₹8,000/day (budget centres) to ₹25,000+/day (certified luxury Ayurvedic resorts).

items: Carry light cotton clothing for the coast and plains; add a light jacket for Munnar and Wayanad (especially November–January nights).
Carry an umbrella or raincoat — rain can come without warning even in the peak season. This is especially true in Munnar and the hills.
Mosquito repellent is essential, particularly for houseboat stays and forest areas (Thekkady, Wayanad).
Dress modestly when visiting temples — cover shoulders and knees. Some temples (like Guruvayur) do not allow non-Hindus inside.
Carry some local currency (INR) for markets, small eateries, and waterfall entry fees — card machines are not reliable everywhere.
Book houseboat stays and Kathakali shows in advance, especially for travel between November and February.
For Ayurveda treatment, choose NABH-certified centres and consult the Ayurvedic doctor on the first day — don't book treatments blindly from a menu.
Respect the environment — Kerala's backwaters and forests are ecologically sensitive. Do not litter; support eco-friendly operators.

What is the best Kerala tour package?

For most first-time visitors, the best Kerala tour package is a 5–6 day itinerary covering Kochi (1 night), Munnar (2 nights), and Alleppey houseboat (1 night). This covers Kerala's three most iconic experiences — colonial history, hill station tea gardens, and backwater cruising — within a practical timeframe. Packages start from ₹15,500 per person. Add Thekkady (wildlife) or Kovalam (beach) for a longer trip.
How much does a Kerala trip cost from major Indian cities?

A 7-day Kerala holiday package including flights costs approximately ₹35,000–₹55,000 per person from Delhi, Mumbai, or Bengaluru (double sharing, all meals, standard hotels). Flights from South Indian cities are cheaper — from Hyderabad or Chennai, the same package runs ₹28,000–₹45,000. Budget travellers can do 5 days starting from ₹20,000 (flight + ground package).
How many days are enough for Kerala?

7–9 days is ideal to cover Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady, and Alleppey with comfortable travel between destinations. A focused 4–5 day trip is enough for 2–3 destinations. If adding Wayanad, Kovalam, or Kumarakom, plan for 9–12 days. Rushing Kerala in under 4 days is possible but leaves little time for the experiences that make the trip worth it — houseboat stays, spice plantation walks, or evening Kathakali shows.
Which month is best for Kerala?

November to February is the best time for most Kerala destinations — beaches, backwaters, wildlife, and hill stations all offer good conditions. October is excellent for post-monsoon greenery and value pricing. August–September is ideal if your main goal is the Onam festival or Nehru Trophy boat race. June–August (monsoon) is good for Ayurveda treatment and waterfall visits but not for beach holidays.

blocks.text: Q1. Which beaches are best in Kerala?

Ans. The most popular beaches in Kerala are Kovalam (well-developed beach resort, safe for swimming), Cherai (near Kochi, famous for Chinese fishing nets nearby), Varkala (clifftop beach with a sacred bathing beach), and Bekal (near a 400-year-old fort in Kasaragod). Marari Beach (near Alleppey) is a quieter alternative popular with nature travellers.
Q2. What are the famous foods in Kerala that travellers should try?

Ans. The popular foods in Kerala are Sadya (a vegetarian feast on a banana leaf with rice and 20+ sides), Avial (a mix of vegetables in coconut gravy), Puttu (a steamed rice cake with coconut), and Karimeen Pollichathu (banana-leaf grilled pearl spot fish). Also try Appam with stew, Kerala fish curry, and Unniyappam for a complete local food experience.
Q3. How many days are enough to fully explore Kerala?

Ans. Around 7 to 9 days are enough to cover the main highlights — Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady, Alleppey, and either Kovalam or Varkala. A 4–5 day trip is enough for a focused tour covering 2–3 destinations. 10+ days allows you to add Wayanad, Kumarakom, and Kasaragod.
Q4. What are the unexplored places in Kerala?

Ans. Some of Kerala's lesser-visited destinations include Munroe Island (backwaters and traditional fishing culture near Kollam), Nelliyampathy (tea plantations and scenic views in Palakkad district), Vagamon (meadows and pine forests between Thekkady and Alleppey), and Beypore (ancient dhow-building port near Kozhikode).
Q5. Which is the best month to visit Kerala?

Ans. October to February is the best time for most tourists — pleasant weather across all regions. March to May is the shoulder season — good deals, fewer crowds, but warmer on the coast. If you want to experience Onam (Kerala's biggest festival) and the Nehru Trophy Boat Race, plan your visit in August–September.
Q6. What are some of the most popular travel destinations in Kerala?

Ans. Alleppey, Kumarakom, Wayanad, Thekkady, and Munnar are the most visited destinations. Kochi (Cochin) is the most common starting point. Kovalam and Varkala are the top beach destinations. Guruvayur, Thrissur, and Trivandrum are important for temple visits.
Q7. Which is the best place for a weekend trip in Kerala?

Ans. Munnar is the most popular weekend destination — it is 4–5 hours from Kochi and Coimbatore. Alleppey (for houseboat) and Varkala (for beach) are also popular weekend getaways from cities in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
Q8. Which is the coldest month in Kerala?

Ans. January is the coldest month in Kerala. On the coast, temperatures range from 22–29°C — comfortable but not bone-chilling. In the hills (Munnar, Wayanad), temperatures can drop to 5–10°C in January nights. December and February are also cool months.
Q9. Which is the most beautiful city in Kerala?

Ans. Munnar is consistently rated Kerala's most scenic destination — its rolling tea gardens, misty peaks, and cool climate set it apart. For a city experience, Kochi (Cochin) has the best combination of history, culture, food, and waterside beauty.
Q10. Which month is the hottest in Kerala?

Ans. April and May are the hottest months in Kerala. Coastal areas can reach 33–37°C during these months. The hills remain cooler (Munnar averages 20–25°C even in summer). The Southwest Monsoon arrives by late May/early June, bringing significant rain and lowering temperatures.
Q11. Is Kerala hot or cold?

Ans. Kerala has a tropical climate — warm and humid throughout the year. Coastal areas like Kochi, Alleppey, and Trivandrum stay between 22–35°C depending on the season. The hill stations (Munnar, Wayanad) are significantly cooler, ranging from 10–25°C. The best overall weather is from October to February when coastal areas are around 25–30°C and the hills are pleasant.
Q12. How can I plan a trip to Kerala?

Ans. The easiest way to plan a Kerala tour is to start with your budget, travel dates, and the type of experience you want — beach, backwater, hills, wildlife, or a mix. Choose a duration (4 days minimum for a short trip, 7–9 days for a comprehensive one). Book flights early (especially for December–January). Contact My Quick Trippers for a customised package based on your group size and preferences — we handle hotels, transport, houseboat bookings, and sightseeing.
Q13. Which is the best month to visit Munnar?

Ans. The best time to visit Munnar is from September to March . October–November is ideal to see waterfalls at full flow and the landscape at its greenest after the monsoon. December–February offers the coolest weather — temperatures can drop below 10°C at night. The Neelakurinji flower (blooms once every 12 years) last bloomed in 2018 — next bloom expected around 2030.
Q14. Is planning a Kerala tour more economical?

Ans. Kerala can be done on a budget (basic guesthouses, KSRTC buses, local eateries) or can be quite expensive (luxury houseboats, hill resorts, Ayurveda centres). Our packages start from ₹14,500 per person for 4 days. Compared to international holidays, Kerala offers excellent value — but it is not necessarily cheaper than North Indian hill stations. Shoulder season (March–May) offers better rates than peak season (November–February).
Q15. What are the must-see cultural experiences in Kerala?

Ans. The top cultural experiences on a Kerala holiday package are: Kathakali dance-drama (Fort Kochi, Thekkady), Kalaripayattu martial art performance (Thekkady, Trivandrum), the Thrissur Pooram festival (May), the Nehru Trophy Vallam Kali boat race (August, Alleppey), and a traditional Kerala Sadya meal on a banana leaf. A visit to a working tea factory in Munnar and a spice plantation tour in Thekkady are also worth adding.

Kanyakumari is a town and municipality in Kanyakumari district in the state of Tamil Nadu, India. It is the southernmost tip of the contiguous Indian subcontinent and the southernmost city in mainland India, and thus it is informally referred to as "The Land's End". Kanyakumari town is about 90 kilometres (56 mi) from Thiruvananthapuram and 20 kilometres (12 mi) south of Nagercoil, the headquarters of Kanyakumari district.

Kanyakumari is renowned for its rich cultural heritage, historical significance, and diverse attractions. From ancient temples and forts to modern amenities and natural beauty, Kanyakumari offers an unforgettable experience for every traveler.

The ideal time to visit Kanyakumari is during the winter months (October to March) when the weather is pleasant and perfect for sightseeing. Monsoon season (July to September) brings lush greenery, while summer (April to June) is suitable for high-altitude areas.

Kanyakumari is well-connected by road, rail, and air. The nearest airport and major railway stations provide convenient access from all major Indian cities. Our tour packages include comfortable AC transport and professional guides.

blocks.text: Khajjiar represents the best of Himalayan biodiversity. Dotted with forests of Deodar and vast expansive meadows, this hill station in Himachal Pradesh is every nature lover’s dream come true. Lined with thick forest cover, rolling green pastures, and refreshing air it is one of the top destinations for family getaways and extended weekend staycation. Over some time, Khajjiar has become the epitome of what real-time natural beauty should look like. It is one place where peace, serenity, and natural beauty come together to create a magical symphony of colors and vibrancy for everyone to enjoy and create memories in.

This place is not just gorgeous but it also has numerous options for you to explore and check out while also having the best time of your life. Some of the best and most famous sightseeing places in Khajjiar include Kalatop Wildlife Sanctuary, the iconic Khajjiar Lake, Dhauladhar range viewpoint, Khajji Nag Temple, Dal Lake, and Panch Pandav trees. You can also go for local shopping sprees and buy souvenirs for your friends, family, or loved ones back home at HP State Handicrafts Centre and Tibetan Handicrafts Centre. As you can see, this hill station is wonderful in every sense as it has something for everyone!

Our specially designed Khajjiar tour packages aim solely at giving you the experience of a lifetime. blocks.text: Day 1: Khatu Shyam Salasar Helicopter tour Itinerary or tour Plan

09:30 am: Departure time from Rohini Heliport At Rohini Airport, you will meet one of our representatives who will welcome you with open arms and assist you with further travel-related requirements. You will board the helicopter, and you will be taken to Khatu Shyam Ji. 10:45 am: Arrive at Khatu Shyam Ji (Freshen-up Break) Once you have arrived at Khatu Shyam Ji, you'll be taken to a nearby hotel where you will relax for some time, and then you will head out for the temple visit. As per the Salasar Balaji Dham helicopter Yatra package, rooms will be allotted on a twin-sharing basis. You can also make a request for separate rooms, subject to availability and by paying extra. 12:15 am: Estimated Departure Time to Salasar Balaji At Khatu Shyam Ji Temple, you will have priority Darshan of the main deity, which is dedicated to Lord Krishna in his Shyam Baba form. As reported by The Print every week, over two lakh pilgrims turn up at Khatu Shyam temple, making it one of the fastest-growing religious hubs in North India. The main attraction of this temple is Khatu Shyam's idol, which is considered to be more than five hundred years old. Devotees visit this temple to offer prayers and have Darshan. The complex of the temple has many other shrines that are dedicated to goddesses and gods. The temple comprises Shyam Kund, a holy pond that heals those who enter it. Devotees take a dip in the pond to seek blessings from the deity and purify themselves. 01:00 PM - Arrival and Darshan at Temple You'll board a helicopter to Salasar Balaji. Salasar Balaji is the only Hanuman temple where Hanuman's idol has a moustache and beard. It is also considered to be a Shakti Sthal (shrine) and Swayambhu (self-created). When you reach Salasar Balaji, you will be taken for priority Darshan. The temple was built in 1754 and is considered a Shakti Sthal. 02:00 PM - Packed Lunch Service and return journey Savor a packed lunch and then board your helicopter for the return journey to Delhi. blocks.text: Himachal Pradesh is the crowning jewel of India which is home to not just some of the most stunning hill escape destinations in the world. Kullu is one such hamlet that is embedded deep inside the green hills and is surrounded by the blissful Himalayan ranges. Mainly famous for its vibrant culture and warm winter clothing this is one of the best places for you to experience sheer, unadulterated bliss. The hill station is placed on the banks of Beas River which supports the thriving biodiversity of flora and fauna. From a lesser-explored remote village to securing a place among one of the top-notch hill resorts, Kullu is every traveler’s dream come true.

Kullu is a wholesome package of fun, adventure, spirituality, and romance. It offers a plethora of options for everyone to indulge in. Being situated at a distance of 500 kms from New Delhi this place also makes for the perfect road trip getaway destination around Delhi with your friends and loved ones. You can go sightseeing to some fantastic places like Rohtang Pass, Beas Kund, Chandratal Lake, and more all year long! No matter what time of the year you choose to book one of our fun and exciting Kullu Tour Packages, you will be creating memories of a lifetime.

Each package is designed and curated with extra care to ensure the safety and comfort of travelers. Guaranteeing a stay to complement your holiday requirements and sightseeing adventures, a tour of Kullu with us will leave a lasting mark on your heart. Displaying deep-cut valleys, gorges, fruit orchards, and thick forests this ‘land of gods’ is all about the good vibes. Other than the obvious and undeniably gorgeous views, this hill getaway is laced with folklore, mythological accounts, and legends that have worked in bestowing it with a great sense of spirituality and respect towards our culture. Alpine pastures as far as your eyes can see accompanied by pollution-free air and unmatched serenity, this place should be explored by you if you already haven’t.

A paradise for trekkers, forest hikers, happy campers, and peace seekers, it has a lot to offer to a curious explorer. Sprinkled with tiny villages all over the cliff sides and blessed with the impeccable natural beauty you can choose to go there with your group of friends or for your honeymoon on the hills with your better half. There are temples, holy shrines, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and so much more than your vacation days will feel like they’re not enough. Packages that you can customize and memories lasting a lifetime what are you still waiting for? Go ahead and book the Kullu tour package of your choice. No matter where you are coming from or who you are traveling with Kullu will leave you fascinated.

blocks.text: Lumbini is considered a pilgrimage for those who follow Buddhism. Lord Buddha was born in Nepal and that makes the land of Nepal holy, and it is a place where one should visit at least once in a lifetime. Apart from being holy and significant, Nepal is a beautiful country and the people there welcome you with open arms. Book your tour package to Lumbini and experience the best of hospitality and guiding, with our experienced tour guides in Nepal.

It is one of the growing tourist destinations and has also been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. There are multiple architectural masterpieces in Lumbini and many different monasteries. Those who are scholars in religious studies also visit Lumbini for research. It is a place with a very rich cultural history. There are places like Maya Devi Temple which is known as the shrine of Lord Buddha’s mother, all these places are something you cannot miss.

One can also include Pokhara or Chitwan in your Lumbini package, both the places are mesmerizing and worth visiting once. Pokhara is a perfect holiday destination with rivers, greenery, and picturesque landscapes, you can do a lot of water activities in Pokhara and enjoy the nightlife. Chitwan is the first national wildlife park in Nepal where you can find many exotic animals.

blocks.text: Rightfully known as the 'Heart of India', Madhya Pradesh is home to majestic tigers, rare birds, and exotic wildlife. And history buffs love the state too, for it has the most regal forts, palaces, ancient cities, and UNESCO World Heritage sites! It also entices spiritual tourists through its ancient temples and Jyotirlingas! There is really a lot to see in Madhya Pradesh - from enjoying wildlife safari to rich cultural tours. Get Madhya Pradesh vacation packages and make the most out of your trip!
Why Choose My Quick Trippers for Madhya Pradesh Tour?

Come discover the heart of India with our customizable Madhya Pradesh travel packages. With My Quick Trippers, you get to visit plenty of locations in less time with our guided tours and pre-planned arrangements. We work hard so that you can enjoy your trip without worries! From meals & accommodation to local transport to sightseeing - we take care of it all! Explore our variety of travel options ranging from Madhya Pradesh culture, nature and history tour to full-fledged Madhya Pradesh family tour deals. You're really spoilt for choice!

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Madhya Pradesh

The best time to visit Madhya Pradesh is during the winter season - October to March , as the weather is mostly cool (8°C to 25°C) and pleasant during this time - ideal for sightseeing, pilgrimage, and spotting wildlife. Moreover, if you come during this period, you can enjoy the live celebrations of festivals like the Khajuraho Dance Festival (February) and the Tansen Music Festival (December).

Another great time for the Madhya Pradesh trip is during the monsoon - July to September. Tourists come here to take in the views of lush green landscapes and hill stations (like Pachmarhi) whose beauty grows exponentially at this time. Also, don't miss out on nature gems like waterfalls (especially Dhuandhar Falls) which are in their full flow then!
Best Places to See on the Madhya Pradesh Tour

Madhya Pradesh is a unique mix of culture, architecture, wildlife, and spirituality. In a nutshell, you won't go back home disappointed, as the heart of India has something for everyone! Here are some of the best tourist places in Madhya Pradesh :
Khajuraho Group of Monuments (UNESCO World Heritage Site)

Khajuraho must be added to your Madhya Pradesh trip packages for it's a stunning collection of 22 temples! Tourists especially admire the exotic erotic art here which is one of its kind in the world. Moreover, it is a vibrant setting for an annual dance festival , cultural performance s, Light and sound show , and much more! It's the perfect place to get to know India's rich heritage and culture.

Close to Katni, Bandhavgarh is another nature park and Tiger Reserve to visit. If you are lucky you might spot a tiger which is likely as the tiger density is quite high here . And Madhya Pradesh is rightly called the 'land of tigers' due to this reason! Also, there are plenty of other animals to look for (Indian Wild Dog, Sloth Bear, Striped Hyena, Sambar Deer, Hanuman Langur, and more!). Many tourists add ju ngle safaris to their Madhya Pradesh tour plan, which are available through both jeep and canter.

Sanchi in Raisen is the go-to place for Buddhists! From attending Buddhist festivals and guided tours to Buddhist monasteries to marvelling at the Ashoka Pillar and exquisite art, Sanchi is simply a hub for Buddhist architecture and culture. Moreover, the place attracts history enthusiasts as well for it's one of the oldest structures in the entire country!

Gwalior is yet another city one must visit on their Madhya Pradesh trip. The seat of power of Scindias was once home to the Rajput Rulers. Immersed deep in history, you'll frequently find here majestic palaces and forts which are truly mindblowing! Gwalior Fort, the tomb of Tansen, Jai Vilas Palace, Scindia Museum, and Man Singh Palace visits give you a glimpse into the royal and glorious past of Madhya Pradesh. If you happen to come here during the Tansen Music Festival (December), you get to enjoy the ethereal classical music.

Orchha is a picturesque town situated on the banks of the Betwa. The Fort and palace here are just astounding! Boating on the river is something you'll find tourists actively engaging in. Also, do add Jahangir Mahal, Ram Raja Temple, Orchha Fort, and Chaturbhuj Temple to your Madhya Pradesh holiday packages.

Welcome to the city of temples! Ujjain is a stronghold of Lord Shiva and most of the temples here are dedicated to him! It also houses the Mahakaleshwar temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas . In addition, Ujjain is the place where the Kumbh Mela takes place, and no wonder it's one of the seven sacred cities for Hindus! You'll see people enjoying evening Aarti at the Ghats, Darshan at Kal Bhairav Temple, and soaking in serenity at Ram Ghat! Book our Madhya Pradesh Jyotirlinga tour and enjoy a spiritual trip to this holy city!

This is the capital city and you'll find here an amazing combination of modernity and historical charm. Bhopal also gives a glimpse into Muslim culture which is evident in the Taj-ul-Masajid, Moti Masjid, Jama Masjid, and Shaukat Mahal. Explore museums, go boating, and savour that delicious Mughlai cuisine - you're in for a treat in Bhopal.
Top Things to Do on the Madhya Pradesh Trip

Madhya Pradesh has a lot in store for you once you step on its soil. From nature lovers and adventure seekers to spiritual tourists and history buffs, there's something for everyone here! To make the most out of your experience, make sure to add the following activities to your Madhya Pradesh holiday packages:

rows: Here, you can see beautifully carved gateways that will transport you right back to ancient times. Moreover, it's the perfect place where you can learn about Emperor Ashoka's contribution to Buddhism.

Come and marvel at the architectural brilliance of the intricately carved temples and erotic sculptures here. Witness the bygone era's glory depicted through carved scenes of love, life, and spirituality. It's one of the most popular Madhya Pradesh tourist spot.
End your heritage tour by witnessing prehistoric cave paintings that are over 30,000 years old! Get up and close with marvels of the Stone Age, witnessing some very early-stage human creativity.

This is one of the best Madhya Pradesh wildlife sanctuaries. Hop on jeeps and go for an adventure-filled safari - spotting Bengal tigers, swamp deer (barasinghas), and a variety of bird species. One fun fact about this park is that it served as the inspiration for Rudyard Kipling's The Jungle Book !
This is a must-visit on your Madhya Pradesh wildlife & heritage tours if you are a wildlife enthusiast as this park has a very high density of tigers. So spotting one isn't too hard here!
Explore this lush forest for its variety of fauna and witness leopards, wild boars, and bison up close.
One among the 12 Jyotirlingas, this temple hosts a grand Aarti which is a must-watch.
Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga Temple is another Jyotirlinga and therefore warrants a visit! Moreover, tourists also enjoy a serene boat ride on the Narmada around here.
You have to visit the location which is known as "Teerthraj"! You can explore various locations here, like Narmada Kund, an ancient temple, and even the origins of the holy river Narmada herself!
Whether it's the mighty Gwalior Fort, the fancy Sas-Bahu Temples, or the classic Jai Vilas Palace Museum, every spot here is immersed deep in royal heritage.

Steeped in Mughal and Rajput architecture, Orchha was once a stronghold of Rajput kings. You haven't seen Madhya Pradesh until you have seen the gems like Orchha Fort complex, Chaturbhuj Temple, and Cenotaphs!

Come watch Mandu for its romantic ruins and architectural spectacle! Get enchanted by Rani Roopmati Pavilion, bowled over by Jahaz Mahal, or just be proud to be on the same land as Baz Bahadur's Palace, the choice is yours!

Ans. Planning for Madhya Pradesh gets easier once you decide your preferences, time to spend on destinations, and the best season. Here's a quick guide:

items: Determine which locations you want to travel to, whether historic, wildlife hotspots, adventurous spots, places with cultural importance, or a mix of them all!
Decide the time you want to visit here. Typically, tourists come here during the winter months as the weather is nice and sightseeing is pleasant.
Pick a duration for your trip. Most tourists cover all major attractions within 3-7 days.

Book accommodation in advance to avoid hassles.
Set a budget - low-cost options to luxury travel!

blocks.text: Q2: How many days are required for the Madhya Pradesh trip?
Ans. Usually, 7-10 days are sufficient to cover key attractions of the state such as Bhopal, Sanchi, Pachmarhi, Khajuraho, Bandhavgarh, and Ujjain.
Q3: What should I pack for the Madhya Pradesh tour?

Ans. If you're visiting in winter, pack cotton clothes for summer. Having comfortable walking shoes is a must as they come in handy during safaris and heritage site exploration. Also, add sunscreens, hats, and insect repellent.
Q4: When is the best time for a wildlife safari on Madhya Pradesh trip?

Ans. The best safari time is from October to March. However, April to June is when the tigers become highly frequent. So plan your travel as per your preferences and what you want most out of this trip.
Q5: What are some hidden gems in Madhya Pradesh?

items: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters (popular for prehistoric rock art)
Tamia: (a nice scenic, secluded hill station)
Chitrakoot (a historical town closely linked to Ramayana)

blocks.text: Q6. What are the best tourist places in Madhya Pradesh?

Ans. If you're a tourist to Madhya Pradesh, make sure you add the following to your itinerary to make the most out of your trip: Khajuraho, Ujjain, Bhopal, Indore, Gwalior, Pachmarhi, Kanha National Park, Bandhavgarh National Park, and Sanchi.
Q7. What is included in the Madhya Pradesh tour package?
Ans. With our MP tour packages, you get accommodation, meals, local transfers, and sightseeing.
Q8. Can the Madhya Pradesh tour package be customised?
Ans. Yes, our packages are fully customizable. You can change the trip duration, add sightseeing stopovers, and pick the vehicle of your choice.
Q9. Is Madhya Pradesh safe for tourists?
Ans. Yes, Madhya Pradesh is quite safe for travellers. However, tourists must exercise precaution. Be wary of pickpockets, especially in the crowded markets. Also, avoid going out late at night.
Q10. What kind of accommodation is available in Madhya Pradesh?

Ans. The state of Madhya Pradesh offers a range of hotels, ranging from budget hotels to luxury resorts. You can also get heritage hotels and guesthouses here. If you're near national parks, you can also stay in jungle lodges
Q11. How much does a Madhya Pradesh tour package cost?
Ans. Our MP tour packages start from INR 6,500 and go up to INR 34,500. These plans vary in sightseeing inclusions, duration, and budget. Pick what suits you best.
Q12. What local foods should I try in Madhya Pradesh?
Ans. While in MP, don't miss finger-licking good Poha-Jalebi, Dal Bafla, Bhutte ka Kees, and Kebabs. Street food is equally good, with options like Indore's famous Sarafa Bazaar.
Q13. What are some of the best hill stations in Madhya Pradesh?

Ans. You can visit Pachmarhi, which is quite a popular hill station in the entire state. There are also other options like Tamia and Amarkantak, which are famous for their scenic and peaceful environments.
Q14. Is Madhya Pradesh a good destination for a honeymoon?
Ans. Yes, MP is quite a nice place for going on a honeymoon. You can indulge in romantic stays at heritage hotels, enjoy the Pachmarhi hill station, and stay in luxe wildlife resorts.
Q15. What adventure activities can I try in Madhya Pradesh?
Ans. You can go for a wildlife safari in national parks. There is a good opportunity for trekking in Pachmarhi. You can also try boating and camping in Bhedaghat and Satpura respectively.

blocks.text: The Madurai Rameshwaram tour is one of Tamil Nadu's most rewarding pilgrimage and sightseeing circuits. Four days. Two cities. And more sacred sites, living legends, and coastal beauty than most people expect.

The journey starts in Madurai — home to the Meenakshi Amman Temple, one of India's grandest Dravidian temples with over 33,000 sculpted figures. From there you travel to Rameshwaram, the sacred island city where the Ramanathaswamy Temple — one of the 12 Jyotirlingas — stands at the edge of the sea. This is where Lord Rama himself is believed to have worshipped Lord Shiva before crossing to Lanka.

Apart from temple Darshan, you'll explore the iconic Pamban Bridge with its spectacular sea views, the haunting ruins of Dhanushkodi, and the birthplace of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam. Thousands of pilgrims and families have trusted My Quick Trippers for a smooth, guided experience here — and we make sure you don't miss a single important stop.

blocks.text: Madurai is one of India's oldest continuously inhabited cities, with a history stretching back over 2,500 years. It is the cultural capital of Tamil Nadu and the second largest city in the state. The city revolves around the Meenakshi Amman Temple at its literal centre — the city's streets were laid out in concentric squares around the temple.

For pilgrims, Madurai offers the Meenakshi Amman Temple, the Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple (one of Murugan's six sacred abodes), and the Koodal Azhagar Temple (one of the 108 Divya Desams). For those interested in history, the Thirumalai Nayakkar Palace and the Gandhi Museum add depth. And Madurai's food — particularly the Jigarthanda cold drink and the famous mutton biryani — is a destination in itself.

Rameshwaram is situated on Pamban Island in the Gulf of Mannar, connected to mainland Tamil Nadu by the Pamban Bridge. It is one of the holiest sites in Hinduism — a place where Lord Rama is believed to have worshipped Lord Shiva before crossing the sea to Lanka to rescue Goddess Sita.

The Ramanathaswamy Temple here is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas and part of the all-India Char Dham pilgrimage (the four dhams being Badrinath in the north, Dwarka in the west, Puri in the east, and Rameshwaram in the south). The temple's corridor is 1,212 metres long — the longest temple corridor in the world. The Theertham Snanam ritual, involving 22 sacred wells inside the temple, is unique to Rameshwaram and forms the spiritual centrepiece of the visit.

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Madurai & Rameshwaram
October to March is the ideal window — weather is pleasant (22°C–32°C), perfect for temple visits, outdoor sightseeing, and the sea bath at Agni Theertham. This is the peak pilgrimage season.

rows: Pleasant weather, 22°C–32°C. Clear skies. Ideal for all sightseeing and temple visits. Peak season.
Post-monsoon freshness, fewer crowds. Occasional showers. Manageable for temple tours.
Temperature 35°C–42°C. Early morning visits (before 9 AM) are essential. Avoid midday travel.
Dhanushkodi beach access can be restricted. Pamban Bridge occasionally closed during high sea warnings.

blocks.text: Note: For Sphatik Linga Darshan, arrive in Rameshwaram by Day 1 evening to be at the temple by 4:30 AM on Day 2. This is the most spiritually significant experience on the tour — plan your travel timing accordingly.

Madurai Airport (IATA: IXM) operates regular flights from Chennai, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Delhi, and Coimbatore. Most metro connections take 1.5–2 hours. The airport is 10 km from city centre — our driver will pick you up directly from the arrival gate.

Madurai Junction (Station Code: MDU) is a major railhead on the Southern Railway network. Excellent connections from Chennai (Vaigai Express, Pandian Express — 8–9 hrs), Bengaluru, Coimbatore, Trichy, and other major cities. This is the most convenient and budget-friendly option for most travellers.

Madurai is on NH-44 (the North-South corridor). Regular bus services from Chennai (460 km, 7–8 hrs), Coimbatore (220 km, 3.5 hrs), Trichy (140 km, 2.5 hrs), and Kanyakumari (244 km, 4 hrs). State government SETC buses and multiple private operators run overnight routes from Chennai and Bengaluru.

items: Dress code: Strict at both Meenakshi Amman and Ramanathaswamy temples. Men: dhoti or full-length trousers (no shorts). Women: saree or salwar-kameez (no sleeveless, shoulders and knees covered). Dress codes are enforced at the entrance.
Theertham Snanam: Carry a change of clothes in your day bag — you get completely wet from bucket-poured water. It is not a light sprinkling. Allow 1.5–2 hours for all 22 wells.
Sphatik Linga Darshan: Happens only at 5:00 AM. Arriving in Rameshwaram on Day 1 evening is the only way to experience this. Do not skip it.
Photography: Restricted inside Ramanathaswamy Temple and Meenakshi Amman Temple. Camera fees apply at select spots. Check at the entrance before shooting.

Dhanushkodi access: Private vehicles are not allowed beyond the Dhanushkodi checkpost. The last 18 km to the island tip is sand — only beach jeeps (local, approx. ₹50–₹150 per person) cover this section.
Cash: Carry ₹2,000–₹3,000 in cash. Temple hundi, beach jeeps, and local prasad shops are cash-only. ATMs in Rameshwaram work but can run short during peak pilgrim season.
Early mornings: Ramanathaswamy Temple opens at 4:00 AM. Early darshan (4–7 AM) means shorter queues and a more peaceful experience. Afternoon queues can stretch to 2–3 hours during peak season.
Senior citizens: Wheelchairs are available inside both Meenakshi Amman and Ramanathaswamy temples. Inform us at booking if special assistance is needed.

blocks.text: Ready to Plan Your Madurai Rameshwaram Tour?

Madurai and Rameshwaram together cover some of the most spiritually significant and architecturally extraordinary sites in all of India — the 33,000 sculptures of Meenakshi Amman, the 1,212-metre corridor of Ramanathaswamy, the pre-dawn Sphatik Linga darshan, and the eerie beauty of Dhanushkodi at the edge of two seas.

blocks.text: Q1. How many days are enough for Madurai and Rameshwaram?

Ans. Four days are enough to visit all major temples, sightseeing spots, beaches, and nearby attractions in both Madurai and Rameshwaram while still having time to relax. If you plan to add Kanyakumari, allow 6 days total.
Q2. Can this Madurai Rameshwaram tour package be customised?

Ans. Yes. The itinerary, number of days, hotel category, and activities can all be customised. Common additions include Kanyakumari (2 extra days), Kodaikanal (1–2 extra days), or Thanjavur Brihadeeswarar Temple (1 day). Contact us on WhatsApp to plan your specific tour.
Q3. What is the best time to visit Madurai?

Ans. October to March is the best time — weather is pleasant (22°C–32°C), ideal for sightseeing and temple visits. Summers (April–June) are hot but manageable if you plan early morning visits. Avoid the peak monsoon months for outdoor sightseeing.
Q4. What are the accommodation options in Rameshwaram?

Ans. Rameshwaram has a full range of options — budget guesthouses, mid-range hotels, beach resorts, and premium properties like the Daiwik Hotels and Hyatt Place. Our package covers standard, deluxe, and luxury categories, with 2 nights in Rameshwaram included.
Q5. How do I reach Rameshwaram from major cities?

Ans. The Rameswaram Express is one of the fastest train options and connects Chennai directly to Rameshwaram (approx. 10–12 hrs). From Madurai, it is 173 km by road (3–4 hrs). Our package includes all ground transport from Madurai Airport or Railway Station — no separate Rameshwaram travel booking needed.
Q6. Is Rameshwaram part of the Char Dham Yatra?

Ans. Yes — Rameshwaram is one of the four Char Dhams of India: Badrinath (north), Dwarka (west), Puri (east), and Rameshwaram (south). This is distinct from the Chota Char Dham of Uttarakhand (Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath). Rameshwaram is also one of the 12 Jyotirlinga shrines of India.
Q7. What is Sphatik Linga Darshan in Rameshwaram?

Ans. Sphatik Linga (also called Mani Darshan) is a naturally formed crystal Shivlinga inside Ramanathaswamy Temple. It is believed to have been installed by Goddess Sita herself and is not man-made. The darshan is available only at 5:00 AM before general temple hours. Our 2-night Rameshwaram stay ensures you can attend this.
Q8. What is Theertham Snanam at Ramanathaswamy Temple?

Ans. Theertham Snanam is the ritual of bathing in water drawn from all 22 sacred wells inside the temple corridors. Each well has a different name and is believed to have unique purifying properties. Temple priests pour water in sequence over pilgrims. The ritual takes about 1.5–2 hours. Carry a change of clothes — you will be fully drenched.
Q9. Is photography allowed inside Meenakshi Amman and Ramanathaswamy temples?

Ans. Photography is restricted inside both temples. Camera fees apply at permitted spots. Phones and cameras must be left at the token counter at Ramanathaswamy Temple. Check with the entrance staff on the day of visit for current rules — these are occasionally updated.
Q10. What should I eat in Madurai and Rameshwaram?

Ans. Madurai is famous for its Jigarthanda (a cold drink made with milk, almond gum, and ice cream — the original version is sold on West Masi Street near Meenakshi Temple), Madurai mutton biryani, and parotta-salna. Rameshwaram is predominantly vegetarian near the temple area — fresh seafood is available at local restaurants away from the temple zone. All hotels in our package serve South Indian breakfast.
Q11. What documents do I need for this tour?

Ans. No special permits are required for Madurai or Rameshwaram. Carry a valid government photo ID (Aadhaar, passport, or driving licence) for hotel check-in. For senior citizens or anyone with health conditions, carry your prescription and a brief medical history card.
Q12. What is the cancellation policy?

Ans. Free cancellations and amendments are available up to 7 days after booking confirmation. No compensation for disruptions caused by weather, natural events, or temple closures. Full terms shared at booking.

blocks.text: The Golden Triangle trip takes you on an exciting journey to the three famous cities in India such as Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur.

items: Route: Delhi → Sightseeing in Delhi → Delhi to Agra → Jaipur to Agra → Jaipur sightseeing → Jaipur - Delhi

blocks.text: When you land at New Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport, a representative will greet you and assist you in making your way to the designated hotel. You’ll spend the night at the hotel.

After breakfast, begin your full-day sightseeing tours of New Delhi and Old Delhi. On a tour of Old Delhi, there will be stops at Raj Ghat, Jama Masjid, and Red Fort are all included. From Jama Masjid to Chandni Chowk, take a cycle rickshaw and take in the scenery. A New Delhi sightseeing tour includes stops at the spectacular India Gate, Parliament House, President House, Humayun’s Tomb, Qutab Minar, and a drive down Rajpath. You’ll eat and spend the night at the hotel. (The monuments in Delhi are closed on Monday) Places You’ll See
Day 3: Delhi to Agra (221 kms, Approx. 5 hrs drive)

After breakfast, travel to Agra, stopping en route to view Sikandra, the tomb of renowned Mughal emperor Akbar. Upon your arrival in Agra, the city home to the Taj Mahal, a representative from our business will assist you in travelling to the desired hotel. Visit the Taj Mahal and the majestic Agra Fort, two well-known love monuments. The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan as a memorial to his devoted wife Mumtaz Mahal. The breathtaking memorial to love is crafted from white marble and has inlay work. In 1565, Mughal emperor Akbar built Agra Fort. Visit Itmad-ud-Daula Tomb, also known as the Baby Taj Mahal by Daulah. Stay the night and eat breakfast in your hotel.
Day 4: Jaipur to Agra (238 kms, Approx. 5-6 hrs drive)

After breakfast, take a drive to Jaipur, also referred to as the Pink City and the capital of Rajasthan. The Mughal emperor Akbar erected Fatehpur Sikri in the late 16th century but abandoned it because of a lack of water. You will stop at this location along the way. You will also see Buland Darwaza, the largest entryway in the world. Continue your journey to Jaipur, the “Pink City,” our representative will assist you in getting to the hotel once you arrive in Jaipur. You’ll eat and spend the night at the hotel. Places You’ll See

After breakfast at the hotel, go out for the hilltop Amber Fort. travel to the fort on an elephant. Later, take in the city of Jaipur’s sights include City Palace, Hawa Mahal, and Jantar Mantar. Enjoy shopping at the thriving neighborhood bazaars throughout the city as well. You’ll eat and spend the night at the hotel. Places You’ll See
Day 6: Jaipur - Delhi (Departure) (261 Kms, 5-6 Hours Drive)
Drive back to Delhi after having breakfast. We will drop you off at the airport or station with happy memories.

blocks.text: Thinking how to visit all five holy temples in a single journey? This 5 Jyotirlinga tour package of Maharashtra makes it simple and convenient.

items: Route: Mumbai - Bhimashankar - Ahmednagar → Ahmednagar - Shani Shinganapur - Parli Vaijnath - Parbhani → Parbhani - Aundha Nagnath - Aurangabad → Aurangabad - Grishneshwar - Ellora - Shirdi → Shirdi - Nasik - Trimbakeshwar - Mumbai

blocks.text: Day 1: Mumbai - Bhimashankar - Ahmednagar (361- 375 km/8 -10 hours)

Start your Maharashtra Jyotirlinga tour after our driver picks you up from your selected location in Mumbai, whether it’s the airport or railway station. Our driver will take you, and then you will continue the tour. If you include a guide, they will come with the driver to help you all day. After pick-up, you will start your tour and visit- Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga Temple- This temple is not only important, but the surroundings are also very stunning, so keep your camera ready. After completing the temple visit, you will drive to Ahmednagar . On arrival, check into the hotel. Stay overnight at Ahmednagar. Note- The Bhimashankar Temple is open for morning Darshan from 4:30 AM to 3:15 PM and for evening Darshan from 4:00 PM to 9:30 PM Places You’ll See
Day 2: Ahmednagar - Shani Shinganapur - Parli Vaijnath - Parbhani (324 km/6-7 hours)

After breakfast, drive to Shani Shingnapur , a well-known temple of Lord Shani. In this village, houses have no doors, and crime is nearly zero because villagers believe Lord Shani keeps them safe. Take blessings here before going on to Parli Vaijnath Temple . Next visit Parli Vaijnath Temple . According to belief, Ravana of Lanka dropped the Shiva idol at this spot. Since then, Parli Vaijnath has been a very special place. Enjoy Pooja and Darshan, then continue your drive to Parbhani . Check in at the hotel and stay overnight. Places You’ll See
Day 3: Parbhani - Aundha Nagnath - Aurangabad (280 - 300 km/ 6-7 hours)

After breakfast, travel to Aundha Nagnath , the Jyotirlinga Temple, for blessings. People believe Dharmraj, the eldest Pandava, built this temple during his 14-year exile (Vanvaas). After the visit, drive to Aurangabad . Once you arrive, check into the hotel. If time allows, explore Bibi Ka Maqbara in the evening, known for its gardens and photo spots. Overnight stay at the hotel. Note- Photography may be restricted inside Aundha Nagnath Temple, so check local rules before taking pictures. Places You’ll See
Day 4: Aurangabad - Grishneshwar - Ellora - Shirdi (150-165 km/3.5-4.5 hours)

Morning after breakfast, proceed to visit the sacred Grishneshwar Temple (Jyotirlinga) for Darshan. Later, explore the famous Ellora Caves (old rock caves with Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain designs) and then visit the Bhadra Maruti Temple (only temple where Lord Hanuman is seen in a sleeping posture). After sightseeing, drive to Shirdi . On arrival, check into the hotel. In the evening, visit the Shirdi Temple for Darshan. Overnight stay at the hotel. Note- Grishneshwar Temple is open from 5:00-5:30 AM to 9:30 PM, Mangal Aarti is 4:00-5:30 AM, Evening Aarti at 7:30 PM; Ellora Caves are closed on Tuesdays. Places You’ll See
Day 5: Shirdi - Nasik - Trimbakeshwar - Mumbai (290-350 km/7-8 hours)

Morning drive to Nashik to visit Panchvati and Ramkund (holy tank where Lord Rama is believed to have bathed). Later visit Trimbakeshwar Temple (Jyotirlinga). After darshan and Pooja, proceed to Mumbai . The 5 Jyotirlinga in Maharashtra tour package ends here, with wonderful memories of this spiritual journey. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: This 3 Jyotirlinga Tour of Maharashtra is designed for pilgrims who want to visit three of Lord Shiva's most revered sacred shrines in a single, well-organised journey. You will be visiting Trimbakeshwar (Nashik), Grishneshwar (Aurangabad), and Bhimashankar (Sahyadri hills) — three of the twelve Jyotirlingas of India, all located within Maharashtra. Each shrine offers its own distinct spiritual significance, architecture, and setting.

items: Route: Arrival in Mumbai Trimbakeshwar Panchavati - Shirdi → Shirdi Grishneshwar - Ellora Shani Shingnapur Ahmednagar → Ahmednagar Bhimashankar Mumbai

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrival in Mumbai (180 km/4 hrs) Trimbakeshwar (30 km/30 min) Panchavati - Shirdi (100 km/2 hrs)

Welcome to Mumbai, the city of dreams! On your arrival at airport/railway station, our team representative will give you a warm welcome! From here onwards, you’ll be taken to your very first Jyotirlinga of Maharashtra , that is, Trimbakeshwar Temple . Perform Darshan and Poojan to your heart’s content. Now, you’ll be transferred to Nashik, where you can indulge in some sightseeing at: Panchvati Ramkund In the evening, you’ll be taken to Shirdi where you’ll check into your hotel. Enjoy an overnight stay there. Note: The Darshan timing of the Trimbakeshwar Temple are from 5:30 am - 09:00 pm, while the Rudrabhishek timing are from 07:00 am - 08:30 am. Places You’ll See
Day 2: Shirdi (100 km/2 hrs) Grishneshwar - Ellora (110 km/3 hrs) Shani Shingnapur (50 km/1 hrs) Ahmednagar

Get up early in the morning and proceed for the Darshan of Sai Baba . Thereafter, you’ll be taken for a trip to yet another Jyotirlinga – Grishneshwar Temple ! After your Darshan, it’s time for a cultural visit to Ellora Caves . The last spot on today’s sightseeing is Shani Shingnapur , a village dedicated to Lord Shani! Finally, you’ll be driven to Ahmednagar for overnight stay. Note: Ellora Caves are closed on Tuesdays. Note: The Darshan timings for the Grishneshwar Temple are from 5:30 am - 09:30 pm. The Mangal Aarti begins at 04:00 am and timing of the Evening Aarti is from 07:30 pm. Places You’ll See
Day 3: Ahmednagar (180 km/4 hrs) Bhimashankar (100 km/2 hrs) Mumbai

Start your day early and have breakfast. Now, proceed towards the final Jyotirlinga of this tour leg, that is Bhimashankar Temple . Perform your Poojan and Darshan, and in turn, seek blessings from the Lord. Afterwards, you’ll be taken back to Mumbai. Our representative will drop you off at the airport or railway station, as per your wish. Your tour here concludes with us. Hope you had nice trip filled with happy memories! Note: The Darshan timings at the Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga are: Morning 04:30 am - 03:15 pm, Evening 04:00 pm - 09:30 pm. Note: The temple hosts Mangal Aarti at 04:00 am, and the evening Aarti at 07:30 pm. Note: If you visit here in the Sawan months, then be aware of the fact that there could be heavy traffic or route diversion, owing to the large pilgrim traffic from Kanwar Yatra. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Best Places to Explore in Maharashtra on Your Trip

If you want to experience a vibrant urban energy, you must visit Maharashtra once in a lifetime. In 2024, Maharashtra welcomed over 3.7 million tourists, the highest among Indian states ( Times of India ). It is one of the most visited travel destinations in India. Here are some of the most popular places to explore in Maharashtra, covered in our travel itineraries-

items: The charm of Mumbai is unbeatable. Known as City of Dreams, Mumbai comes first in the list of top travel destinations in Maharashtra. It is a perfect place for family holidays, romantic getaway, spiritual and adventure trips.

Explore some of the best places like Gateway of India, Marine Drive, Elephanta Caves, markets like Chor bazar, Colaba Causeway. Don't forget to visit Bollywood studios and film sets, these places will amaze your curious mind.

Known as the "City of Gates" Aurangabad stands still with pride by keeping Mughal and medieval history remnants intact. You must have heard about Ajanta Ellora Caves, Bibi Ka Maqbara, Daulatabad Fort and Grishneshwar Temple. These places are the crowning jewels of Aurangabad Tourism.

It is also one of the best places to enjoy a honeymoon in Maharashtra. Explore places like Jayakwadi Dam, Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary, and Goga Baba Hill and enjoy trekking, bird watching, and scenic views with your loved ones.

Nashik is very famous for its sacred sites and cultural experiences. It houses two most famous pilgrimage sites- Trimbakeshwar Temple (one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva) and a revered Shaktipeeth- Saptashrungi Devi Temple.
You will also witness Panchavati, a sacred site associated with Lord Rama's exile. For capturing scenic views, witness Anjaneri Hills, Vihigaon Waterfall and Dudhsagar falls.

Pune's liveliness and rich culture and heritage attract diverse travellers. It has many amazing places to explore like Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati temple, Aga khan Palace, Sinhagad Fort and hill stations like Lonavala and Khandala.
To experience the authentic culture and traditions, you can also plan your Pune sightseeing tour during festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi or Pune Festival.

Kolhapur has a rich heritage and natural beauty. The city boasts of many historical places like Panhala Fort, New Palace, and the revered pilgrimage sites of Shri Mahalaxmi Temple, Jyotiba and Kopeshwar.
You can also enjoy adventure trekking in forts of Vishalgad and Panhala etc. These multifaceted offerings in terms of tourism makes it a must visit travel destination in Maharashtra.

Lonavala is the best place to explore in Maharashtra for family-friendly outings. The beauty of Lonavala will take your breath away. This scenic hill station offers a perfect blend of history, adventure and relaxation in the lap of nature.
It is located in the beautiful Sahyadri Range which is very famous for misty hills, cascading waterfalls, majestic forts and caves etc.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Maharashtra on Your Trip
Not a single day is dull in Maharashtra as there are many things to do here for all types of travellers. Here is the list of best activities to do in Maharashtra, covered in our itineraries-

items: Paragliding is one of the most fun-filled and thrilling adventure activities to do in Maharashtra. You must not miss it.

Through paragliding, you will get a chance to get aerial views of the beautiful Sahyadri Range, Western Ghats, hills and valleys. Some of the best areas to try paragliding in Maharashtra are Kamshet, Panchgani, Saputara, Talegaon etc.

Landscapes of Western Ghats and Scenic Sahyadri mountains offer the best trekking trails to explore in Maharashtra. You must not miss the most popular Kalsubai Peak Trek which is the highest peak in Maharashtra.
You can also try a heritage trekking trail of Rajmachi Fort which passes through scenic dense forests and waterfalls.
Enjoy a perfect blend of adventure and relaxation at the scenic Arabian Sea coastline in Maharashtra.

Enjoy thrilling activities like jet skiing, banana boat rides, parasailing, snorkeling, and kayaking etc. with beachside relaxation with your family. Explore heritage forts like Kolaba Fort near Alibaug.

Don't forget to explore Maharashtra's rich biodiversity spots and enjoy exotic wildlife of the region. Spot Bengal tigers, Indian leopards, sloth bears, Indian bison, deer species and a variety of bird species.
Some of the most popular National Parks in Maharashtra are -Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve, Pench National Park, and Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary.

blocks.text: Top Travel Tips for Memorable Holidays in Maharashtra
Here are some best travel tips to explore Maharashtra for memorable holidays

items: Plan your Visit- Plan your Maharashtra visit during peak tourism season to enjoy culture, festivities, heritage sightseeing and adventure activities. The best time to visit in Maharashtra is from October to March.

What to Pack -Align your packing list with season and planned activities in Maharashtra. Pack versatile clothing perfect for warm days and cool nights. Wear comfortable walking shoes as you may have to walk a lot during sightseeing. Carry sun protection (hat, sunglasses, sunscreen), modest clothes for temple visits, basic toiletries, personal medications, and travel essentials like ID, cash, and chargers to enjoy hassle free trips.
Be Safe- Don't visit less frequented areas in Maharashtra after dark. If you wish to explore offbeat destinations then hire a local guide for a comprehensive Maharashtra Tour.
Maharashtra is culturally diverse. So, to experience the best Maharashtra tour, include a mix of all types of attractions like famous UNESCO sites, beaches, Hill stations, adventure parks etc.
Dress Modestly -Dress modestly in religious places. Cover your head, shoulder and knees. Wearing revealing clothes in religious sites in India is considered disrespectful.
Licensed Guides- Always hire licensed guides to enjoy Maharashtra tourism. They possess local insights on history, culture, heritage, offbeat locations and festivals.

blocks.text: Take a spiritual journey from Chennai to the sacred Mahavatar Babaji Cave ,

blocks.text: You’ll be transferred to Kukuchina (Dwarahat). We shall consider all the arrangements so that you can have a stress-free journey. You also get to explore: ageshwar Temples – 125 ancient temples Haidakhan Babaji Ashram – spiritual retreat Dunagiri Mata Temple – mythology & legends Return to the hotel to have a delicious dinner and overnight stay. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Our Malaysia Tour Packages are a haven for people who love to explore cities and different cultures. It is one of the best International Tourist destinations for Indians. Being one of the seventeenth Megadiverse countries, it has many amazing tourist attractions. Malaysia is so diverse that you'll be mesmerized by its splendor. It's made up of 13 states-Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Selangor, Perak, Pulau Pinang, Kedah, Perlis, Sabah and Sarawak-and three Federal Territories-Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, and Labuan. From Malay, Chinese, Indian and European to Borneo, you will get different cultural influences through food, festivals and attractions. This Southeast Asian country has something for everyone- Beaches, rainforests, rolling hills, long coastlines, awe-inspiring colonial buildings, exciting shopping districts, etc. The vibe of Malaysia delights every wanderer. Malaysia has many beautiful monuments and attractions to explore along with exciting street markets and places to enjoy nightlife. Here are some of the most popular places to explore and best activities to do in our Malaysia Tour Packages:

Explore Malaysia's capital, which has many iconic cultural sights, heritage monuments, sky scrapers and vibrant nightlife. The city's location is at the beautiful meeting point of the Klang and Gombak rivers.

blocks.text: Also known as Malacca, Melaka is a beautiful travel destination to visit in Malaysia. It is a major heritage town in Malaysia. It is very famous for its landmark destinations like Malacca Sultanate Palace, Christ Church, and the Historical Maritime Exhibition.

blocks.text: Genting Highlands — Must-Add for Families & Groups

Genting Highlands is one of Malaysia's top attractions, especially popular with Indian visitors. Located 51 km from Kuala Lumpur at 1,800 metres altitude, it features Resorts World Genting with theme parks (20th Century Fox World), cable car rides, and one of Southeast Asia's largest casinos (for non-Muslims). The cooler mountain air (17-25°C year-round) makes it a refreshing stop after Kuala Lumpur's heat. A half-day or full-day trip from KL is easy to arrange.

blocks.text: The Indian Himalayas are a goldmine for exquisite scenic beauty. No matter which road you take or where you head to, the wonderful Himalayan ranges will never fail to fascinate. Manali is one such Himalayan hamlet. Situated on the banks of the ancient Beas River, Manali is a favourite among travel lovers. Blessed with a mystic charm and adorned with fun sightseeing locations, it has rightfully been called the queen of hills. The peaceful environment, surrounded by historical wonders and adventure experiences, makes a tour in Manali truly memorable. Manali is a hill station that can be easily reached throughout the year. From beating the scorching summer heat to having some fun in the snow, a wholesome time is guaranteed.

Over time, the beauty and magical realm of Manali has opened doors to all sorts of tourists. With a plethora of accommodation and sightseeing options, people from all over the world are making their way to this wonderful Himalayan town. It has also turned into a favourite among people on their honeymoon. Honeymoon goers from across the globe make their way to this peaceful little hill town to get some much-needed break. Every newly married couple wishes to start off their married life on a happy and a tension free note. What better way of doing that than heading to one of the most romantic places in India? With lush greenery all around, rolling green hills and awesome adventures in every corner, a honeymoon in Manali feels like a dream come true. Manali also represents a combination of spirituality and adventure. Couples can get blessings at Hidimba Devi Temple as well as Siyali Mahadev Mandir. Shopping at the Manali Mall Road is a different experience in itself. Trying out delicious local meals and cuisines will bind the whole experience of a happy and memorable honeymoon together.

Why look for a relaxing peaceful solitude elsewhere when you have the wonders of Manali? A place where bonfire nights meet calming scenic vistas and allows couples to bond stronger together. Over time this humble little town has grown into a full-fledged tourist town with several branches one could explore. Be it going for a drive till the other side of Atal Tunnel in Sissu, going for a hot water dip at the Vashishth spring or simply chilling riverside at some cafe or hotel, this place has it all. No matter which time of the year you decide to go, Manali will welcome everyone with open arms and lots of love. After all, nature is the cure for everything and Manali is a blessing when it comes to feeling closer to the wilderness. The next time you are wondering where to go for a honeymoon, make sure Manali makes the list.

blocks.text: Best Places to visit Manali on your Trip

Manali is an ideal destination for couples on their honeymoon, spiritual seekers and people looking to get away from the chaos of city life, or solo travelers (it is a highly safe place) it offers a plethora of fun-filled and refreshing activities for people of all ages. It witnessed a significant rise in tourist footfall in 2024.It recorded the highest number of visitors (2.8 million visitors) among other districts of Himachal Pradesh . Source-( Times of India ). Here are some of the most popular places covered in our Manali itinerary -

items: Don't miss Manali's adventure capital- Solang Valley. It is one of the best places to visit in Manali if you are an adventure lover.
Enjoy activities like paragliding, skiing, and zorbing amidst stunning mountain views.
You will also witness lush green meadows and snowcapped mountains depending on the season. It offers the best natural views for nature photography.
Hadimba Temple is a historical wooden temple dedicated to Hadimba Devi, wife of Bhim, one of the five Pandavas.

The temple is surrounded by the beautiful cedar forests. Its unique architecture and serene ambiance will transport you into the realm of bliss. It is one of the most beautiful temples to visit in Manali.

Enjoy the breathtaking mountain views and snow adventure activities at Rohtang Pass. It is one of the most scenic mountains passes to see in Manali. It is also a gateway to visit Lahaul and Spiti Valley.
It is best for adventure and nature excursions. You can reach here from May to November. It is closed in winter due to heavy snow.
Don't forget to visit this beautiful pilgrimage site for Sikhs and Hindus in Manali- Manikaran Sahib. It is renowned for its hot springs.

Located on the banks of Parvati River, the spiritual ambiance of Manikaran Sahib offers an eternal peak for solace seekers. Devotees from all over India come to Manikaran Sahib to seek blessings of the Guru.
Visit Manali most revered spiritual and wellness destination- Vashisht Temple and Hot Springs. The temple is believed to be over 4000 years old.
Pay your respects to Sage Vashisht, one of the ancient Saptarishis and the Guru of Lord Rama. The temple is also famous for its hot springs known as Vashisht Kund.
The hot waters are believed to have medicinal properties which can heal skin and joint ailments.
Located across the Manalsu River, old Manali is a must not miss if you like to explore the quieter part of Manali. Enjoy the bohemian vibe and explore quaint cafes at Old Manali.
Here you will witness beautiful apple orchards, scenic trekking trails, cedar forests and bustling markets which offer leather goods, winter clothing, handmade jewelry, and local produce.
If you like leisure nature walks, peaceful temple hopping and visiting cafes then Old Manali will delight your soul.
Manu Temple is dedicated to Sage Manu who is known as the creator of Humanity in Hindu mythology. It is one of the most popular temples to visit in Manali.
It is said that sage Manu meditated at the temple spot and saved the Vedas and seven sages from flood.
It is also the origin point of Manali known as Manu-Alaya (abode of Sage Manu)

blocks.text: Are you a Lord Krishna devotee? Then this 3 day trip in the state of Uttar Pradesh is for you! Book our Mathura Gokul Barsana and Vrindavan Tour Package and visit the lands of Lord Krishna in comfort and luxury.

items: Route: Arrival in Delhi - Travel to Mathura - Explore Gokul Temple → Mathura to Vrindavan → Barsana – Nandgaon – Govardhan Parikrama – Delhi

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrival in Delhi - Travel to Mathura - Explore Gokul Temple (180-185 kms, Approx. 5-6 hrs drive)

Your tour will start from Delhi. Our representative will pick you up from the airport/railway station. Your Mathura-Gokul-Vrindavan tour begins! Now you’ll be driven to Mathura , a 4-hour drive approximately. Along the way, we’ll stop for refreshment at a restaurant of your choice. Our very first stop on this tour will be at the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple . This marks the birthplace of Lord Krishna. This is a temple complex and houses various other temples inside it, such as the Krishna Janmasthan Temple and the Garbha Griha . Feel free to explore them! The next temple we’ll be visiting is the Dwarkadhish Temple, where Lord Krishna is worshipped as the king of Dwarka. Do take photographs of the intricate architecture and the temple's façade. After that, we’ll take you to the Vishram Ghat , which is famous for being the place where Lord Krishna rested after he defeated the cruel Kansa. Now, take a lunch break at any of the local restaurants in Mathura. Thereafter, you’ll be taken on a drive to Gokul (20 minutes). Once you get there, get ready for a full-blown temple tour dedicated to Lord Krishna, such as: Gokulnath Temple Raja Thakur Temple Brahmand Ghat Raman Reti Chintaharan Mahadev and 84 Khamba After that, enjoy the Yamuna Aarti at the Ghat. Take in the blessed vibes of the charged atmosphere! Your overnight stay will be in Mathura Places You’ll See
Day 2: Mathura to Vrindavan (18 kms, Approx. 30-35 minutes drive)

Treat yourself to a delicious breakfast in the morning. After that, you’ll be taken to the divine lands of Vrindavan! Lord Krishna spent his youth here. Here, you'll be taken on a temple tour of: Banke Bihari Temple: You’ll find the atmosphere here filled with devotion. Nidhivan Stroll through the forest where once Lord Krishna and Gopis had Rasleela! ISKCON Temple: The serene environment here is next level! Do capture the pics of the temple domes and architecture. Radha Vallabh Ji Temple: This temple symbolises the epitome of the divine love that Radha felt for Lord Krishna. Vaishno Devi Temple: It’s a replica of Jammu’s original shrine. Prem Mandir: This temple has a load of sculptures of Lord Krishna, which depict his life. Do attend the Light and Sound Show here if time permits. Now, return to the hotel and get a restful night of sleep. Note: Banke Bihari Temple remains closed from 12 PM to 5:30 PM daily. Places You’ll See
Day 3: Barsana – Nandgaon – Govardhan Parikrama – Transfer to Delhi (185 km/4 hrs)

Relish a delicious breakfast in the morning Now, you’ll be driven to Barsana , which is the birthplace of Radha Rani. The very first site that you’ll visit here will be the Radha Rani Temple (aka the Shriji Temple or Ladli Ji). Enjoy the enthusiasm that devotees show here, and let some get brushed on you! After this, you'll be taken to the place where Lord Krishna spent his childhood, that is, Nandgaon ! Also, take this time to visit the nearby prominent sites, like Yashoda Kund and Sunehri Kothi . Now, head towards Govardhan . This is the very place where Lord Krishna performed his divine Leela by lifting the whole Govardhan Mountain! Once you’re there, take part in the Govardhan Parikrama , a distance of 7 km. You can also explore the nearby temples, such as: Mansi Ganga Haridev Temple Daan Ghati Temple This concludes your trip. Now, you’ll be driven to Delhi by our driver, where you’ll be dropped off at the airport or railway station (by 10 PM). Hope you have made wonderful memories on this tour. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Morocco has many destinations for tourists to enjoy on Tour Packages. This country has natural landscapes, cultural sites, mountain peaks, sprawling forests and wonderful coast line to provide memorable time on Morocco Tour Packages. With Mediterranean Sea at the backdrop and long rich history, the charm of this country draws tourists on Tour Package from all over the world and over and over again.

Rabat is the present capital of the country and was built in 12th century having many attractions for tourists on Morocco Travel Packages. The minaret of an incomplete 12th century mosque called as Tour Hassan, the Chellah is a place with Roman ruins, delightful gardens and wonderful monuments are popular places to visit. Rabat is also famous for its fabulous gates built centuries ago, the Gate of the Ambassadors and Oudaias Kasbah Gate are most famous amongst all. The Mohammed V Mausoleum is an outstanding example of Moroccan architecture, the Royal Palace and many fort and castles around the city are not to miss attractions of Rabat on Morocco Tour Package. Mamora forests lies on the outskirts of the city and is a popular destination along with exotic beaches, during summer these beaches are perfect place to relax on Morocco Travel Package.

Fes in Morocco is the oldest and the most interesting city for visitors on Tour Packages. Built in 8th century this place has all the charm of an ancient city, it has history and mystery more than any other place in Morocco. Nejjarine Square and fountain, the Er Rasif Mosque, Andalous Mosque, the Royal Palace, the Kasbah and Dar Beth Museum are chief attractions of this magical city. The old city area of Fes is in UNESCO world heritage list, the windy streets with bustling covered markets and ancient mosques this place is full of magnificent structures of Hispanic-Arabic architecture. Medina Bazaar is the biggest market in the world and there are many things which tourists can purchase on Morocco Holiday Package. On the North of this fascinating city the valley of Ouergha is another not to miss attraction along with ancient mosques and interesting shopping places on Morocco Tour Packages.

Marrakech too was once capital of Morocco and today very interesting tourist destination on Tour Packages. This city not only offers captivating historical places but also provides outdoor activities to enjoy. The 12th century mosque Koutoubia dominates city’s skyline and is higher than Notre Dam. Another very exciting and sometimes bewildering place is the City Square or Djeema el Fenaa meaning ‘the place of the dead’, this place comes alive in the night with dance and music shows, fortunetellers, storytellers, acrobats and snake charmers, it is an exotic spectacle and not to be missed in Marrakech. The area on UNESCO world heritage list is full or architectural master pieces and has a large Medina which is not to be missed on Morocco Holiday Package.

The city of Meknes is full of castles and fortresses along with UNESCO world heritage site. This city is also one of the imperial cities of the country and has many historical attractions for tourists. For beach fun tourists on Morocco Tour Package head to El Jadida which has a beautiful Portuguese fort and exotic beaches on Atlantic coast.

Places to Visit in and Around Muktinath on your Trip

In 2025, Muktinath Dham witnessed a significant rise in tourist footfall. It welcomed around 539,872 domestic tourists and 138,664 were foreign tourists from around 72 countries.(Source: TravelandTourworld ). The place gained more popularity after PM Narendra Modi's visit. There are many beautiful places to visit in and around Muktinath Temple. Mentioned here are some of the best places to visit in and around Muktinath Dham, covered in our itineraries. You can also customise your Muktinath Tour package and add many places of your choice-

rows: Muktinath Temple is a central pilgrimage site for Hindu and Buddhist devotees. It is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Mukti in Sanskrit means salvation and Nath means Lord. Hence, Muktinath means- God of Salvation. Devotees from all over the world visit Muktinath to attain salvation.

Jwala Devi Temple is a must visit place after visiting Muktinath. It is dedicated to the goddess of fire. The temple is very famous for its Eternal flame which has been burning continuously for decades naturally.

Mukti Dhara is a 108 holy water spout located behind the temple of Muktinath. Devotees who take holy dip in these 108 water spouts attain spiritual purification and salvation from the cycle of birth and death.

Located at the North side of Muktinath Temple, one must visit Mharme Lhakhang Gompa which is also known as Narsingh Gompa (Temple of 1000 lamps). The Gompa is dedicated to Guru Rinpoche (Padmasambhava).
At the left of the entrance gate of Muktinath Temple lies the sacred monastery of Sangdo. It's an important sacred site for Buddhist worship and meditation.

Situated in central Nepal at an elevation of around 3700 meters, Ranipauwa Village is the main resting point for pilgrims who are visiting Muktinath Dham and trekkers who are crossing Thorong-La Pass. This village has many guesthouses, hotels, restaurants, shops, souvenir shops for pilgrims and trekkers.

Don't miss this historic Tibetan village in the Mustang district of Nepal. It is located in the valley of Kali Gandaki River. It is one of the oldest Himalayan villages. You will get the chance to understand authentic Tibetan culture and breathtaking views of Nilgiri and Tilicho peaks.

Located in the Myagdi District of Nepal's Annapurna region, at an elevation of about 1,200 meters, Tatopani Hot springs is one of the best places to visit around Muktinath Dham. These geothermal hot springs are very popular for their medicinal properties. The mineral rich water offers nourishment to the muscles. Here you will also witness beautiful Himalayan landscapes, terraced slopes, forests, and waterfalls.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Muktinath Temple
Some of the best things to do in and around Muktinath Dham for spiritual upliftment and to rejuvenate your soul are-
Blessings of lord Vishnu and Guru Rinpoche at Muktinath

items: Get the divine blessings of lord Vishnu at Muktinath Dham. Lord Vishnu hare is known as Mukti Narayan. Devotees from all over the world visit here to pay respects to Lord Vishnu. It is believed that Lord Vishnu has taken refuge and liberation here in the form of Shaligram stone.

It is also a prominent pilgrimage site for Buddhists also as this place is one of the 24 holy tantric sites where Guru Rinpoche is believed to have meditated. For Buddhist devotees, Muktinath Temple is known as Chumming Gyasta or Hundred waters.

blocks.text: Take Holy Dip in Mukti Dhara

items: Located behind the Muktinath Temple are 108 water spouts known as Mukti Dhara. As the name suggests, Mukti Dhara refers to the water of Salvation.
If any devotees take holy dip in these 108 water spouts, he/she is believed to attain spiritual salvation and freedom from the cycle of Birth and death.
Pay your respects and bow down to the revered eternal flame at Jwala Devi Temple. The temple of Jwala Devi is located at the temple complex of the sacred Muktinath Dham.
The eternal flame at Jwala Devi Temple has been burning since time unknown, blessing the pilgrims with divine energy and spiritual upliftment.
If you are visiting Muktinath then you must also try the Annapurna Circuit trek. It is one of the most sought-after trekking trails for adventurers, spiritually inclined travellers and nature lovers.
This route starts from Nayapul or Besisahar and heads towards Thorong Phedi. After that trekkers prepare to cross the highest point known as Thorong La Pass.

blocks.text: Try the Local Food in Muktinath

items: In Muktinath, you can enjoy the local and traditional cuisines like Dal Bhat, Momos, Yak butter tea, Thukpa, Yak Meat and Cheese and Tibetan Bread.
These cuisines will introduce you to the Nepali and Himalayan culinary traditions.

Some of the best souvenirs and items to buy in and around Muktinath Dham are Shaligram stones, Tibetan prayer flags, metal statues, Tibetan Thangka Paintings, Rudraksha Beads, jewelry, Handmade Woolen products of Yak or sheep wool.
These items will introduce you to the local artistic traditions of Nepal.

blocks.text: Travel Tips to Make Your Pilgrimage Trip to Muktinath Memorable
Follow these helpful travel tips to make your Muktinath Pilgrimage Tour memorable-

items: Plan your Visit - Always plan your visit to the revered Muktinath Dham during the peak tourist season (Sep-November) and March to May. During these months, the temperature will be pleasant for sightseeing and trekking. You will also enjoy local festivals like Dashain and Tihar. Book your accommodations in advance to make your Muktinath Tour memorable as if you delay your bookings, you may not get your desired hotel in advance.

Dress Modestly- While visiting the sacred Muktinath Dham and other temples, dress modestly. Respect the culture and traditions of the sacred sites. Don't wear revealing clothes. Cover your head, knees and shoulders properly.

Stay hydrated and acclimatize gradually - In high-altitude regions like Muktinath, you must stay hydrated for smooth Darshan. It is very essential for your physical fitness during the tour. Also, don't try to rush and trek the entire route in one go. Acclimatize gradually to high altitude, give your body enough time to adjust to avoid altitude sickness.
Carry Cash - carry enough cash while buying souvenirs from small vendors and shopkeepers. You may not find any option for digital payment and ATMs might not function properly.

Do not go alone- If you are a first-time traveller do not try to take unusual routes as you may get lost in high-altitude regions. Always follow your tour guide and keep emergency contact numbers to approach the right person for help.
Responsible Tourist -As a tourist, it is our responsibility to keep the Himalayan sites serene and clean. Do not litter, carry eco-friendly items and avoid the use of plastic.

blocks.text: Q-1: How many pilgrims can a helicopter carry for the Muktinath Tour?

Ans: The helicopter is designed to accommodate only five to six people at a time to Muktinath. It will be really expensive if you are planning to do the whole helicopter tour for just 2 or 3 people but you can minimize the cost by choosing your journey with 5 to 6 people to divide the expenditure evenly.
Q-2: What are the best months to plan a Muktinath Tour?
Ans: The months of March, April, May, June, September, October and November are the only times in the entire year when the skies are clear and the weather is pleasant for you to visit this Dham.
Q-3: Are there any permits required to do the Muktinath Dham Tour?

Ans: The temple lies within the trekking and conservation zone of Nepal and for this purpose 2 main permits are required which are - Annapurna Conservation Area Project Permit or ACAP and the other one is Trekker's Information Management System Permit or TIMS. Entering this zone without these two permits is considered an offence and you will not be allowed to enter this region without it. If you avail a package all the permits' requirements will be taken care of.
Q-4: Is It Possible to Visit Pokhara Instead of Making My Way Back to Kathmandu?

Ans: Yes, it is possible for you to make your way to Pokhara and spend a few days there as well before heading back to Kathmandu since it falls en route to the helicopter journey. From Pokhara you can make your way back to Kathmandu easily via a tourist bus, cab or taxi. By road the journey takes around 7.5 hours.
Q-5: Why do people visit Muktinath Dham?

Ans: People generally visit Muktinath Dham as it holds immense significance in the lives of devout Hindus. Here Vishnu Ji is worshipped as - Muktinath - or the god of salvation. People come here to take a holy bath under the chilled water flowing through the 108 spouts since it is believed that doing so will free them from all the sins that they have committed in their entire life. So, in short, visiting Muktinath is said to bring salvation to devout pilgrims.
