Ans: From Kathmandu the temple is located at a flying distance of just 1.5 hours and 45 minutes from Pokhara. A helicopter package will allow you to complete your Darshan in a duration of 1 hour. Mussoorie is a hill station and a municipal board in the Dehradun district of the Indian state of Uttarakhand. It is about 26 kilometres (16 mi) from the state Winter capital Dehradun and 289 km (180 mi) north of the national capital of New Delhi. The hill station is in the foothills of the Garhwal Himalayan range. The adjoining town of Landour, which includes a military cantonment, is considered part of "greater Mussoorie", as are the townships Barlowganj and Jharipani.

Mussoorie is renowned for its rich cultural heritage, historical significance, and diverse attractions. From ancient temples and forts to modern amenities and natural beauty, Mussoorie offers an unforgettable experience for every traveler.

blocks.text: The best time to visit Nainital depends on the activities that you're interested in doing here.

Many tourists pick the summers (March - June) to come here. In this window, you can bask in its pleasant weather and enjoy sightseeing at ease. Also, boating is another star attraction of this period.

Another great time to come here is the wintertime (October - February) . The snow blankets the whole region, creating a winter paradise for the travellers. Enjoy snowfall and other snow-related sports such as snowboarding.

You can also come here in the monsoon season (July - September) . Enjoy the lush greenery that the region is blessed with during this period. Moreover, there are fewer crowds, letting you enjoy your tour in peace.
Nainital, therefore, can be visited at any time. That's one of the best things about this hill station - you're welcome throughout the year!
Here are some ways by which you can reach the picturesque hill station of Nainital:

items: By Air: The nearest airport to Nainital is Pantnagar Airport, located about 70 km from the hill station. From the airport, you can easily hire a taxi to reach this beautiful town.

By Train: Nainital tour by train is another great option! Kathgodam Railway Station is the nearest railhead (about 34 km away) and is well-connected to major cities like Delhi, Dehradun, Lucknow, etc.

By Road : Nainital is very well-connected by roads. You can either drive to reach there yourself, or you can visit by the regular buses that run from major cities, like Delhi, Dehradun, etc. Also, the Delhi to Nainital Trip by car is another popular option among tourists.

items: The calm waters and the surrounding green hills of the Naini Lake will put you right in a state of relaxation. The best thing about it is that you can indulge in boating here throughout the day! Also, both paddle boats and rowboats are available here.

This is one of the most exciting things about your Nainital Sightseeing Tour! Simply take a cable car from Mallital to Snow View Point and allow yourself to get spoiled by the rich Himalayan valley views!
Mall Road is definitely a go-to as it's a perfect place to grab a snack or go full-blown souvenir shopping. While you're there, do look for wooden handicrafts and woollen wear.

Q1. How many days are enough for Nainital?
Ans. Usually, three to five days are enough to explore the hill station in depth. In this span, you can easily cover all the major sightseeing destinations in the town.
Nainital is a small hill station that has a definite set of sightseeing places. These places and experiences take no more than 5 days for a leisure holiday, along with proper sightseeing.
Q2. How can I spend 3 days in Nainital?

Ans. You can cover a lot in 3 days in Nainital: Day 1 - visit Nainital Lake, Naini Devi Temple and Nainital Zoo. Day 2 - visit the eco cave garden, shop at Mall Road and take a fun ropeway ride. Day 3 - if leaving Nainital by evening, then after check out in the morning, you can go to Kilbury Bird Sanctuary or Tiffin Top, which will take around half a day to cover and explore.

Ans. The first step is to see if you are going during the right month. Summertime means inflated prices of everything, while wintertime means fewer tourists and lower rates. Q5. What should I buy from Nainital?
Ans. You can buy souvenirs in Nainital like wooden artefacts, hand-woven shawls, woollen textiles, trinkets, handicraft items, and so much more.
Q6. How can I travel locally in Nainital?

Ans. Nainital has developed into a full-on tourist hub. There are rickshaws available if you want to get around the market area. There are also taxis and shared autos available. There are local buses that connect the nearby villages to Nainital. You can even rent a bike or a car if you like.
Q7. Is it safe to travel from Delhi to Nainital at night?

Ans. Travelling from Delhi to Nainital is generally considered safe. The route through NH 9 is well-maintained. However, once you get near Nainital, be wary of the hilly stretches. Hiring a professional driver is a good idea as well.
Q8. Which is better: Mussoorie or Nainital?

Ans. Both Mussoorie and Nainital are beautiful hill stations. However, they offer different experiences to the tourists. If you want to enjoy boating or lakes, then pick Nainital. And if you want to soak in the colonial charm or take short hikes, then Mussoorie is a better option for that.
Q9. What is Nainital famous for?

Ans. Nainital is mainly famous for Naini Lake, Naini Temple, Tiffin Top, Kilbury Bird Sanctuary, and shopping marketplaces. It has also gained popularity for being the gateway to several other places like Mukteshwar, Binsar, Pangot, Bhimtal, and Almora.
Q10. What is the best time to visit Nainital?

Ans. The months of March to June mark the best time to come, especially if you want to get some refreshing mountain air in summer. If you wish to avoid the tourists, then going there during the autumn-winter months of October to February is fine too.

blocks.text: Dotted with several beautiful heritage sites, mesmerizing beauty, and an incomparable culture, Nepal offers its visitors some of the most memorable experiences. The best time to visit Nepal is September to November and March to May. Let's know in detail-

items: These are the best months to plan your trip to Nepal. The skies are crystal clear with dry weather. You will get high visibility for enjoying scenic treks. You will witness more crowds at popular tourist spots. Book your hotels in advance. It is also a time to enjoy vibrant festivals like Dashain and Tihar.

The season offers warm weather to enjoy sightseeing comfortably. It is also the best time for trekking and outdoor activities. You will also witness many wild flowers and Rhododendrons in full bloom. It's the best time if you enjoy nature photography.
Holi, Buddha Jayanti, Ghode Jatra are some of the most famous festivals celebrated in these months.

It is not a favorable time to plan your trip in Nepal. You may witness heavy rains due with potential risks of landslides, roadblocks etc. These months are not suitable for trekking and adventure activities.
Your sightseeing plans may get postponed or delayed due to heavy rain. But you can enjoy Teej, Gai Jatra, Krishna Janmashtami festivals in these months.
It is the best time for cultural exploration but one should only plan a Nepal trip during winter if they can bear the cold.

If you like less crowd, high-altitude trekking trails and cold weather, these months are best for you. Losar, Maghe Sankranti, Basant Panchami are some of the most popular festivals celebrated in these months.

blocks.text: Best Places to visit in Nepal on your Trip

items: The capital of Nepal, Kathmandu is one of the oldest inhabited places in the world. You will be amazed to know that its history dates back to the 2nd Century AD.

There are many places to explore in Kathmandu for sightseeing such as Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath Stupa, Boudhanath Stupa, and Pashupatinath Temple etc. You will find a perfect blend of history, culture and vibrant city life.

For Hindu Devotees, The sacred Pashupatinath Temple is an important pilgrimage site here which is dedicated to Lord Shiva and the scenic Boudhanath Stupa is a prominent Buddhist site. Don't miss the lively Thamel district which is very famous for shopping and exciting nightlife.
In Pokhara you will witness breathtaking natural landscapes and opportunities for amazing adventures. It is one of the best places to explore in Nepal.

Pokhara is also known as Lake City as it is very popular for breathtaking Phewa Lake. You can enjoy boating and capturing mesmerizing sights of Mt Annapurna. Adventurers must try trekking to the world renowned Annapurna Peak.
Some other notable tourist attractions to see in Pokhara are Devi's fall, Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave, Mahendra and Bat Caves, World Peace Pagoda, Begnas Lake and Bindabasini Temple.

Chitwan is a paradise for adventure and nature lovers in Nepal. It's popular because of Chitwan National Park which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its awe-inspiring biodiversity and wildlife. Here you will see one horned Asiatic rhinoceros, Bengal tigers, elephants, and over 500 bird species.
You can also enjoy exciting jungle activities like safaris, birdwatching, canoe rides, and visits to indigenous Tharu villages.
Witness stunning sunrise and sunset views at Siraichuli Hill and enjoy birdwatching and hiking at Bishazari Tal (Twenty Thousand Lakes).
Located in the northeastern part of Nepal, Khumbu Valley is one of the must visit tourist destinations in Nepal. It is also known as the Everest region.
Witness iconic sights of Mt Everest and the scenic Khumbu glacier.
Trekkers from far are drawn to Khumbu valley for trekking to Everest base camp. There are many beautiful Sherpa villages to explore such as Namche Bazaar, Khumjung, and Khunde.
Some of the most prominent tourist attractions to explore here are Syangboche Monastery, Everest View Point, and Kala Patthar. Also enjoy Sherpa culture with festivals like Mani Rimdu.

Muktinath in Nepal is a prominent attraction for Hindu devotees as it houses the iconic Muktinath Temple which is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. It is also one of the 108 Divya Desams of Lord Vishnu worshipped by Vaishnavas.
One of the most important key features here is 108 sacred water spouts which are known as Mukti Dhara. It is believed that taking holy dip in these spouts will free you from karmic backlogs.
Muktinath is also important for trekkers as it is an important stop on the popular Annapurna Circuit trekking route. You will get stunning views of Annapurna Mountain and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Nepal on your Trip

Covered in our Nepal Itineraries are a mix of adventure, cultural, natural and spiritual activities. Based on your interests, you can also customize your Nepal Tour Packages and include activity according to your preferences. Here is a list of our best recommended activities to do in Nepal-

items: If you are planning to explore Nepal then, Everest Mountain Flight is something you must not miss. It is the most scenic flight from Kathmandu. You will get guaranteed window seats to witness the breathtaking views of Mt Everest and other Himalayan Peaks.
From above you will also witness aerial panoramas of glaciers, valleys, and peaks like Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu without trekking.

September to April is the best time to enjoy paragliding in Nepal. It is one of the best activities to enjoy here. You can enjoy it in Pokhara in Sarangkot which is the most popular paragliding destination in Nepal.
Paragliding in Pokhara offers scenic views of Annapurna Peak, Dhaulagiri mountain, Manaslu Peak, Pokhara Valley and Phewa Lake.

Nepal is blessed with deeply sacred spiritual places which you must visit in your Nepal Tour. Not only will it enrich your mind with divine grace but also fine-tune your tired spirit from the chaos of the world.

Some of the most popular spiritual places you must visit here are Boudhanath Stupa, Pashupatinath Temple, World Peace Pagoda, Kopan Monastery, Muktinath Temple, Lumbini, Swayambhunath and Namo Buddha etc.

Bungee jumping is one of the best things to do in Nepal as it has some of the world's highest Bungee jumping points. Out of many Bungee Jumping points, you must try Bhote Koshi River Bungee jumping point which is a 160 m drop from a suspension bridge.
The next iconic Bungee Jumping point is Kushma Bungee Jump which is the second highest Bungee Jump. It is a 228 meter drop, offering intense adrenaline rush amidst the beautiful natural setting.

Your Nepal holidays will be incomplete if you don't indulge in a wildlife safari adventure here. There are many thrilling wildlife sanctuaries and national parks to enjoy nature and wildlife safari with your loved ones.

Some of the most notable National parks to explore wildlife and rich biodiversity of Nepal are Parsa National Park, Shuklaphanta National Park, Banke National Park, Chitwan National Park and Bardia National Park.

blocks.text: Nepal Visa & Entry Requirements for Indian Tourists 2026

items: Indian Citizens: No visa required to enter Nepal. However, you must carry a valid Indian Passport (minimum 6 months validity) OR a valid Voter ID Card issued by the Election Commission of India. Aadhaar Card is also accepted at most border checkpoints as of 2023.
OCI Card Holders & NRIs: OCI cardholders must carry their OCI card along with their foreign passport. A separate Nepal visa is not required but passport must be valid.
Other Nationalities: Most foreign nationals can get a Nepal Visa on Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. 15-day visa: USD 30, 30-day visa: USD 50, 90-day visa: USD 125.
Note: Land border crossing (Sonauli, Raxaul etc.) requires same documents as above.

blocks.text: Nepal Trekking Permits — What You Need to Know

items: TIMS Card (Trekkers' Information Management System): Required for most trekking routes. Cost: INR 600 approx. for SAARC nationals (Indians included). Available at Nepal Tourism Board office in Kathmandu or Pokhara.
Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP): Required for Annapurna Circuit, Poon Hill, and Muktinath treks. Cost: NPR 3,000 approx.
Sagarmatha National Park Entry: Required for Everest Base Camp trek. Cost: NPR 3,000 approx. for SAARC nationals.
Upper Mustang & Manaslu: Restricted Area Permit required — cost significantly higher (USD 500+ for Mustang). Contact us to arrange.
Currency: Nepalese Rupee (NPR). As of 2026, approximately 1 INR = 1.6 NPR (check current rates before travel).

Indian Rupees accepted? Yes — Indian currency notes of INR 100, 200, 500 are widely accepted in Nepal, especially near border areas and tourist zones. However, carry Nepalese currency for remote areas.
ATMs: Available in Kathmandu, Pokhara, and most tourist towns. Limit per withdrawal is typically NPR 35,000. Carry some cash for trekking routes.
Exchange: Best rates at authorized money changers in Thamel (Kathmandu) or Pokhara Lakeside. Airport exchange rates are less favorable.

blocks.text: Experience spiritual fulfilment as you embark on a sacred aerial journey to Omkareshwar and Ujjain's sacred sites.

items: Route: Indore → Indore – Omkareshwar – Ujjain → Bhasma Aarti and Return to Indore

blocks.text: As you arrive at Indore Railway Station or Airport, you will meet our courteous representative, who will welcome you gladly. You can spend the evening as you want. You can explore the local markets, embark on a sightseeing tour, or spend some leisure time in your hotel unwinding from the stress of the day. Places You’ll See

Post a tasty breakfast, you'll be picked up from your hotel. You'll be taken to the airport, where you will meet our ground representative, who will inform you about all the helicopter boarding formalities. You're advised to arrive at least two hours before the flight to the helipad so that you can complete all the boarding formalities on time. After around 25 minutes of aerial journey, you will reach Omkareshwar Helipad. About Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga Omkareshwar Temple is considered to be one of the holiest shrines in India and one of the twelve revered Jyotirlingas . The sacred temple is located on Mandhata Island, which is situated at the meeting point of the Kaveri and Narmada Rivers. The island is in the shape of the Hindu 'OM' symbol. On this island, there are many temples, and the actual Jyotirlinga is believed to be in the Mamleshwar temple. To facilitate travelers to have a fast and secure Darshan of Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga, PM Shri Heli Tourism Service was started by the MP Tourism Board, as reported by NDTV . Once you have arrived at Omkareshwar, you will be transferred to Omkareshwar Temple. At Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga, you'll have VIP Darshan of Sri Omkareshwar Mahadev. After the divine Darshan, you will be taken back to the helipad. After flying for around 40 minutes, you will reach the Ujjain helipad. Once you have arrived at Ujjain, you will be transferred to your pre-booked hotel. Then you will visit the famous attractions, including Harsiddhi Temple, Ram Ghat, and the local markets. In the evening, you will return to your hotel and savor a tasty dinner. Have an overnight stay at your hotel. Places You’ll See
Day 3: Bhasma Aarti and Return to Indore

Wake up early in the morning, and then you will head to the Mahakaleshwar Temple as per our Omkareshwar Ujjain air travel package. Next, you'll attend the Bhasma Aarti, which happens daily at approximately 4:00 AM. About Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga is one of the holiest places dedicated to Shiva in India. The temple is a Jyotirlinga and one of the holy abodes of Lord Shiva. It is located at Ujjain in the state of Madhya Pradesh. This sacred temple is located on the side of the river Shipra. The presiding deity of this temple is Shiva in the lingam form, and it is believed to be Swayambhu. After the Darshan, you will head back to your hotel and have a luscious breakfast. You will be transferred to Ujjain Helipad from where you will take your flight to Indore Helipad. With this Omkareshwar Ujjain Helicopter Tour package will come to an end. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Best Places to Visit During Odisha Trip

Odisha is one of the best travel destinations in India. We usually hype about the beauty of northern states of India but come to Odisha and you will realize what you are missing. Here is a list of must visit places in Odisha to know its true essence-

Puri, a serene coastal city in Odisha is a soul pleasing tourist destination to fine tune your senses with inner peace, recreation activities and sacred wisdom. This place is a perfect blend of spiritual solace with heritage, culture and nature. Here are some of the most popular places to see in Puri -

items: Lord Jagannath Temple - It’s not wrong to say that Jagannath Puri Dham is the soul of Odisha. Millions of devotees visit Odisha’s Rath yatra just to get one glimpse of the sacred Jagannath Idol. The temple of Lord Jagannath’s divine grace is something which is very difficult to explain in words.

Kuruma Buddhist Site - This site is still under excavation which makes it more beautiful as it takes us back in time. It’s a beautiful place to learn about Buddhist heritage. Locally it is also known as Yama Dharma Pitha. It is one of the most popular heritage places to see in Puri.

Chandrabhaga Sea Beach - Located at the eastern side of the majestic Sun temple of Konark, Chandrabhagha Sea beach is a scenic spot to relax with your loved ones. The endless blue of the ocean is everywhere as far as your eyes can see. Nourish your soul with the pleasing views of the ocean, golden sands and sunrise and sunset.

Sakhigopal Temple, Satyabadi, Puri - Sakigopal Temple is a sanctuary of inner peace. The temple is dedicated to Lord Krishna. The idol of Shri Radha Rani is also present in the temple. During the occasion of Anla Navami, the temple allows devotees to embrace Radha Rani’s feet.

Raghurajpur Handicrafts - Witness the beautiful Pattachitra art which is a very popular art form practiced in this village for decades. Here, every family is engaged in some kind of art form or crafts. You will also see paper Mache products, stone carving art, palm leaf etching, tusser paintings and cow dung toys etc.

Sun Temple Konark - Faith, art and astronomical genius, The Konark Sun Temple is the most beautiful architectural marvel built in the 13th century. The temple is in the shape of a grand chariot with 24 intricately carved stone wheels. Each wheel has precise sundials with eye pleasing carvings on the spokes.

blocks.text: Deogarh is very popular for its natural beauty and cultural richness. It was earlier an integral part of Sambalpur but got its distinct identity in 1994, making it one of the youngest administrative divisions in Odisha. You will be mesmerized to see its beautiful hilly, forested areas and scenic waterfalls. It's nature's bliss.

items: Jagannath Temple Deogarh - It is one of the most popular temples in Deoghar. Here Lord Jagannath, Lord Balarama and Devi Subhadra are the main presiding deities. Like Puri, Jagannath Rath yatra is the main festival of this temple.

Gohira Dam Deogarh - Enjoy the scenic view, listen to the serene silence of nature and spend some fun-filled moments with your family as it’s a great picnic spot. Also get divine blessings from Lord Shiva at the temple situated near the Dam.

Kailash Palace Deogarh - It was built by Raja Dibya Sankar Dev in 1919. It has many scenic natural sights to capture as this place is surrounded by hills and mountains from all sides. It is also one of the top ecotourism spots in Odisha.

Olata Bata, Deogarh - Located 2 km away from Deogarh Bus Stand, Olata Bata is a giant fiscus tree which holds immense religious significance for the people. Its leaves grow in the opposite direction from normal trees which makes it a very unique sight to see.

Jhadeswar Temple - The temple was constructed during the reign of Raja Brajasundar Deb in 1854. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva. The lingam of Lord Shiva here is not implanted, it’s a Swayambhu (self-manifested form of Lord Shiva).

blocks.text: Lying at the serene confluence of Koel and Sankha rivers, Rourkela sits amidst the hilly terrains, laterite rich red soils bordering scenic forests. It proudly showcases one of India’s largest steel plants which also gave it a nickname- Ispat Nagar (Steel city of India).

items: Ved Vyas - Visit this serene secluded spot at Rourkela for peaceful vibes. It’s a place where Ved Vyas wrote Mahabharata. You will witness the scenic confluence of Koel, Sankha and Saraswati River. It also houses Vedic ashram which is a center of traditional Vedic education, healing practices, Sanskrit studies and religious activities etc.

Hanuman Vatika - It houses the beautiful 75ft tall statue of Lord Hanuman which makes it a must visit place in Odisha. The Vatika was designed by Shri Laxman Swami of Hyderabad in 1994. It is a very popular spot for spiritually inclined people, leisure lovers and solace seekers.

Vaishno Devi Temple - Vaishno Devi Temple in Rourkela is the replica of the original Vaishno Devi Temple of Jammu& Kashmir. It is situated atop the Durgapur Hill. The temple offers scenic views as it is surrounded by dense forests. Also visit Bhairavnath Temple located near Vaishno Devi Temple.

Khandadhar - This stunning waterfall will blow your heart away with its pleasing views. It’s a great spot for nature photography. Khandadhar is also known as Sword waterfall because of its sword-like shape of falling water.

Pitamahal Dam - Don’t miss this scenic recreational spot across Pitamahal river. The river is a tributary of Sankha River which merges with Koel River to form Brahmani River. Enjoy the scenic sunset and boating with your family.

blocks.text: 4- Sambalpur - Where Mahanadi Flows with Culture

Jewel of western Odisha, Sambhalpur is very famous for its natural beauty and handloom crafts especially Sambhalpuri sarees. It is one of the most famous tourist destinations to visit in Odisha. It is also known as the cultural capital of Odisha.

items: Hirakud Dam - It is one of the largest dams in the world built on the scenic Mahanadi River. It is 200ft in height. There is a lake behind the dam which is Hirakud reservoir. It spreads across 746 sq km.

Samaleswari Temple - Samaleswari Temple is located on the serene banks of Mahanadi River. It’s a soul pleasing sight. The presiding deity of the temple is goddess Samaleswari. It is a shakti Pitha which got its mention in the Odia Mahabharata by Adikabi Sarala Das.

Pataneswari Kali Temple - Pataneswari Kali Temple is dedicated to goddess Kali who is considered as the sister of Smaleswari Devi. The temple is also located near the iconic Samaleswari Temple. It was built by Balram Dev, the first Chauhan ruler of Sambhalpur in the 16th century.

Gudguda Waterfall - surrounded by Sal, Pia Sal, Mahul forests and hills Gudguda waterfall is a scenic nature paradise for peace lovers. It is also very famous for Mountain trekking opportunities and weekend picnics.
Huma Temple - You will be stunned to see the famous leaning Shiva Temple. It was built in the reign of the fifth ruler Balilar Singh of Sambhalpur. You can also enjoy boating here at Mahanadi River.

Ramsagar Park - It is one of the best places for nature lovers to visit in Odisha. There are many native trees and plants in this park which makes it the greenest place in Sambhalpur. Enjoy boating and leisure walks at this stunning nature paradise.

blocks.text: 5- Balasore- Sandy Shores and Timeless Stories

Natural wonder and deep history, Balasore captivates the heart of every traveller in Odisha. It’s a scenic place to witness how ancient temples, colonial remnants have shaped Odisha’s glorious past. History buffs and science enthusiasts will surely love Balasore.

items: Bhimkund - Take a deep plunge into mythology at Bhimkund. It’s a scenic spot of freshwater decked with a dramatic gorge. It is believed that this place was created by Bhima of Mahabharata. The waters of Bhimkund are considered holy, devotees who take a holy dip in it get relief from their sins.

Khairachora Gopinatha - The temple is dedicated to Lord Krishna. It is believed that the idol of Lord Krishna was carved by the arrow of Lord Rama for the worship of Devi Sita. It was brought by Langula Narasingha Dev to Balasore from Chitrakut in the 13th century.

Chandaneswar Temple -The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. You will also witness here a black statue of Nandi which is a center of prime attraction. Chadak Mela is one of the main festivals celebrated here. In this festival devotees observe a strict fast by not even swallowing saliva.

Saisura Waterfall - It’s a peaceful nature retreat to visit in Odisha. Perfect for weekend getaways, photography and nature lovers, its beauty never fades. Very few travellers visit Saisura Waterfall which makes it a hidden gem of Odisha.

Chandipur Sea Beach - It is also known as Odisha’s Hide and Seek beach due to the occurrence of a unique phenomenon where the sea water recedes up to 5km during low tide. It happens twice a day. It houses too many marine species like red crabs, sea urchins, starfish etc. You can spend your night at small and large eco camps located near the beach to spend the night with your family and friends.

blocks.text: Capital city of Odisha, Bhuvaneshwar is a must not miss place to make your Odisha Tour memorable. It is a hub of beautiful ancient temples and heritage sites older than 6th century AD. Bhuvaneshwar gives eternal and spiritual vibes as its name is also derived from Tribhuvaneshwari- Lord of the three World (Lord Shiva).

items: Lingraj Temple - It is one of the most famous temples to visit in Bhuvaneshwar. It was built in 11th century AD in Kalinga style of architecture which is a marvelous sight to behold. The presiding deity of this temple is Lord Shiva in his Harihar form.

Udyagiri and Khandagiri Caves - These are beautiful pairs of rock cut cave complexes near Bhuvaneshwar. The complex dates back to 1st and 2nd century BCE. It was built for the meditation and stay purpose of Buddhist monks in the reign of King Kharavela of Kaling.

Nandan Kanan Zoological Park - It’s one of the most famous places for wildlife lovers in Odisha. It is located inside Chandaka Forest in 400 hectares. The most marvelous creature White Tigers are a must not miss here. It is also the first zoo in India to breed white tigers from colored parents.

Odisha State Museum - Founded in 1938, it is a must visit place in Odisha if you are interested in knowing about the heritage and culture of Bhubaneswar and Odisha. This museum houses many artefacts, tools, manuscripts, amours and weapons of the erstwhile rulers of Bhuvanaeshwar. You will also learn about the ruling dynasties of Odisha and Bhuvaneshwar here.

Parsurameswara Temple - It is one of the oldest temples in Bhuvaneshwar dedicated to Lord Shiva who is worshipped as Lord Mukteswara. It was built in Kalinga style of architecture in the reign of Somavanshi dynasty who were great devotees of Lord Shiva.

blocks.text: Try different traditional cuisines in Odisha and treat your soul with wholesomeness. Here are some of the famous dishes to try in Odisha-

items: Pakhala Bhata - It’s one of the most famous dishes to taste in Odisha. It’s a comfort food of Odisha made with love in every household. It is a fermented rice served with curries, fried fish, or green chilies etc.

Chenna Poda - It’s a sweet gift of Odisha to the world. Try this tasty caramelized cheesecake called Chenna Poda in Odisha. It has a caramelized crust on the outside and from inside it is soft and chewy.
Dalma - Try Dalma, a wholesome dish of lentils and vegetables cooked with seasonal spices. It’s a comfort dish in every Odia household.
Kanika Bhat - If you are in Odisha, you must not miss Kanika Bhat. It is a sweet rice made of resins, ghee, and cashews. It is served in temples or on special occasions.
Chenna Jhili - You must try these sweet deep fried cheese balls dipped in sugar syrup. It’s a local favorite sweet dish in Odisha.

blocks.text: The name Pachmarhi is said to have originated from the Hindi words Panch (“five”) and Marhi (“caves”). Tradition holds that during their thirteen years of exile, the five Pandava brothers of the Mahabharatha era built these caverns. The lofty position of the caverns makes them an excellent vantage point. One of the most famous tourist attractions in India is the isolated hill village of Pachmarhi, which is entirely covered in stunning flora. Pachmarhi does add a new flavour to this Central Indian curry, and the state is widely recognised for its rich heritage, historical sites, and lush forest. The Pachmarhi 3 days / 2 nights tour will take you on a short yet exciting journey.

The My Quick Trippers representative will receive you at Pachmarhi and take you to the hotel for check-in and rest. You can come out later in the day to stroll around the town and shop from the local market. Overnight stay will take place in the Pachmarhi hotel.

On day 2 post breakfast you will drive to the various tourist spots in Pachmarhi all through the day. Your day will start with ‘Jata Shankar’ visit which is a ‘sacred cave’ situated under lose boulders displaying nature’s unique architecture. Move on to ‘Christ Church’ which crucially reminds of the colonial rule here. The architecture of the church reminds you of the European style of architecture especially with the altar and walls brought from that region. You can take a break and get back to your hotel to take lunch. Post lunch you will be taken to other sites of tourist attraction in Pachmarhi. Go to the Bee Falls to get closer to nature and then move on to the ‘Vaniki Sangrahalya’ (Bison Lodge) followed by the ‘Bal Udayan (Children’s park). To get a scenic view of the sunset visit the ‘Noka Vihar’ and take a boat ride in the Pachmarhi Lake here. Proceed to Dhoopgarh which is the ‘highest peak’ in the Pachmarhi region. Return to your hotel for night stay.

Day 3 is the final day and after a filling breakfast, you will check out of the hotel. The My Quick Trippers representative will assist you safely to the point from where you will return home with unforgettable memories.

Ans. A tasty and wildly popular street food from Madhya Pradesh is called Bhutte ki Kees. Essentially, this dish is prepared from crushed, sautéed corn.
Q4. Which River Is Near Pachmarhi?

Ans. A branch of the Tawa River, the Denwa River meets the Narmada River close to Bandrabhan. Dhar, Dudher, Nagdwari, and Sonbhadra are tributaries of the Denwa River, which receives drainage from the entire Pachmarhi plateau.
Q5. Which Time Of Year Is Ideal For Pachmarhi?

Ans. Pachmarhi is beautiful year-round, although summer is the ideal season to visit. The summertime climate of Pachmarhi is temperate, with temperatures ranging from 22 to 35 degrees Celsius. Despite the fact that Pachmarhi is a hill station and has beautiful summers, the days are warmer than the nights.

blocks.text: Explore South India’s famous temples with the Pancha Bootha Sthalam Navagraha Tour Package.
Day 1: Tirupati - Srikalahasti - Kanchipuram (Approx. 175 kms/ 3-4 Hours)

Start your tour with a pick-up from your chosen spot in Tirupati, whether it’s the airport, railway station, or any other location. Our My Quick Trippers team will pick you up and help you all day. If you book a guide, they will join the driver to assist during sightseeing. After pick-up, you will start your tour and visit- Srikalahasteeswara Temple: Part of the Pancha Bootha temples, which represents the Air element (Vaayu). A fascinating fact about this temple is that a lamp keeps moving on its own, even without any wind. Once the darshan is complete, travel to Kanchipuram. On arrival, check into your hotel for the night. Note: Srikalahasteeswara Temple is open from 6 am to 9 pm. Places You’ll See

After breakfast check out of the hotel and visit Kamakshi Amman Temple, dedicated to Goddess Kamakshi. This temple is also one of the Shakti Peethas, where Goddess Sati’s navel ( nabhi ) fell. Then, see Varadharaja Perumal Temple , a famous Vishnu temple and one of the 108 Divya Desams. Now continue the journey to the Kailasanathar Temple , which is around 1,300 years old, dedicated to Lord Shiva. Then proceed to Ekambareswarar Temple, which represents the Earth element ( Prithvi ). Travel to Kumarakottam Temple , dedicated to Lord Murugan. If time permits, you can also visit Kanchipuram’s markets, famous for silk sarees. Later, drive to Tiruvannamalai. This town is known for the Annamalaiyar Temple. The temple is one of the largest in India and is part of the Pancha Bootha, connected to Fire (Agni). This place is beautiful, so don’t forget to take some photos. When you arrive, check into your hotel and stay overnight in Tiruvannamalai. Night stay at Tiruvannamalai Places You’ll See
DAY 3: Tiruvannamalai – Pondicherry - Chidambaram - Kumbakonam (205 - 210 kms/ 5.5-6 Hours)

After breakfast check out from the hotel and drive to Pondicherry. Visit Auroville Matrimandir , where people from different parts of the world come to meditate and experience peace. Try to meditate here - this place is known for its inner peace. Then check into your hotel and visit Sri Aurobindo Ashram, one of India’s most famous and wealthiest ashrams, where people from across the world come for spiritual peace. Next, travel to Arulmigu Manakula Vinayagar Temple, dedicated to Lord Ganesh. Then visit Puducherry Museum , famous for its impressive collection of 81 ancient metal statues from India’s history. You will love the artwork ! Later, drive to Chidambaram, a town famous for the Thillai Nataraja Temple, spread over 40 acres. Nataraja Temple is one of the Pancha Bootha temples and represents the element of Sky (Akasha). After that, proceed to Kumbakonam. If time permits, explore two temples - Gangaikonda Cholapuram and Vaitheeswaran Koil. Note- Puducherry Museum remains closed on Mondays and public holidays. Places You’ll See

Morning after breakfast, check out of the hotel and proceed for sightseeing in Kumbakonam a town famous for its many temples. Explore Adi Kumbeswarar Temple and also visit the nearby Mahamaham Tank where pilgrims take a holy bath. Then go to Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Next continue your Navagraha temple tour and visit Thingalur (Moon), Alangudi (Jupiter), Thirunageswaram (Rahu), Suriyanar Kovil (Sun), Kanjanur (Venus), Vaitheeswaran Koil (Mars), Thiruvenkadu (Mercury), Keezhaperumpallam (Ketu) and Thirunallar temple (Saturn). After completing the temple visits return to your hotel in Kumbakonam for an overnight stay. Places You’ll See

After breakfast, drive to Thanjavur (Tanjore). On arrival, visit Brihadeeswara Temple , the main attraction of Thanjavur and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its tall vimana tower is so high that you can see it from miles away - it feels like it touches the sky (a great photo spot). Visit Thanjavur Palace next, where the Maratha rulers lived from 1674 to 1855. Then, visit Thanjavur Art Gallery to see a collection of old metal and stone statues and other historic items from Tamil history. Later, drive to Tiruchirappalli (Trichy). On arrival, check into the hotel for an overnight stay. Places You’ll See

After breakfast, check out from your hotel and begin your sightseeing tour of Tiruchirapalli (Trichy). Your first stop will be the famous Sri Ranganatha Swamy Temple in Srirangam - one of the 108 holy Vishnu temple known as Divya Desams. Next, proceed to Jambukeswarar Akilandeswari Temple , this temple is part of Pancha Bhoota temples and represents Water. You can see water naturally flowing around the Shiva Lingam and even if you remove the water, it comes back - this is a unique fact here. Then, visit the Ucchi Pillayar Temple , dedicated to Lord Ganesha, and located on the top of Rockfort (a beautiful spot to click pictures). Next, stop at the Government Museum in Rani Mangammal Mahal. From old paintings to fossils and old items, the museum is full of fascinating things that visitors will enjoy exploring! After that, go to the Butterfly Park and see colorful butterflies all around. Then, visit Nakshatra Vanam , a special garden with 27 trees linked to stars and 12 trees representing the zodiac signs. Your Pancha Bootha Sthalam and Navagraha Tour finishes with happy memories, and later we will drop you at Trichy Airport or railway station for your home. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: The Prayagraj Maha Kumbh Mela is the largest religious gathering attracting people from all over the world.

Kumbh Mela was recognised by UNESCO in 2017. It was listed among the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO as it's not just a religious gathering, it is a congregation of diverse people and cultures that promotes harmony.

According to Hindu mythology, Kumbh Mela is associated with the legend of Samudra Manthan (the churning of ocean) where the drops of nectar fell on the four Kumbh locations and hence the Mela is held every 12 years rotating between these four locations Prayagraj (Allahabad), Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nashik.

We have well curated packages for our travelers that offer comfortable accommodation, safe transfers, sightseeing and meals. Our packages are customizable, allowing travelers the flexibility to tailor the itinerary according to their personal preferences. This Maha Kumbh Mela is once in a lifetime experience not to be missed. So, what are you waiting for? Plan your dates, explore our Kumbh Mela tour packages and book the best suited one for you.
Kumbh Mela is famous for its historical and mythological stories that attract a lot of devotees:

items: In the 7th century, a Chinese traveler Xuanzang wrote about Prayagraj. He described its temples and rituals, indicating that the Kumbh Mela began during that time.

Kumbh Mela is also popular for it’s another story, because it is believed that Lord Vishnu was carrying a pot of Amrit (nectar), which fell in specific places like Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik, and Ujjain. People who drink the nectar become immortal. After this event, these spots are important in Hinduism.
Prayagraj is mentioned in the Rigveda and Buddhist writings. These writings describe that being good is more important than taking baths for cleanliness.

Another interesting part of Prayagraj’s history is found in the Mahabharata. It is said that the Pandavas came to Prayagraj to perform rituals for their ancestors. This place is holy because performing rituals here strengthens the bond between living people and their family members who have already passed away.

blocks.text: What Tourists Can Expect at Kumbh Mela 2025
In 2025, there will be a huge crowd of people. Pilgrims, sadhus, and visitors from all over the world will come to Prayagraj for this spiritual event. The main events at the Kumbh Mela are:

Sadhus and Akharas - A big highlight of the Kumbh Mela is the sadhus, or holy men. They are respected for their discipline and spiritual knowledge. Sadhus are a part of different groups called Akharas. Some sadhus focus on their spiritual goals, while others offer blessings to visitors.

Shahi Snan- During the Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj, sadhus take a holy dip in the river before other people, this ritual is known as the Shahi Snan. Visitors can enjoy the energy of the chanting and music during the royal bath at the Kumbh Mela.

Spiritual discussions and cultural activities- At the Kumbh Mela, spiritual leaders talk about Hindu philosophy like rituals, moral values, and life lessons. Tourists can also go for cultural shows, including dance performances, folk art displays, and music events.

items: You can fly to Prayagraj Airport (Bamrauli Airport), located just 15 kilometers from the Kumbh Mela.
Taxis or auto-rickshaws are easily available at the airport to reach Mela.
The nearest main railway station is Prayagraj junction, which is connected to many cities.
When you reach, local transport options, like auto-rickshaws or taxis are available for the Mela.
You can reach Prayagraj by bus or vehicle. Convenient bus services are available, including many private buses from nearby areas.

blocks.text: While in Prayagraj, tourists should explore city’s popular historical and cultural attractions:

items: Triveni Sangam - This is the meeting point of three holy rivers - the Ganges, Yamuna, and Saraswati Rivers.
Allahabad Fort - This fort was built by Emperor Akbar. Tourists can enjoy great views of the rivers, and it is a perfect place to explore history.
Anand Bhawan - It was the home of Jawaharlal Nehru (Gandhi family). Now there is a museum inside, visitors can see personal belongings, photographs, and documents of the Nehru family.
Swaraj Bhawan - It is a special place where you can learn about India's struggle for freedom.

blocks.text: Travel Tips for the Kumbh Mela

items: Choose a meeting point - When you are traveling with family or friends, make sure to decide a specific area to meet, if you get lost in the crowd.
Phone network : Purchase a local SIM card for a better connection because SIM cards from other states cannot work well.
Book accommodation in advance : Make sure to book your hotel in advance and choose a location a bit away from the event area to avoid crowds.
Keep yourself hydrated : Drink enough water, especially during rituals and carry a water bottle with you.
Use apps to manage crowds : Some apps can track crowded places and suggest less busy paths.
Have emergency contacts : Keep local emergency numbers and find out where the nearest hospitals or clinics are.

blocks.text: The Kumbh Mela is a spiritual event and the biggest fair in India, with a long history and traditions. It started in the 7th century and is connected to the stories of Lord Vishnu’s nectar of immortality. Pilgrims from around the world visit Prayagraj for celebration. This city is mentioned in ancient texts like the Rig Veda and Mahabharata.

The main highlights of Kumbh Mela 2025 include the Shahi Snan, where sadhus or visitors take a holy dip, along with spiritual discussions on Hindu teachings. Tourists can also enjoy cultural activities with unique experiences. For a smooth trip, travelers are advised to book hotels in advance, use local SIM cards for good connectivity, and stay hydrated. They can also explore Prayagraj’s famous attractions, like Triveni Sangam, Anand Bhawan, Allahabad Fort and more places. With careful planning, visitors can connect with the spiritual energy of the Kumbh Mela and create the best memories.
Q1: What are the things visitors can buy during Kumbh Mela?
Ans. There are many things to purchase, such as religious items, handmade artifacts, spiritual books, holy water from the Ganges, clothes and many more.
Q2: What is the duration of Kumbh Mela?
Ans. Kumbh Mela usually takes 1 to 3 months and visitors have plenty of time to explore.
Q3: Do tourists need any permit to visit this fair?
Ans. No, a permit is not required to enter Kumbh Mela, but international visitors should carry ID proof.
Q4: How can I stay updated on event schedules?
Ans. You can check official websites for the event date and venue.
Q5: How can I avoid overcrowded routes?
Ans. Arrive early or use crowd management apps to avoid the busiest areas for a smoother journey.

blocks.text: Odisha is known as the soul of India for good reason. A well-planned Bhubaneswar Puri Konark Tour Package lets you experience the state's most iconic destinations within a compact 70 km triangle — Puri, Konark Sun Temple, and Bhubaneswar. Puri is one of the four sacred Char Dhams, home to the Jagannath Temple and the world-famous Rath Yatra. Konark's Sun Temple, built in the 13th century, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the finest examples of Kalinga architecture. Bhubaneswar, with over 600 ancient temples, is the historic capital that started it all.

This Bhubaneswar Puri Konark trip covers all three cities in 4 days and 3 nights. Hotel stays, daily breakfast, private AC vehicle, airport pickup, and an English-speaking guide are included. You visit the Jagannath Temple, Konark Sun Temple , Chilika Lake, Khandagiri-Udayagiri Caves, Dhauli Stupa, and Pipli village — in a well-paced circuit that works for first-time visitors, families, and pilgrims alike.

Rath Yatra 2026 falls on July 16. If you plan to visit around that date, book at least 8 weeks in advance — hotels across Puri fill up fast. The Jagannath Temple also closes for 14 days during Anavasara (after Snana Purnima, roughly June–July) when Darshan is not available. Our team flags these dates at the time of booking.
Best Time to Visit Puri, Konark & Bhubaneswar

rows: Pleasant weather, active dolphin season at Chilika, clear skies at Konark
Warm but manageable; good for temple visits in early morning
High heat and humidity; outdoor temple circuits are exhausting

items: Rath Yatra — July 16, 2026: Lord Jagannath's chariot procession from the main temple to Gundicha Temple. The Jagannath Temple remains closed this day, but all visitors — including non-Hindus — can have darshan of the deities on the chariots. Puri hotels fill up 2–3 months ahead.
Bahuda Yatra (Return) — July 25, 2026: The chariots return and the Suna Besha ritual follows — deities adorned in gold.
Anavasara Closure — approx. mid-June to early July 2026: Temple closed for 14 days after Snana Purnima. Exact dates confirmed by our team at time of booking.
Konark Dance Festival — December 1–5, 2026: Classical dance performances at the open-air amphitheatre at Konark Sun Temple.

blocks.text: Konark Sun Temple Light & Sound Show 2026

The Konark Sun Temple hosts a nightly Light & Sound Show after regular visiting hours. The 40-minute show narrates the history of King Narasimhadeva I and the Sun God Surya through projected lights and audio. Wireless headphones are provided in Hindi, English, or Odia.

items: March to November: 7:30 PM and 8:20 PM (two shows nightly)
December to February: 6:30 PM and 7:30 PM (two shows nightly)

blocks.text: Ticket Price: ₹30 per person (separate from temple entry ticket of ₹40)

Tickets are available at the Konark site entrance or online on the ASI e-ticketing portal. Online booking is recommended during peak season (October–February). This show is an optional add-on — not included in the package price. If you want to attend, let us know at the time of booking and we will adjust the Day 2 schedule to allow for it.

By Air Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar (IATA: BBI) is connected to Delhi (approx. 2 hours), Mumbai (2.5 hours), and Kolkata (1 hour). Puri is 60 km from the airport, around 1.5 hours by road. Our representative meets you at the terminal exit.

By Train Bhubaneswar Railway Station is on the Howrah–Chennai main line. Key trains from Delhi: Bhubaneswar Rajdhani (22–25 hours). From Kolkata: multiple express trains (5–6 hours). Puri Railway Station also receives direct trains from Kolkata and Delhi — pickup from both stations is available.

By Road Delhi to Bhubaneswar: approx. 1,750 km via NH44 (26–28 hours by overnight bus or self-drive). Kolkata to Bhubaneswar: 480 km via NH16, 7–8 hours. All transfers within this tour — Bhubaneswar to Konark (65 km), Konark to Puri (35 km) — are covered by the package vehicle.

Enjoy a restful night of sleep at the hotel.

blocks.text: Q1. What is the price of the Bhubaneswar Puri Konark tour package in 2026?

Ans: Starting from ₹13,250 per person on twin sharing (4 days/3 nights from Bhubaneswar). Price covers hotel, daily breakfast, private AC vehicle, guide, and all transfers. Meals other than breakfast and entry fees are extra.
Q2. What is included in the package?

Ans: Hotel stay (twin sharing), daily breakfast, private AC vehicle for all transfers and sightseeing, airport/railway pickup and drop, English-speaking guide, drinking water, driver allowance, toll, and parking. GST included.
Q3. Are there any hidden charges?
Ans: No hidden charges. Monument entry fees are extra — Konark Sun Temple ₹40 (Indians), Khandagiri-Udayagiri Caves ₹15 (Indians). Lunches, dinners, and personal expenses are also not included.
Q4. Can non-Hindus visit the Jagannath Temple?

Ans: Non-Hindus are not allowed inside the main temple. They can view the 65-metre Vimana tower and Sudarshana Chakra from the Raghunandan Library rooftop, opposite the main gate. During Rath Yatra (July 16, 2026), all visitors can have darshan of the deities on the chariots.
Q5. What are the Jagannath Temple darshan timings?
Ans: Temple opens at 5:00 AM and closes at midnight. Best time: before 8:00 AM or after 4:00 PM. Mid-day sees partial closures for ritual food offerings. Entry is free for all Hindu devotees.
Q6. When is the Jagannath Temple closed in 2026?
Ans: The temple closes for 14 days during Anavasara (after Snana Purnima, approx. June–July 2026). Exact dates are confirmed by our team before booking is finalised for June–July travel.
Q7. What is the Konark Light & Sound Show and is it included?

Ans: It is an evening show at Konark Sun Temple — 40 minutes, two shows nightly, tickets ₹30. It is not included in the package. If you want to attend, inform us at booking and we adjust the Day 2 schedule.
Q8. Is this tour suitable for senior citizens?
Ans: Yes. All sites are accessed by vehicle with short, flat walks. Jagannath Temple has priority entry for senior citizens. Chilika is a boat ride with no trekking involved.
Q9. What is the best time to visit Puri and Konark?
Ans: October to February is the most comfortable — cool weather and active Chilika dolphin season. Avoid May–June (extreme heat). For Rath Yatra, plan around July 16, 2026 and book 8 weeks ahead.
Q10. How many days are enough for this Odisha circuit?
Ans: 4 days/3 nights is sufficient for the main highlights. A 5-day extension can include Raghurajpur Craft Village or Sakshi Gopal Temple. Contact us for customised options.
Q11. Can I customise this package?
Ans: Yes. Duration, hotel category, and departure point can all be adjusted. Call or WhatsApp +91-8171158569 for a custom quote based on your group size and dates.
Q12. How do I reach Bhubaneswar from Delhi or Kolkata?

Ans: From Delhi: direct flights (2 hours) to Biju Patnaik Airport or Rajdhani Express (22–25 hours). From Kolkata: express trains to Bhubaneswar (5–6 hours) or direct to Puri. Pickup from both airport and railway station is included.

blocks.text: Our Puri Tour Packages are available from Delhi to Puri, catering to all budget styles. From visiting major attractions like Puri Jagannath Temple, Sun Temple , Chilika Lake to Chandrabhaga beach, to arranging for guided Darshan, you will get a hassle free Puri journey with My Quick Trippers.

Going to Puri is like diving deep into the world of serenity and eternal bliss. This eastern Indian state of Odisha is located on Bay of Bengal. It houses the most famous Jagannath Temple (incarnation of Lord Krishna) which today is a major pilgrimage site for Hindu devotees.

Giving a beautiful contrast to the intensity of the temple, the soul pleasing beaches are ideal for enjoying sunsets and beach walks. The sacred Pancha Tirtha (five sacred bathing sites) adds charm to the sacred Jagannath pilgrimage experience by offering Nirvana to the devotees. A trip to Puri is not an ordinary journey, it's a voyage to the mystical realm where liberation burns within the soul's deepest frame.

According to recent records, the number of tourists visiting Puri in 2023-2024 was around 1.10 crore at the end of the year. This shows a remarkable growth in tourism related revenues in Puri. blocks.text: October to February are the less crowded months to plan a wonderful Puri trip with your family. The winter months in Puri are the best time to plan your Puri sightseeing holidays along with outdoor adventure activities like bird watching, boating and swimming etc.
Festival Months to Visit in Puri

June to September months is best to enjoy the iconic festival of Rath Yatra in Puri. These months welcome the monsoon in Puri. Tourists experience heavy rainfall, high humidity and thunderstorms which might hinder plans for outdoor adventure and sightseeing. But these months are best to enjoy the Rath Yatra Festival, Devotees in large numbers visit Puri during this time to see the grand chariot of Lord Jagannath. But for general tourism, it is not the best time to plan your trip to Puri.
Best Time to Book Puri Tour Packages for Cheaper Rates

You can book affordable Puri Travel packages in summer months (March to May). It's the off-season for the Puri sightseeing tour but you will get budget hotels, transportation and packages. During this time, the most prominent attractions- Puri Temple, Puri beach, Konark Sun Temple, etc. will be less crowded. If you prefer peace and are a budget conscious traveller then you must book a Puri trip during these months.
Best Places to Visit in Puri on Your Trip
Some of the key attractions included in our Puri Tour Packages are-

rows: Puri's most popular pilgrimage destination for Hindu devotees. The king Anantavarman Chodaganga of Eastern Ganga dynasty in the 12th century built this sacred shrine in Kalinga style.
Puri Beach is a fantastic destination to relax your senses amidst the clear waters, golden sands, cool breeze, sunrise and sunset views.

A beautiful UNESCO World Heritage Site, Konark Sun temple is a legacy of King Narsimha Deva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, built in the 134th century. It is a must visit place to embrace the heritage of Odisha.

Don't miss Asia's largest brackish water lagoon on the beautiful eastern coastline of Odisha. It is the one of the most famous places in Puri to visit for recreation and witness the faunal wealth of the lake like endangered Irrawaddy dolphins, flamingos and pelicans etc.

It is an international wetland Bird Sanctuary to visit for nature lovers, couples, families and bird watchers in Puri. It opens from October to March. It houses around 150 species of birds like flamingos, bar-headed geese, grey herons, Spoon-billed Sandpipers etc.

blocks.text: Apart from being known as the land of palaces and maharajas, Rajasthan is also one of the prime romantic destinations. With the atmosphere enveloped in colorful beauty and surreal landscapes, Rajasthan can be your next favorite exotic destination for you and your better half. Explore the many vibrant faces of Rajasthan with My Quick Trippers’s, 6 days and 5 nights romantic tour of Rajasthan.

You will be transferred to your allotted hotel upon your arrival in Jaipur. Later you will be taken on a brief sightseeing tour of the city like – Hawa Mahal (palace of winds) – one of the most prominent landmarks of the city, representing the fine craftsmanship of the city; you will also be taken to Jantar Mantar – which is one of the most well preserved observatories in the subcontinent.
You will finally be taken back to your hotel for an overnight stay.

Post breakfast, you will be taken on a brief excursion of Amber Fort palace – which is a classic sign of romance, and perched atop a large platform from where you can take a breathtaking view of the Jaipur city; Nahargarh fort will be your next destination which is located all along the Aravali ranges. Next stop for you will be the holy Laxmi Narayan temple – a Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Laxmi and Lord Vishnu.
Later in the evening, you will be made to visit the teeming colorful marketplaces of Jaipur.
You can shop for locally made souvenirs like – traditional blue pottery, camel leather products, lac bangles, silk quilts, Jaipur handicrafts, bandhej and many more.
You also have the freedom to try out some delectable cuisines like – dal baati churma, laal maas, the iconic Rajasthani thali, Kachori and a whole plethora of others.

You will be driven to Pushkar in the morning after breakfast, which is located at a distance of 2 hours and 40 mines. Upon arriving at Pushkar you will be immediately checked in to your hotel for staying the night. After freshening up you will be taken to Brahma Mandir – one of the few temples that is dedicated to Lord Brahma. It is a common belief that the Lord had personally chosen Pushkar as the temple site making it extremely pious. You will then proceed towards the sacred Pushkar Lake – which is surrounded by 52 bathing ghats and a dip here is believed to cleanse all your sins and skin related diseases.
After spending a memorable day in one of the most fascinating destinations in India, you will then be made to head back to your hotel.

Early in the morning, you will be made to head for Udaipur, which is located at a distance of 5 hours and 10 mines. Upon arriving at this beautifully enchanting town you will be made to check in to your hotel for a night stay.

Your sightseeing tour of Udaipur will commence in the morning starting with a visit to the famous city Palace museum – a beautifully created palace complex, which has served as the resident place for numerous ruling dynasties. Jagdish Mandir will be your next destination, which is situated just outside the royal city palace and is dedicated to Lord Jagannath and is one of the major tourist attractions in Udaipur. Saheliyon ki bari will be your next destination, a beautiful garden complete with numerous fountains, lotus pools and elephant statues made of marble. You will then be taken to bhartiya lok kala mandir which is a folk art museum.
After a day of exploration and fun you will be guided back to your hotel for staying the night.
After the completion of your breakfast, you will be transferred to the airport or railway station from where you will depart towards Delhi and onto your desired location.

blocks.text: Q1. Is Rajasthan Suitable For A Honeymoon?

Ans. However, if you are celebrating your honeymoon during the winter and want to experience some royalty as a couple, there is no better place to go than Rajasthan. Rajasthan, one of India's most romantic honeymoon destinations, has many charming places offering a variety of romantic things to do, attractions to visit, and places to stay.
Q2. When Is The Best Time To Go On A Honeymoon In Rajasthan?

Ans. Other than winter, the monsoon season is the best time to visit Rajasthan. The honeymoon months of July to September (Monsoon) are ideal, when the arid and barren landscape transforms into a lush green haven.
Q3. What Is Rajasthan's Distinguishing Feature?

Ans. The ruins of the Indus Valley civilisation at Kalibangan and Balathal, the Dilwara Temples, a Jain pilgrimage site at Rajasthan's only hill station, Mount Abu, in the ancient Aravalli mountain range and eastern Rajasthan, and the Keoladeo National Park of Bharatpur, a World Heritage Site, are among its major attractions.
Q4. What Are Rajasthani Eating Habits?

Ans. Rajasthani cuisine is influenced by the state's rich heritage and arid climate. Their cuisine is distinguished by the scarcity of fresh fruits and vegetables. Beans, lentils, gramme flour, corn, barley, millet, bajra, bread, and dairy products are all common ingredients (esp. Ghee).
Q5. What Is The Name Of Rajasthani Clothing?

Ans. Rajasthani women traditionally wear Ghagra, Choli (also known as Kanchli or Kurti), and Odhni. The Ghagra is a full-length, embroidered and pleated skirt available in a wide range of colours, prints, and fabrics such as silk, cotton, georgette, and crêpe.

blocks.text: Best Places to Visit in Rajasthan on Your Trip

Rajasthan has a splendid past of ancient Rajasthan rulers. The ceremonial lifestyle and bravery of royal Rajput families are being reproduced from its heritage and historical destination. In 2025 Rajasthan saw a massive surge in tourist footfall. The state welcomed 37.8 million domestic tourists in just the first two months (January and February) of 2025 which shows that it is one of the most visited tourist destinations in India. ( Source : Rajasthan Tourism. Online ). Mentioned here are the list of the best places to visit in Rajasthan, covered in our Rajasthan tour itinerary.

items: Known as Pink city, Jaipur is one of the top tourist destinations to visit in Rajasthan. Founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh, It was one of the earliest planned cities of India. Domestic as well as international travellers cannot resist the charm of Jaipur. It boasts of majestic forts, palaces, and colorful markets which display royal extravagance.
Some of the best places to visit here are Hawa Mahal, Amber Fort, City Palace, Jal Mahal, Johri Bazaar, Bapu Bazaar and Chokhi Dhani.
Dominated by the imposing Fort of Mehrangarh, the blue city of Jodhpur attracts the traveler from far and wide.

Forts, palaces, temples and havelies, its attractions reflect royal splendour. Explore Jaswant Thada, the scenic white marble cenotaph, the majestic Umaid Bhawan Palace, beautiful alleys of Navchowkiya, Turji Ka Jhalra, Mehrangarh Fort, Chamunda Mata Ji Temple etc.

Located at the heart of Thar Desert, Jaisalmer, the golden city will mesmerize you with its awe inspiring forts and Palaces. See the most beautiful Jaisalmer Fort, famed for yellow sandstone architecture.
Also visit the scenic havelies like Patwon Ki Haveli and Nathmal Ki Haveli, known for intricate carvings.
One must not miss the city's Jain temple heritage. There are 7 Jain temples located inside the fort, highlighting the artistic and religious heritage of India.
Bliss of Southern Rajasthan, Udaipur, the city of Lakes which will take your breath away with its scenic beauty.
Explore Saheliyon ki Bari, famed for its scenic fountains and lotus pool, beautiful Fateh Sagar Lake and Lake Pichola which offers stunning views and recreation opportunities with family and friends.
Also explore Jag Mandir, the stunning lake garden palace and Taj Lake Palace, the white marble beauty.
Renowned for the tranquil Pushkar Lake and is home to one of the world's few Brahma temples, Pushkar offers solace to Peace seekers. It is also known as Tirthraj.
The lively fairs and spiritual vibe of Pushkar makes it one of the most sought after stops for travellers.
Pushkar's lively fairs and spiritual ambience make it a captivating stop for pilgrims and travelers

Located in the Southwest direction of Jaipur, Ajmer is a popular religious attraction for both Hindu and Muslims. It is a final resting place of a renowned Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti. Hindu and Muslims devotees from all across the globe visit Ajmer Sharif Dargah to honor the shrine of the Sufi saint and get his divine blessings.
It is also a very popular Jain pilgrimage spot. Visit Jain Golden temple which is also known as Soni Ji Ki Nasiya which Honours Lord Rishabhdev (Adinath).
The land of Chittorgarh has kept the stories of bravery, passion and pride intact through its rich culture and heritage. The city is named after the magnificent structure of Chittorgarh Fort.
There are many places to explore in Chittorgarh which you must not miss such as Chittorgarh Fort, Vijay Stambh, Kirti Stambh, Fateh Prakash Palace, Kalika Mata Temple and Tulja Bhavani temple etc.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Rajasthan on your Trip

Rajasthan has so much to offer to the travellers that might get confused what to do here. What you want to do will depend on your interest and energy. There is something to enjoy for everyone. We have picked the best activities to do in Rajasthan. Based on your interests, you can customize your Rajasthan tour packages and add the best things as per your preferences.

items: Zip-Lining in Rajasthan is a must try adventure activity if you are a thrill seeker. It is available at many locations which combine thrill with heritage views.

You can try Zip-lining in Mehrangarh Fort. The six thrilling Ziplines here will cover the entire fort, battlements and the desert lake. It will take 90 minutes to get the best views of Mehrangarh fort and Jodhpur.
You can also try Zip lining at Neemrana Fort Palace. It is India's first heritage Zip line. Through zip-lining you will get the stunning views of Aravalli hills and the entire Neemrana Fort.

Rajasthan boasts of some of the best wildlife and bird Sanctuaries in India. You can enjoy wildlife safari at Ranthambore National Park, Sariska National Park, Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary or Keoladeo National Park.
You can also go for camel safari and stay in a luxury desert camp in Thar Desert near Jaisalmer or Bikaner.
Enjoy the beauty of star-lit sky, cultural folk music performances and dances, delicious traditional meals, puppet shows and cozy beddings while camping in Rajasthan.
Don't miss the village themed resort- Chokhi Dhani in Jaipur while enjoying your sightseeing here. If you want to truly experience Rajasthan's culture and heritage then Chokhi Dhani is a must visit.
Here you will enjoy many cultural shows and performances like Kalbeliya, Ghoomar and Chari dance and other most popular shows like Puppet shows, traditional fire act, and bamboo acrobatics.
Also enjoy the drama enactment of the famous battle of Haldighati which displays the courage of Maharana Pratap and other Rajputs.
There are many rides to enjoy here like Camel rides, elephant rides, horseback rides, bullock cart rides and boat rides in a village lake called Tal Talaiya.
Trekking in Rajasthan is a perfect blend of adventure, heritage fort routes and scenic views. October to March are the best months to enjoy trekking here.

Alwar and Mount Abu have the best trekking trails for adventure lovers. You can also enjoy trekking in Jaipur at Nahargarh Fort. It's a 1-2 hours moderate trek which starts from the city to Aravalli hills and ends at the Historical Nahargarh Fort.
Jawai Hills are also perfect for trekking in Rajasthan. It boasts of dramatic granite domes, natural caves and volcanic trails.
Enjoy a fun-filled day with Elephants at Dera Amer. Here you can enjoy exciting elephant rides and join them on long walks through the desert scrub.
The tranquil desert views, organically local grown food, dining near elephants in a natural setting and spacious tents will make your camping at Dera Amer memorable forever.

Rural Tourism in Rajasthan offers rich experiences of traditional village life, eco-tourism, cultural and heritage of the region. You must visit some of the most beautiful villages like Bishnoi Village near Jodhpur which offers tourists a chance to see the village lifestyle, animal conservation practices, pottery and cow milking techniques.
Also visit, Mandwa, Khimar, and Khuri, Samode to experience village culture, festivals , learn organic farming, enjoy traditional music, dances and savor most authentic Rajasthan cuisines.

blocks.text: Useful Travel Tips to for Memorable Rajasthan Holidays
Here are some most useful travel tips for safe and fun-filled holidays in Rajasthan with your family and friends-

items: Best time to Visit- Plan your Rajasthan tour in peak tourism months (October- March). During this time the weather will be fantastic for sightseeing and outdoor adventure activities. Though, you will have to book your tickets and hotels in advance due to the peak tourism season. You will also witness crowds at famous tourist spots in Rajasthan.

Duration- At least spend 7-12 days to enjoy a comprehensive Rajasthan Tour. Rajasthan has many opulent places, and forts, temples, bustling bazaars, and many adventure opportunities. It is not possible to cover the best of Rajasthan in just 2-3 days. In a short duration you will only be able to see only one or two places. It is not enough for the best Rajasthan trip experience. So, plan your duration to cover most of Rajasthan.

Advance Booking- Advance booking is important if you are trying zip lining and other adventure activities in Rajasthan in peak tourism season. If you wish to enjoy camping at desert camps then also you need to book your luxury tent in advance.
Comfort over Budget- If comfort is your priority then we recommend you to hire a private car or taxi for Rajasthan sightseeing. If you are travelling with kids or elders then, it is the best option.
Cultural Experiences- Don't miss places where you will get a chance to listen to folk music and see dance performances for authentic cultural immersion.

What to Pack- In winters, carry jackets, woolen clothes as the temperature during this time will be 10-27°C.In summer, carry light breathable fabric, stoles and comfortable footwear. During Monsoon, carry a raincoat, rain gear, light jackets and sturdy shoes.
Cash- Carry enough cash to buy souvenirs from small vendors and shopkeepers. If you are visiting rural areas, you may not find digital payment options.
Anti-Theft Bag- Take special care of your belongings. Carry Anti-theft bags to keep your important documents like passport, ID, license and cash etc. safe.
Emergency Contact- Keep emergency numbers of relevant persons whom you can approach anytime for help during unforeseen circumstances apart from tour operators.
Safety- Always hire licensed operators for adventure activities who provide safety gears. Check their ID and expiry date of the license.
Modest Clothing- Wear covered clothes at sacred sites. Respect the culture and customs of the spiritual places.

blocks.content: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary, also known as Sasan Gir, is a national park and wildlife sanctuary in Gujarat, India. It was established in 1965 in the erstwhile Nawab of Junagarh's private hunting area, with a total area of 1,410.30 km2 (544.52 sq mi), of which 258.71 km2 (99.89 sq mi) is fully protected as a national park and 1,151.59 km2 (444.63 sq mi) as wildlife sanctuary. It is part of the Khathiar-Gir dry deciduous forests ecoregion.

Gir National Park is renowned for its rich cultural heritage, historical significance, and diverse attractions. From ancient temples and forts to modern amenities and natural beauty, Gir National Park offers an unforgettable experience for every traveler.

blocks.text: The Madurai Rameshwaram Kanyakumari tour package shows you temples, beaches, beautiful landscapes and rich South Indian culture. Journey begins in Madurai famous for its Meenakshi Amman Temple. An interesting fact about this temple is that it has around 33,000 carvings and statues covering every corner..

items: Route: Madurai - Rameshwaram → In Rameswaram - Full day Sightseeing Tour → Rameswaram - Kanyakumari → Kanyakumari - Kovalam - Thiruvananthapuram → Thiruvananthapuram

blocks.text: Day 1: Madurai - Rameshwaram (173 km / 4 Hours Drive)

Our My Quick Trippers representative will meet you at Madurai Airport or Railway Station to start your tour comfortably. If you’ve booked a guide, they will join the driver to help you throughout the day. After pick-up, your Madurai sightseeing tour includes: Meenakshi Amman Temple- This temple has a unique ritual. In the past, 1,000 thousands of devotees joined Goddess Meenakshi i’s wedding, and this tradition continues in cultural festivals. Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple On arrival in Rameshwaram, check in at the hotel. Later, visit: Ramanathaswamy Temple Agni Theertham- This holy beach is where pilgrims dip to wash away their sins. Ramjharoka Temple After sightseeing enjoy an overnight stay in Rameshwaram. Note- Agni Theertham is best to visit early morning, when many devotees take a holy dip. Places You’ll See
Day 2: In Rameswaram - Full day Sightseeing Tour

Early in the morning, around 5:00 AM , proceed to the Spatika Linga Darshan, also called Mani Darshan , where the natural crystal Shivling (not man-made) is very important in Hinduism and looks very beautiful. Later you will head out for Agni Teertham to have a holy bath in the sea. Further proceed to the main temple through North gate and Take sacred bath with holy water of the 22 wells, inside the Ramanathaswamy Temple during Theerth Snanam. Then proceed for darshan and pooja at the main temple. After the holy bath and Darshan, return to the hotel for breakfast. After breakfast, proceed for a sightseeing tour of Rameshwaram, which covers the Five-faced Hanuman Temple (famous for floating stones from Ram Setu), Ramar Patham, Kothandaramaswamy Temple, Gandamadana Parvatham (a hilltop temple with Rama’s footprint and beautiful views), Rama Setu/Adam’s Bridge (the chain of stones said to be built by Rama’s army), Former President A. P. J. Abdul Kalam’s House, and Dhanushkodi. Note- The APJ Museum opens at 7am and closes at 8pm. Places You’ll See

Early in the morning, visit the temple again or take a Samudra Snanam (holy dip in the sea). After breakfast, leave the hotel and go to Kanyakumari, where the Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, and Indian Ocean meet. It's a beautiful spot to take photos. Kanyakumari is famous as the only place on earth where you can see both sunrise and sunset over the ocean. Kanyakumari is famous as the only place on earth where you can see the sunrise over the Bay of Bengal and the sunset over the Arabian Sea. On arrival, check into the hotel and rest. Overnight stay at the hotel. Places You’ll See
Day 4: Kanyakumari - Kovalam - Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) (100 Kms/3 Hr )

Early in the morning, you can watch the beautiful sunrise in Kanyakumari. The calm atmosphere makes it a perfect time to take pictures. After breakfast visit the Swami Vivekananda Rock Memorial and its meditation hall where you can meditate for some time. Walk over the Sea by Glass bridge to reach Thiruvalluvar Statue. Next, visit Kanyakumari Mandir (Kumari Amman Temple). This temple is built in Kerala-style architecture, so just get ready to click photos. Then, see the point where the three oceans meet. Stop near Gandhi Mandapam, where Mahatma Gandhi’s ashes were once kept for public viewing. Don’t forget the Thiruvalluvar Statue, dedicated to the poet who wrote the Thirukkural. Later drive towards Trivandrum and stop at Thanumalayan Temple in Suchindram. This temple is known for its architecture and the 22-foot-high statue of Hanuman. Continue to visit the Padmanabhapuram Palace. If time permits visit Kovalam Beach before reaching Trivandrum. On arrival, check into your hotel and later visit the Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu/Krishna. Overnight stay at Trivandrum. Note - Some temples, including Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple, may have strict dress codes. Please dress modestly. Places You’ll See
Enjoy your morning breakfast as your Madurai Rameshwaram Kanyakumari package concludes. You will then be transferred to Trivandrum Airport or the railway station for your onward journey.

blocks.content: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary, also known as Sasan Gir, is a national park and wildlife sanctuary in Gujarat, India. It was established in 1965 in the erstwhile Nawab of Junagarh's private hunting area, with a total area of 1,410.30 km2 (544.52 sq mi), of which 258.71 km2 (99.89 sq mi) is fully protected as a national park and 1,151.59 km2 (444.63 sq mi) as wildlife sanctuary. It is part of the Khathiar-Gir dry deciduous forests ecoregion.

Gir National Park is renowned for its rich cultural heritage, historical significance, and diverse attractions. From ancient temples and forts to modern amenities and natural beauty, Gir National Park offers an unforgettable experience for every traveler.

blocks.text: The best time to visit Rishikesh is in the summers ( March to June ) and winters ( October to February ). The summers are perfect if you're planning on doing rafting or going camping. Winters, on the other hand, pose as an ideal time to indulge in sightseeing or engage in yoga or meditation sessions.
Monsoon (July to September) is another pleasant time as the holy city treats you with lush greenery. However, adventure activities like rafting are closed in this period owing to safety reasons.
You can reach Rishikesh by all three modes of transport, that is, train, plane, and highway lanes! Here's a quick travel guide to the 'Yoga capital of the world':

items: By Air: The nearest airport to Rishikesh is in Dehradun (Jolly Grant Airport). It's situated about 21 km from the city, and you can easily hire a taxi or a cab to reach Rishikesh from here. Also, the airport serves all the major cities in the country, such as Delhi, Mumbai, etc.

By Train: You'll find the nearest railhead in Haridwar . The Haridwar Junction is about 25 km from Rishikesh, and transport like taxis/autos is easily accessible from here. Trains from major cities to Haridwar run on a regular basis.

By Road: Those who love road travel can take the NH 334. You can arrive here in your personal vehicle, or take the regular buses that run on this route from cities like Delhi, Dehradun, and Haridwar. The Delhi to Rishikesh road trip is one of the most popular options among travellers.

Here are some places that must make it to your Rishikesh tour itinerary:

rows: The Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat is one of the best experiences the city can offer you. Watch the holy confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers here.
Lakshman Jhula and Ram Jhula sightseeing should definitely be a part of your Rishikesh Tourism Packages! These Iconic suspension bridges are the best spots to capture the panoramic Ganga river views.
A Parmarth Niketan Ashram visit is a must as it's the largest ashram in the city. You can do yoga and meditation here.
Requiring just a short trek, this waterfall is so worth the effort. You can enjoy a picnic here while feasting your eyes on the cascading waterfall views!

The Beatles Ashram exploration is really exciting, for you get to see graffiti art here and some serene meditation huts. The place got super popular after the rock band 'The Beatles' visited here in 1968.
