Go to Mohan Chatti (83 m) for Rishikesh's most sought-after adventure sport. And the good thing is that they have certified professionals there who make sure your stay there is safe.
The Neer Garh waterfall trek should definitely be tried, as it's rewarded with a beautiful waterfall at the end! You also get to explore the scenic trails along the way.

blocks.text: Here are some travel tips that will come in handy on your tour:

items: Pack woollen clothes for this trip, as the nights can get cold there.
Carry with you a good pair of sturdy shoes. Also, bring trekking shoes if you're planning on doing trekking there.
Please keep in mind that alcohol and non-vegetarian food are strictly prohibited in Rishikesh, as this is a spiritual place.

Q1. What Is The Best Time To Visit Rishikesh?

Ans. The most preferred time to travel to Rishikesh is between February and mid-May, when the weather is quite pleasing. However, be aware of the fact that the temperature starts going down to sub-zero levels in the winter months hence, Rishikesh in winter witnesses chilly cold weather. And it might be interesting to note that Rishikesh welcomes a huge influx of tourists throughout the year, despite the season.
Q2. How Can I Plan A Trip To Rishikesh?

Ans. To plan the Rishikesh trip, you must first decide the time you're going to visit there. After that, you can plan your itinerary keeping in mind the places that you would like to see and the activities that you want to indulge in there. Also, it's always a good idea to book you stay in advance. Finally, decide on the mode of transport that you'd take to reach there, such as plane, trains or the good old road route.
Q3. What Can I Do In Rishikesh?

Ans. Despite being reckoned as a spiritual city, the destination offers you a great opportunity to get indulged in activities like river rafting, bungee jumping, mountain climbing, mountain biking, etc. Also, it is a perfect place to meet your inner self through meditation! This spiritual city in India really has a lot to offer its travellers.
Q4. What Is The Rishikesh Famous For?

Ans. Rishikesh is famous for several things like its ancient temples, sacred Ghats, adventure activities, and also for the local markets from where you can buy some really amazing souvenirs for yourself and your loved ones.
Q5. How Can I Go From Delhi To Rishikesh?

Ans. There are direct buses from Delhi to Rishikesh on regular basis. Rishikesh is not much far away from Delhi (at a distance of only 255.3 km) and both the cities are pretty well connected with the motorable roads. You can also take the plane or choose the railway systems to reach here.
Q6. What Is There To See In Rishikesh?
Ans. There is a lot to see in the city as it is home to various ancient temples, ghats, Ram Jhula, Laxman Jhula, local markets, waterfall, and much more.
Q7. What Time Is The Ganga Aarti In Rishikesh?

Ans. The Ganga Aarti takes place at the divine Triveni Ghat between 6 pm and 7 pm every day. However, the timings can change a bit depending on the season. Hundreds of devotees gather at the Ghat to be a part of this scared event.
Q8. What Is The Yoga Capital Of The World?
Ans. Rishikesh is considered to be the Yoga capital of the world as the city offers a perfect environment to perform meditation and yoga. The city also organizes Yoga Festival every year!

blocks.text: Sanchi, located in the state of Madhya Pradesh in India, is a significant historical and religious site renowned for its ancient Buddhist monuments and UNESCO World Heritage Site status. Sanchi tour packages offer visitors a chance to explore the rich history, architectural marvels, and spiritual ambiance of this fascinating destination.

Sanchi is primarily known for its Great Stupa, a massive hemispherical dome-shaped structure that is considered one of the oldest stone structures in India. Built to house the relics of Lord Buddha, the stupa is adorned with intricately carved gateways, known as Toranas, which depict scenes from the life of Buddha.

Apart from the Great Stupa, Sanchi is home to numerous other Buddhist structures and monasteries, such as the Ashoka Pillar, the Gupta Temple, and the Eastern Gateway. These architectural wonders showcase the mastery of ancient Indian craftsmanship and provide insights into the rich Buddhist heritage of the region.

Sanchi tour packages often include visits to nearby attractions like Udayagiri Caves, Vidisha, and the Archaeological Museum. The Udayagiri Caves feature elaborate rock-cut sculptures and caves that were once used as dwelling places for monks. Vidisha, located close to Sanchi, houses ancient temples, ruins, and the famous Heliodorus Pillar, which is of historical significance.

The Sanchi tour experience is enhanced by the serene and picturesque surroundings of the town. Visitors can enjoy peaceful walks amidst lush green gardens and soak in the tranquil atmosphere that pervades the area.

Sanchi tour packages provide a unique opportunity to delve into the ancient Buddhist heritage of India, explore remarkable architectural marvels, and experience a sense of spiritual tranquillity in a historically significant setting.

blocks.text: Saraswati Pushkaralu is a Hindu festival dedicated to the River Saraswati.

items: Route: Haridwar/ Dehradun – Rishikesh - Pipalkoti → Pipalkoti -Mana Village - Saraswati Pushkaralu- Badrinath → Badrinath - Srinagar → Srinagar – Devprayag - Haridwar -

blocks.text: Day 1: Haridwar/ Dehradun – Rishikesh - Pipalkoti (200kms/7 hrs)

Welcome to Haridwar/ Dehradun. You are greeted and assisted on arrival at Dehradun Airport /Railway station by our representative and drive to Rishikesh for Sightseeing which covers the magnificent ashrams and famous Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula, Shivanand Ashram, Gita Bhavan, Parmarth Niketan, later drive to Pipalkoti, en-route visit Nandprayag, Karanprayag, Rudraprayag, on arrival check into hotel. Overnight stay at Pipalkoti.Places You’ll See
Day 2: Pipalkoti -Mana Village - Saraswati Pushkaralu- Badrinath (80 kms /4 Hrs)

In the morning, drive to Badrinath (Mana). Once you reach Mana village, take a holy bath in the Saraswati River, perform Pooja rituals, including Pind Daan Shradh for ancestors. Now, proceed to Vyas Gufa, Ganesh Gufa, and Bhim Pul in Mana village. After that, go back to Badrinath, check into a hotel, then take a dip in Tapt Kund before visiting Badrinath Temple. You have to get tickets from the counter for Maha Abhishek and Abhishek at the temple. Overnight stay in Badrinath.Places You’ll See

Next morning, go to the temple, enter through the colorful entrance, and have Darshan of Badrivishal along with Ganesh, Kubera, Garuda, Narada, Uddhav, Nar, and Narayan. Visitors will also see small temples dedicated to Laxmi Mata, Nar-Narayana, Hanuman, Ghantakarna, and Kamdhenu. You can receive ‘Charnamrit’ (holy water) inside the temple. Now, get into the vehicle and proceed to Rudraprayag. Arrive in the evening and check into the hotel for a night stay.Places You’ll See
Day 4: Srinagar – Devprayag - Haridwar - (120 kms/4 hrs)

On the fourth day, drive back to Rishikesh. Visit places like Sivananda Ashram, Ram Jhula, Laxman Jhula, Gita Bhavan, and the Parmarth Niketan. Then, go towards Haridwar. We will drop you at the Railway Station or Bus Stand. This concludes the journey, filled with joyful moments.Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Saraswati Pushkaram is a holy festival of the River Saraswati that takes place once every 12 years. Devotees celebrate this because they believe taking a bath in the river cleanses their soul and gives them moksha (salvation). According to Purana, during Pushkaralu, Guru Brihaspati (Jupiter) increases the river’s holiness and importance. Many devotees visit here to perform puja and rituals for blessings.

This is the best time to go for Darshan and receive spiritual blessings. Saraswati Pushkaram 2025 will take place from May 15 to 26 in Mana village near Badrinath. People believe that the Saraswati River flows underground and appears at Mana. Visitors should never miss this holy Yatra. Our Saraswati Pushkar Yatra package includes the best hotels, transportation and a guide to make your journey easy. We welcome visitors from Delhi or Haridwar. Book this holy journey now, where you will experience the divine energy with the natural beauty of Badrinath.

blocks.text: The best time to visit Shimla depends on what kind of experience you're looking for. Here's a breakdown of the seasons:

items: This season offers pleasant weather to enjoy the best views of Shimla and enjoy the adventure activities. It is also the best time to enjoy trekking, boating and enjoying the lush green landscapes. Also look for Shimla Summer Festival. It's one of the most popular festivals in Shimla held in May- June in the Ridge area. You will enjoy the local Himachali culture with folk music and dance performances like Nati and Gidda.
You will also behold various handicraft exhibitions, fashion shows, flower shows, and enjoy savoring delicious cuisines at the food stalls in this festival.

Marked by the clear skies and cool mountain breeze, this season of the year is for people who love to explore nature spots. The weather is pleasant for nature, sightseeing, trekking, photography and adventure activities. You will also experience occasional showers in September as it is the tail end of monsoon.

The vibrant cultural festivals like Dussehra, Diwali make this time of the year best for the travelers looking for a perfect blend of nature and cultural experiences in Shimla. During this time, you will also witness less crowds than in the summer months.

During this time, you will experience heavy showers with potential landslides and slippery roads. It is not an ideal time to explore Shimla with family. If you are tolerant of disruptions like landslides and heavy rains, then only you should plan your Shimla visit in these months.

Due to heavy rain, your travel plans for sightseeing, or any adventure activities may get postponed or delayed. However, one thing which is best during this time is that due to refreshing monsoon showers, you will see lush green landscapes.

It is the best season of the year for those who love to see snowfall and enjoy snow adventure activities in Shimla. The temperature during this time will drop down to subzero levels but if you are tolerant of cold then these months are best for you.
Travelers can enjoy snowboarding, skiing, go karting, etc. Winter festivals like Christmas and New Year make Shimla holidays more enjoyable.

blocks.text: Best Places to Visit in Shimla on your Trip

Shimla is a heaven for wanderers looking for the best Himalayan escapes with their family and friends. In 2025 till May, Shimla welcomed around 9,99,065 tourists which shows Shimla remains a top choice for travellers who visit Himachal Pradesh. Source-( Travel Trade Journal ). Here are some of the most popular places in Shimla, Covered in our Shimla Itineraries-

items: The scenic Ridge is the heart of Shimla. It is one of the most popular points of tourist interests in Shimla. Surrounded by the majestic Himalayan mountains, you will be spellbound by the panoramic views.

It is the best place for shopping, leisurely walks and capturing the beauty of the mountains. The place has many statues of the eminent figures like Mahatma Gandhi, Indira Gandhi, Dr. Y.S. Parmar, and Atal Bihari Vajpayee. It also includes the iconic Christ Church and the Tudorbethan-style State Library.

Don't miss Mall Road in Shimla as it is the best place if you truly want to understand the local culture and lifestyle. The vibrant atmosphere of Shimla is delightfully chaotic. It is the best place for shopping in Shimla.
You will also witness many food stalls offering the best street food of the mountains. The beautiful views of the valley and colonial era buildings are major sights to behold.
The highest peak in Shimla, Jakhu Hill houses one of the majestic 108 ft statues of lord Hanuman.
Usually, people visit Jakhu Temple through trekking. You will witness beautiful Deodar forests along the way.

While on his way to gather information on Sanjeevani Booti (medicinal Herb) Lord Hanuman stopped on Jakhu Hill. The temple is a place where his footprints are still kept intact. The idol of Lord Hanuman is a self-manifested idol in the Sanctum.
Kufri, located a few km away from Shimla is a must visit Hill Station to enjoy fun-filled picnic and adventure activities.
It's a very famous place to enjoy winter sports like skiing, snowboarding. You will also capture the beauty of Mahasu Peak, the highest viewpoint of the region.

Apart from adventure activities, this place is best to enjoy Yak rides, nature walks, picnics, enjoying fun activities at amusement parks like Kufri Fun World and Indira Tourist Park and wildlife spotting at Himalayan Nature Park.

blocks.text: Viceregal Lodge - Indian Institute of Advanced Studies

items: Viceregal Lodge - Indian Institute of Advanced Studies is a landmark destination of Shimla. It is of immense historical and political importance in Shimla.
The architecture of Viceregal Lodge is a sight to behold. It was built between 1880 and 1888 in the Jacobethan (Jacobean + Elizabethan) style by British architect Henry Irwin.
It's an observatory hill which has many beautiful gardens, houses, a Research Institute and opulent halls.
Christ Church is a popular spiritual destination to visit in Shimla. It is the second oldest Church in North India.
You will be amazed to see the beautiful neo-gothic style architecture. It has five stained-glass windows which represent Christian virtues.
It's a peaceful spot for self-retrospection and don't miss its silhouette. It's one of the most captured landmarks in Shimla.

blocks.text: Best Things to do in Shimla on your Trip
Shimla offers many activities for tourists which is the reason why holidays in Shimla never get dull. Here are some of the best activities to do in Shimla-

items: Enjoy the iconic Kalka Shimla Toy Train ride, it's a UNESCO heritage site in Himachal Pradesh. The Kalka Shimla narrow gauge train journey will show many beautiful tunnels, bridges and Pine forests along the way. You will be able to capture the beauty of Shimla like never before.
If you want to soothe your senses and relax, this ride is a must not miss to behold the mountains from a unique perspective.
Visiting Shimla and not going to Kufri will be unfair. It is the best place to visit if you love adventures.

Here you will enjoy fun-filled picnics, yak rides, Sledding, pony rides, mini amusement park rides, go karting, skiing, snowboarding etc. It's an ultimate destination to unleash the adventurer spirit in you at Shimla.

blocks.text: Ice Skating at Shimla Ice Rink

items: Ice Skating in Shimla is a must not miss. This exciting adventure activity is enjoyed in an open-air rink which offers best views of majestic Himalayan Mountains.
It is the only naturally formed ice skating rink located in Lakkar Bazaar in Shimla which operates in winter (December to February). There are also many food stalls to enjoy the local cuisine.
Explore one of the highest waterfalls in Shimla- Chadwick Falls, located near the summer hill area. The beautiful cascading waterfall is approximately 86 meters in height.
It falls into a deep gorge which is surrounded by the scenic Pine and Deodar forests. It is one of the most beautiful places to visit in Shimla for nature lovers and couples.
You have to indulge in a short walk through a forest trail to access Chadwick falls. Visit here during Monsoon (July to October). During this time, its beauty is at its peak.

blocks.text: How to Reach Shimla by Air, Train and Road

Shimla is one of the most popular hill station destinations in Himachal Pradesh . So, it is well connected by Air, Train and Road from the major Indian cities. Here is a detailed overview on Shimla's connectivity by Air, Train and Road -

rows: You will get flights to Jubbarhatti Airport (Shimla Airport) via Delhi. There are limited flights and it's not functional in all seasons. Take flight from Chandigarh Airport for Shimla.
You will get a train from Delhi to Kalka. You can also visit Shimla via Kalka Shimla Toy Train; It's a UNESCO Heritage site.
NH1 /NH22 is the best route to reach Shimla from Delhi by Car. It will take approx. 7-9 hours.
You will get direct flights to Shimla Airport via Chandigarh Airport. However, the access is limited.
A train from Chandigarh to Kalka is available + you can also reach Shimla via Kalka- Shimla Route.
Shimla will be accessible by road via NH5 from Chandigarh by Car. / It will take 3-4 hours.
From Kalka via car, you will reach Shimla in 3 hours. You can also take buses to reach Shimla from Chandigarh as it is frequently available.
There are no direct flights to reach Shimla from Dehradun. You will get access via connecting airports
You will not get direct trains for Shimla. Take trains from Dehradun to Kalka and then go by Kalka Shimla Toy Train.
It will take 6-7 hours by road via car or Bus to reach Shimla from Dehradun. Take NH344 or NH 5 by car and enjoy the scenic winding roads through the Himalayan region.
You will get direct flights to Delhi via Mumbai and Kolkata and then you can hire a taxi, or bus to reach Shimla.
You will get a train to Kalka from Delhi and then you can go via Toy train (Kalka- Shimla).
It's a long road trip, not commonly preferred. Take flights or train for a comfortable journey.

blocks.text: Travel Tips for fun-filled Shimla Trip
Here are some of the most useful tips to follow if you want to enjoy a memorable holiday in Shimla with your loved ones.

items: Best Time to Visit - Prefer Peak tourism season (summer and winter) to enjoy accessibility to all the famous places and adventure activities in Shimla.

What to Pack- Always pack weather appropriate clothes to enjoy the best of Shimla Tourism in comfort and style. You need to carry warm woolens, thermals, gloves, mufflers and sturdy footwear in both summer and winter season as the temperature during these seasons are freezing. The nights get colder and even in day time, you will feel the need to wear light warm clothes. In high- altitude areas you can wear light breathable clothes as the sun rays will be strong. Carry sunscreen moisturizer and polarized sunglasses to enjoy sightseeing.

Cash- Carry enough cash to support small business as the shopkeepers may not have digital payment modes at remote locations. At popular bazaars and city areas you will get ATM facilities but in remote, high-altitude areas these facilities may not be available.

Plan in advance - Book your hotel and tickets in advance to enjoy Shimla holidays during peak season. Booking at the last minute will be frustrating and you may not get your desired hotel due to peak tourism season. So, it is best to book your tickets and hotel in advance.

Enjoy on Foot- If you don't have mobility issues and are comfortable to walk then explore some of the most popular places in Shimla like the Mall Road, Ridge, Bazaars by foot to experience the soul of Shimla. You can hire local buses, taxis or scooters to reach Kufri and Mashobra.
Be a responsible Tourist- Protect the natural beauty of Shimla. Don't use plastic as it is banned in Himachal. Don't litter anywhere. Use reusable bags to carry your stuff.
Emergency - Always carry emergency numbers of your tour operator and relevant people who you can approach during the time of emergency.
Licensed operator - Hire licensed operator to try adventure activities in Shimla. Check their ID proof for your safety.

items: Pleasant Pilgrimage Tour to The Revered Shirdi

blocks.text: Pleasant Pilgrimage Tour to The Revered Shirdi

The town of Shirdi is situated 300km away from Mumbai. It lies right in the middle of Maharashtra’s ‘sugar cane belt’. It happens to be the most visited pilgrimage site immediately after Tirupati which lies in Andhra Pradesh.

This is owing to the fact that this place belongs to Sai Baba, a revered religious and spiritual guide who is also considered God’s incarnation and worshipped with devotion and fervour. People belonging to various faiths and ‘walks of life’ meet here at Shirdi to worship their favourite ‘Sai Baba’ in reverence and awe. They get inspiration from the teachings of Sai Baba. They gather at Shirdi to pay their homage to this divine human being. Every year several thousand pilgrims visit this place to gain spiritual blessings from Shirdi Sai Baba, making it one the most important tourist destinations in India.

My Quick Trippers offers an exclusive tour package to Shirdi Sai Baba that will take you through Shani Shingnapur and Nashik. The pilgrimage tour packages organized by this well-reputed online travel agency are aimed at allowing you to smoothly enjoy the trip and at making your spiritual advances the way you prefer to. All provisions related to the pilgrimage including the stay and the shrines for visit, are selected in order of high demand of visitors for the location. With professional assistance, this online company ensures that your Shirdi trip is a religiously blissful one without any bumps on the way. And for the convenience of the customers My Quick Trippers also provides customization of the tour packages to meet the budget requirements of the customers.
Day 1 : Shirdi Arrival and Shani Shingnapur Visit:

You will be picked up by My Quick Trippers representative from Kopargaon /Nagarsol/Manmad railway station and taken safely to Shirdi where you will check into a hotel booked for you. After freshening up you will visit the ‘Shirdi Temple’ for ‘darshan’. This place is flocked with devotees who need to travel 296km from the city of Mumbai to visit this Temple that is built over Sai Baba’s Samadhi. Both the Hindu and Muslim communities deeply revere this place and make it point to visit this blessed place. After your ‘darshan’ is over you will take a launch to reach Shani Shingnapur, a tiny Maharashtra village famous for the ‘Shani Temple’ located here. Inside the shrine is a ‘black rock’ 5.5ft in height which signifies the presence of the Hindu deity, Lord Shiva. The village too is popular because none of the houses here has a ‘door’ and surprisingly no report of robbery has been registered here. The residents of this village believe that anyone who tries to steal will be heavily punished by Lord Shiva. Return to Shirdi to spend the night.
Day 2 : Shirdi to Nashik (140km/ 3 hours) and Back

On day 2 after a filling breakfast you will go one to visit the ‘Trimbakeshwar Shiva Temple’ and then move on to the ‘Kalaram Temple’, the ‘Muktidham’, the ‘Seetha Guha’, the ‘Panchavati Goraram Temple’, the ‘Kapaleswar Temple’, the ‘Godavari Ghat’ and the ‘Chandramouleshwara Mandir’ after which you will return to Shirdi. While ‘Muktidham’ is a popular located on Nashik road where Hindu deities are worshipped, ‘Panchvati’ is another significant pilgrimage centre where Lord Ram is supposed to have dwelt with brother Laxman and wife Sita. The ‘Godavari Ghat’ houses the ‘Godavari Temple’ that was constructed by Gopikabai, mother of ‘Elder Madhavrao Peshwa’ in the year 1760. This temple remains open strictly while the ‘Kumbh Mela’ is on. As you cover all these places, you will keep coming closer to Nashik which again has mythological prominence with Lord Ram spending his exile (final four months) in Tapovan, next to Nashik. Important tourist spots along the periphery of Nahsik are inclusive of the ‘Dudhsagar Falls’, the ‘Gangapur Dam’, the ‘Pandavleni Caves’, the ‘Museum of Numismatics’, the ‘Nandur Madhyameshwar Bird Sanctuary” and the ‘Anjaneri Parvat’. The wine exported from Nashik is world-famous. After visiting the vineyards you will be taken back to Shirdi for spending the night.
Day 3 : Departing Shirdi and End of Tour

On the final day, you can visit the ‘Shirdi Temple’ one final time and return to the hotel for breakfast after which you will be safely transported to Kopargaon/ Nagarsol/ Manmad railway station to get back home with spiritual awakening and lots of blessings.

blocks.text: Sikkim, nestled in the lap of the Himalayas, is a small yet captivating state in northeastern India. Sikkim tour packages offer a unique opportunity to explore this hidden gem, known for its breathtaking landscapes, vibrant Buddhist culture, and adventure activities.

One of the major attractions in Sikkim is its stunning natural beauty. The state is adorned with snow-capped mountains, lush green valleys, cascading waterfalls, and serene lakes. The mighty Kanchenjunga, the third highest peak in the world, dominates the skyline and offers a mesmerizing backdrop for travellers. Popular destinations like Gangtok, Pelling, and Lachung provide access to these picturesque landscapes and serve as gateways to explore the beauty of the region.

Sikkim is also renowned for its Buddhist monasteries and spiritual sites. The Rumtek Monastery, one of the largest and most significant monasteries in Sikkim, attracts visitors with its intricate architecture and serene atmosphere. The Enchey Monastery, Pemayangtse Monastery, and Tashiding Monastery are other notable places of religious and cultural importance.

Adventure enthusiasts will find plenty of opportunities in Sikkim. Trekking in the Himalayas is a popular activity, with options ranging from the famous Kanchenjunga Base Camp Trek to the shorter Dzongri Trek. River rafting, paragliding, and mountain biking are also available for those seeking an adrenaline rush.

Sikkim’s rich cultural heritage is deeply rooted in its Buddhist traditions. The state celebrates several festivals, including Losar, Saga Dawa, and Bumchu, which offer a glimpse into the vibrant local culture. Travellers can witness traditional dance performances, participate in rituals, and savour authentic Sikkimese cuisine during these festivals.

Sikkim tour packages provide an unforgettable experience of exploring pristine natural landscapes, immersing in Buddhist spirituality, and enjoying thrilling adventure activities. Whether you seek tranquillity amidst the mountains, cultural immersion, or adrenaline-pumping adventures, Sikkim has something to offer for every traveller.

blocks.text: Singapore Travel Guide - Festivals, Food, Shopping

In Singapore, there is a constant buzz of delightful activities, which travellers will enjoy a lot. People of Singapore celebrate one festival after another almost every month of the year. Let's know in detail about the vibrant Festivals Celebrated in Singapore -

items: Chinese New Year - it falls between mid-January and mid-February. It is celebrated for two days. People feast and give Hong bao, red packets of 'lucky money'.

Thaipusam - This is a Hindu festival celebrated between January and February. At this festival, devotees worship Lord Murugan and practice mindfulness. The festival begins at dawn at the Srinivasa Perumal Temple in Serangoon Road.

Dragon Boat Festival - This festival is celebrated to honor a Chinese patriot, Qu Yuan, who drowned himself in 278 BC as a form of protest against the imperial court. On this day small packets of rice are thrown into the water to distract fishes, and people decorate their boats with dragon heads and tails.

Vesak Day - This festival is celebrated to honor Lord Buddha's birth, death and enlightenment. At dawn, you will see a huge candlelight procession by the devotees. As a part of the celebration, caged birds are released, and free meals are offered to the poor and needy.

Singapore Food Festival - Don't miss this festival, as you will get to taste Singapore's rich flavors. This festival celebrates Singapore's rich culinary heritage, which features local perennial food favorites such as Hainanese chicken rice, Chilli crab, Laksa, and satay.

Theemithi Festival - It's a unique festival which you must witness in Singapore. It is celebrated at Sri Mariamman Temple on South Bridge Road. Male devotees walk barefoot across glowing coals in honor of Draupadi, a legendary heroine of Mahabharata deified by South Indians.

blocks.text: Due to Singapore's cultural diversity, you will get various cuisines here. You will never go hungry on this beautiful island. The life of the people of Singapore revolves around food. There has been a constant debate about where to get fresh crabs, spicy chilli sauce, Indian food, chicken rice, etc. From Indian, Japanese, Korean, and Thai to Middle Eastern, you can sample different cuisines without any hassle. blocks.text: Best Places to Visit in Singapore

Singapore is one of Asia's best travel destinations. It has many incredible tourist routes and tones of historical marvels, cultural attractions, clubs, and nature reserves. Let's know some of the popular places to visit in Singapore to make your trip awesome.
This district of Singapore will take your breath away with many colonial buildings, museums, memorials and institutions. It is the cultural heart of the city. Some of the best places to see here are

items: St Andrew Cathedral - It is a Gothic-style church built by Indian convict laborers by using a special plaster material called Madras Chunam. The recent structure you see here today is designed by Ronald MacPherson.
The Padang- Padang is a popular historical marvel in Singapore which was used as a platform for Europeans to play cricket and socialise in the cool evenings.
City Hall - City Hall is one of the major historic landmarks of Singapore. It was constructed in 1929 to house the municipal council.

Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall - This place was used as a social hall to conduct public meetings and events. Now it is used as a place to witness theatrical performances, concerts, and festivals. Both the buildings display beautiful neoclassical architecture.
Raffles Landing Site - A place where Sir Stamford Raffles first landed on January 28th, 1819. Here you will also see a white poly-marble statue of Sir Stamford Raffles.
Mica Building - Once upon a time, it used to be the largest government building in Singapore, which was used to house the Hill Street Police Station and barracks.

blocks.text: This district in Singapore is very popular for its large number of museums. By visiting the museums, you will be able to know about Singapore's early stories through art and war relics. If you are planning to visit here, then explore-

items: Fort Canning Park - Also known as Forbidden Hill, it is one of the best places to visit in Singapore. Fort Canning used to be a home of Malay kings who ruled in the 14th century. Sir Stamford Raffles also built his residence here in 1819.
Singapore Philatelic Museum - You will get unique insights on Singapore's history. See postcards, first-day covers and stamps from the private collections of many famous philatelists.
Peranakan Museum - Learn about the history, culture and heritage of Peranakan. It was set up by Hokkien immigrants to preserve their cultural heritage.
National Museum - The National Museum was designed by J.K. McNair in 1887 in the Neo-Palladian style. Witness the most beautiful glass rotunda, elegant Palladian motifs and fish-scale zinc tiles.

blocks.text: Marina Bay is a prominent waterfront area which is famous for its cultural landmarks, entertainment hubs and beautiful display of the city's skyline. If you are visiting here, then explore-

items: Marina Bay Sands - It is a beautiful luxury resort with three towers which connect Sand Sky Park. It features a casino, luxury hotel, high-end boutiques, restaurants, nightclubs, bars and convention facilities.

Red Dot Design Museum - It's a perfect place to explore for creative souls in Singapore for product innovation, art, technology and global design trends. It is run by a German body that presents the prestigious Red Dot Award.
Gardens by the Bay - Embrace the beauty of this futuristic marvel with giant super trees, cloud forest conservatories and flower domes.
Merlion Park - It's the best place to capture pics with your loved ones in the beautiful backdrop of the Marina Bay skyline.

blocks.text: The best time to go on a Somnath trip is during winter – from October to March. The weather during this time is pleasant (10°C to 25°C) with clear skies and is therefore ideal for sightseeing, pilgrimage, and exploring other attractions like beaches.

Moreover, if you come during this period, you get to enjoy Mahashivratri (February/March) festival which is celebrated here with great zeal and fervour. Also, Kartik Purnima (November) also falls in this window and warrants a visit as it’s a highly significant religious day, celebrated with special events and prayers.
In addition, beach visits are a breeze during the winter season.
Best Places to See on the Somnath Tour

Somnath is a perfect place where you can enjoy natural, serene locations as well as see age-old remarkable architecture. And on top of that, there are some highly significant temples that you must visit, at least once in your life. To enjoy all aspects of the city, make sure to add the following to your Somnath trip packages:

It goes without saying that you should add Somnath Temple to your Somnath tour package! Moreover, this temple is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva , and therefore, must be visited on a Somnath trip.

The very first thing that will capture your attention will be the temple’s beautiful architecture. What you see here is a Chalukya-style architecture , dating back to the 11th century. The whole form of the temple is in ‘Kailash Mahameru Prasad’, showcasing the excellent skills of the masons of that era! Another tourist-favourite thing about this magnificent monument is the intricate designs carved on the temple.

And you have to see the evening Aarti! It is organised with a grand Light and Sound Show, keeping the entertainment of the visitors in mind. Moreover, since the temple is located at the seaside, you can soak in the mesmerizing views of the Arabian Sea, which are especially gorgeous at nighttime.

As the name implies, this is the confluence point for three rivers - Hiran, Kapila, and Saraswati. This is a highly tranquil area with picturesque views and therefore it is recommended to include it in your Somnath holiday packages. Moreover, this is also a site of pilgrimage, so you’ll often see people taking holy dips in hopes of cleansing their sins. Tourists also wander off to nearby ghats as they are equally serene and perfect for a relaxing stroll.

This place is incredibly important for all the Lord Krishna bhakts because as per the legends this was where he was mistakenly shot and left his earthly body. What you find here is a serene temple of Lord Krishna with a beautiful idol of him shown in a reclining pose – symbolizing the event. There’s also a marker here that points to the exact spot where he was hit by the arrow. You’ll also find many scenes from his life, adding to the wholesome experience of exploring God’s life.

This cave is famous for the Gufa the Pandavas resided during their exile. It’s also believed that Pandavas worshiped Lord Shiva here to seek his blessing in their difficult times. However, the main shrine inside the case is of Goddess Hinglaj Mata, a highly revered deity. Many pilgrims come here to offer their prayers and offerings. Also, there are many altars here as well dedicated to Pandavas and some other gods.
The place draws in history enthusiasts as well because of its cultural importance and its association with Mahabharat lore!

Just a short walk away from the Somnath Temple lies a beautiful beach surrounded by aquamarine waters. Take a leisurely stroll, enjoy Gujarati snacks & beverages at a food stall, or go for a camel ride, this place is bountiful of fun and rich experiences. Moreover, the sunrise and sunset are quite a sight here and you’d find many here just relaxing and taking in the serene views. Golden sands, lapping waves, and postcard-perfect view - this site is ideal for getting into a quick photography session, and unsurprisingly, many tourists do. It’s just that tempting!

This historic gate once was a gateway to Somnath, acting as a major entry point for both pilgrims and other tourists. Now, it’s a historic structure with immense culture and heritage. On the gate, you’ll find traditional Gujarati architecture with ornate designs and intricate carvings of floral patterns, mythological figures, and more. The gate is glorified further with its three majestic arches , embellished with motifs and inscriptions - signifying the grandeur of ancient India!
Top Things to Do on the Somnath Trip
Somnath trip is a highly cultural and spiritually enriching journey. To make your experience truly wholesome, add these quintessential and quirky things to your Somnath travel package.

Experience the divine firsthand by attending both the morning and evening aarti at the Somnath temple. The entire experience is truly another level of spiritual and must be a part of your Somnath trip. The evening aarti is especially gorgeous with its backdrop being the setting sun.
Attend the Light and Sound Show
The Light and Sound show is a mesmerizing experience that consists of stunning visuals and compelling storytelling. The narration is the story is generally available in Hindi and Gujarati.
Expect a rich storytelling that narrates the riveting history of the temple – how it underwent destruction and reconstructions over the centuries.

It also emphasizes the temple’s spiritual significance as one of the 12 Jyotirlingas. And to top that are the stunning visual effects, supported by the advanced lighting technology that lights up the whole temple and the surrounding areas. And the whole show is further powered by the captivating sound effects with stirring background music and voiceovers – transporting viewers to the bygone era.

However, the Light and Sound Show is not just an entertainment, but a deeply moving experience that highlights the temple’s spiritual legacy and rich heritage. It’s a must-attend on your Somnath trip.

Other than the Light and Sound Show, the Somnath Museum is another great way to know the history of the Somnath temple. Here you see the visual exhibits in the form of miniature models that depict the temple’s history and present-day form – perfect for visitors to understand the temple’s evolution over the centuries.

In addition, on display are pottery, coins, and utensils from the previous eras, giving visitors a glimpse into the lifestyle of ancient times. You can also spot age-old inscriptions here in Sanskrit and other ancient languages!

Take a little detour from Somnath and meet the regal lions at the Gir Forest National Park. Many tourists opt for a combined Somnath Gir tour package to enjoy the wildlife at its full glory on their Somnath trip!

Located on the serene Triveni Sangam, Gita Mandir’s calm and spiritual vibe couldn’t get elevated any further with this strategic location. Dedicated to Lord Krishna, the temple walls are ornate with inscribed Gita verses. Moreover, the temple is designed to have an echo feature , which essentially means whenever the mantras are chanted in the temple premises, they get echoed around, creating a truly whimsical spiritual experience!
Gujarati cuisine is super delicious involving multiple flavours. Try the following dishes on your Somnath trip:

items: Gujarati Thali : This wholesome mean includes Rotis, Dal, Kadhi, Shak, Khichdi, and Thepla. It is served with Chaach, Papad, and pickles.
Dhokla : Enjoy the soft and spongy yellow snack.
Undhiyu : Gorge on this seasonal vegetable dish, slow-cooked with a blend of spices.
Fafda : Relish this savoury & sweet crispy snack.
Thepla : Do not forget to try this thin wheat flatbread, frequently paired with yogurt and pickles.
Handvo : Enjoy this salty rice and lentil cake, topped with sesame seeds.
Sweet Dishes : Give a nudge to your sweet tooth and try local desserts like Ghari, Mohanthal, and Shrikhand.

seo.meta_description: Karnataka is every traveler’s paradise city. With My Quick Trippers’s Karnataka special group tour package of 10 days and 9 nights you.

og_tags.og:title: Special Group Tour Package for Karnataka for 10 Days
og_tags.og:description: Karnataka is every traveler’s paradise city. With My Quick Trippers’s Karnataka special group tour package of 10 days and 9 nights you.

items: Special Group Tour Package for Karnataka

blocks.text: Southern India is truly a treat for every traveler since it is dotted with numerous holy shrines, sculptures that are intricately created and natural beauty which is incomparable. My Quick Trippers presents you with the Karnataka special group tour package planning for 10 days and 9 nights where you will be immersed in the true spirit of southern India.
Once you arrive in Bangalore you will be made to proceed towards your hotel after which a brief sightseeing tour of the city will commence.

You will be taken to Cubbon Park, which is a lush green park and pans over a massive area of 300 acres. A wonderful site for nature lovers and peace seekers this place is considered to be the lungs of Bangalore.

You will then be made to proceed towards Lalbagh botanical gardens which houses India’s largest tropical plants collection and also has a lake, making it the perfect place for families to spend some quality time.

You will then be taken to Bangalore Palace, which was built in the year 1878 using intricate designer architectural form and the massive ground in front of the palace is used for holding public events.
Before heading back to your hotel you will be made to visit the famous and holy ISKCON temple.
Day 2 : Bangalore – Shravanabelagola – Hassan – Belur – Halebidu – Hassan

Early in the morning, your 3-hour journey towards Shravanabelagola will commence which is an extremely important Jain pilgrimage center and showcases the peak of architectural brilliance. Here you will be made to visit the famous Gommateshwara Bahubali which is the main attraction. It is also the place of death for Chandragupta Maurya after he became a monk and took up an ascetic way of life.

After paying your respects here you will be driven to Hassan, which is at a distance of just an hour from here and had served as the seat for Hoysala Empire. The entire district is dotted with numerous ancient important temples. After getting checked in to your hotel you will be driven to Belur, which is also at a mere distance of an hour from Hassan.
In Belur you will be made to visit the Chennakeshava Temple complex which is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and highly revered among the South Indian population.

From Belur you will proceed towards Halebidu, which is located at a distance of half an hour and had served as the capital for the Hoysala Empire during the 12th century. Here you will be made to visit Kedareshwara and Hoysaleswara Temple. After this holy temple tour, you will be made to drive back to Hassan where you will be spending your night, since there are no hotels or accommodation places available in Belur or Halebidu.

Your morning will commence after breakfast where you will be made to proceed towards the sacred 400-year-old, Sri Nimishamba (an incarnation of goddess Parvati) temple and is at a distance of 2km from Srirangapatna by the banks of River Cauvery.
Entry Fees: free entry for all

Your next location will be the famous UNESCO world heritage site of Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, which is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and houses a large towering Rajagopuram which rises up to a height of 237 feet. The holy temple is located on the confluence point of River Cauvery and Kollidam on an island.
Temple Timings: 9 am to 12 pm; 1:15 pm to 6 pm; 6:45 pm to 9 pm
*during festival seasons the darshan timings are prone to change.

You will then be taken to witness some of the major attractions in Mysore starting with a visit to the Chamundeshwari Temple, which is located atop Chamundi hills and at a distance of 13 km from Mysore. In order to reach the temple you will be required to climb 1,008 stairs and halfway across you will encounter the statue of Nandi the bull which is the vehicle of Lord Shiva. This site is not only a prime pilgrimage destination but it also rewards the visitors with a breathtaking panoramic view of the Mysore city lying below.
Temple Timings: 7:30 am to 2 pm; 3:30 pm to 6 pm.

Your next stop at Mysore will be the 14th-century magnificent palace of Mysore. This palace is the 2nd most visited tourist attraction in India. The entire palace is adorned with beautiful and intricate artworks, majestic domes and gateways and designer carvings and engravings making it a must visit site.
Finally, you will be headed back to your hotel.
Early in the morning, post breakfast, you will be made to proceed towards the magical city of Coorg which is at a distance of 2 hours and 45 mines.

En route you will be made to visit Talakaveri, which is considered to be the birth place of River Cauvery. One can take holy dip in the water within the temple premises which was constructed to mark the sacred place.

You will then finally proceed towards one of the most pleasant hill stations in India, Coorg. Here, before checking in, you will be made to visit the famous Abbey falls, where the cascading water plunges down from a massive height of 70 feet. There are 200 steps that lead downwards towards the base of the falls from its main entrance.
Your next holy stop will be at one of the most prominent Hindu temple for Lord Shiva, Omkareshwara temple. This ancient temple is situated in the town of Madikeri amongst a fish-filled pond.
Temple Timings: 6:30 am to 12:30 pm; 12:30 pm to 3:30 pm; 3:30 pm to 8:30 pm
You will then be headed back to your allotted hotel in Coorg.
Day 5 : Coorg – Kukke (73 km) – Dharmasthala (60 km) – Kalasa (90 km) – Hornadu (6 km)

Early in the morning, you will be driven to Kukke Subramanya Temple, which is dedicated to the lord of serpents, Subramanya. It is situated on the lush green slopes of Western Ghats amongst the dense green forest and by the bank of River Kumaradhara.

After Darshan, you will be taken to Dharmasthala, where you will be made to visit the sacred, massive 57 feet Gommateshwara statue (one of the tallest standing statues in the world), which is a monolithic structure and is dedicated to Jain god Bahubali.
Timings: Open at all hours for visitation.
Entry Fees: free entry for all

Your next and final pious location for the day will be at Kalasa, Kalaseshwara Temple, which is a small Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and offers a magnificent view of the surrounding hills due to its location atop a hill.
Temple Timings: 7:30 am to 1 pm; 3:30 pm to 8:30 pm
You will finally head towards Hornadu where you will be checked in to your hotel.
Day 6 : Hornadu – Sringeri (42 km) – Kateel (92 km) – Mangalore (18 km)
You will be taken for an early morning darshan at Annapoorneshwari Temple, which is located on the bank of River Bhadra among the lush greenery of Western Ghats and is dedicated to goddess Parvati.
Temple Timings: 6:30 am to 9 am; 11 am to 2 pm; 7 pm to 9:30 pm

After the holy Darshan, you will be driven to Sringeri which is an ideal spot for every nature lover or photography enthusiast. Here you will savour the refreshing surrounding nature at Agumbe Ghat. After spending some quality time here, you will finally be headed to Mangalore.
En route you will be made to stop at Kateel for darshan at the famous Kateel Durga Mandir popularly known as Shri Durgaparameshwari Temple which is located by the River Nandini.
Upon arrival at Mangalore you will be straightaway headed to your allotted hotel in Mangalore after which you will enjoy the pleasant and relaxing sunset by the beach.
If time permits you will be taken to Mangala Devi Temple, a 9th century temple which is dedicated to the Hindu goddess Shakti.
Temple Timings: 6 am to 1 pm; 4 pm to 8:30 pm

Early in the morning, before breakfast, you will be made to proceed towards Kudupu Sri Anantha Padmanabha Temple, which is located at a distance of 10 km from the main city of Mangalore and is dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
It is vital for you to make reservations for the darshan before heading to the temple.
Temple Timings: 6 am to 12:30 pm; 5 pm to 8:30 pm
After the puja rituals you will be made to head back to your hotel where you will have your breakfast before proceeding towards Udupi.

At Udupi you will be made to visit Sri Krishna Matha mandir, which is a famous Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Krishna and Dvaita Matha. You will then be made to visit Anantheshwara Temple which is known for being over 1,000 years old and is located really close to Krishna Matha Temple.
Temple Timings: 6 am to 8 pm (it does not close for afternoon)
Make sure you wear appropriate clothing while visiting the temple since it is extremely important.

You will finally be made to head towards Murdeshwar, en route you will be made to visit Anegudde (30 km), which is home to one of the most famous Lord Ganesha temple, Sri Vinayaka Devasthana and one of the seven ‘Mukti Sthalas’ in Karnataka.

You will then proceed towards Mookambika (before reaching Murdeshwar) in Kollur, and the temple is dedicated to Goddess Lakshmi or also known as Mookambika Devi. Dating back to 800 AD this temple is amidst a pleasant and green location.

Finally, after reaching Murdeshwar you will be made to check in to your hotel before heading out for a holy visit at one of the main attractions here which is the world’s second-tallest Lord Shiva statue (123 feet).
You will then be headed towards Murudeshwara Temple which sits atop Kanduka hill and surrounded by Arabian Sea on three sides, it is also adorned with intricate carvings all over.
Temple Timings: 3 am to 1 pm; 3 pm to 8 pm
In the evening you will be taken for spending some peaceful and relaxing time by the Murdeshwar beach, before heading back to your hotel.
Day 8 : Murdeshwar – Idagunji – Gokarna – Goa (240 km)
Your morning journey towards Goa will commence while stopping en route at Idagunji and Gokarna.

At Idagunji you will be made to visit the famous Ganpati temple, and it sees numerous visitors on an everyday basis. It is also located by the holy banks of River Sharavathi and was built in 4th-5th century CE.
Temple Timings: 6 am to 1 pm; 3 pm and 8:30 pm

You will then proceed towards Gokarna, an important pilgrimage centers in Karnataka where you will be made to visit Mahabaleshwar temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva. The temple here is known for housing one of the original lingams in India making it a prime pilgrimage destination for Hindu devotees.
After darshan, you will be driven towards India’s party destination, Goa.
Upon arriving here you will be checked in to your hotel after which you will be free to watch the glorious setting sun while relaxing by the beach.

After breakfast in the morning, you will be taken for a sightseeing tour of South Goa which will start off with a visit to some of the most pristine beaches like, Miramar beach, Colva beach and Dona Paula beach. You will then be taken to one of the most regal and pious old churches at old Goa, Bom Jesus Basilica.
Old Goa is also home to Mangeshi temple (built in 1560), and is one of the largest and most frequently visited temples in Goa.

Finally, you will be made to go on a cruise on River Mandovi, which comprises of Goan dance, singing and music performances accompanied by delicious traditional Goan cuisines and is one of the prime things to do in Goa.

After breakfast, early in the morning, you will be made to proceed towards the UNESCO world heritage site of Hampi which is a group of monuments. Spread over an area of 4,100 hectares, the Hampi ruins are set by the banks of Tungabhadra River and the ruins here date back to 14the century.
Your journey will finally conclude here after being transferred to Hosapete Junction Railway Station.

items: Route: Arrival in Sri Lanka - Chilaw - Anuradhapura → Anuradhapura - Trincomalee → Trincomalee - Kandy → Kandy - Nuwara Eliya → Nuwara Eliya - Kataragama → Kataragama - Colombo

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrival in Sri Lanka - Chilaw - Anuradhapura

Upon arrival, you will be assisted by our tour representative who will make you head towards Anuradhapura via Chilaw. Upon arriving at Chilaw your Ramayana tour will kick start with a visit to Manavari Temple - the spot where Lord Rama had forst established a lingam after killing Ravana. This is an extremely sacred place since there are only two Ramalingam (lingams established by Lord Rama) in the world, one of them being in Rameshwaram. You will then be taken to Munneswaram Temple - this is the exact place where Lord Rama had prayed to Lord Shiva after committing Brahmahasti (priest killing). Places You’ll See

Early in the morning you will be made to proceed for Trincomalee but first you will be made to take a brief tour of Anuradhapura starting with a visit to Kanniya hot water spring well - a collection of 7 wells which is believed to possess natural healing powers and the place where king Ravana is believed to have carried out the last rites for his mother. After covering a 2 hours road journey and upon arriving at Trincomalee you will be taken to visit the famous Koneswaram Hindu temple - which was built by Rishi Agastya after getting instructions from Lord Shiva who was highly impressed by King Ravana’s devotion. The temple is extremely unique since it is a temple which was built by the lord for his devotee. You will be duly checked in to your hotel for spending the night. Your evening will end on a relaxing note at Nilaveli Beach where you will also witness the majestic sunset. Places You’ll See

Early in the morning you will start off your journey towards Kandy, while stopping on your way for visits to some of the most mesmerizing tourist attractions like - Sigiriya rock fortress - a UNESCO world heritage site, and popularly dubbed as the 8th wonder of the world is a triple moated defense from where a massive rock emerges to a height of 600 feet, which is complete with gardens and swimming pools on the summit. You will then head on to Cobra cave - named so because of its shape and the place where Sita was held in captivity whose walls are covered in prehistoric inscriptions and artworks. Upon arriving at Kandy which is located at a distance of 4 hours and 5 mines you will be checked in to your hotel, after which you will be made to attend the local and traditional Kandy dance show presentation. Places You’ll See

Early in the morning, you will be taken on a local sightseeing of Kandy, where you will be made to visit the famous temple of the tooth - a sacred 16th-century site for Sri Lankan Buddhists which houses Lord Buddha’s tooth relic. You will then be escorted to Shri Bhakta Hanuman Temple - where Lord Hanuman wandered looking for Sita and is visited by numerous devotees throughout the year. Ramboda waterfalls will be your next destination - which is one of the most pristine and picturesque cascading waterfalls in Sri Lanka . The island country of Sri Lanka is popular all over the world for its high-quality tea; you will be taken for a visit to the tea factory and tea plantation estates. Here you will also have the option of buying yourself some locally produced tea. Your next destination for the day will be upon your arrival at Nuwara Eliya, Seetha Amman temple - a modern vibrant and attractive building which is dedicated to Lord Rama and Sita and enshrines both their statues. Finally, you will be taken to the colorful and lively Ashok Vatika - the place where Sita preferred to stay in captivity under the Ashoka tree, hence the name. You will then be duly checked in to your hotel after a wholesome sightseeing tour, where you will be staying overnight. Places You’ll See

Your early morning visit will be on an extremely colorful not, where you will be made to visit Hakgala botanical garden - one of the 5 most popular botanical gardens in Sri Lanka and was Ravana’s favorite places where he kept a very depressed Sita. Gayathri Amman temple at Nuwara Eliya will be your next destination - which houses numerous Swayambhu (self-created lingams). Next, you will be taken to the historic site of Divurumpola Temple - the spot where Sita had performed her Agnipariksha to prove her purity and took her oaths. Several years later the villagers still pledge their fidelity or take oaths. Dhowa rock temple will be your next stop - it holds immense relevance since during the 1st century BC this place had served as the refuge place for King Walagamba. It also holds Buddhist importance since there is also a small stupa present inside the cave. The small mountain hamlet of Ella will be your next destination which possesses this was also one of the places where Ravana was hiding Sita. The Ella cave is located at the massive Ella waterfalls (1080 feet). After exploring this glorious site you will be made to head on to Kataragama which is located at a distance of 4 hours where you will be checked in to your allotted hotel for the night. Places You’ll See

You will be made to visit the famous Kataragama Hindu temple in the morning - the place where Lord Kartikeya had requested to proceed to the battlefield by Lord Indra during the last day of war. Later you will be made to proceed towards Ussangoda - the place which was one of the burnt up areas caused by Lord Hanuman’s blazing tail when he was testing the might of Ravana. Galle fortress will be your next destination which was built by the Portuguese in 1588 which till present day reminds the visitors of the colonial past. After covering a road journey of 5 hours you will reach the magnificent city of Colombo - the largest city of Sri Lanka where upon arrival you will be checked in to your hotel for an overnight stay. Places You’ll See

Early in the morning, you will be taken on a fun riverboat safari on Bentota Madu. You will also be taken to the famous turtle farms. Your sacred temple tour of the day will kick start with Panchamuga Anjaneyar Temple - the only temple on the island which is dedicated to the Panchamuga form (five faces) of Lord Hanuman. You will also be made to visit Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara - a Buddhist sanctuary which is said to be visited by Lord Buddha himself. There is also a Hindu shrine present within the sanctuary. Depending on the availability you will also be taken on a city-wide tour of Colombo which will cover the Independence Memorial Hall, old parliament and Galle face garden. Places You’ll See
From Colombo, you will be made to head on to the airport which is a 1-hour journey where you will be made to board the flight heading towards your onward destination.

Peak Tourism Months: December to April

items: If you love the beaches of South Sri Lanka or the West coast beaches, then this is a perfect time to travel to Sri Lanka with family for a relaxing tour. You can also explore hill country like Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, and Ella.

The weather will be pleasant with delightful rains and mist, especially in the afternoons. You also get to experience the vibrant celebrations of Christmas (late December) and Tamil New Year (mid-April).

items: If you want to explore all the major destinations in Sri Lanka, then these months are best due to fewer crowds.
During this time, you will see the beauty of Udawalawe National Park, Polonnaruwa, Anuradhapura, Trincomalee, and Galle at its peak.
Monsoon is the best time to explore Sri Lanka for nature lovers.
It is the best time to explore the eastern coast beaches of Sri Lanka and many cultural events in the north.
You can enjoy festivals like Esala Perahera (July–Aug), Poson Poya (June), Nallur Festival (July) and explore Yala National Park, Arugam Bay, Passekudah, Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil (Jaffna), Colombo.
If you hate crowds and want to enjoy a quiet trip, opt for a Sri Lanka holiday package during October to November.
The weather is overall pleasant with occasional rainfall.

With fewer tourists, you get to explore the mesmerizing beauty of Sri Lanka in a much more relaxed and uncrowded environment. If you want a Sri Lanka trip on a Budget, then check out our best Budget tours for Sri Lanka.

blocks.text: Why You Should Come to Sri Lanka?

Sri Lanka welcomed over 2 million international tourists in 2024, and the momentum continues in 2025-26. Indian tourists contributed over 2,40,000 arrivals in the first half of 2025 alone — making India one of the top source markets for Sri Lanka tourism.

It has become a favorite destination globally due to its rich culture. It offers a blend of scenic beaches, wildlife parks, tea plantations, and traditional art tours, which keep the day of the tourists memorable.
Other Reasons to Visit Sri Lanka

items: Anuradhapura is one of the oldest planned cities in South Asia, with over 2,300 years of recorded Buddhist civilisation. It remains one of the most sacred pilgrimage destinations in Asia and a recognised UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Sri Lanka has kept the genuine Buddha tooth relic with great care. It is one of the best things to explore in Sri Lanka.
You can also witness prehistoric art, which dates back over 2000 years, depicting animal and Buddhist motifs.

For Science lovers or curious travellers, Sri Lanka tourism offers an interesting opportunity, like Whale watching with marine biologists near Mirissa. Those who love to know about Marine biodiversity must experience this once in their lifetime.

If you are an Indian National and planning a trip to Sri Lanka, then it's good news for you. Indian Nationals don't need a Visa to travel to Sri Lanka ; they only need an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization) through the official Sri Lanka ETA website .
The ETA is needed for short-term purposes. It is granted for 30 days to an Indian tourist. Double entry facility is also an option from the date of first arrival to Sri Lanka within 30 days.

To apply for an ETA, submit an application form online to the Department of Immigration and Emigration. Pay the required processing fees and submit the application. After submission of the form, you will receive an acknowledgement promptly.
You also need to have a valid passport of not less than 6 months from the date of arrival.
You can extend your ETA up to 6 months at the Immigration Services Centre in Colombo or at the Department of Immigration and Emigration in Battaramulla.
