blocks.text: Places to Visit during the Sri Lanka Trip

A Sri Lanka trip must include an exploration of its stunning beaches, diverse wildlife, and ancient temples. Most Sri Lanka travel packages involve these aspects to give you a rich, fulfilling experience. Here are the top places that must be on your Sri Lanka itinerary :

This is the commercial capital of Sri Lanka and also the largest city here. Colombo is best known for providing cultural experiences through its colonial architecture. Meanwhile, you also get to experience the modern development spread throughout the capital. It's the best of both worlds, really! Top attractions here include:

items: Colombo National Museum: It's an absolute must for history buffs who would like to learn about the island's rich history and culture.
Pettah Market: This market is perfect for collecting souvenirs and purchasing local goods.
Galle Face Green: This urban park provides a gorgeous backdrop for your sunset strolls.
Gangaramaya Temple: This is a Buddhist temple that houses a museum within itself. Tourists admire it for its remarkable architecture.

blocks.text: This city is a serene hub, surrounded by lush green forests. Moreover, it's also a UNESCO World Heritage site and therefore must be included in your Sri Lanka Heritage Tour Package . The best tourist places here are:

items: Temple of the Tooth: This temple holds a very sacred relic of the Buddha and is therefore considered the holiest Buddhist site in the entirety of Sri Lanka.
Kandy Lake: This man-made lake is nestled in the heart of the city. Tourists often saunter around here during the early mornings.

Cultural Show: Don't miss the traditional Kandyan dance here which is native to Sri Lanka. The dance is often accompanied by the drum performance and is a great evening show for the travellers. Many Sri Lanka tour packages include this show in the itinerary.
Royal Botanical Gardens: This is one of the largest and oldest botanical gardens in Asia. Travellers love the orchid collection here.

blocks.text: Sigiriya is an ancient fortress complex on the island. Tourists and even locals are so impressed with this monument that they often label it as the eighth wonder of the world! Top attractions here include:

items: Sigiriya Rock: This rock formation is as high as 200 meters. On top of it lies the palace. Tourists often enjoy climbing the rock and soaking in the panoramic views of gardens and frescoes down below.
Pidurangala Rock: This is another rock formation that provides scenic views. The sunset views from here are otherworldly.

blocks.text: This was once the capital of Sri Lanka in ancient times, and now is a recognized UNESCO World Heritage site! Here, you get to experience the sacred sites and old ruins. It definitely should be included in your Sri Lanka holiday package if you are a history enthusiast. Top Attractions here include:

items: Sri Maha Bodhi Tree: Meet the oldest historically documented tree in the world! This tree is believed to have grown from the original tree under which Buddha attained enlightenment.
Abhayagiri Monastery: This is a huge monastic complex that is as old as two millennia.
Ruwanwelisaya Stupa: This site is especially important if you are a Buddhist pilgrim. This massive Stupa houses the largest collection of Buddhist relics in the whole world.

blocks.text: Located in the central highlands, Ella is a beautiful hill station that has picturesque views and majestic waterfalls. It's also great for tourists who love hiking, as it has long hiking trails. Notable attractions here are:

items: Ella Rock: Get the bird's-eye view of the stunning valleys and tea plantation when you hike on Ella Rock. Many Sri Lanka tour packages include this site as the panoramic views here are to die for.
Nine Arches Bridge: This scenic bridge has a lot to offer to your Sri Lanka trip. Built during the colonial era, it is surrounded by lush greenery and immerses you in a serene atmosphere.
Ravana Falls: Get a rejuvenating dip in this beautiful waterfall. It's a hit with both tourists and locals alike!

blocks.text: Often called 'Little England,' Nuwara Eliya sits at 1,868 metres above sea level and is unlike anywhere else in Sri Lanka. The cool, misty climate, colonial-era bungalows, and vast tea estates feel like a completely different world from the tropical coast. Whether you are doing a beach + hill country combination or simply want to experience Ceylon tea at its source, Nuwara Eliya is essential. Top attractions include:

items: Pedro Tea Estate: One of Sri Lanka's finest tea estates, offering a guided factory tour from leaf to cup — with free tasting at the end. About 2 hours.
Gregory Lake: A serene man-made lake at the heart of town, perfect for a morning walk or a short boating session.
Horton Plains National Park: About 30 km away. Home to 'World's End' — a sheer 870-metre drop with sweeping views of the southern plains on clear mornings.
Victoria Park: A beautifully maintained botanical garden home to many migratory bird species between March and August.

blocks.text: Galle is a coastal city on Sri Lanka's southwest tip, best known for its 17th-century Dutch colonial fort — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Walk the ramparts at sunset and the Indian Ocean views are unforgettable. The fort's cobblestone lanes have boutique cafes, galleries, and excellent restaurants. Galle combines history and beaches in a way that no other Sri Lankan city does. Top attractions include:

items: Galle Fort: Walk the full perimeter of the fort walls — the lighthouse and the Dutch Reformed Church are the most photographed spots.
Unawatuna Beach: One of Sri Lanka's most beautiful beaches, just 6 km from Galle. Calm, curved bay perfect for swimming and snorkelling.
Galle National Museum: Colonial-era artifacts and local heritage. About 1 hour.

blocks.text: Yala holds the highest density of wild leopards of any protected area in the world. Jeep safaris operate twice daily — at dawn (5:30–6:00 AM) and afternoon (3:00 PM). Beyond leopards, Yala is home to elephants, sloth bears, saltwater crocodiles, and over 200 bird species. Best visited between February and July when wildlife activity peaks. Most of our Sri Lanka Heritage Tour and Group Tour packages include a Yala safari stop.
Things to Do during the Sri Lanka Trip

There is a plethora of activities you can do in Sri Lanka. Whether you are an adventure seeker, a history buff, or a nature lover, you're in for a treat when in Sri Lanka. Here are a few things you must include in your Sri Lanka tour package:

items: Sri Lanka is a treasure trove of cultural and historical landmarks with a number of temples, cities, and monuments to discover.
Some must-visit sites include Sigiriya Rock Fortress, Temple of the Sacred Tooth, Anuradhapura, Dambulla Cave Temple, Galle Fort, and Polonnaruwa.
The central highlands of the island are famous for their lush tea plantations. While you are on your Sri Lanka trip, do not miss the tea factory tour.
You can go see how Ceylon tea is made from scratch and sample the finest teas.
You can visit the Dambatenne Tea Factory in Haputale or the Pedro Tea Estate in Nuwara Eliya for a top-notch experience.

blocks.text: The island is famous for its beaches. Some popular tourist beaches here are Unawatuna, Mirissa, Arugam Bay, Bentota, and Nilaveli.

items: Sri Lanka is home to various national parks and reserves where you can enjoy wildlife.
Some popular parks are Yala National Park, Sinharaja Rainforest, Wilpattu National Park, Udawalawe National Park, and Minneriya National Park.

blocks.text: Sri Lanka is an adventure lover's paradise. You can enjoy plenty of adventure activities here, like hiking (at Horton Plains National Park and Baker's Falls), white-water rafting (at Kitulgala), and hot-air ballooning (at Galle).

Between November and April, the waters off Mirissa are home to Blue Whales — the largest animals ever to have existed on Earth. Sperm Whales and pods of Spinner Dolphins are also regularly spotted. Morning boat departures operate at 6:30 AM from Mirissa harbour. Tours run for approximately 4–5 hours with licensed operators. This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience that many travellers rate as the highlight of their entire Sri Lanka trip.
7. Scenic Train Ride — Kandy to Ella

The 7-hour train journey from Kandy to Ella through Sri Lanka's central highlands is consistently rated one of the most beautiful train rides in the world. Passing through misty mountains, tea estates, waterfalls, and jungle valleys, it is an experience worth planning your itinerary around. Reserve a seat in the observation car in advance — it fills up fast during peak season. Sit on the left side when travelling from Kandy for the best valley views.
8. Visit a Tea Factory in Nuwara Eliya

The central highlands produce world-famous Ceylon tea. Both the Pedro Tea Estate in Nuwara Eliya and the Dambatenne Tea Factory in Haputale offer guided tours showing the full production process — from picking and withering to rolling, fermenting, and drying — ending with a free tasting. About 1.5 to 2 hours per visit. A fascinating experience even if you are not a tea drinker.
What to Eat during the Sri Lanka Trip

Sri Lankan cuisine is a delicious mix of flavors like spicy, tangy, and aromatic. The food is mainly centered on fresh vegetables, meat, seafood, and rice. Here are some of the dishes you must try on your Sri Lanka trip:

This is the staple diet of the island. The meal consists of a big serving of steam rice along with a number of small servings of curries (either vegetable, dhal, fish, or meat curry). Often these are supplemented with condiments like pickled vegetables and spicy sambals.

Hoppers are rice flour pancakes that are soft in the center and crispy around the edges. They are eaten as a breakfast or dinner and often served with dhal or lamb curry. The hoppers come in three varieties — plain hopper, sweet hopper (sweetened with palm sugar), and egg hopper (cooked with egg at the center).
This is a common street food prepared by stir-frying Godamba roti with meat, eggs, and vegetables. It is cooked on a griddle and served with a dipping sauce to make a savory and spicy dish.
This traditional Sri Lankan dish is made with fresh local fish like mackerel or tuna. To give it a spicy and tangy flavor, it is cooked with tamarind and Sri Lankan spices.
This delicious meal is made of vegetables, curry (generally meat curry), and rice and is then wrapped in a banana leaf and steamed.

Sri Lanka's signature dessert — a steamed custard pudding made with coconut milk, eggs, and kithul palm jaggery. Silky in texture, subtly spiced, and mildly sweet. Found on the menu at almost every good Sri Lankan restaurant. Don't leave the country without trying it at least once.

Delicate steamed noodle cakes made from rice flour, served with coconut sambol and dhal curry. A popular breakfast and dinner across Sri Lanka, especially in the central highlands and coastal towns. Lighter than regular hoppers and a favourite among first-time visitors to Sri Lankan food.
Sri Lanka produces some genuinely excellent things worth bringing home. Not just souvenirs — quality items you will actually use and enjoy.

items: Ceylon Tea: Buy directly from estate shops or trusted brands like MLESNA and Dilmah. Available in loose leaf and gift-pack formats. Choose from single-estate teas or classic Ceylon blends.
Ceylon Cinnamon: Real Ceylon cinnamon is softer, lighter, and sweeter than the cassia variety common in India. A meaningful and inexpensive gift. Best bought in Pettah Market or spice shops.

Gemstones: Sri Lanka is one of the world's leading producers of blue sapphires, cat's eye, and moonstones. Purchase only from certified dealers — look for the Sri Lanka Gem & Jewellery Association certification. Avoid roadside shops.
Batik & Handloom Fabrics: Beautiful hand-printed textiles. Fixed-price government stores (Laksala) are reliable for quality. Bargaining is possible in local markets.
Wooden Masks & Crafts: Traditional Kolam masks from Ambalangoda are distinctive and make excellent wall decor. Look for handmade pieces over machine-pressed ones.
Ayurvedic Products: Sri Lanka has a strong Ayurvedic tradition. Herbal oils, soaps, and creams made from local ingredients are widely available and affordable.
Pettah Market, Colombo — for spices, fabrics, everyday goods
Odel Shopping Mall, Colombo — for branded clothing and souvenirs
Kandy City Centre — for gems and handcrafts
Galle Fort boutiques — for premium artisan goods
Laksala Government Handicrafts — reliable fixed-price quality
Local tea factory shops — for estate-fresh Ceylon tea

blocks.text: Colombo has a lively nightlife scene — rooftop bars, beach clubs, and live music venues. The Galle Face area and Colombo Fort neighbourhood have the highest concentration of spots. Most close around 2 AM. Galle's fort area has excellent wine bars open late. Mirissa and Arugam Bay have relaxed beach shack atmospheres, especially during peak season.
Major Festivals — Plan Your Trip Around These

rows: Sri Lanka's most spectacular event — elephant parade, fire dancers, drummers honouring the Sacred Tooth Relic. Hotels in Kandy book up months ahead.
Celebrates birth and enlightenment of Buddha. Lantern displays, free food stalls, and illuminated floats across the country.
Commemorates the introduction of Buddhism to Sri Lanka. Huge lantern displays and pilgrimage walks.
Traditional New Year with rituals, sweets, and family gatherings. Public holidays across the country.
Major Hindu festival at Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil — colourful processions, devotional music, and rituals.
Festival of Lights celebrated by Hindu communities across Sri Lanka.

blocks.text: How to Reach Sri Lanka from India
Sri Lanka is one of the easiest international destinations to reach from India — no long-haul flight, no complicated connections. Just a short hop across the Palk Strait.
Direct flights operate from several Indian cities to Colombo's Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB):

items: One-stop options: Travellers from Pune, Ahmedabad, or Kolkata can connect via Mumbai or Chennai — total travel time around 5–8 hours including layover.
Booking tip: Flights from Chennai and Kochi are typically the most affordable. Book 6–8 weeks in advance during peak season (December–March) for the best fares.

blocks.text: A ferry service connecting Nagapattinam (Tamil Nadu) to Kankesanthurai (northern Sri Lanka) is available for travellers who prefer sea travel or are exploring northern Sri Lanka. Check current schedules before planning as availability may vary.
Once you land in Colombo, navigating Sri Lanka is straightforward. Here are your main transport options:

items: Private AC Vehicle (included in our packages): The most comfortable option for inter-city travel. All our packages include a dedicated private vehicle with driver — no public transport hassles, flexible stops, and air-conditioned comfort throughout.
Scenic Train: The Kandy–Ella route is world-famous. Book reserved seats (especially the observation car) well in advance during peak season — they sell out fast.
Tuk-Tuk: Perfect for short distances within towns. Always agree on the fare before you get in. Average city ride: equivalent to ₹30–80.
PickMe App: Sri Lanka's equivalent of Ola/Uber. Reliable in Colombo and major tourist towns. Download before your trip.
Bus: Most economical but not recommended for long distances if you are on a schedule. Suitable for short hops between nearby towns.

blocks.text: Sri Lanka Travel Tips for a Memorable Vacation
Here are some practical as well as destination-specific travel tips to make your Lanka trip fun-filled with your family and friends-

items: Try Unique Places: Explore all the unique places and try different activities to enjoy the best of Sri Lanka Tourism . Your itinerary should have a blend of history , culture, adventure, nature, and spiritual trips.
Don't miss the Fun: Don't miss the Mirissa adventure tour if you are in Sri Lanka. You will learn very unique and interesting insights into Marine biology.
Village tours for authentic experiences: You can also explore Sri Lankan villages and experience their lifestyle and culture for an enriching Sri Lanka trip.

Pack Wisely: Sri Lanka enjoys tropical weather, so pack your clothes accordingly. For temple hopping, you must cover your shoulders and knees. Modesty is the best policy when you are on a spiritual tour. If there is any sacred offering, receive it with both hands to show respect.
Hotels near main destination: For nature and wildlife enthusiasts, book hotels, lodges, or guesthouses near the main destination.
Sample Cuisine Wisely: Not everything will suit your taste buds in Sri Lanka. So, sample the cuisines wisely. Avoid too many spicy foods.

When to visit: You can avoid the monsoon if your priority is not a specific trip. Consider December - March the best time to go west, south, and hill country in Sri Lanka. For east tours, consider April to September.
Affordable Calls: In Sri Lanka, the major local SIM card providers are Dialog and Mobitel. So, buy a local SIM from city outlets or airports to make your calls and text messages affordable.

Currency & ATMs: Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR) is the local currency. ATMs are widely available in Colombo and major tourist towns. Carry some cash for national park entry fees, smaller towns, and temple donations. Most hotels and larger restaurants accept credit cards.

Dress Code at Temples: Carrying a light scarf or shawl is more reliable than relying on temple-provided sarongs. Remove footwear before entering any temple premises. Never turn your back to a Buddha statue for a photo.

Book Yala Safari in Advance: During peak season (December–April), Yala National Park jeeps fill up days in advance. Do not assume you can book on arrival. Our packages include pre-booked safari slots to avoid disappointment. Note: Yala briefly closes in September each year — check dates when planning.

blocks.text: The 4 Days Srisailam Mallikarjuna tour package from Hyderabad takes travellers to a destination where every spot feels special and worth exploring.

items: Route: Hyderabad - Srisailam → Srisailam - Hyderabad → Hyderabad Sightseeing → Hyderabad Sightseeing - Departure

blocks.text: Day 1- Hyderabad - Srisailam (213 Kms, 4-5 Hours Drive)

We’ll start your Jyotirlinga trip by picking you up from your preferred location - Hyderabad Airport or Railway Station. Our driver from My Quick Trippers will come to pick you up and take you to Srisailam. If you’ve booked a guide, he’ll come with a driver and stay with you all day to assist. On the way, you’ll visit- Srisailam Dam Bhramaramba Devi Temple Sakshi Ganapathi Temple- This temple may be small, but it is special - people believe the Pandavas visited here. Hatkeshwar Temple Octopus View Point- Enjoy the amazing view of the Krishna River between hills. Its shape is like an octopus (a great photography spot) Chenchu Lakshmi Tribal Museum Paathala Ganga- Many visitors come to Pathala Ganga for boating and to see its caves. It’s a great spot for nature lovers. Ropeway, Srisailam After you arrive, check in at the hotel. In the evening, visit the holy Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga Temple located on the Nallamala Hills. Enjoy your night’s stay at Srisailam. Note- Mallikarjuna Temple is open from 4:30 AM to 3:00 PM and 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM . Places You’ll See
Day 2- Srisailam - Hyderabad (214 Kms / 4-5 Hours Drive)

Start your day with prayer at Lord Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple . Then explore Sri Bhramaramba Ammavari Shakti Peeth Temple , where Goddess Sati’s neck is believed to have fallen. Now go to Paladhara-Panchadhara , a very beautiful spot surrounded by nature. If you get a chance, try camping as well. Climb Sikharam Hill to visit Shikaresvara Temple , then proceed to Sakshi Ganapathi Temple and Pathala Ganga , and don’t forget to take a boat ride on Krishna River . Later, drive back to Hyderabad . If time permits visit the Statue of Equality near Hyderabad Airport . Spend a comfortable overnight stay in Hyderabad . Places You’ll See

Start your day with breakfast and then explore Ramoji Film City . Ramoji Film City is one of the world’s biggest and most famous film studios, listed in the Guinness World Records. Enjoy a day full of entertainment, shows, and sightseeing. Return to the hotel for an overnight stay in Hyderabad. Places You’ll See

After breakfast check out from the hotel and go for sightseeing. The places you visit today will depend on your departure time (optional). Start your day at the historic Golconda Fort . Try clapping at the entrance - the echo travels nearly a kilometer. In the past, it helped warn soldiers during attacks. Now proceed to Nehru Zoological Park . Then, explore the famous Salar Jung Museum . Next, go to Chowmahalla Palace , a beautiful place that took around 100 years to build. Its stunning design will surely impress you. Later, visit Charminar . Try to visit in the evening if possible; the colorful lights make it look truly beautiful. In the evening, visit Laad Bazaar , famous for its bangles, pearls, and traditional Hyderabad items. Drive through Hussain Sagar Lake and Lumbini Park if time allows. After sightseeing, you’ll be dropped at Hyderabad Airport or Railway Station for your next journey. Your Srisailam Mallikarjuna travel package ends with happy memories! Note - Hyderabad city sightseeing is not available on Fridays as many places remain closed. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Taiwan has been a favorite destination for tourists on Tour Packages since long time. Taiwan is called ‘Ilha Formosa’ which means ‘Beautiful Isle’ in Portuguese which it really is, this island is adorned by soaring mountain peaks covered in mist and lush green forests with magnificent coastal land and basins. Spread in over 36 thousand sq. kilometer this island has population of more than 22 million. People of Taiwan have preserved their culture and heritage but have also kept themselves abreast with modernism, this is evident at once when one steps in this country on Tour Packages and which makes this even more enjoyable destination.

In the cities of Taiwan visitors on Tour Package comes across skyscrapers and malls and other commercial facilities which herald Taiwan’s economic status but ubiquitous pagodas, ancient temples and well preserved buildings show the deep roots of past and culture in the hearts of Taiwanese people. The country side has some breathtakingly beautiful waterfalls, lakes, landscapes and dense forests which make it a fascinating place for tourists on Taiwan Tour Packages.

Taipei is the capital city of Taiwan and one of the most modern cities of Asia. Yangmingshan National Park is the prime attraction of this city for tourists as this place has vast mountain range which overlooks the city and add up to the beauty of this park. This park is a peaceful place and has variety of flora and fauna to enchant visitors on Taiwan Travel Packages, there are numerous hot springs in the park which provide soothing time away from hustle and bustle of the city.

National Palace Museum in Taipei is another destination visited by tourist on Taiwan Holiday Packages, this is museum and an art gallery, and is believed to possess maximum number of Chinese artifacts and artwork in the world. Some stunning exhibits of this place are carved olive-stone boat, Jade cabbage and painting of ‘One hundred Horses’. Dragon and Tiger pagodas in the city of Kaohsiung is another attraction for tourists on Taiwan Tour Packages, it is a seven tiered architecture with paintings of heaven, hell and 24 obedient sons. These pagodas lie in Lotus Pond accompanied by Tung Confucius Temple and Chi Ming pagoda.

Green Island is just at 10-12 minutes air ride away from Taipei and has beautiful beaches with fascinating coral reefs, rich flora and fauna and steep seaside cliffs. Aquatic life of Green Island is rich and famous and glass bottom boat ride make it an enjoyable place on Taiwan Travel Packages. Fort Santo Domingo is a historical site built in 16th century at the coastal town of Tamsui. This fort has interesting history and was won and destroyed quite a few times, today it has a museum and is an interesting place to visit on Taiwan Holiday Packages.

Sun Moon Lake in Nantau is another popular place to visit on Taiwan Tour Package, this lake covering an area a shade less than 8 Sq. KM is a mesmerizing place. The poetic setting of this lake and variety of birds that are seen around this lake make it a romantic and enchanting place for visitors. Close to lake is an area which is recognized as habitation of an Aboriginal Tribe called as Thao tribe.

Start your Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry trip with a pick-up from your selected location in Chennai airport or railway station. Our driver will come to receive you and then you will continue the tour of Mahabalipuram. If you choose a guide, they will travel with the driver and help you on the journey. After pick-up you will start your tour and visit- Krishna Mandapam - This is a rock-cut temple made from a single rock. It has beautiful pictures that shows the stories of Lord Krishna and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Arjuna’s Penance Cave Temples - Around 1,300 years old, these caves are peaceful and have stunning rock art – perfect spot for photography. Pancha Rathas After covering the main sightseeing in Mahabalipuram, you will drive to Pondicherry. On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay at Pondicherry. Note- Krishna Mandapam is open every day from 7 AM to 6 PM. Places You’ll See
DAY 2: Pondicherry - Chidambaram - Kumbakonam (Approx. 133 km / 2.5 Hours)

After breakfast, check out of the hotel and go to the Auroville Matrimandir , a calm place for meditation. The Matrimandir and its surrounding gardens have a stunning view, great spot for photography. Then, drive to the hotel and check in. Next, visit Sri Aurobindo Ashram one of India’s most famous ashram. Around 1,200 people live here in its calm spiritual community. Afterward, visit Arulmigu Manakula Vinayagar Temple , an ancient temple dedicated to Lord Ganesh. Visit the Puducherry Museum , famous for its 81 Chola metal statues, one of the largest collections in India. Later proceed to Chidambaram , a temple town famous for the Thillai Nataraja Temple. The temple, spread over 40 acres is dedicated to Lord Shiva as Nataraja. Explore Gangaikonda Cholapuram , popular for the Brihadeeswarar Temple. This UNESCO World Heritage Site has one of the largest Shiva Lingas, 13 feet tall, with excellent architecture (perfect place for photos ). Finally drive to Kumbakonam. After arriving, check into the hotel for an overnight stay. Note- Puducherry Museum is closed on Mondays and holidays. Places You’ll See
DAY 3: Kumbakonam - Thanjavur (Tanjore) - Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) (150 km/ 3.5-4 Hours)

After breakfast, check out and visit Kumbakonam , a city filled with unique temples. On arrival, start exploring the sights. See the Adi Kumbeswarar Temple. Nearby is a large temple tank called Mahamaham Tank , where devotees take holy dips. Next travel to Darasuram , a small town near Kumbakonam , to visit Airavatesvara Temple. Later drive to Thanjavur (Tanjore). On arrival, visit the Brihadeeswara Temple that was built entirely without using any iron or cement. Then, explore Thanjavur Palace where the Maratha rulers lived between 1674 and 1855. Next go to Thanjavur Art Gallery filled with beautiful metal and stone art. These works show the rich culture of Tamil history – perfect for art lovers.. After sightseeing proceed to Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) . Arrive, check into hotel and stay overnight. Places You’ll See

Morning after breakfast, check out the hotel and proceed for sightseeing at Tiruchirappalli. First, visit Sri Ranganatha Swamy Temple , which is one of the 108 Divya Desams (holy shrines of Vishnu). Then proceed to the Jambukeswarar Akilandeswari Temple where water from a small underground flow falls on the Shiva Lingam - something truly special. After that, visit Ucchi Pillayar Temple, dedicated to Lord Ganesha, located on Rockfort , with stunning city views from the top ( don’t forget to take photos ). Then visit the Government Museum at Rani Mangammal Mahal, where you can see collections of art, history and local wildlife. After that visit the Butterfly Park to see colorful butterflies, and explore Nakshatra Vanam, which has 27 trees linked to stars and zodiac signs in Indian astrology. After sightseeing, proceed to Madurai. On arrival, check in to the hotel and enjoy an overnight stay. Note- Government Museum timings are 10 AM to 5 PM. Places You’ll See

On the fifth day of your trip , have breakfast, check out of the hotel, and start your sightseeing tour of Madurai. Visit Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple , a beautiful old temple near the Vaigai River (looks stunning in the evening due to lights). Then, see Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple. Later, drive to Rameshwaram , located on Pamban Island. According to mythology, Rama made a bridge here to reach Lanka and rescue Sita from Ravana. On arrival, check into your hotel. Then explore Ramanathaswamy Temple, Agnitheertham, and Ramjharoka Temple. Stay overnight in Rameshwaram. Places You’ll See

Early in the morning, around 5:00 AM , proceed to the Spatika Linga Darshan , also called Mani Darshan , where the natural crystal Shivling (not man-made) is very important in Hinduism and looks very beautiful. Later you will head out for Agni Teertham to have a holy bath in the sea. Further proceed to the main temple through North gate and Take sacred bath with holy water of the 22 wells, inside the Ramanathaswamy Temple during Theerth Snanam. Then proceed for darshan and pooja at the main temple. After checking out of the hotel, proceed to visit Five-faced Hanuman Temple. Next, explore Ramar Patham and Kothandaramaswamy Temple, Rama Setu/ Adam’s Bridge (stones placed by Lord Rama that don’t sink), and visit Gandamadana Parvatham , where Lord Rama’s footprint is believed to be. Also, explore A. P. J. Abdul Kalam’s house , the home of India’s famous scientist and former President. Go to Dhanushkodi , an old town at Rameshwaram Island. If time allows, explore and enjoy the beaches. On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay in Rameshwaram. Places You’ll See

In the morning, visit the temple once again or take a Samudra Snanam (holy dip in the sea). Afterward, check out of the hotel and drive to Kanyakumari , the point where the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea, and the Indian Ocean meet. Kanyakumari is famous for being the only place where you can see both the sunrise and sunset over the ocean. On arrival, check into your hotel and relax for the rest of the day. Stay overnight at the hotel. Places You’ll See

Early in the morning, you can watch the beautiful sunrise in Kanyakumari. The calm atmosphere makes it a perfect time to take pictures. Later return to hotel for breakfast. After breakfast visit the Swami Vivekananda Rock Memorial - a quiet place surrounded by the sea. Walk over the Sea by Glass bridge to reach Thiruvalluvar Statue. If you have time, take a boat ride. Next move to the famous Kanyakumari Temple , also known as Kumari Amman Temple. This temple is built in Kerala-style architecture , so just get ready to click photos. You can also visit Triveni Sangam where the three oceans meet, and Gandhi Mandapam , built at the place where Mahatma Gandhi’s ashes were kept before being put into the sea. Don’t miss the impressive Thiruvalluvar Statue built in memory of the great Tamil poet and philosopher. Later drive towards Trivandrum. On the way visit Thanumalayan Temple at Suchindram famous for its beautiful architecture and the 22-foot-tall statue of Lord Hanuman. Then continue to Padmanabhapuram Palace known for its traditional Kerala -style design. Don’t forget to take some photos. If time permits stop at Kovalam Beach for a short visit before heading to Trivandrum. On arrival, check into the hotel and later visit Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Overnight stay at Trivandrum. Places You’ll See
After breakfast, your trip to Pondicherry and Tamil Nadu ends with happy memories as you are transferred to Trivandrum Airport or railway station for your onward journey.

blocks.text: Places To Visit On Your Trip To Tamil Nadu
Our signature Tamil Nadu Trip Packages cover some of the most popular as well as hidden gems in Tamil Nadu. Let dive into details-
Kodumbalur Moovar Koil- Offbeat and Sacred Gem

items: It is an ancient temple complex of three Shiva Temples which dates back to the 9th century.

If you are interested in Chola architecture then it is a must visit temple as it is one of the oldest surviving temples of that period. The temple was built by Boodhi Vikrama Kesari of Irukkuvel Clan.
Located in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, The Meenakshi Amman Temple is a place where stories come to life. It has 14 spectacular Gopurams covered in thousands of colorful stucco figures.
The temple is dedicated to goddess Meenakshi and Lord Sundareswarar. The temple was built by the Pandya dynasty.
In the 14th century, Meenakshi Amman Temple was invaded and looted by Malik Kafur but later the temple was renovated by Nayak rulers in the 17th century.
Mahabalipuram has exquisite ancient temples to captivate tourists from all over the world. Its rock cut temple architecture is so sublime as if it is breathed into being by gods.
Witness the beautiful monolithic bas reliefs, legendary Shore Temple, the iconic Pancha Rathas and Arjuna’s Penance.
It is also the best place to learn about ancient sculpting techniques and stone carving.

The Pamban Island of Tamil Nadu is sacred as it is nourished by a sacred pilgrimage place called Rameswaram. It is in the top list of the best places included in our Tamil Nadu Spiritual Package Tours.

It is also a famous Chardham pilgrimage site. Devotees from all across the globe come to Rameswaram to visit Ramanathaswamy Temple and offer their prayers to Lord Shiva. It is believed that the Shivling in the temple was constructed by Devi Sita to help him offer his prayers to atone for his sin of killing Ravana.
It also houses 22 holy water Theerthams (sacred water bodies) which have healing properties. A holy dip is believed to dissolve the sins and karmic backlog of devotees.

blocks.text: Kodaikanal - Scenic Hill Station in Tamil Nadu

items: Don’t forget to explore the “Princess of hill Stations”. It is one of the best hill stations to enjoy peaceful vacations with your family in Tamil Nadu. Nature lovers and solace seekers often pick this place for recreation.
It’s a perfect place for a relaxing family vacation in Tamil Nadu. Here, enjoys boating, cycling, photography of breathtaking plains and valleys, birdwatching and soothing nature walks.
Pondicherry is also known as Puducherry. It is a scenic coastal town which offers relaxing beach getaways in Tamil Nadu.
It is also a French colonial heritage town. There are many well- maintained colonial heritage buildings and French style cafes to explore.
Visit Auroville for peace, Promenade beach for leisure strolls, Puducherry Museum to witness traditional crafts.
Explore French bakeries such as Baker Street, Zuka and Bouche Sucree and try various French pastries and delicacies.

The vibrant Metropolis Chennai will captivate your heart and mind. It offers a perfect blend of history, culture and nature. Chennai is renowned for its traditional arts, music and dance forms. If you are here, you must watch Bharatnatyam Dance performances.
Chennai also houses many serene eco-parks like Semmozhi Poonga which houses around 500 exotic plants. Here you can enjoy fun-filled picnics, nature walks with your family.
You can also explore Snow Kingdom which is one of the largest indoor snow centers to enjoy snow and snow related fun activities in any season.

blocks.text: Top Things to Do on Your Trip in Tamil Nadu

Tamil Nadu is a place where no tourist can feel bored. There is something to do for every kind of traveller. Because it has so much to offer tourists often get confused as to what to do here to have an authentic Tamil Nadu tourism experience. So here is a short list of our top picks of things to do in Tamil Nadu-
Wander at the UNESCO Sites of Mahabalipuram

items: The archeological genius of Mahabalipuram is Mind-boggling. Capture the exquisite shore temple and other exquisite rock cut temple architecture.
Learn about the ancient technique of stone carving from local artisans.

blocks.text: Offer Prayers at the ancient temples of Madurai and Thanjavur

items: Don’t just visit Meenakshi Amman Temple but also stay for a night ceremony where the deities are put to sleep. Witness the sacred rituals like Abhishekam, Alankaram and Deepa Aaradhanai etc.

Offer your prayers to the sacred Brihadeeswarar Temple. The temple houses a famous Bronze Nataraja Statue, displaying Lord Shiva as a cosmic dancer. Here you will also learn a detailed history about the Chola Empire through inscriptions and murals in the temple complex.

blocks.text: Recreation at the Hill Stations in Tamil Nadu

items: The cool climate and scenic views of the soothing hill stations of Tamil Nadu such as Yercaud, Kodaikanal, Ooty will delight your soul. Visit any of the scenic hill stations in Tamil Nadu and capture beautiful natural views.

Enjoy trekking in lush green forests, boating at Ooty lake or Kodaikanal Lake or spend quality time with your family at lakeside points. Honeymooners and families often visit Tamil Nadu Hill station Tour Packages to enjoy an unforgettable holiday.
Enjoy Birdwatching at Mudumalai and Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuaries. These popular bird Sanctuaries in Tamil Nadu offer wild escape to nature lovers and bird watchers.
Bring Binoculars and capture unique birds like Darters, Painted Storks and Spot Billed Pelicans etc.

blocks.text: Spiritual Shores of Rameswaram and Kanyakumari

items: Indulge in ritual baths at Rameswaram. It houses 22 sacred Teerthams (holy water bodies) which are believed to dissolve the karmic backlog of devotees.
Explore the beauty of Dhanushkodi beach and ruins. Capture the scenic sunrise and sunset views.

Witness the confluence of Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal and Indian Ocean at Kanyakumari. Visit Kumari Amman Temple dedicated to goddess Parvati. Also visit Adikesava Perumal Temple which is one of the 108 Divya Desams dedicated to Lord Vishnu.

blocks.text: Enjoy a thrilling Wildlife Safari in Tamil Nadu

items: Adventure lovers must try a thrilling wildlife safari in Tamil Nadu. You can book Annamalai Tiger Reserve Safari or visit Kalakad-Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve and Guindy National Park (Chennai).
Spot various animals like Tigers, Nilgiri Langur, Chital, Jackal, blackbucks, Lions, Gaur, Elephants and endemic lion-tailed macaques.

blocks.text: Tamil Nadu Travel Tips for Memorable Holidays with Family

Tamil Nadu is a travel destination which will offer you a perfect blend of cultural, spiritual heritage, scenic hill stations, vibrant cities and beautiful beaches. Here are some useful tips for you to follow for a memorable holiday with your loved ones-

items: If you want to enjoy the best of Tamil Nadu hospitality in general then you should plan your trip in winters - November to February. It is ideal for enjoying outdoor adventures and sightseeing of all the famous destinations.
While planning for temple visits, dress conservatively. You need to wear covered clothes. Carry shawls, stoles and Dupattas to cover your head and shoulders.
Respect the customs and traditions of a place. There is a local custom of folding the banana leaf after eating.
While we offer multilingual guides, it is still better to learn important phrases in Tamil to understand the communication better with locals.
Try to avoid beaches and remote areas after dark and keep your belongings safe. Use anti-theft luggage and bags to keep your belongings and documents safe.
Always carry enough cash for small purchases and temple visits. You may not get online payment facilities at some places.
Carry weather specific clothes for a comfortable Tamil Nadu sightseeing tour.

blocks.text: This Tamil Nadu pilgrimage tour Package will surprise you with its mix of heritage, seaside beauty, and rich culture. From Chennai, the trip takes you first to Mahabalipuram, famous for the Pancha Rathas, where each temple is made from a single big stone.

items: Route: Arrival Chennai - Mahabalipuram - Pondicherry → Pondicherry- Chidambaram- Kumbakonam → Kumbakonam-Tanjore -Trichy → Trichy - Rameswaram → Rameshwaram - Madurai - Kodaikanal → Kodaikanal Sightseeing

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrival Chennai - Mahabalipuram - Pondicherry (250 - 280 km/ 6 - 7 hours)

Start your Tamil Nadu trip. Your journey begins in Chennai, where our My Quick Trippers team will meet you at Chennai Railway Station or airport and take you to Mahabalipuram to see the main sights. Later, continue to Pondicherry for local sightseeing. If you have a guide, they will join the driver and help you for the whole day. Explore These Places in Mahabalipuram Five Rathas- ancient rock-cut temples, the best destination to click photos. Cave Temple- A beautiful temple around 1,200–1,300 years old. Arjuna’s Penance- In Mahabalipuram, a huge rock shows a story from the Mahabharata. Arjuna is shown meditating to gain special powers surrounded by gods, animals and magical scenes. In Pondicherry, you will visit- Artificial Beach- A man-made seaside spot. Auroville Ashram- It is a peaceful community where people from around the world live together. Many visitors come here from far away to experience its unique meditation. Once sightseeing is done, spend the night in Pondicherry. Note- Carry water, sun protection, and comfortable walking shoes. Photography is allowed at most places, but follow local rules. Places You’ll See
Day 2: Pondicherry- Chidambaram- Kumbakonam (140 km/3-4 hours)

In the morning, go to Chidambaram and spend time at the Nataraja Temple. This temple covers an area of 40 acres. It is famous for its unique architecture and is perfect for taking pictures. Later, drive to Kumbakonam . On arrival, in Kumbakonam, visit Oppiliappan Koil, Thiruvenkadu,Thirunageswaram (oldest temple around 1,100 years), Thirumanancheri (known for beautiful surroundings), Patteeswaram , Alangudi , Suriyanar Kovil (best for morning sunrise views), Kanjanur , Vaitheeswaran Temple , Keezhaperumpallam , Thingalur , Thirunallar . Overnight stay at the hotel. Places You’ll See

After breakfast, visit Tanjore to see the Brihadeeswarar Temple , famous for one of the largest Shiva lingams in India. Next, explore Tanjore Palace and its museum . Later, travel to Trichy . See the Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple in Srirangam , visit Rockfort (best place to click photos from the top because of city views), then also visit Samayapura , and Thiruvanaikaval . After having dinner, continue to Rameswaram and stay overnight there. Note- Brihadeeswarar Temple timing is 6am -12:30pm , 4pm - 8:30pm Places You’ll See

After breakfast, travel to Rameswaram. Enjoy sightseeing in Rameswaram and visit Pamban Bridge (famous sea bridge with amazing views), Ramanatha Swamy Temple , Ramar Patham (believed footprints of Lord Rama), Kothandaramaswamy Temple , Agni Theertham (holy water for ritual baths), Dhanushkodi (scenic beaches to click photos), Hanuman Temple and floating stonenear Hanuman ji temple (sacred stone that floats on water called Ram Setu). Then, return to the hotel, enjoy dinner, and stay overnight. Places You’ll See
Day 5: Rameshwaram - Madurai - Kodaikanal (Distance approx, 313 km/ 6-7 hours)

Early in the morning, start with Spatika Lingam Darshan at the Ramanathaswamy Temple in Rameswaram . After that, proceed to Madurai . Visit the Meenakshi Amman Temple and enjoy its stunning design. This temple has 14 colorful towers , which makes it more unique than many other temples. After sightseeing in Madurai , drive to Kodaikanal . On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay at Kodaikanal. Note- Meenakshi Amman Temple is closed during lunch hours (around 12:00pm - 4:30pm ), so plan your visit accordingly. Places You’ll See

After breakfast start sightseeing in Kodaikanal . Enjoy beautiful hills and fresh mountain air. In Kodaikanal , visit Bryant Park (a beautiful garden with colorful flowers), Coakers Walk , Pillar Rock , Suicide Point (breathtaking views of valleys and forests for photos), Silver Falls (180 feet waterfall hidden in the forest), Bear Shola Falls , Kurinji Andavar Temple (special Kurinji flowers bloom here once every 12 years) and Kodaikanal Lake ( perfect for boating and relaxing ). Return to the hotel for relaxation after a day full of sightseeing. Overnight stay at Kodaikanal . Note- Kodaikanal is at a high altitude, so the weather can be cool even during the day. Carry warm clothes. Places You’ll See

After breakfast, drive to Ooty . Stop at Palani to visit the Murugan Temple (famous for its 600+ stairs going up the hill) and visit Coonoor to enjoy the beautiful tea gardens and hill views. After arriving in Ooty , check into the hotel. Places You’ll See

After breakfast proceed for Ooty sightseeing. Explore the key attractions and enjoy the natural beauty of this hill station. In Ooty, visit Botanical Gardens , Rose Garden (India’s largest with 2,000+ rose varieties), Ooty Lake (boating and horse rides), Doddabetta Peak (known for the highest Nilgiri peak with valley views), Government Museum , Pykara Falls (scenic waterfall for photography), Chocolate Factory , Golf Course and Lady Canning’s Seat . Have dinner after sightseeing and continue your night journey to Tiruvannamalai . Note- Since it’s a hilly area, download maps before you start. Places You’ll See

Check into the hotel in Tiruvannamalai . After that, proceed for sightseeing. Have Darshan of Lord Annamalaiyar at the famous Annamalaiyar Temple . Unlike most temples, Annamalaiyar Temple has a special ritual called Girivalam, where devotees walk around the Arunachala Hill at night on full moon days for spiritual blessings. Overnight stay at the hotel in Tiruvannamalai . Places You’ll See
Day 10: Tiruvannamalai - Kanchipuram - Thiruttani (Approx. 195 km/ 5.5 hours )

Start your day with a road trip to Kanchipuram . Once you arrive visit the famous Ekambareswarar Temple , dedicated to Lord Shiva, which has the 6th-tallest Gopuram (towered entrance) in the world. Next stop at the Kailasanathar Temple , an ancient temple made of sandstone. Unlike many temples that are painted, its stone designs are left natural, which gives the temple its unique charm. After Darshan, you will travel by road to Thiruthani . When you reach, check into the hotel for an overnight stay. Places You’ll See
After breakfast, your Tamil Nadu pilgrimage tour package ends, and you will be taken to your departure location for your home.

items: Route: Chennai Arrival → Chennai - Mahabalipuram → Mahabalipuram - Tanjore → Tanjore - Trichy - Madurai → Madurai - Rameshwaram → Rameshwaram - Kanyakumari

blocks.text: Arrival at the Chennai airport. Our representative meets and welcomes you on your arrival to Chennai Railway station/Airport. Later our representative assists you to transfer to Cochin Hotel. Later visit Kapaleeswarar Temple and Ashtalakshmi Temple, evening free to Explore the beaches, overnight stay at hotel. Places You’ll See

Morning, after breakfast drive to Mahabalipuram visit Crocodile Farm and Dakshinachitra (Craft village). Visit Shore Temple (UNESCO World Heritage site) and other heritage sites (Pancha Ratha, Varaha Cave Temple, Tiger Cave, Krishna Mandapam, Balancing rock, Arjuna’s Penance, all within 1-2 km radius) in the evening. Overnight in Mahabalipuram. Places You’ll See

After breakfast drive to Tanjore, Upon arrival, check in at pre-booked hotel then explore the local tourist attractions which include Brihadeeswara temple, Nandi temple and the Royal Palace complex. Overnight in Tanjore. Places You’ll See

Morning Proceed to Madurai on the way visit Trichy where you see the Rock Fort Temple, Jambukeswarar Temple and Srirangam Temple. Now proceed to Madurai. On arrival check in at hotel. Later explore the marvelous temples and other attractions of this city. The famous places you will visit here include Meenakshi Amman Temple, Gandhi Museum and Thirumalai Nayak Palace. Drive back to hotel. Overnight in Madurai. Places You’ll See

After breakfast at hotel. Drive towards Rameshwaram. On arrival check in at pre-booked hotel then go for city tour covering the sightseeing of the most famous attraction of this place is Rameshwaram temple, a prominent Jyotirlinga of Lord Shiva. Other temples you will visit here include Ramjharoka Temple, Kothandaramaswamy Temple and Ramanathaswamy Temple. Stay overnight at the hotel in Rameshwar. Places You’ll See

Today, after breakfast at hotel leave for Kanyakumari, it is the city where you can witness the confluence of three mighty water bodies- Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean and the Bay of Bengal. The famous places you will visit here include Vivekananda Rock Memorial, Suchindram Temple, Kanyakumari Temple and the Gandhi Mandapam. Enjoy Sunset of Kanyakumari from the tip of India, overnight at Hotel. Places You’ll See

Departure Early morning enjoy the sunrise on the beach. After breakfast transfer to Kanyakumari Trivandrum Airport/ Railway Station for Journey to onwards Destination. Thank you for your patronage and looks forward to serving you again in the near future.

blocks.content: Tawang is a town and administrative headquarter of Tawang district in the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh. It lies on NH-13 section of Trans-Arunachal Highway. blocks.text: Ideally, you can explore Thailand in the months of November to February. Let's know in detail about the best tourism months and off months in Thailand with temperature.

November to February is the best time to enjoy vacation in Thailand with family and friends. The weather is cooler, pleasant and drier for sightseeing and enjoying various outdoor activities, cultural programs, beach vacation and exploring flea markets.

These months are not very preferred for Thailand vacation for tourists. The weather will be very hot for sightseeing if you are visiting Thailand from March to May (Summer)as the northern regions of Thailand are marked by intense heat and humidity. July to October is characterized by heavy rainfall and high humidity which may hinder your sightseeing plans. Due to less crowd, you will get hotels at a low price for stay.
Temperature- Up to 40°C from (March to May) and 23°C to 29°C from (June to October)
Best Places to Explore in Thailand on Your Trip

In 2024 Thailand welcomed around 2 million Indian Tourists which shows the country's popularity for tourism purposes amongst Indian travellers. In 2025, the number has already crossed 1 million by mid- year. Source( India Outbound ). Here are some of the best places to see in Thailand-

items: Bangkok is one of the must visit destinations to explore in Thailand to experience the vibrant CityLife, grand palaces, Sacred Temples like Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha).
It is Known as the Venice of East due to its beautiful network of canals and buildings on Stilts.
Witness a dynamic mix of modernity and tradition with exciting nightlife, bustling markets and cultural landmarks.

blocks.text: Chiang Mai- The Rose of the North

items: Chiang Mai is a beautiful city of North Thailand known for its rich cultural heritage and ancient temples such as Wat Chedi Luang.
Vibrant night markets and unique festivals like Loi krathong makes the place a tourist magnet.
Tourists are also drawn to the beautiful natural sceneries including Doi Suthep and Doi Inthanon National Park.

Ayutthaya used to be the second capital of the Siamese Kingdom. It is renowned for its ancient temples, royal ruins, and historical parks like Wat Mahathat with the iconic Buddha head tangled in Banyan roots.
Also, explore Ayutthaya Historical Park which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It has extensive ruins of ancient temples, palaces, and statues, reflecting the grandeur of the Siamese Kingdom.
Stunning limestone cliffs, clear turquoise waters, and beautiful beaches like Railay Beach makes Krabi a must visit destination in Thailand for creating fun-filled memories.
It's a popular hotspot for beach lovers for relaxing vacation.
You can also enjoy rock climbing's, and island-hopping adventures to Phi Phi Islands and others.

blocks.text: Chiang Rai- Soul of Golden Triangle

items: Chiang Rai is a destination famous for its unique cultural and natural attractions. Some of the most popular places to see here are - Wat Rong Khun (White Temple), Wat Rong Suea Ten and Wat Huay Pla Kang.
Also, explore the Golden Triangle circuit where Thailand, Myanmar, and Laos meet along the Mekong River.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Thailand on Your Trip
Enjoy a rich mix of cultural, natural, and recreational experiences in Thailand. Here are some of the best activities to do in Thailand for tourists-

items: Thailand is a wonderful place for beach lovers. If you want to spend your time with family then you can simply visit any amazing beach of Thailand and enjoy a laid-back vacation.
Explore Phi Phi, Koh Samui, and Koh Tao where the calm waters and vibrant coral reefs are ideal for snorkeling, swimming, and marine life encounters.
Explore some of the most important cultural landmarks in Thailand like The Grand Palace, Wat Arun, and Wat Phra Kaew. These places form an integral part of Thailand's spiritual and cultural wealth.
By exploring temples and cultural landmarks you will experience Thai customs, Buddhism, and learn about royal traditions.
Boats selling fresh produce, local snacks, and handicrafts, the floating markets of Thailand are a must not miss.
You can also savor Thai street food, interact with local vendors and interact with the market's lively canals by boat.

blocks.text: Bathe, feed, and learn about elephant conservation in Elephant Sanctuaries like Elephant Jungle Sanctuary, Maerim Elephant Sanctuary, Joy Elephant Sanctuary and community-based Elephant Sanctuary by Karen tribes.
For families, animal lovers and conscious travellers it's a great way to enjoy tourism in Thailand.

A road trip is possible from India to reach Thailand. You have to drive via the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway from northeast India to Mae Sot, Thailand.
You need an International Driver's Permit and multiple visas. It is recommended only for adventurous travelers.

items: You need a Visa to travel to Thailand as Indian citizens require a Visa. You can get it online or on arrival at major airports.

blocks.text: Visa Information for Thailand Vacation for Indian Tourists

items: For Indian Tourists, you need a Visa to enjoy a wonderful vacation in Thailand. You can stay visa free for up to 60 days but you need to apply for TDAC Card - Thailand Digital Arrival Card online within 72 hours before arrival.
You need to have a valid passport for at least 6 months from the date of arrival and a proof of return travel within 60 days.
You also need to show proof of accommodation and sufficient funds on your bank.

blocks.text: Useful Travel Tips to enjoy Thailand Vacation for Indian Tourists
Here are some useful travel tips to enjoy Thailand holidays safely -

items: Pick the peak tourism season to enjoy the best of Thailand Tourism -November. You will have comfortable weather and will get a chance to enjoy festivals like Loy Krathong in November.
Carry all the important documents like ID, Permits, passport etc. for verification. Use Anti-theft bags to keep all your important documents safe while sightseeing in Thailand.
Respect the culture and customs of Thailand. Respect Buddhist monks, speak softly near them. Also practice Thai greetings called 'Wai'. Dress modestly in temples and other sacred sites.
As a tourist, it is our responsibility to not litter in any tourist place or any other spot. Not only it damages tourist reputation but also ruins the image of the home country.

Keep emergency numbers for safety. Do not go out alone at any place, especially in the dark. Download local apps like Skyscanner, Bookaway, or 12Go to easily get bus, train, and boat schedules and fares.

Thailand enjoys a tropical; climate. So, pack cotton or linen clothes, 3-4 T-shirts or tops, 2-3 shorts, 1-2 pairs of pants or jeans for temple visits and cooler evenings. Lightweight pajamas or sleepwear, rain jacket, sunscreen, mosquito repellent, light jacket or hoodie for night and one dressy outfit for fine dining etc.

blocks.text: DAY 01: Arrival - Chennai - Tirupati (3 hrs/140 kms)

Arrive at Chennai and meet our representative at Chennai Railway Station/Airport. Our representative will make all the arrangements to transfer you to Tirupati, which is dotted with cultural and historical treasures. This is a famous pilgrimage town in Andhra Pradesh, home to the Vaishnavite shrine of Tirumala Venkateswara Temple. After reaching Tirupati, you will check into your hotel and relax for some time. You will then head to the Tirumala Hills, that is known to be the sacred abode of Lord Venkateshwara. The Tirumala hills are a group of seven peaks, namely Anjanadri, Vrushabadri, Narayanadri, Seshadri, Neeladri, Garudadri, and Venkatadri. Please Note:- Without a darshan ticket, you won't be able to have darshan at Tirupati. You can opt for Sarva Darshanam. You can choose from two options. Without or with a token, Sarva Darshanam will take more time for darshan. 12-18 hours on weekends, 8-12 hours on regular days, and 12-36 hours on festival days. Without a Darshan Ticket, you may be able to visit Tirumala, but you won't be able to have Darshan at the Main Temple. Places You’ll See
Day 02: Tirupati Darshan-(3 Hrs/110 Kms)- Vellore -(2Hrs/95 Kms)-Tiruvannamalai

Have a delicious breakfast in the morning, and then you will head to Kanipakam and Srinivasa Mangapuram. Later, you will head to Vellore, which houses the Golden Temple. After arriving at Vellore, you will visit the Golden Temple that is situated at Sripuram and built in honor of goddess Lakshmi. The temple's architecture is star-shaped, and the goddess has been placed in the middle of the star. Then you will head to Tiruvannamalai, a renowned pilgrimage center situated at the foothills of Annamalai hills. Once you have arrived, you will check into your pre-booked hotel and visit the main temple. Tiruvannamalai houses Annamalaiyar Temple, which is dedicated to Shiva and worshiped as Annamalaiyar or Arunachalesvara. It is one of the largest temples in India that houses four gateway towers. The Shiva Lingam here has an association with the Pancha Bhoota, specifically the element of Fire. After the darshan, you will head back to your hotel and have an overnight stay. Places You’ll See
Day 03: Tiruvannamalai - (220 Kms/ 5 Hrs)- Thanjavur (Tanjore) - (75 Kms/ 2 Hrs)-Tiruchirappalli (Trichy)

Relish a delicious breakfast in the morning, and then you will check out of your hotel and get ready for sightseeing in Thanjavur. You will visit the famous attractions, including the Brihadeeswara Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the biggest temple in the region. This architectural marvel was built by Raja Raja Chola during the 11th century. You will then visit Thanjavur Palace, a historical structure in Thanjavur. It was the Maratha rulers' official residence from 1674 to 1855. Then you will visit the Thanjavur Art Gallery, where you will see a treasured collection of stone sculptures, bronze icons, and other artifacts, which testify to the golden age in Tamil history. You will then embark on a drive to Tiruchirappalli, renowned for its historical attractions. After arriving in Tiruchirappalli, you will check into your hotel and have an overnight stay. Places You’ll See

Relish a tasty breakfast in the morning, and then you will check out of your hotel. You will get ready for a sightseeing tour of Tiruchirapalli. You will visit the Sri Ranganatha Swamy temple, which is dedicated to Lord Ranganatha Swamy and is considered to be the most important of the one hundred and eight main Vishnu temples. You will then visit the Jambukeswarar Akilandeswari Temple, which is built in honor of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvathi. The temple has an association with the Pancha Bhoota, specifically the element of Water (Jala). Then you will get ready to visit Ucchi Pillayar Temple. This seventh-century Hindu temple is situated at the top of Rockfort and is dedicated to Lord Ganesha. You will also visit the Government Museum, which is located in Bharathidasan San town at Rani Mangammal Mahal. The museum comprises a wide range of exhibits related to anthropology, epigraphy, geology, zoology, paintings, and history. You will then head to Tropical Butterfly Conservatory Campus, the Tropical Butterfly Conservatory. Then you will drive to Madurai. After arriving at Madurai, you will check into your hotel and have an overnight stay. Places You’ll See

Post breakfast, you will check out of the hotel and head out for a sightseeing tour of Madurai. You will visit the famous attractions such as the Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple, which is situated on the southern banks of the river Vaigai. The complex has twelve gateway towers, ranging in height from 45-50 m. Then you will head to Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple, one of the six abodes of Lord Murugan. You will then head to Rameshwaram, which is situated on Pamban Island and is separated by the Pamban channel from mainland India. According to legend, Rameshwaram is considered to be the spot from where Rama built a bridge to rescue his consort Sita from Ravana. You will then head to Rameshwaram and check into your hotel. You will then visit Ramanathaswamy Temple, Ramjharoka Temple, and Agnitheertham and have an overnight stay at your hotel in Rameshwaram. Places You’ll See

Early morning, you will take a dip in the sacred water of Agni Theertham, and then you will go for Sphatik Lingam Darshan. After the darshan and holy bath, you will head back to your hotel and have a tasty breakfast. You will then head out for a sightseeing tour of Rameshwaram, which includes Ramar Patham, Five-faced Hanuman Temple, Gandamadana Parvatham/ Lord Rama footprint, Kothandaramaswamy Temple, Former President A. P. J. Abdul Kalam House, Rama Setu/ Adam's Bridge, and Dhanushkodi. You will then head to Kanyakumari -the Indian Peninsula's southernmost point and the confluence of three oceans - the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean. After arriving at Kanyakumari, you will check into your hotel and have an overnight stay. Dhanushkodi: Adam's Bridge is the main attraction of Dhanushkodi. You can reach this place by hiring a jeep (4-wheel drive). It is a tip of the island where normal cars don't go. Kothandaraman Temple: This is the sacred site where Vibhishana surrendered to Lord Rama. In this temple, Rama, the main idol, has been depicted with a bow and arrow. Places You’ll See
Day 07: Kanyakumari - Kovalam - Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) (2 Hrs/100 Kms)

Early in the morning, you will head out for a sunrise view in Kanyakumari. You will then head back to your hotel and have a Scrumptious breakfast. You will then head out to visit the Swami Vivekananda Rock Memorial, the meditation hall, and the Smarak. You will then head to Kanyakumari mandir, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Other attractions that you will visit include Gandhi Mandapam, which has been built on the place where the urn containing the ashes of Mahatma Gandhi was kept before immersion for public viewing. You will also see the Thiruvalluvar Statue, and then you will drive to Trivandrum. On the way to "Suchindram", you will visit the Thanumalayan temple, known for its splendid architecture. Later, you will visit the "Padmanabhapuram Palace," a sixteenth-century wooden palace where the Travancore king resided. If you have time, you can visit Kovalam beach, and then you will head to Trivandrum. After arriving at Trivandrum, you will check into your hotel. After relaxing for some time, you will visit the Sri Padmanabhaswamy temple, which is dedicated to Visnu/Krishna. You will then have an overnight stay at your hotel in Trivandrum. Places You’ll See

Savour a lip-smacking breakfast, and then you will check out of your hotel. You will be transferred to Trivandrum railway station or the Airport from where you will continue your journey to your hometown. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: On the Tirupati Thanjavur Rameshwaram Kanyakumari Madurai Tour, each city welcomes you with its own charm, rich history and cultural heritage. The journey begins from Tirupati. Don't miss its popular Venkateswara Temple. According to The Times of India around 50,000 people visit this temple every day.

items: Route: Tirupati - Vellore -Tiruvannamalai → Tiruvannamalai - Thanjavur -Tiruchirappalli → Tiruchirappalli - Madurai → Madurai - Rameshwaram → In Rameswaram → Rameswaram - Kanyakumari

blocks.text: We'll start your tour by picking you up from your selected spot in Chennai, whether it's the airport or railway station. Our representative from My Quick Trippers will meet you and take you to Tirupati . If a guide is included, he'll travel with you and provide support during the tour. When you reach Tirupati, you'll explore its sites such as- Tirumala Hills - Here you'll see seven beautiful peaks - Seshadri, Neeladri, Garudadri, Anjanadri, Vrushabadri, Narayanadri, and Venkatadri. The cool air and peaceful view make you feel fresh and happy. Varahaswamy Temple Sri Venkateswara Temple- It is believed that Lord Vishnu stayed in this temple. You'll also notice locals make colorful Rangolis here, which look beautiful, and the whole atmosphere is amazing. When the Darshan is done, come back to Tirupati and rest at your hotel. Enjoy a comfortable night stay in Tirupati. Note- To skip the crowd, book ₹300 special Darshan tickets on the TTD website ( https://tirupatibalaji.ap.gov.in/#/login ) for the Venkateswara Temple. Places You’ll See

Morning after breakfast, proceed to visit Srinivasa Mangapuram and Kanipakam. Later, drive to Vellore, known for its Golden Temple. On arrival, go to the Golden Temple at Sripuram. The gold-plated temple shines beautifully in the sunlight - a great spot for photography. After the visit, proceed to Tiruvannamalai. On reaching, check in at the hotel then explore Annamalaiyar Temple , where Lord Shiva is worshiped as Arunachalesvara or Annamalaiyar . This temple is one of the largest in India located at the base of Annamalai Hill. Return to the hotel. Overnight stay at Tiruvannamalai. Places You’ll See

Morning after breakfast, check out from the hotel and proceed to Thanjavur for sightseeing. Visit the famous Brihadeeswara Temple . Inside, you can see old paintings on the walls that attract every visitor. Later, visit Thanjavur Palace. The Kaveri River flows near the palace, and the view is lovely. It feels so calm when you sit there. Then travel to the Thanjavur Art Gallery, where you can see the real history of Tamil Nadu in an interesting way. After sightseeing, drive to Tiruchirappalli (Trichy). On arrival, check into the hotel. Overnight stay at Trichy. Places You’ll See

After breakfast, check out from the hotel and proceed for sightseeing in Tiruchirappalli. Explore Sri Ranganatha Swamy Temple at Srirangam, which is also one of the largest temple spread over 156 acres, where every corner is worth seeing. Next, visit Jambukeswarar Akilandeswari Temple , dedicated to Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. Then, proceed to Ucchi Pillayar Temple , dedicated to Lord Ganesha , located on the top of Rockfort. You can see beautiful, amazing views of the entire city (don't miss the evening view if time allows). Continue your trip to the Government Museum , built within the Rani Mangammal Mahal. Now, travel to the Butterfly Park filled with colorful butterflies, and later visit Nakshatra Vanam, a peaceful garden nearby and a perfect spot for a picnic. After sightseeing, drive to Madurai . Once you reach, check into the hotel. Overnight stay in Madurai. Note- Wear comfortable footwear as you'll walk a lot while exploring temples and forts. Places You’ll See

After breakfast check out of the hotel and explore the beautiful city of Madurai. Visit Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple popular worldwide for its amazing architecture and interesting facts. As you enter, fragrance of Agarbatti (incense) and the positive atmosphere give a truly amazing feeling. Later, go to Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple. After exploring the city, get ready to travel to Rameshwaram. On arrival, check into the hotel. Later, proceed to Ramanathaswamy Temple, Agnitheertham ( a holy bathing spot ) and Ramjharoka Temple. Relax and spend the night at your hotel in Rameshwaram. Places You’ll See

Start early at 5:00 am with a holy dip at Agni Theertham. Next, visit Sphatik Lingam Darshan, also known as Mani Darshan . The shining crystal lingam here looks truly beautiful and the interesting thing is that it is not man-made. After that, take a holy bath in the 22 wells inside the Ramanathaswamy Temple, known as Theerth Snanam. Once you finish the holy bath and Darshan, return to the hotel for a nice breakfast. After that, go for a local sightseeing tour in Rameswaram and visit places like the Five-faced Hanuman Temple, Ramar Patham, Kothandaramaswamy Temple, Gandamadana Parvatham (famous for Lord Rama's footprint), Rama Setu, Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam's House, and Dhanushkodi. Overnight stay at Rameswaram. Places You’ll See

In the morning, you can visit the Ramanathaswamy Temple again or take a holy dip in the sea, known as Samudra Snanam. After that, check out of the hotel and drive to Kanyakumari , the meeting point of three oceans - the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea, and the Indian Ocean. Kanyakumari is the only place where you can enjoy both sunrise and sunset over the sea. After reaching Kanyakumari, check into the hotel. Check into the hotel and get some rest. Overnight stay in Kanyakumari. Places You’ll See
Day 08- Kanyakumari - Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) (91 Kms / 2 Hours Drive)

Start your morning with a peaceful sea view and some fresh cool air and have breakfast. After breakfast, proceed to visit the Swami Vivekananda Rock Memorial. The ocean view around the rock looks truly beautiful - even Prime Minister Narendra Modi also meditated here. Explore the Kumari Amman Temple , one of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas . It is believed that the spine of Goddess Sati fell here, which makes this temple a very holy place. After that, travel to the Triveni Sangam , the point where the three oceans meet, and then proceed to Gandhi Mandapam , the place where Gandhi's ashes were kept before being placed in the sea. Visit the Thiruvalluvar Statue, which is dedicated to the well-known Tamil poet. The statue is about 133 feet tall. On the way to Trivandrum , go to the Thanumalayan Temple at Suchindram , known for its 22-ft Hanuman statue and stunning architecture (best photography spot). As you reach the Padmanabhapuram Palace , you'll be surprised by its wooden work and traditional Kerala-style design. If time permits, visit Kovalam Beach before reaching Trivandrum. After reaching Trivandrum , check into the hotel. In the evening, visit the Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple , which is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Stay overnight in Trivandrum . Note- Keep some cash with you because small shops or temple counters might not take online payments. Places You’ll See
After breakfast, your trip ends with sweet memories. You'll be dropped at Trivandrum Airport or railway station for your home. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Tirupati Balaji, also known as Lord Venkateswara, is an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. Devotees from all over India visit Tirupati Balaji Temple (Tirumala Temple) to get his divine blessings. Tirupati Balaji temple is the Bhuloka Vaikuntam (earthly abode of Lord Vishnu). Visiting here is equivalent to visiting the real Vaikuntam (the original heavenly abode of Lord Vishnu).

items: According to Hindu Mythology, Rishi Bhrigu, the sage of Fortune, once wanted to know who is supreme among Lord Shiva, Lord Brahma, and Lord Vishnu.

He asked Lord Shiva and Lord Brahma but was unsatisfied with their answer. So, he visited Lord Vishnu for his answer, but when he didn't get any answer, he kicked in the chest of Vishnu, where Goddess Lakshmi resides.
Goddess Lakshmi felt insulted and left Vaikuntha to stay on earth.
To bring Lakshmi back, Lord Vishnu reincarnated as Sri Venkateswara and appeared on Tirumala hill. There he met Padmavati, who is an incarnation of Goddess Lakshmi, and married her.

The marriage was funded by Lord Kuber, the god of fortune. It is said that Lord Venkateswara took a loan for his marriage with Padmavati from Lord Kuber. The donations made by devotees today symbolically help him repay his loan.

blocks.text: Best Time for Tirupati Balaji Darshan 2026

Post-monsoon (July to September) and winter months (October to February) are the best times of the year to plan your Tirupati Balaji Darshan. The temperature during this time ranges from 15°C to 30°C, which is ideal to take the divine blessings of Lord Venkateswara.

items: The weather during post-monsoon and winters is cool and misty, making the divine Darshan possible and bearable.

December and January are the most preferred months for pilgrims to book tickets for Tirupati Balaji Darshan. Tickets during this time booked very fast and completely sold out. So, it is better to book your tickets for Tirumala Venkateshwara Temple Darshan in advance.
Brahmotsavam (September/October) -a 9-day festival at Tirupati Balaji where the processions of deities are carried on different vehicles.
Vaikuntha Ekadashi (December/January) -This festival marks the beginning of Uttarayana.

blocks.text: Months to Avoid for Tirupati Balaji Darshan
Summer (March to June) is not a favorable time for Tirupati Balaji Darshan. The temperature can range up to 40-45°C, which makes Darshan unbearable due to heat and humidity.
Best Things to Do in Tirupati Balaji
Within the temple premises of Lord Venkateshwara (Tirupati Balaji) and near its surroundings, there are many things to do to elevate your spiritual and cultural experiences. Let's know in detail.

items: Take a holy dip at Swami Pushkarini, Papavinasanam, and Akshaya Ganga Theerthams before visiting Swamy Venkateshwara Temple.
The main activity of any pilgrim at Tirupati Balaji is to get the divine blessings of Lord Venkateshwara at Shri Venkateshwara Swamy Temple.
You can stand in a Vaikuntam Queue complex II to get a glimpse of Lord Venkateshwara. It's a free Darshan scheme for the general public.
If you want a quick Darshan of Lord Venkateshwara, then you can book the Special Darshan scheme in advance through TTD portal.
Take part in a daily seva program at the temple, which starts at 2:30 am with Suprabhatam (awakening of the lord) and ends at 7:00 pm to 8:00 pm after Shuddhi (night rituals).
Take Darshan of other sub-shrines in the temple like Padmavati Amma, Varaha Swamy, and Anjaneya.

Explore S.V. Museum, which displays ancient and historical artifacts of the medieval period. It has around 6000 historical items from different periods in history. Witness Srivari Vahanas used during the festival of Brahmotsavam, original copper plates of Annamayya's compositions, and the Varahaswamy copper inscription.
There is a meditation hall on the roof of the museum to indulge in meditation and embrace mindfulness.

Places to Visit Around Tirupati Balaji
Apart from visiting Swamy Venkateswara Temple, you must visit these places to completely dive deep into the spiritual, natural, cultural, and historical whirlwind of Tirumala.

items: If you are interested in exploring historical places, then you must visit Chandragiri Fort, which is located 15 km from Tirupathi.
Yadava rulers built the fort in the 11th century.
It houses a museum that displays amazing artifacts from the time of the Vijayanagara Empire.
TTD Garden is also known as Balaji Garden. It is located near Tirupati Balaji Temple. It's a scenic garden spread over 460 acres, which offers refreshing vibes to solace seekers.
The flowers of these gardens are used for temple rituals of Tirumala Temple.
Located 3 km from Sri Venkateshwara Temple, visit this naturally occurring rock formation.
It is a perfect spot to hang out for nature lovers. Capture blissful views of nature and nourish your soul with enchanting views.
This place is more than 1000 years old, which also makes it one of the most popular historical spots around Tirupati.
Talakona waterfall is one of the best scenic spots in Andhra Pradesh. It is also the tallest waterfall here. Seek solace in the lap of nature. The height of the waterfall is approximately 270 ft.
It is surrounded by the dense forests of Sri Venkateshwara National Park, which is teeming with rich wildlife and flora. You can also enjoy scenic hikes and birdwatching at this spot.

One of Asia's largest zoos, Sri Venkateshwara Zoological Park is a wonderful destination for wildlife enthusiasts. If you are looking for adventure apart from spiritual bliss, then you must come here with your family and friends.
There are around 31 mammal species and 7 reptile species in the zoo. Spot some amazing animals like Royal Bengal tigers, white tigers, leopards, crocodiles, exotic birds, etc.
Located in Tirupati, it is a must-visit sacred place to fine-tune your spirit with divine wisdom. The temple is dedicated to Sri Govindaraja Swamy.

There are many other temples located within the main temple complex. Some of the most notable temples are Shri Kurath Alwar Temple, Shri Parthasarathy Swamy Temple, Shri Kalyana Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Shri Anjaneya Swamy Temple, and many others.
