blocks.text: The route to Tirupati Balaji Temple is not complex, as it has good air, rail, and road connectivity. Let's know in detail how to reach Tirupati Balaji-

items: The best way to reach Tirupati Balaji is by taking a flight. You will get direct flights from New Delhi, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Bangalore, and Indore to reach Tirupati Airport, which is also known as Renigunta Airport.
From the airport, you will get taxis or buses, or you can also hire private AC vehicles to reach Tirumala.
If you prefer to go to Tirupati by rail, then the closest railway station is Tirupati Junction, which is located 10 km away from Tirupati.
From the railway station you will get private buses or buses run by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams to reach the foot of the hills of ALIPIRI and SRIVERIMETU.
There are two well-carved stone footpaths to reach Tirumala. From the ALIPIRI footpath, you will reach Tirumala in 3 hours, and from SRIVERIMETU, you will reach Tirumala in 1 hour 30 minutes.

blocks.text: If you prefer a road route, then take NH44. You will get regular buses run by APSRTC or private buses to reach Tirumala. If you are coming by your own vehicle, then you have to take the ghat road route, which has time restrictions. There is a Ghat road that is laid between Tirupati and Tirumala.

items: The distance from Ghat Road to reach Tirumala is 17.80 km.
The distance from Ghat Road to reach Tirupati is 18.00 km.
The timings of the opening of Ghat Road: 3:00am to 00:00 hours (21 hours).

blocks.text: Useful and Safety Tips for a Memorable Tirupati Balaji Darshan
Some useful Tips for safe and memorable Tirupati Darshan are as follows-

items: Before starting your Tirupati Darshan, take a holy dip in Swami Pushkarini and worship Sri Bhu Varaha Swamy.
If you are in Tirumala, then bathe in Papavinasanam and Akasha Ganga Theerthams, as these are the most sacred Theerthams to nourish your mind and spiritual purification.
Please deposit your offerings at Hundi.

If you are a senior citizen and want to get the divine blessings of Tirupati Balaji, then you have to submit your Aadhaar card and a valid medical certificate issued by the concerned surgeon/specialist if there is any health issue.
Consuming liquor or any non-vegetarian food is highly prohibited in and around temple premises.

You have to wait politely for your turn to get a glimpse of Lord Venkateshwara Swamy, as devotees wait long in the queue if they are opting for General free Darshan. For special Darshan, you don't have to wait that long.
Do not wear flowers at Tirumala Temple; the flowers are reserved for the presiding deity only.
In case of any emergency or accident while coming from Ghat Road, call 0877-2263636/9000503089 and 108 to get the help of an auto clinic/crane and ambulance.
Dress modestly in the temple. Women need to wear covered clothes like Sarees, Chudidars, and Pajamas, and men should wear Dhotis, Kurtas, or Pajamas with upper cloth.

blocks.text: Q1. How many days are enough for Tirupati Darshan?

Ans. If you only want to get the divine Darshan of the Tirupati Tirumala Temple, then 2 days and 1 night is sufficient, but if you also want to offer Seva and explore other temples, the zoological park, and waterfalls, then take 4-5 days.
Q2. How to book Darshan tickets for Tirupati Balaji?
Ans. You can book Darshan tickets for Tirupati Balaji through the official site, Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD).
Q3. How can you buy Seva tickets for Tirupati Balaji?

Ans. To buy Seva tickets, you need to register yourself at the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam online portal and then book seva tickets. You have to book 120 days in advance for Sevas, as slots fill quickly in peak pilgrimage season.
Q4. How can you book accommodation for Tirupati Balaji?

Ans. After registering at the TTD portal, you have to choose an accommodation location-Tirupati or Tirumala-and then select your stay date and room category. Fill in all the pilgrim details and make payment. You must have valid ID proof to book accommodation for Tirupati Balaji Darshan.
Q5. What are the best months for planning Tirupati Balaji Darshan?
Ans. July to February are the best months to plan your Tirupati pilgrimage tour, as the weather will be pleasant at Tirumala Hill for sightseeing and Darshan.
Q6. What is Kalyanakatta in the Tirupati Balaji Temple?

Ans. If a devotee has a wish and he/she wants to get it fulfilled, then they have to do Kalyanakatta in Tirupati Balaji. Kalyanakatta is a ritual where a devotee is tonsured to fulfill their vows. It is done free of cost.
Q7. What are the sacred offerings devotees give to Lord Balaji as a part of the Fulfilment of the vow?

Ans. When the vow is fulfilled, the devotee's Tulabharam (offering of sugar candy, sugar, rice, jaggery, etc.) is equal to his/her weight. They also offer Niluvu Dopidi (ornaments or other jewels worn by the devotee) at Srivari Hundi.
Q8. What are the most popular temples to visit in Tirupati apart from Swamy Venkateswara Temple?
Ans. Apart from Swamy Venkateswara Temple, devotees can visit Sri Govindaraja Swamy Temple, Kapila Theertham, Kalyana Venkateswara Temple, Kodandarama Temple, and Padmavathi Temple.
Q9. What is the nearest airport for Tirupati Balaji?
Ans. Renigunta Airport (Tirupati Airport) is the nearest airport to reach Tirupati. It is located 14-16 kilometers away from Tirupati.
Q10. What are the main rituals of Tirupati Balaji?

Ans. Tirupati holds numerous rituals on a daily, weekly, and periodic basis. Some of the most prominent rituals in the Tirupati Balaji temple on a daily basis are Suprabhata Seva, Thomala Seva, Ekanta Seva, and Archana, etc.

blocks.text: Trivandrum, also known as Thiruvananthapuram, is the capital city of Kerala, India. It is a vibrant and culturally rich city that offers a wide range of experiences for visitors. Trivandrum tour packages provide an opportunity to explore the city’s historical sites, religious landmarks, beautiful beaches, and diverse cuisine.

One of the major attractions in Trivandrum is the iconic Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, dedicated to Lord Vishnu. This magnificent temple is known for its stunning architecture, intricate carvings, and religious significance. It is a must-visit for spiritual seekers and those interested in Indian mythology and culture.

Trivandrum is also home to several museums and art galleries that showcase the region’s history and art. The Napier Museum, known for its Indo-Saracenic architecture, houses a vast collection of artifacts, including ancient sculptures, bronze idols, and historical artifacts. The Kerala Science and Technology Museum and the Natural History Museum are also worth exploring.

For nature lovers, Trivandrum offers beautiful beaches such as Kovalam and Shanghumugham. These beaches are known for their golden sands, clear waters, and breathtaking sunsets. Visitors can relax on the beaches, indulge in water sports, or simply enjoy the tranquil atmosphere.

Trivandrum is also a hub of traditional Ayurvedic treatments and wellness centres. Travellers can indulge in rejuvenating Ayurvedic massages, therapies, and yoga sessions to unwind and revitalize their senses.

Food enthusiasts will delight in the diverse cuisine of Trivandrum. From delectable seafood dishes to traditional Kerala delicacies like Appam, Puttu, and Fish Curry, the city offers a gastronomic journey that will tantalize the taste buds.

Trivandrum tour packages offer a blend of history, spirituality, natural beauty, and culinary delights. Whether you are interested in exploring ancient temples, relaxing on pristine beaches, or immersing yourself in the rich cultural heritage of Kerala, Trivandrum has something to offer for every traveller.

blocks.text: Udaipur, popularly known as the “City of Lakes” is located in Rajasthan, North West of India. Previously being the capital of Mewar, Udaipur was founded by Rana Udai Singh. This place finds a very important place in Indian history due to the bravery of the Rajput chiefs and rulers of Udaipur in preserving the independence, religion, and culture against the Mughals. Based on its glorious past and its colorful culture Udaipur has grown up to be a special tourist destination that attracts tourists from all walks of life and all parts of the globe. Udaipur has been voted as the World’s best city to travel to in an online poll by My Quick Trippers. Book your Udaipur Tour Packages and get an insight into this marvelous honeymoon destination.

Udaipur presents a myriad of attractions to gratify tourists of all tastes, though the main attractions continue to be the picturesque lakes and magnificent forts and palaces that characterize the whole of Rajasthan. The Lake Palace or Jag Niwas built in white marble on the banks of Lake Pichola is the main attraction of Udaipur. The beautifully carved-out structures and the lovely gardens against the backdrop of the Aravalli ranges leave the visitor’s gaze in amazement. Enjoy this honeymoon experience with Udaipur Honeymoon Packages.

A honeymoon in Udaipur can be romantic and colorful with the hymns of Mirabai’s love and devotion to Lord Krishna and the love ballads of courageous Rajputs ringing in the air. Enjoying boating in the beautiful lakes of Udaipur allows the newlyweds to open up and the exalted monuments set the beginning of undying love and responsibility to carry throughout life. Visit Udaipur with our best-priced Udaipur Honeymoon Packages for a memorable honeymoon trip.

blocks.text: Want to go on a trip that is filled with cultural exploration, beautiful architecture, and spirituality through and through? Then book our Indore Ujjain Omkareshwar Maheshwar Mandu Tour Package and travel to these beautiful places in utter luxury and comfort.

items: Route: Arrival in Indore – Sightseeing in Ujjain → Ujjain to Omkareshwar → Omkareshwar – Maheshwar – Mandu → Mandu Sightseeing + Indore

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrival in Indore – Sightseeing in Ujjain (60 km - 2-2.5 hrs)

Once you arrive at Indore airport or railway station, our tour representative will greet you with a warm welcome. Now, you’ll be taken on a sightseeing tour in Ujjain – the city famous for hosting the Kumbha Mela . Our very first stop will be the Mahakaleshwar Temple , which is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. Seek Darshan and the blessings of the lord here. Also, take pictures of the Shri Mahakal Lok corridor and the magnificent temple architecture. Later, we’ll go on a temple tour: ISKON temple Harsiddhi Mata Temple(Shaktipeeth) Sandipani Ashram Bade Ganesh Ka Mandir Mahakal Lok Gadkalika Temple In the evening, take a trip to the Ram Ghat . Also, we’ll visit the Mahakaleshwar Temple again to attend the mesmerising evening Aarti . Now, you’ll be taken to your pre-booked hotel. Check in and get a restful night of sleep. Note: You can book for the Bhasma Aarti online at https://shrimahakaleshwar.com/bhasmarti . Note: You can also book for VIP Darshan online by visiting https://shrimahakaleshwar.com/sheeghra-darshan . Places You’ll See
Day 2: Ujjain to Omkareshwar (139 km / 3-4 hrs)

Have a delicious breakfast in the morning. Now, you’ll be taken to the town of Omkareshwar , which is in the shape of the ‘OM’ symbol, and is also very dear to Lord Shiva. Once you get there, take a holy dip in the Narmada River first. After that, proceed to Darshan and Poojan in this yet another Jyotirlinga of this tour – Omkareshwar Temple . Now, we’ll take you to the Mamleshwar temple , which is famous for having inscriptions from the 11th century! Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar funded this temple, and now it is a cherished and protected monument of ASI. After that, do the Parikrama of Narmada . This 7 km path is laid out in a circular track up the stairs. On this Parikrama, you’ll also witness several temples and ashrams! Later, you can go on an exciting boat ride on the Narmada River, payment for which will be made on a direct basis. We’ll also take you to The Statue of Oneness , which is dedicated to Adi Shankaracharya (if time permits). Your overnight stay will be arranged in Omkareshwar . Places You’ll See
Day 3: Omkareshwar – Maheshwar – Mandu (130-140 km/ 3.5-4 hrs)

Have a delicious breakfast in the morning. Now, you’ll be driven to the city of Maheshwar , which was once the capital of Ahilyabai Holkar’s kingdom! Here, you’ll be visiting: Ahilya Fort & Palace – The residence of the Holkar queen! Akhileshwar Temple – It’s inside the fort complex itself. Narmada Ghats – Enjoy boat rides here. Also, take pictures of the gorgeous sunset here! Now, you’ll be taken to the historic town of Mandu , which is popularly called as the ‘ City of Joy ’. You’ll be visiting the following: Roopmati Pavilion Echo point Dai Ka Mahal Baz Bahadur's Palace Jami Masjid After the sightseeing tour concludes for the day, you’ll be taken to your hotel for an overnight stay. Places You’ll See
Day 4: Mandu Sightseeing + Transfer to Indore (95-100 km/ 3-4 hrs)

Treat yourself to a delicious breakfast in the morning. Now, it's time for some sightseeing. The very first tourist attraction that you’ll be visiting today is The Royal Enclave Jahaz Mahal . This ship-like palace is famous for its beauty. Do capture pictures of the stunning Jahaz Mahal reflections in water! After that, we’ll be visiting the following: Hindola Mahal Darwazas of Mandu Hoshang Shah's Tomb Now, you’ll be driven to Indore , where you’ll be visiting the Rajwada and Lalbagh Palace . Also, stroll through its bustling markets and indulge in the sweets and street food here, for which Indore is famous. Now, you’ll be transferred to the Indore airport or railway station, as per your choice. This concludes your trip with us. Hope you had a nice journey! Note: If you're travelling during the Sawan month , then your route might get diverted due to the Kanwar Yatra . Places You’ll See

How to Reach Ujjain from Ahmedabad?
There are a variety of ways via which you can reach Ujjain from Ahmedabad:

items: By Train : Railways are such a good way to cover the tour between the two cities, as there are direct trains available which you can book easily at the IRCTC website. Get on the Ahmedabad Junction and deboard at Ujjain Junction. The entire journey will take you about 8 to 9 hours.
By Road : Simply get on the NH 47. You can also hire a private taxi or take a bus to get here. Many luxury buses also run on this 400 km route.
By Air : The nearest airport to Ujjain is in Indore, which is located about 55 km away. The good thing is that there are direct flights available from Ahmedabad.

Q1. In which month is Mahakaleshwar less crowded?

Ans. Mahakaleshwar Temple is the least crowded in the months between October and February. It's most crowded in the Shravan month. It also sees a lot of pilgrim traffic on festivals and even Mondays. So, if you're looking for a peaceful Darshan, then avoid these days.
Q2. How to get VIP Darshan in Mahakal?
Ans. You can get VIP Darshan either via online (visit the shrimahakaleshwar.com) or offline (simply go to the temple's ticket counter). The cost of a VIP Pass per person is INR 250.
Q3. Can I attend Bhasma Aarti without booking?

Ans. No, you must book online before going for the Bhasma Aarti. This has been done as there's a huge demand for this special Aarti. You can book online by vesting the official Mahakaleshwar website. Try to book at least 30 days before the actual trip.
Q4. How much time is required for Ujjain Darshan?

Ans. On weekdays, when there's less crowd, it'll take you about 1–2 hours. However, on special occasions like festivals, Shravan month, or even Mondays, the crowd is large, and it might consume 3 to 5 hours in Darshan and Poojan.
Q5. Should we visit Omkareshwar or Mahakaleshwar first?

Ans. Religiously, there's no rule on which Jyotirlinga to visit first. But logistics-wise, you should visit the Mahakaleshwar Temple first, and then cover the Omkareshwar tour. This is also a popular path taken by most pilgrims as Ujjain offers you good transport connectivity. Simply take a taxi or bus for the Omkareshwar tour!

How to Reach Ujjain from Chennai
There are many options to travel, but the best way to reach Ujjain from Chennai is explained below-

Ujjain doesn't have an airport, so the nearest one is Indore, 55 km away. From Chennai, you can fly. IndiGo has direct flights, while some other airlines stop at Hyderabad, Bangalore, or Mumbai. The flight takes about 2–3 hours.
From Indore to Ujjain- You can reach Ujjain by taxi (1.5 h), train (1-1.5 h), or bus (2 h).
Driving from Chennai to Ujjain takes 22–24 hours. Take breaks for rest and food, and be ready for tolls.
No direct buses are available. You can take a bus from Chennai to Indore, then take a bus or taxi to Ujjain.
Chennai → Bangalore → Hyderabad → Nagpur → Indore → Ujjain

Chennai to Ujjain best season is from October to March when weather is cool and pleasant-
Weather - With temperatures from 12°C to 30°C it's a great time to explore the city.

If you're planning a trip, don't miss the best places to visit near Ujjain for an unforgettable experience-

Kal Bhairav Temple is one of Ujjain's most famous temple. It is known for its unique tradition, where devotees offer alcohol to the God, a ritual you won't find in most Indian temples. The temple is near the Shipra River, which has a beautiful and peaceful view. Visiting this place is a truly unforgettable experience for anyone traveling to Ujjain.
Meghdoot Resort Water Park and Club

Meghdoot Resort Water Park and Club in Ujjain is a great place for families and friends to enjoy a fun day. The water park has exciting water slides, pools, and areas where kids and adults can have lots of fun. After playing in the water, guests can relax in the resort's comfortable rooms, enjoy delicious meals at the restaurant, or try sports and games in the open areas. It's a perfect spot for a memorable day.

Ujjain is known for the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga Temple. As one of the 12 Jyotirlingas, the daily Bhasma Aarti is a special ritual you shouldn't miss. The temple is full of positive energy, and many visitors feel a spiritual experience they've never had before. The temple is decorated with beautiful artwork, and its design impresses everyone who visits.

Vishnu Sagar Talab in Ujjain is a historic pond surrounded by temples and old buildings. It was used for water and religious rituals. Today, visitors come to enjoy the calm pond and see the beautiful heritage around. It's also a great place for taking photos. During festivals, the area fills with people celebrating and enjoying the events.
Best Travel Tips for Ujjain Tour
Before going to Ujjain just keep some important things in mind for a good journey-
Ujjain is a holy city. Wear modest clothes at temples. Women can wear Sarees, Salwar Kameez or simple clothes and men should avoid sleeveless shirts.
Ujjain is safe city overall but be careful in busy spots. Keep your wallet, phone and bag close to you in markets and temples.
Early morning visits are peaceful, less crowded and better time for Darshan.
Some temples don't allow photography inside so follow instructions.

It is called the city of Mahakal because of Mahakaleshwar Temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas. It is believed that whoever comes here with a pure heart is blessed by Lord Mahakal who fulfills their wishes. Apart from this Ujjain is famous for the Kumbh Mela, a big spiritual event held every 12 years.

There are plenty of destinations to explore in this city, known for its history and culture, where visitors can enjoy experiences they will always remember-

Ujjain's main highlight is the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga Temple, specially known for its Bhasma Aarti. This ritual happens every morning before sunrise. Long ago, the sacred ash, called Vibhuti, used in the Aarti was prepared from human ashes taken from the Shamshaan Ghat (cremation ground) and applied on the Shivling.
Not many people know about this unique ritual. This temple is very old - it was built thousands of years ago. Travelers must visit here if they are in Ujjain.
Travel Tips- Photography inside the temple is not allowed.

Jantar Mantar, also called Vedh Shala, is a historic observatory in Ujjain. It was built by Maharaja Jai Singh in the 17th century to study stars and planets. It is the oldest of his five observatories - the others are in Delhi, Jaipur, Mathura, and Varanasi.

What makes it special is that all the instruments here are made of stone, not metal or modern machines. The instruments are so accurate that even today, they can show the exact positions of the sun, moon, and other planets. In the past, they were also used to tell time.
Travel Tips- Visit early in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the heat.

One of the most visited place in Ujjain is Ram Ghat, which is close to Harsiddhi Temple near the Shipra River. It is one of the oldest bathing Ghats and an important spot for the Kumbh Mela. Bathing in the river is refreshing, but the real magic happens in the evening Aarti at 8 PM, which gives a soulful experience that visitors should never miss. Tourists can see the lamps float on the river, and listen to the prayers and music that makes every visit truly special.
Travel Tips- Buy a small Diya and float it on the river - it's an unforgettable experience.

Bhartrihari Caves is a peaceful spot hidden in the hills where the famous poet and saint, Bhartrihari, lived and meditated. The caves have small spaces made into the rock where he might have rested or written his poems. Even in the heat outside, the cave stays cool, where you would enjoy meditating. Bhartrihari Caves is an unexplored spot that everyone should see.
Travel Tips- People with breathing or suffocation issues should avoid going inside the cave.

You can reach Ujjain by direct train. Rails from Pune to Ujjain Junction take 12-14 hours.
Ujjain is about 579 km from Pune. You can drive on NH52 and NH52B or take a bus.

Ans: It's just 1.4 km away, about a 10-minute drive by car.

Ans: Yes, the highways are safe but night driving should be avoided.

Ans: The toll for driving from Pune to Ujjain is usually between ₹600 and ₹800 one way. It can change a little depending on highway.
Q-5: What is famous about Ujjain?

Ans: Ujjain is known for its old temples, sacred Ghats along the Shipra River, and colorful religious festivals. City is especially famous for Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, one of Lord Shiva's 12 Jyotirlingas, and for the Kumbh Mela where thousands of pilgrims come every year.

blocks.text: Ujjain Tour Package 2026 is the ideal way to explore one of India's seven sacred Moksha-puris and the spiritual heart of Madhya Pradesh. Home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga — the only south-facing Jyotirlinga in India — Ujjain attracts devotees throughout the year for Darshan, Bhasma Aarti, and its centuries-old religious traditions.

Known in ancient texts as Avantika and Ujjayini, the city has been a major centre of Shiva worship for more than 2,000 years. The Mahakaleshwar Temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas , draws pilgrims from across the country, while the famous Bhasma Aarti at 4:00 AM remains one of the most distinctive temple rituals in India.

Our Ujjain Tour Package includes Mahakaleshwar Darshan, Bhasma Aarti booking coordination, Ram Ghat Aarti, and Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga sightseeing with comfortable hotel accommodation and private transportation. Packages start from ₹6,250 per person and cover hotel stay, vehicle, and meals. Bhasma Aarti coordination is included in all packages of 3 days and above. Contact our team to check 2026 availability and customize your itinerary according to your travel plans.

blocks.text: Considered as a Moksh-puri (salvation place), Ujjain is full of spiritual glory, ancient historical treasures, and captivating architecture. Whether you want to experience its rich cultural heritage or discover your spiritual connection with the divine, Ujjain has it all. Our Ujjain travel package picks all the must-see and the to-do activities to give you an all-round, full-fledged experience!
There are several destination here that should be on your itinerary. Here's the list:

This temple is glorified for having a strong divine presence. And therefore, no wonder, it is probably the most famous destination in the city and that's why many Ujjain tour packages include a trip to this famous temple. This temple is also one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. And one thing that makes it stand out is the fact that Aarti here is performed with sacred ash itself, known as Bhasma Aarti!

Darshan timings: 4:00 AM to 11:00 PM daily. Bhasma Aarti at 4 AM requires advance booking at shrimahakaleshwar.com. The Mahakal Lok corridor — a 900-metre walkway with Shiva sculptures along Rudra Sagar lake — is part of the same complex and free to visit.

Ram Ghat is a pious bathing Ghat in the city. Devotees from all over India come here to take their holy dips, especially during Simhastha Mela and Kumbh Mela. It is situated on the banks of Shipra River and is a sight to behold during the evening Aartis. The evening Aarti at Ram Ghat takes place daily at sunset — no booking required, free to attend.

As the name suggests, this temple is dedicated to Kaal Bhairav — a highly fierce form of Lord Shiva. He is also considered to be the guardian deity of the city of Ujjain. And thus, a visit to this temple is a must and should definitely be on your Ujjain holiday package. This temple is famous for its vibrant atmosphere and unique rituals like the traditional offering of liquor (sharaab) to Kaal Bhairav — this is the only temple in India where such an offering is part of the official temple ritual

You are in for a treat when you visit this Lord Ganesha temple. The temple is remarkably beautiful and has a superior architecture. It is widely believed that worshipping Lord Ganesha here can remove all obstacles from your life.

This popular astronomical observatory was built by the famous astronomer-king Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur, who also built similar observatories at Delhi, Jaipur, Mathura, and Varanasi. It was specially designed to make astrological calculations and study celestial bodies. What once served as the astronomical observatory, is now a popular tourist spot of the city — making almost on every Ujjain travel package. Also known as the Jantar Mantar, tourists flock here to see this 17th century gem for its notable collection of instruments (such as Sun dial).

This Ashram is famous as the place where Lord Krishna and Balram received education from his guru Sandipani. Devotees come here to find a peaceful place for meditation and inner reflection. Besides the serene atmosphere, people love to see the ancient stone idols and the ashram ruins.

This one surely needs to be on itinerary of the history buffs. This fort, although now in complete ruins, once served as the powerful shield to protect the city from neighbouring kingdoms. Historical enthusiasts just love this age-old structure for its strategic importance. Tourists also enjoy the surrounding views from here and make it a part of their Ujjain travel package.

This temple is one of the Shakti Peethas and holds a special importance in the hearts of Aadi Shakti devotees. The temple is dedicated to Goddess Harsiddhi and she is believed to grant her followers with prosperity and strength. The entire temple complex provides a very peaceful, serene environment. Also, during the Navaratri festival, the temple brims with cheer and liveliness. During Navratri (Oct 2026 — exact dates per Hindu calendar), the temple hosts special puja sessions and is illuminated throughout the night. This is the most crowded but also the most vibrant time to visit.

The Mahakal Lok is a 900-metre open corridor connecting the main gate to the Mahakaleshwar temple entrance. Inaugurated in October 2022, it features hand-carved sandstone pillars, murals depicting stories from Shiv Purana, and a landscaped walkway along Rudra Sagar lake. Entry is free. Best visited early morning (before 8 AM) or after 7 PM when the pathway is illuminated.
To make the most out of your Ujjain holiday trip, make sure you include the following activities in your plan:

items: Take a Dip in the Shipra River: This is one of the most sacred things that you can do in Ujjain and it's often a part of an Ujjain travel package. It is a widely held belief that bathing at the Ghat absolves your sins and provides spiritual growth. Pilgrims can be found offering D iyas along the riverbank in the morning and evening.

Attend the Bhasma Aarti: The distinct ritual of Bhasma Aarti (Aarti performed with real sacred ash) is performed only at the Mahakaleshwar Temple. Bhasma Aarti happens daily at 4 AM — advance booking at shrimahakaleshwar.com is mandatory as seats are limited.

Visit Temples: Ujjain is home to various temples and visiting them is a must for any Ujjain tour. Some notable mentions are Kaal Bhairav Temple, Chintaman Ganesh Temple, Harsiddhi Temple, Mangalnath Temple etc.
Take a Boat Ride on the Shipra River : The boating experience is especially beautiful during sunrise and sunset.

Shop in the Local Markets: You can buy anything from local handicrafts to traditional clothes to souvenirs here. The markets also sell prasad and other religious items. Markets near Ram Ghat and Mahakaleshwar Temple are the most vibrant and popular ones.
Explore Historical Sites : Ujjain houses a number of ancient monuments, archaeological sites, and ruins. Noteworthy mentions are Ujjain Fort, Siddhavat, and Bade Ganeshji Ka Mandir.

Ujjain is about 55 kilometres away from the airport. After reaching the airport, you can either hire a taxi/cab or use the local transport like bus. It takes about 1.5 hours by road from there on. Bhasma Aarti booking: Book at shrimahakaleshwar.com. For regular days, slots open 1 week ahead. For Maha Shivaratri (15 Feb 2026) and Shravan month, book months in advance. Offline counter seats exist but are not guaranteed.
Arrive by 3:30 AM for Bhasma Aarti: The aarti starts exactly at 4 AM. Latecomers are not permitted entry. Keep your booking confirmation and ID ready at the gate.

Dress code at Mahakaleshwar: Men entering Garbhagriha must wear dhoti — no kurta, no pants allowed inside. Women must wear saree. Dhoti available for rent near the entrance for approximately ₹50. Western clothing will be turned away.
Monday crowds: Every Monday, general queue at Mahakaleshwar can reach 4–8 hours. If your visit falls on a Monday, book Sheeghra Darshan or arrive before 6 AM.

Cash at Ujjain: ATMs are available within 500 metres of Mahakaleshwar. Withdraw before entering the temple lanes — the alleys get extremely congested during peak hours and ATM access becomes difficult.

Omkareshwar — plan a full day: Omkareshwar is 130 km from Ujjain (2.5–3 hours each way). Darshan queue there can take 2–4 hours. Do not plan Ujjain and Omkareshwar on the same day — it makes both rushed. Our 4-day packages allocate a dedicated day for Omkareshwar.
Summer heat: April–June temperatures in Ujjain reach 42–45°C. Plan all temple visits between 5–9 AM and after 6 PM. Carry water and ORS sachets.
Photography: Photography is prohibited inside Mahakaleshwar sanctum and during Bhasma Aarti. Allowed in outer areas and Mahakal Lok corridor.

blocks.text: Force Majeure: Temple closure, government restriction, or natural disruption — full rescheduling or credit offered. Bhasma Aarti tickets follow the temple trust's own refund policy (typically non-refundable). Confirm on shrimahakaleshwar.com at booking time.
Q1: Is Ujjain safe for tourists?

Ans. Yes, Ujjain is generally a safe tourist spot. The city has a calm vibe with a strong religious background. Locals are used to tourists. Nonetheless, exercise caution and be mindful of your belongings and follow safety protocols.
Q2: Is there a dress code for temples in Ujjain?

Ans. It is crucial to dress modestly while visiting temples as Ujjain is a deeply religious city. For both men and women, it's recommended to cover shoulders and knees. Many temples may have their own dress code so do your research before visiting a temple.

For Bhasma Aarti specifically: men must wear dhoti (no upper garment for Garbhagriha entry); women must wear saree. This is strictly enforced at Mahakaleshwar. Dhoti rental available near temple entrance for approx. ₹50.
Q3: Is Ujjain good for solo travellers?

Ans. Yes, Ujjain is good for solo travellers. The serene environments of the city are often seen as a conducive environment by tourists for introspection and personal reflection. Also, being a solo traveller, you can explore historical sites, temples, markets etc. at your own pace.
Q4: How long should I stay in Ujjain?
Ans. 2–3 days covers Ujjain city comfortably. To add Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga (130 km away), budget 4 days minimum. For Ujjain + Omkareshwar + Maheshwar + Mandu, a 5–7 day tour is ideal.
Q5: What are some local foods that I should try?

Ans. The Madhya Pradesh local cuisine offers a variety of delicious dishes such as, Dal Bafla, Poha, Bhutte Ka Kees, and sweets like jalebi and Malpua. Ujjain near the temple zone is fully vegetarian — non-veg food is not available within the temple precinct area.
Q6: How do I book the Bhasma Aarti at Mahakaleshwar in 2026?

Ans. Visit shrimahakaleshwar.com to register online. Select your date, fill in personal details, and upload a valid ID proof. Pay the fee online and collect your confirmation. For Maha Shivaratri (15 Feb 2026), Shravan month, and Mondays, book well in advance — slots fill fast. Our team handles this booking for guests on 3-day and longer packages.
Q7: What is the Bhasma Aarti timing and what makes it special?

Ans. Bhasma Aarti begins daily at 4:00 AM and ends around 6:00 AM at Mahakaleshwar Temple. It is the only ritual in India where Lord Shiva is worshipped with sacred ash (bhasma) as the primary offering. The ritual is conducted before sunrise in a setting that has continued uninterrupted for centuries. Advance booking is mandatory — walk-in entry is not permitted.
Q8: What is the cost of an Ujjain tour package from Delhi in 2026?

Ans. The 8-day Best of Madhya Pradesh tour from Delhi starts at ₹32,500 per person (twin sharing), covering Delhi–Bhopal–Ujjain–Indore–Mandu. For Ujjain-only packages starting from Indore, the 2-day option begins at ₹6,250. Contact our team for a quote based on your dates and group size.
Q9: What is included in the Ujjain tour package?

Ans. All packages include accommodation (twin sharing, 3-star hotels), daily breakfast and dinner (vegetarian), private AC vehicle for all transfers, guided sightseeing, and GST. Bhasma Aarti booking coordination is included in 3-day and longer packages. Airfare, lunch, personal expenses, and temple ticket fees are not included.
Q10: Is there any entry fee at Mahakaleshwar temple?

Ans. General darshan is free — no entry fee. Bhasma Aarti attendance requires a paid ticket (fees vary by category — check shrimahakaleshwar.com for current rates). VIP Darshan and Sheeghra Darshan also have separate fees payable at the official portal or counter.
Q11: What documents are needed to visit Mahakaleshwar?

Ans. General darshan needs no documents. For Bhasma Aarti and VIP darshan, carry a government-issued photo ID matching your booking name — Aadhaar, PAN, voter ID, or passport. Foreign nationals must carry their passport.
Q12: Is Ujjain suitable for senior citizens?

Ans. Yes. The Mahakaleshwar complex has wide pathways and the main darshan hall is accessible. However, general queue on Mondays and during Shivaratri can involve 4–8 hours of standing — we strongly recommend Sheeghra or VIP darshan for senior travellers. Ram Ghat, Mahakal Lok, and Kaal Bhairav are all walkable without steps. Ground-floor rooms arranged on request.
Q13: Can I customize the Ujjain tour to add Indore or Bhopal?

Ans. Yes — all packages are fully customizable. Common additions: Indore (55 km, street food + Rajwada Palace), Bhopal (190 km, Bhimbetka rock shelters + Sanchi Stupa), Maheshwar and Mandu (included in our 4-day packages). Share your interests when enquiring and we build the itinerary accordingly.
Q14: What is the best time to visit Ujjain in 2026?

Ans. October to March is the best season — pleasant weather (8°C–28°C), Kartik Mela, and Maha Shivaratri. Maha Shivaratri 2026 falls on 15 February (Sunday) — the biggest Shiva festival at Mahakaleshwar, but book accommodation and Bhasma Aarti slot at least 3 months ahead. Avoid April–June (45°C heat). Shravan (Jul–Aug) is spiritually significant but very crowded.
Q15: What vehicle is used for the Ujjain packages?

Ans. All packages use Ministry of Tourism approved private AC vehicles — Innova Crysta for up to 4 passengers, Tempo Traveller for groups of 5–8. All toll, parking, driver allowance, and fuel are included in the package price.
Q16: What is the cancellation policy?

Ans. Cancellations 60+ days before departure: 10% charge. 45–59 days: 25%. 30–44 days: 40%. 15–29 days: 60%. 8–14 days: 80%. 0–7 days: 100% non-refundable. Force majeure events qualify for rescheduling or credit. Bhasma Aarti tickets follow the temple trust's own refund policy — confirm at shrimahakaleshwar.com at booking time.

items: Route: Arrive at Varanasi → Varanasi - Vindhyachal – Prayagraj → Prayagraj - Ayodhya → Ayodhya - Lucknow → Lucknow - Naimisharanya - Lucknow

blocks.text: Your Uttar Pradesh Darshan tour will start as you arrive at Varanasi and meet our courteous representative, who will brief you about the rest of the tour and ensure you have a smooth Yatra. You will check in at your pre-reserved hotel in Varanasi and freshen up. After some time, you’ll go on a sightseeing tour and Visit the famous attractions, including Vishwanath temple, Annapurna Temple, Kashi Vishalakhi, Manas Mandir, Durga Mandir, Birla Mandir, and Sankat Mochan Mandir. Later, you will embark on a picturesque drive to Sarnath - the site where Gautam Buddha delivered his first sermon. After reaching Sarnath, you will visit the famous attractions such as the Buddha temples, Chaukhandi Stupa, the Dhamek Stupa, and the archeological museum. In the evening, you will enjoy a boat cruise on the river Ganga. You will also attend the Ganga Aarti ceremony. You will have an overnight stay in your Varanasi hotel. Vishwanath Temple Darshan Timing: 04:00 AM to 11:00 AM Evening/Noon Slots: 12:00 PM to 07:00 PM and 08:30 PM to 09:00 PM Sapta Rishi Aarti: 07:00 PM to 08:30 PM Please Note: Sugam Darshan, Pooja, and Aarti can be booked online During the Sawan month, the Kanwar Yatra may impact the tour, which can cause route diversion or heavy traffic. Places You’ll See

You will relish a delicious breakfast in the morning, and then you’ll head out on a scenic drive to Prayagraj. On the way, you will visit Sitamarhi , which is believed to be the place where Mata Sita went inside the earth. Have a Darshan of Mata Sita at Janki Temple , and then you will head out on a drive to Prayagraj. Next, go to Prayagraj , and visit Triveni Sangam , where the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers meet. Take a holy dip and enjoy a boat ride. Then travel to Bade Hanuman Mandir. People believe that Hanuman Ji stopped here to rest after burning Lanka. Visit the Akshayavat Temple and Tree at Patalpuri Temple in Prayagraj Fort , believed to be the spot where Ram, Lakshman, and Sita rested. People pray here to wash away sins. Now proceed to Prayagraj Fort , also called Allahabad Fort built by Akbar in 1583 beside the Yamuna River near where it joins the Ganga (Great photo spot). Stop at Alopi Devi Temple , a well-known holy Shaktipeeth. Optional: if time allows, visit Lalita Devi Temple, Shri Nagvasuki Temple where people pray for blessings. Then, explore , Anand Bhavan, the Nehru family’s home. After the sightseeing tour, you will have an overnight stay in your hotel. Places You’ll See

After a delicious breakfast, you will head out on a drive to Ayodhya. After arriving at Ayodhya, you will visit Rama Janmabhumi , which is considered to be the birthplace of lord Rama. Later, you will visit Dasharath Bhavan, Kanak Bhavan, and Hanuman Garhi. In the evening, you will visit the Saryu River. By taking a dip in this river, you can get rid of the sins you have committed in your past and present life. You will have an overnight stay in your pre-reserved hotel. Hanuman Garhi Darshan Timing 05:30 am to 10:00 pm Places You’ll See

Have a yummy breakfast in the morning, and then you will drive to Lucknow. You will visit the Gomti river front, Bada Imambara (Bhulbhulliya) Ambedkar Park, and Hazratganj market. In the evening, you will return to your hotel and have an overnight stay. Places You’ll See

Post breakfast, you will head out on a drive to Naimisharanya. The main attraction of this place is the Naimisaranya Temple , a sacred destination for Hindus. You will then visit other popular attractions, including Chakra Teerth, Vyas Gaddi, Dadhichi Kund, Swayambhu Manu, Suth Gaddi, Pandav Kila, Satrupa, and Hanuman Gaddi. blocks.text: Best Places to Visit during Uttar Pradesh Trip

India’s most populous state in Uttar Pradesh today is a rich religious, natural, and historical tourist destination. Come let’s know some of the best tourist destinations in Uttar Pradesh to visit during this trip:

Varanasi is one of the oldest living cities in the world. It is believed that Lord Shiva himself created this holy city with the essence of all his sacred energies. Varanasi has many ancient temples and Ghats. In puranas, Varanasi was named as Avimukth as Lord Shiva never expressed or left it. In every corner the sacred vibes will nourish the soul. It is one of the must visit places in Uttar Pradesh.

items: Dashashwamedha Ghat - It is one of the most famous sacred ghats to visit in Varanasi. This place was named Dashashwamedha after Lord Brahma performed Ashvamedha Yagya. The final construction of the ghat was done by Bajirao Peshwa in 1735 AD.

The Kashi Vishwanatha Temple - Close your eyes and imagine Varanasi. What do you see? The first image which pops in our mind is the sacred Kashi Vishwanath Temple. The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is the landmark destination of Varanasi. It is the first place where the sacred light of Lord Shiva in the form of Jyotirlinga manifested.

Goddess Annapurna Temple - Located near Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Goddess Annapurna Temple is dedicated to the mother of the universe (Devi Parvati) who blesses devotees with abundance and nourishment.

Sankat Mochan Temple - In 16th century, a saint named Tulsi Das established the idol of Lord Hanuman under a fig tree which later became known as Sankat Mochan Temple. It is believed that he created some parts of his epic Ramcharitmanas. You must visit Sankat Mochan Temple, if you are in Varanasi.

Chausath Yogini Temple - Situated above the Chausath Yogini Ghat, the temple is dedicated to goddess Kali. It is also a 64 Yogini temple. You will see 64 female deities attending to the goddess. In ancient Varanasi, it is said that there used to be many more Yogini temples but today this temple remains containing all their spiritual energies.

Tulsi Manas Temple - Tulsi Manas Temple is dedicated to Lord Ram. It is said that at this place saint Tulsi das used to live and wrote his epic Ramcharitmanas. You will see many sacred verses of Ramcharitmanas inscribed on the walls of the temple.

Assi Ghat - Here the sacred confluence of Asi River and Ganga River takes place, it is also one of the most popular ghats to visit in Varanasi. The sunrise here starts with enchanting Vedic chants and Kriya Yoga.

blocks.text: Don’t forget to visit these two most sacred cities- Mathura and Vrindavan in Uttar Pradesh. Mathura is a birthplace of Lord Krishna and Vrindavan is that sacred place where he spent his childhood. Together these places are considered as major pilgrimage circuits for Krishna Devotees. Here are some of the most popular places to visit in Mathura and Vrindavan:

items: Shri Krishna Janma Bhoomi - Believed to be the birthplace of Lord Krishna, Shri Krishna Janma Bhoomi temple is a landmark destination of Mathura. Devotees from all over India visit here to take divine blessings from Lord Krishna.

Dwarkadhish Temple - Dwarkadhish Temple in Mathura worships Lord Krishna in his kingly avatar as Lord Dwarkadhish. It was built in 1814 by Seth Gokul das Parikh who was a treasurer in the court of Gwalior. The idol of Lord Dwarkadhish is made up of black marble and you will witness the beautiful white marble idol of Radha Rani.

Jain Siddha Kshetra Chaurasi - It’s a major Jain pilgrimage site in Mathura. It’s a sacred place where Jambu Swami, the last Jain saint attained nirvana at the age of 84 (Chaurasi in Hindi). Hence this place is named as Jain Siddha Kshetra Chaurasi.
Gurudwara Holigate - It is a prominent Sikh religious site in Mathura. It is located near the Tilak Dwar area. Attend Kirtanas, prayers and community service- Langar.

Prem Mandir - Located in Raman Reti Road in Vrindavan, Prem Mandir celebrates and worships the divine love of lord Krishna and Radha Rani. There are beautiful carvings in the walls of the temple depicting the scenes from the divine life and pastimes of Lord Krishna, Radha Rani, Lord Rama and Devi Sita.

Rangji Temple - Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, Rangji Temple is one of the most popular temples to visit in Vrindavan. The temple follows Shri Vaishnava Agama tradition and holds daily prayers, music and rituals to worship Lord Vishnu as Lord Ranganatha.

Bankey Bihari Temple - It is one of the most famous temples of lord Krishna. This temple was built by the guru of Tansen (great musician) Swami Haridas, who was a great devotee of Lord Krishna. The Lord is named as Bankey because of his posture which is bent at three places- neck, wrist and knee.

blocks.text: Ayodhya is a place in Uttar Pradesh where the spiritual heart of India resides gracefully in the epic tales of Ramayana. It is the birth place of Lord Rama. Devotees from all across India come to Ayodhya to seek divine grace from Lord Rama. Recently the construction of Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in 2024 has made Ayodhya a global spiritual destination. Here are some of the most famous tourist places to visit in Ayodhya :

items: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple : Lifeline of Ayodhya, Ram Janmabhoomi Temple is a sacred place where Lord Rama was born. It is a prominent pilgrimage place in Ayodhya for Hindu devotees.

Hanuman Garhi Temple : Dedicated to Lord Rama, Hanuman Garhi Temple is a massive fortress-like temple. It is said that Lord Hanuman is the protector and presiding deity of Ayodhya. The temple offers scenic views of the entire city of Ayodhya.
Ram Ki Paidi : Witness Ram Ki Paidi- a serene series of iconic ghats (river steps) on the banks of the Sarayu River. Take a holy dip here to get rid of all the karmic backlogs and embrace solace.

Kanak Bhavan : It’s a marvellous temple worth capturing for Instagram. The exquisite beauty of Kanak Bhawan will take your breath away. The Kanak Bhawan is a gift to Lord Rama and Devi Sita after their marriage by Devi Kaikeyi.
Nageshwarnath Temple : Built by the son of Lord Rama- Kush, Nageshwar Nath Temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. Maha Shivratri is celebrated here with great pomp and show.
Saryu River : Flows along Ayodhya, Saryu River is a sacred river in which taking a dip is considered auspicious. Witness the ethereal Saryu River aarti in the evening.
Treta Ke Thakur : It’s a place where Lord Rama performed Ashvamedha Yagya. The temple houses idols of lord Rama, Devi Sita and Laxman.

blocks.text: Formerly known as Allahabad, Prayagraj is one of the most popular travel destinations to visit in Uttar Pradesh. It is a major religious site for Hindu devotees. It houses the most sacred site for the world’s largest gathering called Kumbh Mela which is held every 12 years. Beyond spiritual significance, it also has many beautiful colonial era monuments. In essence, Prayagraj has a perfect vibe for history, spiritual and cultural enthusiasts. Here are some of the most popular places to visit in Prayagraj :

items: Sangam : Don’t miss the sacred confluence of Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati rivers. It’s the same sacred place where one of the world’s largest religious gatherings takes place every 12 years. Take a holy dip to get rid of all karmic backlogs.

Allahabad Fort : Allahabad Fort is one of the most popular and massive forts which showcase Mughal era’s craftsmanship. The fort was built by emperor Akbar in 1583. It is located near the serene banks of Sangam.

Anand Bhavan : Witness the ancestral home of Nehru- Gandhi family in Uttar Pradesh. It houses a museum which displays artefacts related to the freedom struggle. There are rooms which have still kept the essence of India’s independence movement intact.

Khusro Bagh : It’s a beautiful large walled garden showcasing intricate Mughal era tombs of Prince Khusro and other family members. Prince Khusro was the eldest son of emperor Jahangir and Sultan Begum.

Allahabad Museum : A historical museum located within Chandrashekhar Azad Park is very famous for its unique displays of ancient sculptures, paintings, rare documents and historical artifacts, known for its collection of ancient sculptures from Maurya, Gupta period.

Nagvasuki Temple : Dedicated to Nag Devta, Nagvasuki Temple is one of the most famous religious sites to visit in Prayagraj. It is located in Daraganj. The Nag Vasuki idol is a five hooded idol installed by sage Kashyapa.

blocks.text: Agra is a crowning jewel of Uttar Pradesh’s tourism landscape. It is one of the most visited tourist destinations for Indians as well as foreigners. It houses the iconic Taj Mahal, one of the new seven wonders of the world. Beyond Taj, it also has many Mughal era heritage monuments which today offers unique insights on India’s majestic past. Here are some of the most popular places to visit in Agra:

items: Taj Mahal : The lifeline of Agra- The Taj Mahal is an iconic white marble monument built by emperor Shah Jahan in the memory of his beloved wife Mumtaj Mahal. Tourists from all over the world come to Agra to witness this beautiful symbol of Love.

Agra Fort : Agra Fort is one of the most famous red sandstone forts of the Mughal era in India. It’s a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Within Agra Fort, there are many beautiful structures like Diwan-i-Khas, Diwan-i-Am, Nagina Masjid, Sheesh Mahal etc.

Fatehpur Sikri : Once, Fatehpur Sikri was an abundant town built by emperor Akbar to honor a saint Salim Chishti. In fact, it served as a Mughal capital for a decade but due to water scarcity, the town was abandoned. It has many beautiful Mughal eras like Buland Darwaza, Panch Mahal, Jodha Bai’s Palace etc.

Mehtab Bagh : Don’t miss the beautiful Moonlight Garden called Mehtab Bagh. It is one of the most popular attractions in Agra. It is perfectly aligned with the iconic Taj Mahal. The Bagh is quite peaceful which offers refreshing vibes.

Itimad-ud-Daulah's Tomb : Also known as ‘Baby Taj’ Itimud-ud-Daulah’s Tomb is a beautiful marble tomb carved with semi-precious stones. It is said that the structure of this tomb was considered as a draft for the Taj Mahal design.
Kinari Bazaar : Located near Taj, Kinari Bazaar is a hub in Agra to experience its local life, shops, food handicrafts, leather goods and culture.

blocks.text: You will be mesmerized to witness the beauty of one of the most famous Buddhist pilgrimage sites of India . It is a revered place where Prince Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under a Bodhi Tree and became Buddha. The iconic Mahabodhi temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is one of the major centres for Buddhist culture and learning. Here are some of the most popular places to see in Bodhgaya:

items: Mahabodhi Temple - This tall pyramid shaped temple is a sacred place where Lord Buddha attained enlightenment. It’s a major centre for Buddhist learning. It’s a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Bodhi Tree - Witness the most sacred fig tree which still carries the divine essence of lord Buddha as he used to meditate here.

Great Buddha Statue - Embrace the inner peace by viewing the 80 ft tall outdoor statue of Lord Buddha in meditation pose. The statue is surrounded by other disciple statues and serene landscaped gardens.
Thai Monastery - It’s golden tiled sloping roofs and colossal bronze Buddha Statue will amaze your curious mind. Indulge in a peaceful meditation session for self-introspection.
Sujata Temple & Stupa - The temple and the Stupa was built in the honor of Sujata who offered food to Buddha. The temple is the symbol of her compassion and divine grace.

Bodhgaya Archaeological Museum - Don’t miss this stunning archaeological museum. You will learn about many things related to Buddhism. It houses many artefacts, sculptures, antiques related to Buddhist traditions.

blocks.text: Try Delicious Cuisines of Uttar Pradesh

Food of Uttar Pradesh is an invitation to know the poetry of flavours, stories behind ancient traditions, rituals and sacred philosophies. Let’s know about some of the best street food to try in Uttar Pradesh :

items: Try Delicious Biryani, Korma and Nihari. In Uttar Pradesh, at many top-rated food joints you will find these food items. Don’t miss this cuisine. These cuisines follow the tradition of Dum (slow cooking technique). The food is cooked slowly in a pot over a low flame. The pot is sealed with wheat dough to capture every flavor and aroma.

Try Temple Food. Though it is not a street food, food in Uttar Pradesh is a medium of service and devotion. In temples you will find Bhandara Prasad. The prasad is prepared without garlic or onions. Try Mathura’s Peda, Varindavan’s Makhan Mishri or Kashi’s Launglata.
Visit Varanasi’s Ram Bhandar to try Kachodi sabzi. It is one of the most popular street foods of Uttar Pradesh.
Try Kebabs, Sweet dishes like Malaiyo, Paan, Sheermal, shahi Tukda, Phirni, etc to tickle your taste buds with the richness of Uttar Pradesh.

blocks.text: Shop for the Famous Handicrafts & Souvenirs

Uttar Pradesh is very famous for its rich handicrafts and souvenir items. Through their craftsmanship Uttar Pradesh tells centuries old stories behind each craft and artistic traditions associated with it. Here are some of the best things for shopping at Uttar Pradesh :

items: Look for Banarasi Saree and Brocades . Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its high quality Banarasi Sari with gold and silver Zari work.
Lucknow Chikankari - It is a must not miss in Uttar Pradesh. You will get finest hand embroidered designs crafted on cotton, muslin kurtas and dupattas.
Your trip to Uttar Pradesh will be incomplete without trying Kannauj Attar . The perfumes are crafted with regional flowers and herbs.
Look for the best Meenakari jewelleries . The ornate enamel and gemstones will take your breath away.

blocks.text: Best Places to Visit on your Trip to Uttarakhand

Uttarakhand has amazing destinations to captivate senses. No doubt, People have been visiting Uttarakhand ever since the beginning of time for performing meditation, spending time coexisting with nature, and observing the natural beauty blessed by the gods themselves. Here are some of the best points of tourist interests in Uttarakhand.

items: Visit this renowned pilgrimage town and “Yoga capital of the world”. The place attracts huge number of spiritual seekers, adventure lovers and solace seekers.

You can try amazing adventure activities like rafting, trekking, witness Ganga Aarti and visit ashrams, yoga and meditation hubs. It is also a getaway to the famous Chardhams – Gangotri , Yamunotri , Kedarnath and Badrinath Dhams.
Haridwar is one of the seven holiest places in Hinduism. It is a popular spiritual getaway to fine-tune your spirits looking for peace.
Embrace the peace of Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Paudi Ghat. Visit numerous temples and ashrams. It is also a best starting point for the holy Chardham Yatra.

Located in Chamoli district, the Valley of Flowers in Uttarakhand is one of the most popular places for nature lovers. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It will show you stunning natural views for photography.
The valley has rich floral wealth. It has floras with over 500 species of flowers including endangered flowers like Brahma Kamal, Blue Poppy etc.
Located in Nainital, it is India’s oldest Tiger reserves and National Park. If you love wildlife adventures then you must book a wildlife Safari in Jim Corbett National Park.

The park has 9 safari zones for wildlife viewing and nature sightseeing. Each zone offers unique natural views. Here you can try Jeep safari, Canter Safari, Bird watching, nature walks and elephant safaris etc.

No doubt. You must visit Chardhams in Uttarakhand- Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath Dham. Every traveller or devotee craves to get a once in a lifetime opportunity to visit these holy places.
If you plan your Chardham Yatra in summer (April- May) or in August to September, you will be able to get the divine Darshan of the duties.
These sites are considered the holiest pilgrimage places for Hindu devotees. You need to book in advance for this Yatra.
Don’t miss this picturesque Ski destination in Uttarakhand. It is the one of the best places to visit in Uttarakhand if you love adventure.
The beauty of Auli is unbeatable as it is surrounded by lush coniferous and Oak trees, attracting nature lovers also from all across India.
Try the best activity Ski here. Its slopes are good for both seasoned and beginner skier. Nearby Auli, you can also visit Adi Shankaracharya Ashram in Joshimath.

The city of lakes – Nainital is captivating the hearts of tourists for decades with its scenic beauty. It is one of the best hill stations in Uttarakhand for family vacations, honeymoon and solo weekend trips.

Nainital is a scenic wonder. It houses the most beautiful Naina Lake and a Shaktipeetha, Naina Devi temple. These two places are the most popular ones but don’t miss these iconic spots too like Eco cave garden, Mall Road, Snow view point, Naina Peak etc.

Uttarakhand, the place with unparalleled charm not only delights the heart with its awe-inspiring tourist attractions but also never disappoints when it comes to activities to do here. Mentioned here are some of the best things to do as per our Uttarakhand itineraries.
Embark on Soul Pleasing Spiritual Journeys

blocks.text: Dive Deep into the Enchanting Wilderness

You can book your wildlife Safari at Jim Corbett National Park, Rajaji National Park, Binsar wildlife Sanctuary or Ashok Musk Deer Sanctuary.
There are many rare Himalayan wild creatures to see like snow leopard, Musk deer and Himalayan Brown Bear etc. Also capture Tigers, Himalayan Monal, Serow, Red panda and Himalayan Tahr.

blocks.text: If Safari is Not Enough Try Thrilling Adventure Activities

items: Apart from wildlife safaris, you can also try numerous adventure activities like river rafting, bungee jumping in Rishikesh and Shivpuri, trekking in Valley of flowers, Nag Tibba, Skiing in Auli, camping in Rishikesh, Chopta and Dhanaulti.
You can also try paragliding in Ranikhet and Mukteshwar and mountain biking in Rishikesh and Mussoorie.

blocks.text: Uttarakhand Travel Tips for Unforgettable Memories with Your Loved Ones

items: Offbeat Beauty- We often plan trips to crowded and popular places. This time, try offbeat destinations too. The offbeat destinations in Uttarakhand are less crowded and beautiful. Some of our best picks are-Binsar, Munsiyari, Chakrata, Chopta, Sattal for peaceful moments.
Licensed Guides- Hire only licensed adventure guides to safely do your adventure activities. Accidents happen when we fail to take precautions and be careless about safety.

Dress Modesty- Respect the traditions and customs. Uttarakhand is known as Devbhoomi so it has numerous temples. If you are visiting any temples, dress conservatively. Cover your head, knees and shoulders.
Take Permission- Don’t take photos and videos of sacred sites without permission.
Enough Cash- Keep enough Cash as there are many remote places where you won’t find ATM’s or strong net connectivity for digital payments.
What to Pack- Pack weather specific clothes to get the best experience of sightseeing tours. Also, carry a comfortable footwear as you may have to walk a lot as Uttarakhand is a hill destination.

Physical Fitness- You need to be physically fit to try trekking and other adventure activities. People will mobility issues have limited options but they can visit the scenic hill stations, temples and indulge in having delicious cuisines etc.
Advance Planning- If you are planning your Chardham Yatra then you need to register your Yatra in advance from official website .
Cleanliness- Protect the serenity and beauty of the mountains. Keep your surroundings clean, don’t litter.

blocks.text: Ready to explore a state full of rich history and colorful culture? The Varanasi Prayagraj Ayodhya Naimisharanya Tour lets you experience it all.

items: Route: Arrival Varanasi → Varanasi - Vindhyachal - Prayagraj → Prayagraj - Ayodhya → Ayodhya - Lucknow → Lucknow - Naimisharanya - Lucknow

blocks.text: Start your Travel Plan with a convenient pick-up from your selected location in Varanasi, either airport or railway station, where our My Quick Trippers team will receive you and take you comfortably to your hotel. If you choose a guide, they will join the driver to help you all day. After check-in, proceed for sightseeing in Varanasi- Durga Mandir Mana Temple Sankat Mochan Mandir Birla Mandir In the evening, attend the famous Ganga Aarti at the Ghats, or enjoy it from a boat for a spiritual experience. You will stay overnight at a hotel in Varanasi. Note- Timing of Ganga Aarti can change with the season. Places You’ll See
Day 2: Varanasi - Morning Boat Ride, Sarnath Visit (10 km/31 min), and Temple Tour

Enjoy a calm morning boat ride on the sacred Ganges Ghats as the sun rises. You may also take a bath at your hotel or in the holy Ganga River. Next, visit Annapurna Mandir, Vishalakshi Mandir, Vishwanath Temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas. It’s also a wonderful place for taking memorable photos. Then go to Sarnath, the sacred place where Lord Buddha gave his first teaching. Later, visit other famous sites in Sarnath such as the Buddhist temples, Dhamek Stupa, Chaukhandi Stupa and the archeological museum. In the evening enjoy some free time to shop in Varanasi on your own (optional). Relax and stay overnight at the hotel. Note- Pooja, Aarti, and Sugam Darshan can be booked online only. Weblink: https://shrikashivishwanath.org Note: In the month of Sawan, the Kanwar Yatra may cause heavy traffic. Places You’ll See
Day 3: Varanasi - Vindhyachal - Prayagraj (155 km/ 3 hrs)

Have breakfast and then continue your journey to Prayagraj. Enroute visit Vindhyachal Devi for a Darshan at Shaktipeeth. Later visit Sitamarhi , the temple where Mother Sita went into the earth. Next, go to Prayagraj, and visit Triveni Sangam , where the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers meet. Take a holy dip and enjoy a boat ride. Then travel to Bade Hanuman Mandir . People believe that Hanuman Ji stopped here to rest after burning Lanka. Visit the Akshayavat Temple and Tree at Patalpuri Temple in Prayagraj Fort, believed to be the spot where Ram, Lakshman, and Sita rested. People pray here to wash away sins. Now proceed to Prayagraj Fort , also called Allahabad Fort built by Akbar in 1583 beside the Yamuna River near where it joins the Ganga (Great photo spot). Stop at Alopi Devi Temple , a well-known holy Shaktipeeth. Optional: If time allows, visit Lalita Devi Temple, Shri Nagvasuki Temple where people pray for blessings. Then, explore Anand Bhavan, the Nehru family’s home. Spend the night at your hotel in Prayagraj and take some rest. Note- Timings of Vindhyachal Temple 5–10PM, Prayagraj Fort 9AM–6PM, Museum 10AM–5PM, Anand & Swaraj Bhawan 9:30–5 PM. Places You’ll See
Day 4: Prayagraj - Ayodhya (166 km/ Approx. 4 hr 20 minutes)

After breakfast, drive to Ayodhya and visit Ram Janmabhoomi to light Diyas, join rituals and feel the spiritual peace there. Later, explore Hanuman Garhi, Dasharath Bhavan (Lord Rama’s father palace) and Kanak Bhavan (temple dedicated to Sita and Rama). Visit the Saryu River in the evening, where bathing is believed to remove all sins. If time allows, also enjoy boating (optional). Return to the hotel for overnight stay in Ayodhya. Note- Hanuman Garhi Temple is open from 5AM to 11PM. Places You’ll See

After breakfast start your journey to Lucknow. Visit Bara Imambara (Bhool Bhulaiyaa) and explore it’s fascinating maze. Don't forget to take photos of this beautiful spot. Next visit Ambedkar Park and then proceed to the Gomti Riverfront. Later, explore Hazratganj Market for shopping and local experiences. Reach the hotel, check in and spend the night in Lucknow. Places You’ll See
Day 6: Lucknow - Naimisharanya - Lucknow (180 km/ 3 to 4 hours)

Drive to Naimisharanya after breakfast, a sacred Lord Vishnu temple. Start your tour to the Lord Vishnu Temple and continue sightseeing in Naimisharanya , including Chakra Teerth, Dadhichi Kund, Vyas Gaddi, Sut Gaddi, Swayambhu Manu, Satrupa, Hanuman Gaddi and Pandav Kila. After sightseeing, return to Lucknow and then proceed the airport or railway station for your next journey. The spiritual journey ends here. You will carry beautiful memories of Naimisharanya, and this UP tour package will be truly unforgettable. Places You’ll See

items: Route: Arrive in Varanasi → Varanasi - Bodhgaya → Bodhgaya – Gaya – Varanasi → Varanasi - Prayagraj – Varanasi

blocks.text: Your Varanasi Bodhgaya Prayagraj trip begins when our My Quick Trippers team welcomes you at the airport or railway station and takes you to your hotel. If you add a guide, they will come with the driver and help you during the whole day. After you check in, visit these places in Varanasi- Vishwanath Temple Annapurna Mandir Vishalakshi Mandir Kal Bhairava Durga Mandir Mana Mandir Sankat Mochan Mandir Birla Mandir Ganga Ghats (River Front) - Watch the famous Ganga Aarti, and you can also enjoy it from a boat (Optional). After exploring the main attractions in Varanasi, stay overnight at your hotel in Varanasi. Note: Pooja, Aarti, and Sugam Darshan can be booked online only. Weblink: https://shrikashivishwanath.org Vishwanath Temple- Morning Darshan- 4:00 AM to 11:00 AM Afternoon Darshan- 12:00 PM to 7:00 PM Evening Darshan- 8:30 PM to 9:00 PM Places You’ll See

After breakfast, start your journey to Bodhgaya visit the Mahabodhi Temple , a UNESCO World Heritage site built by Emperor Ashoka. Explore here beautiful gardens, old stone artwork, and the holy Bodhi tree where Buddha meditated. Later, explore other important sites like Animesh Lochana Temple (over 2,300 years old), Buddhist Dharma Chakra (Buddhist monument), Lotus Tank, Archaeological Museum, Thai Temple, Indosan Nipponji Temple, Gelugpa Tibetan Monastery and the Giant Buddha Statue (about 80 feet tall). Overnight stay in Bodhgaya. Note - Some temples and museums don’t allow photos so please follow the rules. Places You’ll See
Day 3: Bodhgaya – Gaya (15 km/35 min) – Varanasi (257 km/ 6hr)

In the morning visit the Vishnu Pad Temple , famous for the sacred footprint of Lord Vishnu known as Dharmasila. A 40 cm long footprint of Lord Vishnu is in solid rock and covered with a silver plate. Perform Pind Daan (offerings and prayers for your ancestors) at this holy place. It is believed to help your ancestors’ souls rest in peace and bring you happiness and good luck. First, do prayers at Brahma and Gayatri Ghat, then at Pita Maheshwar, and lastly at Pretshila. After the rituals, proceed for the drive to Varanasi, which takes around 6 hours. On arrival, check in to the hotel and enjoy an overnight stay in Varanasi. Note- Vishnupad Temple timings are 5:00 am to 12:30 pm and 2:00 pm to 11:00 pm. Places You’ll See
Day 4: Varanasi - Prayagraj – Varanasi (240 km/ Approx. 6 hours)

After breakfast, continue the journey to Prayagraj and visit Triveni Sangam, where Ganga, Yamuna, and the invisible Saraswati meet. Take a dip and pray there. After the holy ritual, take a half-day tour of Prayagraj and visit Allahabad Fort (a historic fort with great views of the river), Allahabad Museum, Anand Bhawan (the home of the Nehru family), and Swaraj Bhawan (where freedom leaders once stayed). Stop at Alopi Devi Temple, a well-known holy Shaktipeeth. Next, return to Varanasi and check into your hotel for an overnight stay. Places You’ll See
Day 5: Varanasi - Morning Ganga Boat Ride, Sarnath Visit, Temple Tour & Departure

Total distance- 30 to 40 Approx. Experience the morning in Varanasi with a sunrise boat ride on the Ganges. See people performing prayers and rituals on the Ghats. You can bathe at your hotel or take a holy dip in the river. After that, visit the Vishwanath Temple, a very sacred temple in India. Then go to Sarnath, where Lord Buddha gave his first teaching. Be sure to see the Dhamek Stupa, a tall and beautiful Stupa that’s great for photos. You can also see the Buddha temples, Chaukhandi Stupa and Archaeological Museum. After sightseeing your Varanasi Bodhgaya Prayagraj tour ends as you are transferred to Varanasi Railway Station/ Airport for your next journey. Note - Varanasi needs a lot of walking around temples and Ghats. Wear comfortable shoes. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Today you will arrive at Varanasi. After arriving at Varanasi Railway Station/ Airport, you will be greeted by one of our representatives who will transfer you to your pre-booked hotel, where you’ll check in and relax for some time. Later, you’ll head out for Kashi sightseeing Visit famous temples, including the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple. Visit Vishalakshi Temple Darshan at Annapurna Temple Darshan of Baba Kal Kalbhairav at Baba Kal Kal Bhairav Temple Evening: In the evening, you will embark on a boat cruise on the River Ganges. You will explore the famous Ghats of Varanasi and experience the city’s sacred vibes (For this, you will have to pay an additional cost). Later, you will attend the Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat. You can do this either during a private boat ride or from the Ghat itself. Have an Overnight Stay in Varanasi Vishwanath Temple Darshan timing - 04:00 am to 11:00 am 08:30 pm to 09:00 pm and 12:00 pm to 7:00 pm Sapta rishi 07:00 pm to 08:30 pm Please note: You can book Sugam Darshan, Pooja, and Aarti online. Places You’ll See

Relish a tasty breakfast, and then you’ll head to Bodhgaya , the site of Lord Buddha’s enlightenment. After arriving at Bodhgaya, you will check into your pre-reserved hotel. You will begin your sightseeing tour by visiting the Mahabodhi Temple , one of the most famous Buddhist temples in the world. It is considered to be the site where Buddha attained enlightenment under the Maha Bodhi Tree , which is considered to be the original Peepal tree’s descendant. Explore the other popular attractions, such as Buddhist Dharma Chakra Animesh Lochana Temple Lotus tank Thai Temple Archaeological Museum Gelugpa Tibetan Monastery Indosan Nipponji Temple Giant statue of Buddha You can meditate or explore the surreal surroundings of Bodhgaya in the evening. You will have an overnight stay at your hotel in Bodh Gaya. Places You’ll See
Day 3: Bodhgaya – Gaya (35 min/12 km) – Varanasi (7hr/250 km)

Early in the morning, you will be transferred to Vishnupad Temple , which houses Lord Vishnu’s sacred footprint. It is the site where Pind Daan is performed by people to liberate their ancestors from the endless cycle of birth and death. Situated on the banks of the River Phalgu, Vishnupad Temple is one of the most famous Hindu temples in Gaya, Bihar, India. It’s a major pilgrimage center for those who want to attain salvation. You will then visit Maa Sarva Mangala Gauri Shakti Peeth and head to Pretshila. Later, you will head back to Varanasi, and you will check into your pre-booked hotel. You can spend the evening as you want. You can attend Ganga Aarti at the sacred Ghats. You will have an overnight stay in Varanasi. Places You’ll See

Early Morning: You will start your day with a boat ride on the River Ganges. You can explore the sacred Ghats such as Harishchandra Ghat, Assi Ghat, and Manikarnika Ghat. If you have time, you can visit the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. Later in the Morning You will head to the famous temples of Varanasi: Durga Mandir New Vishwanath Temple Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple Tulsi Manas Temple Explore the Bharat Kala Bhawan Museum and the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) campus. Afternoon In the afternoon, you will embark on a drive to Sarnath. You will also explore: Chaukhandi Stupa Dhamek Stupa Buddhist Temples Evening Boat ride on the Ganga River at Dashashwamedh Ghat. Have an overnight stay in Varanasi. Places You’ll See

Morning: Relish a tasty breakfast in the morning, and then you will head out on a drive to Prayagraj. On the way, you will visit the Vindhyachal Devi Temple and seek Mother Divine Shakti’s blessings. You will then visit Sitamarhi , where Mother Sita entered the earth. You will then head to Prayagraj and explore famous sites, including Anand Bhavan. Visit Lalita Devi Temple: One of the 51 sacred Shakti Peeth. Visit Alopi Devi Temple Seek spiritual bliss at Shri Nagvasuki Temple Evening Aarti at Ghat Have an overnight stay in Prayagraj. Places You’ll See

Early Morning: You will visit Triveni Sangam—the confluence of the mythical Saraswati, Ganga, and Yamuna rivers, where you can take a holy dip. Holy bath and boat ride in Sangam: Enjoy a boat ride on the Sangam & Yamuna River. Bade Hanuman Mandir: Seek blessings at the Hanuman Mandir. Visit Akshayavat Tree and Temple: Within the Patalpuri temple in Prayagraj Fort, the sacred fig tree is worshiped as Akshayavat. Devotees believe that Sita, Ram, and Lakshman rested under this tree. Visit Prayagraj Fort: Built in 1583 by Akbar at the confluence of the Yamuna and Ganges Rivers. Later, you will head out on a drive to Ayodhya. Once you have arrived, you will check into your pre-booked hotel and relax, and later you will have the sightseeing tour of Ayodhya. Evening: At Ram ki Paidi , you will witness the divine Sarayu Aarti. Stroll by the Ram ki Paidi Ghats. If you have time, you can visit Ram Janmabhoomi Temple. Overnight stay at your hotel in Ayodhya. Places You’ll See
Day 7: Spiritual and Cultural Exploration of Ayodhya & Departure

Visit the Saryu River: You will take a dip in the Saryu River. Visit Ram Janmabhoomi Temple , the birthplace of Lord Rama. Absorb the sacred vibes of Hanuman Garhi Temple , which is dedicated to Lord Hanuman. Explore the Kanak Bhavan Temple , which is renowned for its gold-plated domes. Visit Nageshwarnath Temple , which is dedicated to Lord Shiva. Explore Dashrath Mahal , King Dashrath’s residence. If you have time, you can Visit Valmiki Ramayana Bhawan , where you can see illustrated depictions of the Ramayana epic. You will visit Treta Ke Thakur Temple. Evening: You will depart from Ayodhya. Our driver will drop you at your preferred location. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Vietnam Visa Information for Indian Citizens

items: 1. Indian citizens need to have a valid visa to enjoy holidays in Vietnam. The passport must have six months' validity from arrival, with two blank pages for a visa stamp.
2. If you are applying for a single-entry e-visa for Vietnam, it will cost around INR 1500. You can apply for a visa through any Vietnamese government portal or a reputable tour Agency.

1. Respect the local culture and customs - The people of Vietnam are reserved, but they are also outgoing and friendly. While visiting any religious place, you need to cover your knees and shoulders. Dress modestly to respect Vietnam's sacred traditions and culture, especially in spiritual places.

2. Get the Visa in Advance- Without a Visa, you won't be able to travel to Vietnam. You must apply for a Visa 10-20 days before your travel date. Don't forget to bring pre-approval papers and a visa upon arrival.
3. Pack weather-specific items- The weather in Vietnam varies according to the region. Check the weather patterns before planning your journey and pack accordingly.
4. Wear comfortable footwear. Vietnam has many beautiful tourist attractions within walking distance. You need to wear sturdy and comfortable shoes while exploring Vietnam.

Q1: Is Vietnam Visa Free for Indians?
Ans: No, a Vietnam visa is not free for Indians. After getting a VPP approval letter, you must apply for a visa through the e-visa system for a visa-on-arrival (VOA).
Q2: What is the cost of a Vietnam visa for Indian Travellers?
Ans: If you are applying for a single-entry visa for Vietnam, it will cost around INR 1500. It is also very easy to use from a Vietnamese government portal.
Q3: Can I cover Vietnam in 5 Days from Delhi?
Ans: Yes, you can cover your Vietnam trip from Delhi within 5 days. Plan your Vietnam Itinerary and budget. You can also book our budget Vietnam Tour package to explore Vietnam in 5 Days.
Q4: Is a Vietnam Trip for Indians from Delhi costly?

Ans: Vietnam is one of the most visited countries by Indians due to affordability. If budget-conscious, book any of our budget Vietnam Travel packages from Delhi. Our package cost starts from INR 15,000. Hence, a trip to Vietnam from Delhi is not costly for Indians.
Q5: How far is Vietnam from Delhi?

Ans: If you take a direct flight from Delhi to Vietnam, you will arrive in 4-5 hours. The distance from Vietnam to Delhi is around 3586 km. If you take connecting flights, the travel time will be extended, especially in cities like Bangkok or Singapore.
Q6: Which airlines fly from Delhi to Vietnam?
Ans: Some major airlines that fly from Delhi to Vietnam are Vietnam Airlines, VietJet Air, Air India and Indigo Airlines. Some of these airlines operate direct flights to Vietnam from Delhi.

blocks.text: If you want to see the natural beauty, ancient architecture, and hustle-bustle of an active metropolis, all rolled into one, then come to Vietnam! This country enchants you with its green rice fields, mist-covered mountain peaks, rivers lakes, and unique floating villages! While you’re falling for its scenic landscapes, Vietnam will take you by surprise with its modern skyscrapers and vibrant city life. And that’s not all! Vietnam has a long history and places of sublime cultural importance - a true paradise for history buffs. Tourists often choose Vietnam tour packages to enjoy its rich heritage and one-of-a-kind charm

items: Best Places to Visit during Vietnam Trip
