blocks.text: Why Choose My Quick Trippers for Vietnam Tour Packages?

Whether you like to splay out on sandy beaches near azure waters, cycle through the peaceful, pristine villages in the countryside, or explore the rich history of Vietnam, there is something for everyone here! This postcard-perfect country is a must-visit, at least once in your life. To make your travel easy and truly hassle-free, we bring you the best of the best Vietnam travel packages . A Vietnam trip with us will give you the best experience of Vietnam! So don’t wait, witness its unparalleled charm and book your Vietnam tour today!
Best Places to Visit during Vietnam Trip

Vietnam has it all – from calm, serene countryside to a modern world, like no other! So do include a mix and match of these places in your Vietnam travel packages to make the most out of your trip. Here’s a list of must-visit places in the Asian country:

The capital city of Vietnam, Hanoi, is a city with a charm of its own kind! From boasting of modern vibrant places to possessing colonial charm to still practicing ancient traditions, Hanoi captures the past and present spirit of Vietnam supremely well and therefore is a must-visit on your Vietnam trip.

items: Old Quarter : This complex of narrow streets will wow you with cafes, traditional shops, and must-try street food.

Hoan Kiem Lake : This serene lake is perfect for refreshing yourself. In addition, it holds Turtle Tower and Ngoc Son Temple at its centre. They are a sight to behold and therefore should definitely be on your Vietnam holiday package.
Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum : Pay homage to Vietnam’s one of the most revolutionary leaders, Ho Chi Minh, as this is his final resting place!
Temple of Literature : Visit Vietnam’s very first university, dedicated to renowned Chinese philosopher Confucius.
Vietnamese Women’s Museum : Get to know how Vietnamese women changed and influenced the culture and history of the country over the years in this class-apart museum.

blocks.text: This UNESCO World Heritage Site must be added to your Vietnam travel packages as it’s famous for its dreamlike karst limestone formations and pillars rising from emerald waters.

items: Enjoy a nighttime traditional junk boat cruise and soak in the stunning views.
Take Kayaking through hidden lagoons and also caves, such as Sung Sot.
Go see the rare floating villages like Cua Van.
Discover with your own eyes the incredibly beautiful Bai Tu Long Bay. (Recommended for a Vietnam trip as it’s less crowded)
Opt for a luxury cruise with premium amenities and services.

blocks.text: Get your camera ready as you’re up for enjoying a picturesque town. Nestled in the vast mountains, Sapa is especially famous for its rich hill tribe culture and beautiful terraced rice fields. It is advised to add this beautiful location to your Vietnam holiday package during winter (December-February), mainly for the coveted views of snow-clad mountains. You can also come here in September to watch those golden rice fields in their full glory.

items: Go for jaunting trekking to scenic villages like Lao Chai, Ta Van, and Cat Cat village.
Visit the Fansipan Mountain, also known as the "Roof of Indochina". Most tourists either hike or take a cable car to reach the summit, to enjoy the breathtaking panoramic views.
Walk into the famous Sapa market and shop for local textiles and ethnic handicrafts.

Note on Snow at Sapa: Snow at Sapa is possible in December-January but is not guaranteed every year. Climate patterns have changed significantly. Do not plan specifically to see snow — treat it as a possibility, not a certainty.

blocks.text: This central Vietnam attraction was once the imperial capital of the country! Today, it’s a proud tourist hotspot for exploring ancient architecture and the history of Vietnam. Many Vietnam trip packages include this destination to give the travellers a taste of the country’s heritage.

items: Imperial City (Citadel): This vast complex houses gardens, temples, and even palaces for a wholesome sightseeing experience. An essential visit for your Vietnam trip!
Tombs of Emperors : See the ancient royals resting in peace by visiting the graves of the greats like Tu Duc, Khai Dinh, and Minh Mang.

Thien Mu Pagoda: Located on the Perfume River, this beautiful seven-storeyed temple lures tourists with its rare architectural structures. It once acted as the major organising point for the Buddhist movement and now it’s the unofficial symbol of Hue! Also, many travellers love to take a fun dragon boat ride on the Perfume River during the evenings!

blocks.text: Fancy some downtime near turquoise waters and swaying palm trees? If yes, then head straight to Phu Quoc Island on your Vietnam trip. This tropical paradise pleases its tourists with refreshing clear waters and sandy beaches. You’re really in for a treat! People generally include this destination on their Vietnam tour packages during November-April as this is the most pleasant season.

items: Sao Beach : Come take a dive in its crystal blue water or saunter around in white sand.
Phu Quoc National Park : Spot the interesting wild animals or go for unforgettable hiking adventures.
Night Market : Visit the night market for some souvenir shopping or gorge on some local seafood.

blocks.text: Offering lush greenery and oh-so-stunning karst landscapes, the beautiful city of Ninh Binh is an all-time tourist favourite. Also known as “Halong Bay on land”, this site is famous for its incredible picturesque sceneries.

items: Visit Hoa Lu, the ancient capital of Vietnam. Once highly politically significant, it now serves as an excellent tourist hub.
Enjoy the thrilling boat rides through Tam Coc or Trang An’s waterways.
Enjoy the vast panoramic views of rice fields by climbing the Mua Cave.

blocks.text: This is the largest city in Vietnam, and therefore expect to see a bustling, vibrant metropolis. Located in southern Vietnam, it is famous for both – its modern skyscrapers and rich history.

items: War Remnants Museum : Visit this amazing museum which showcases the Vietnam War in a rather somber but fitting manner.
Cu Chi Tunnels : Get a movie-like thrill exploring this underground tunnel network, used exclusively during the war!
Ben Thanh Market : It’s perfect for relishing street food and shopping for local goods.

blocks.text: Dotted with palm trees, this coastal town is a popular beach resort with stunning hotels and restaurants. The wind condition is mostly steady and therefore it’s popular for water sports like sailing, kitesurfing, and windsurfing. Moreover, it’s a popular gateway from Ho Chi Minh City, therefore, many Vietnam travel packages include this coastal escape in the itinerary.

items: White and Red Sand Dunes : They’re perfect for sandboarding or riding an ATV.
Fairy Stream : Surrounded by colourful cliffs, this shallow stream has whimsical landscapes to offer with vivid colours from nature's own unique palette!

blocks.text: Top Things to Do on Your Vietnam Trip

Vietnam is a tourist dreamscape with a rich blend of history, natural beauty, and vibrant culture. To get a full taste of Vietnam, you must include the following activities in your Vietnam holiday package:
1. Enjoy the Vibrant Chi Minh City
This bustling city has a lot to offer to its travellers:

items: Visit the historic Cu Chi Tunnels and the War Remnants Museum.
Enjoy the nightlife at bars and clubs, especially in District 1 as it’s always teemed with tourists.
Wine and dine at the Ben Thanh Market.

blocks.text: 2. Discover the Ancient Charm of Hoi An
Hoi An has a beauty of its own. Consider doing the following things:

items: Stroll in the yellowish glow of lanterns in the streets of the Old Town
Be a part of the Lantern Festival
Enjoy the blue-green waters at An Bang Beach

blocks.text: Explore this region comprising vast rivers, islands, and swamps. To take your experience one notch up, try:

items: Boat riding through the beautiful lush canals.
Shop in the floating markets like Cai Rang.
Enjoy a staycation in a riverside village.

blocks.text: This turquoise water beach is super relaxing. Enjoy things such as:

items: Unwinding on beaches like Sao Beach
Diving or snorkelling around coral reefs
Visit fish sauce factories and local pepper plantations

blocks.text: Do not miss out on iconic dishes like:

items: Pho : A comfort noodle soup for many
Banh Mi : This is the Vietnamese version of a baguette sandwich
Bun Cha : This dish tastes as good as its name sounds. This grilled pork with noodles is a “love at first taste” for many.
Cao Lau : This traditional noodle soup is straight from the city of Hoi

blocks.text: If you hit Vietnam in the right season, cycling through its countryside is a breeze! Whether you ride in serene villages or through lush paddy fields, you’re guaranteed to have a refreshing journey throughout.

Coffee is more than just a beverage in Vietnam. It’s a special ritual enjoyed with friends and family and is usually accompanied with hearty conversations. To get to the core of the coffee culture, you can do the following things on your Vietnam trip:

items: Try Ca phe sua da – it’s Vietnamese iced coffee with condensed milk
Drink traditional egg coffee in Hanoi
Take a trip to coffee plantations Da Lat and Buon Ma Thuot

blocks.text: 8. Relish the Charm of Cham Islands
Enjoy this magical island with picture-perfect natural beauty. To get a wholesome experience, you must include the following activities on your trip to Vietnam:

items: Go for scuba diving or snorkelling in the clear blue waters
Relish fresh seafood and sandy beaches

Frequently Asked Questions about Vietnam Tour Packages
Q1: What is the best time to visit Vietnam?
Ans. The best time to visit Vietnam is from March to April, as the weather is pleasant with clear skies and therefore this time is perfect for sightseeing and outdoor activities.
Q2: How many days are ideal for visiting Vietnam?
Ans. There are two recommended durations:
5-7 days : You can cover major tourist hotspots like Ho Chi Minh City, Ha Long Bay, and Hanoi.
10-14 days : In this window, you can include additional destinations like the Mekong Delta, Sapa, Hue, and Hoi An.
Q3: How much does a Vietnam tour package cost from India?
Ans. The cost of a Vietnam tour depends on various factors, like your travel style, duration, and sights in the itinerary. Here’s a quick summary:
This includes budget hotels, eating local and street food, transport through public or shared transport, and basic entry fees for sightseeing.
This involves 3-4 star hotel stays, dining in local restaurants, transport through private vehicles/domestic flights, and guided tours for sightseeing.
This one boasts of luxury hotels or resort stays, fine dining, transport through private transfers or domestic flights, and sightseeing via luxury cruises and private tours.
Q4: What should I pack for a Vietnam tour?

Ans. Pack breathable, lightweight clothes as Vietnam’s climate is humid and warm. However, for northern regions like Hanoi or Sapa, pack a sweater or light jacket. Carry swimwear for beaches and hotel pools. Bring sunscreen and a hat for protection from the sun.
Q5: How to plan for a Vietnam trip with family?

Ans. A 7-10 day trip is recommended for a Vietnam family trip. Sights like Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi, Mekong Delta, Ha Long Bay, Hoi An, Da Nang, and Ho Chi Minh City must be included in your Vietnam tour packages. Some family-friendly activities include cycling through villages & rice fields, relaxing on beaches, going on cruises, and exploring the natural beauty of the country.

blocks.text: It is designed for pilgrims who want to seek the blessing of the goddess Yamuna on the auspicious event of Pushkaralu which takes place only once every 12 years. It is marked by the special astrological event when Jupiter enters Cancer. This holy tour will take you to the revered Yamunotri Temple from Delhi via Haridwar, Dehradun, Mussoorie, Barkot, and Janki Chatti.

items: Route: Arrive Delhi – Haridwar → Haridwar – Dehradun – Barkot / Janki Chatti → Barkot - Yamunotri Snan – Barkot → Barkot – Delhi

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrive Delhi – Haridwar (220 km/5 Hrs)

Once you arrive at the New Delhi Airport/Railway Station, you’ll be warmly greeted and assisted by our tour representative. Now, you’ll be driven to Haridwar. Enjoy the scenic drive all along. Once you reach the holy city, check into your hotel and relax for a while. In the evening, head to Har Ki Pauri for bathing on the sacred banks of the River Ganges. Also, attend the evening Ganga Aarti . Visit Brahma Kund , too. This is believed to be the very spot where drops of Amrit (nectar) fell. If time permits, also visit the Manasa Devi Temple. Places You’ll See
Day 2: Haridwar – Dehradun – Barkot / Janki Chatti (240 kms / 9 Hrs)

After breakfast in the morning, set out for a morning drive to Barkot via Dehradun & Mussoorie. Along the way, we’ll make a stop at the Kempty Falls . Enjoy the scenic Himalayan views here. Continue your drive to Barkot . Once you get there, check into your hotel and enjoy an overnight stay. Places You’ll See
Day 3: Barkot - Yamunotri Snan – Barkot (45 Kms road / 6 kms Trek)

Start your day early and drive towards Janki Chatti (trek starting point) in the morning. When you get there, begin your trek or hire a pony/Doli (on a direct payment basis). Once you arrive at Yamunotri, take a holy dip in the waters of the River Yamuna. At Surya Kund , cook rice in the hot spring. This is the Prasadam that you can also take home. Also, offer your prayers at the Divya Shila and seek blessings. After your Darshan, trek back to Janki Chatti. Now, you’ll be driven back to Barkot for an overnight stay. Yamunotri Temple : The temple is dedicated to Goddess Yamuna who is believed to be daughter of Lord Surya and sister of Yamraj. Surya Kund: There are a number of thermal springs close to the temple, which flows into numerous pools. The most important of these is “Surya Kund” and is dedicated to Lord Surya. Divya Shila: According to mythology, river Yamuna came out for the very first time from “Divya Shila”. This is the worship place of Yamuna Mata. Trek Options: By Walk: 6 Kms / 2-3 Hrs one way Horse: ₹3,000 per person (Approx) Palki: ₹8,000 to 10,000 per person (Approx) Places You’ll See

In the morning, you’ll head back to Delhi after breakfast. Enjoy the scenic views along the way. We’ll also take a few comfort breaks as required. Once we arrive in Delhi , you’ll be dropped off at Delhi Airport/Railway Station. Hope you have a memorable trip full of beautiful memories. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Get a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to attend Yamuna Pushkaralu, one of the most revered Hindu festivals that is celebrated once every twelve years when Jupiter enters Gemini. This year it will be held from June 2, 2026, to June 13, 2026. It is believed that if you take a dip in the Yamuna River during this period, your soul gets purified and you get to seek divine blessings.

items: Route: Dehradun and Local Sightseeing → Dakpatthar Visit and Yamuna Pushkaralu Rituals → Haridwar / Dehradun

blocks.text: Day 01: Arrival at Dehradun and Local Sightseeing

You begin your journey by arriving at Dehradun Airport or Railway Station , where a tour representative receives you and helps with the transfer. The drive itself is short, but traffic around Dehradun and Haridwar can sometimes slow things down, especially during pilgrimage seasons. After checking into your pre-booked hotel , it’s advisable to rest for a while. The terrain and climate here are different from the plains, and even light travel fatigue can show up early. Later in the day, you visit two well-known local attractions: Robber’s Cave, a narrow river cave that requires a short walk on uneven ground Tapkeshwar Temple, a naturally formed cave temple where water continuously drips over the Shivling Both places are popular, so expect crowds in the afternoon. Comfortable footwear is important here. The evening is kept light. You return to the hotel and settle in for an overnight stay, allowing your body to adjust before the next day’s rituals. Places You’ll See
Day 02: Dakpatthar Visit and Yamuna Pushkaralu Rituals

This is the most spiritually significant day of the tour and also the most physically engaging. After an early start, you drive towards Dakpatthar , a quiet stretch along the River Yamuna. The area is calmer than Haridwar, but during Yamuna Pushkaralu, the ghats can still become crowded at peak ritual hours. Here, you take a holy dip in the Yamuna, followed by participation in the Yamuna Pushkaralu rituals. These rituals often take time, depending on priest availability and crowd flow, so patience is important. Elderly travellers or those with mobility concerns should move cautiously, as river steps can be slippery. Post rituals, you return to Haridwar by afternoon. In the evening, the focus shifts to the River Ganga: A sacred dip at Har Ki Pauri , where crowd density is usually high Attendance at the evening Ganga Aarti , which is spiritually uplifting but involves standing for a long duration A visit to Brahma Kund , traditionally believed to be the spot where drops of Amrit fell After a long but fulfilling day, you return to the hotel for a quiet overnight stay . Places You’ll See

The final day is intentionally kept simple. After breakfast, you check out from the hotel and proceed towards Dehradun Airport or the railway station , depending on your onward journey. Morning departures are usually smoother, while afternoon travel may face traffic near Haridwar. With this, the Yamuna Pushkaralu 2026 journey concludes . The experience is less about sightseeing and more about participation, patience, and spiritual intent—something that tends to stay with travellers long after they return. Places You’ll See

Pushkar is an ancient temple town located on the shore of Pushkar Lake near Ajmer City and headquarters of Pushkar tehsil in the Ajmer district in the Indian state of Rajasthan. It is situated about 10 km (6.2 mi) northwest of Ajmer and about 150 km southwest of Jaipur. The town lies at an elevation of about 510 metres and is surrounded by hills on three sides, with Nag Pahar forming a natural boundary between Ajmer and Pushkar.

Pushkar is renowned for its rich cultural heritage, historical significance, and diverse attractions. From ancient temples and forts to modern amenities and natural beauty, Pushkar offers an unforgettable experience for every traveler.

The ideal time to visit Pushkar is during the winter months (October to March) when the weather is pleasant and perfect for sightseeing. Monsoon season (July to September) brings lush greenery, while summer (April to June) is suitable for high-altitude areas.

blocks.text: The Yamuna Pushkaralu Spiritual Tour offers you a trip of divine purification during the auspicious Yamuna Pushkaram.

items: Route: Arrive Varanasi Sightseeing → Varanasi – Prayagraj → Prayagraj - Ayodhya → Ayodhya / Varanasi Departure

blocks.text: Once you arrive at Varanasi Airport/Railway Station, you will be warmly greeted and assisted by our representative. You’ll be taken to your hotel now. Check in and relax for a while. After this, you’ll be taken for a sightseeing tour of: Shri Kashi Vishwanath temple Annapurna Temple Vishalakshi Temple Baba Kal Bhairav Temple In the evening, you’ll be taken for boat cruise on the river Ganga . Also, explore historic Ghats of Varanasi and soak in the spiritual aura of the holy city. Later, be a part of the mesmerizing Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat . Return to the hotel for an overnight stay. Key Notes: Vishwanath Temple Darshan timing - 4:00 AM to 11:00 AM & 12:00 PM to 7:00 PM, 8:30 PM to 10:00PM Aarti Timings - Mangla Aarti - 3:00 AM, Sapta Rishi Aarti - 7:00 PM to 8:30 PM, Shayan Aarti 10:30 PM Darshan Booking - Devotees book their Sugam Darshan tickets online: https://shrikashivishwanath.org Places You’ll See

In the morning, you’ll be driven to Prayagraj. On arrival, check into your hotel. Later, you’ll be taken to the Triveni Sangam – confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers. Take a holy dip here and perform other sacred rituals. After this, take a boat ride in Sangam. Now, you’ll be taken to the following places: Bade Hanuman Mandir: Seek Darshan of Lord Hanuman. Akshayavat Temple and Tree: This sacred fig tree is believed to be the one under which Ram, Lakshman, and Sita rested. As per the ancient Hindu texts, it’s believed that whoever worships Akshayavat gets freed from sins. Prayagraj Fort (Allahabad Fort): This was built by Akbar in 1583. Its vicinity to the sacred Yamuna River gives it a spiritual touch. Alopi Devi Temple: This is also a Shaktipith temple. Lalita Devi Temple: It is revered as Madhaveswari Devi in scriptures. It is believed that the fingers of Maa Sati’s hand fell here. Shri Nagvasuki Temple: Devotees believe that worshipping here removes obstacles, protects from snake afflictions (Sarpa Dosh), and brings peace and prosperity. Your overnight stay will be in Prayagraj. Places You’ll See

After breakfast, you’ll be driven to Ayodhya. Enjoy a sightseeing tour of the following places: Ram Janmabhoomi Temple: This is the birthplace of Lord Rama. Hanuman Garhi Temple: It’s a temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman. Kanak Bhavan Temple: It’s known for its gold-plated domes. Ram ki Paidi: This is yet another temple dedicated to Lord Rama. Dashrath Mahal: This was the residence of Lord Ram's father, King Dashrath. In the evening, you’ll be taken to attend the Saryu River Aarti at Naya Ghat. Also, take this time to stroll around the Saryu River banks. Your overnight stay will be in Ayodhya. Key Notes: Sri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple timings: Darshan Timing - 7:00 AM to 12:00 PM & 1:00 PM to 7:00 PM Aarti Timings - Mangla Aarti - 4:00 AM, Shringar Aarti - 6:00 AM, Shayan Aarti 10:00 PM Other Temples timing: Hanuman Garhi Temple - 4:30 AM to 12:00PM - Bhog Time - 12:30 PM to 9:00 PM Kanak Bhavan Temple - 8:00 AM to 11.30 AM & 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM Dashrath Mahal - 8:00 AM to 12.30 PM & 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM Darshan Booking: Devotees book their Sugam Darshan tickets online at: https://online.srjbtkshetra.org/#/mobileVerification . Places You’ll See

In the morning after breakfast, you’ll be taken to Ayodhya airport, Lucknow or Varanasi (depending on the return flight). If you visit Lucknow, you’ll be taken on a sightseeing tour of: Bada Imambara (6:00 AM – 5:00 PM, Fridays 3:00 PM – 5:00 PM, Closed on Mondays) Rumi Darwaza Residency Complex (10:00 AM – 5:00 PM) After this, you’ll be transferred to the airport. And this concludes your trip with us. Places You’ll See

blocks.text: Yamunotri Yatra is a holy trip that is highly revered in Hinduism. On this sacred pilgrimage, you visit the Yamunotri Temple , located in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand. The shrine is dedicated to Goddess Yamuna .
It is also one of the Dhams in the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit , and is visited first in the Yatra.
Why Yamunotri Is First Dham in Char Dham Circuit?

As per the Hindu customs, the Char Dham Yatra should be done in a clockwise direction , starting from the west. And Yamunotri falls on the westernmost side of the Char Dham circuit, and hence it's visited first.

Another reason is that Char Dham Yatra follows the origin of the sacred rivers : from west to east. And Yamuna (originating at Yamunotri) lies west of River Ganga (originating at Gangotri). Hence, the order:

Also, from the travel perspective, it is practical to start your Yatra from Yamunotri. This Dham is located at the lowest altitude among all the Dhams, and therefore helps the pilgrims acclimatise better and helps them only gradually move towards the other higher altitudes sites.

blocks.text: Here is the detailed route map, starting from Haridwar:
Haridwar → Rishikesh → Chamba → Mussoorie → Kempty Falls → Barkot → Nainbagh → Purola → Janki Chatti → Yamunotri Temple (6 km trek)
The total distance from Haridwar to Yamunotri is about 311 km (including the trek). The total time is about 14-16 hours by road , in addition to 3-4 hours of trekking .
If you start from Delhi, then the total distance up to Yamunotri is about 450 km (including trek). It will take about 14–16 hours by road + 3–4 hours trek.
The history of Yamunotri goes back to the ancient ages . This is another reason the place where the temple is located is considered to be extremely pious in nature.

Yamunotri is also the place where the prominent Hindu Sage Asit Muni used to stay and take his bath in both the rivers of Ganga and Yamuna, which in those times used to flow next to each other. So the sage set up his hermitage here.
Later on Adi Shankaracharya, the propagator of Advaita Vedanta, re-established this temple as a part of the Char Dham Yatra circuit , which further increased its spiritual significance in Hinduism.

Yamunotri Temple is dedicated to the goddess Yamuna. It also honours the Yamuna River , as the river is considered to be the manifestation of the Goddess herself. This makes the Yamunotri temple a unique and one of the rarest temples in India.
The Goddess is also the sister of Yama, the God of death, in Hindu mythology. It's said that whoever visit the temple does not suffer from untimely or painful death .

People from all over the globe flock here to offer their prayer to the goddess at her place of birth. Devotees make their way to the shrine after covering a gruelling trek from Janki Chatti to worship the glistening black pyramidal stone . The stone is said to be the form of the goddess herself, making it her holy abode.

blocks.text: The registration for the Yatra is mandatory . The Uttarakhand government has made it compulsory in order to better track the pilgrim movement.
You can register in two ways: online and offline.
For online registration , simply visit the official portal of the Uttarakhand Tourism . You must have a valid government ID (Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, etc.) and a phone number for OTP verification.
For offline registration , there are counters available at Haridwar, Rishikesh, and other base towns. You must also produce your government ID.

blocks.text: Here are some travel tips for the Yatra:

items: Do not forget to register for the Yatra , as it is mandatory.
Always check the weather before travelling for the day. This is because the Himalayan weather can change suddenly.
Don't start your trek in the afternoon . This way, you can avoid afternoon weather changes and crowd congestion.
Avoid trekking alone , and try to trek in a group. This will be useful in emergency situations.
Follow instructions given by temple staff and police.
Carry cash as ATMs are limited in remote areas.
In order to avoid sun damage , wear sunscreen and sunglasses. Also, wear a cap.

Yamunotri, also Jamnotri, is the source of the Yamuna River and the seat of the Goddess Yamuna in Hinduism. It is situated at an altitude of 3,293 metres (10,804 ft) in the Garhwal Himalayas and located approximately 150 kilometres (93 mi) North of Uttarkashi, the headquarters of the Uttarkashi district in the Garhwal Division of Uttarakhand, India.
